lore: Messages and directives are sent, faster than light, on subspace radio signals, amplified by networks of relay stations.
game_text: Plays on a Bajoran ship; its controller targets one of their Bajoran facilities on this spaceline (nullified if none). Ship must do nothing but move toward it. Nullified on arrival at its location.

name: Incoming Message: Cardassian
lore: Messages and directives are sent, faster than light, on subspace radio signals amplified by networks of relay stations.
game_text: Plays on a Cardassian ship; its controller targets one of their Cardassian facilities on this spaceline (nullified if none). Ship must do nothing but move toward it. Nullified on arrival at its location.

name: Incoming Message: Ferengi
lore: Messages and directives are sent, faster than light, on subspace radio signals amplified by networks of relay stations.
game_text: Plays on a Ferengi ship; its controller targets one of their Ferengi facilities on this spaceline (nullified if none). Ship must do nothing but move toward it. Nullified on arrival at its location.

name: Kevin Uxbridge
lore: Immortal omnipotent being called a Douwd. Lived secretly as a human. Took a human wife who was killed by the Husnocks at Delta Rana IV.
game_text: Nullifies any one Event card in play (except for Treaty cards) OR any other card played as an Event card. (Immune to Amanda Rogers.)

name: Kevin Uxbridge
lore: Immortal omnipotent being called a Douwd. Lived secretly as a human. Took a human wife who was killed by the Husnocks at Delta Rana IV.
game_text: Nullifies any one Event card in play (except for Treaty cards) OR any other card played as an Event card. (Immune to Amanda Rogers.)

name: Kevin Uxbridge: Convergence
lore: A Douwd, a race of sentient energy beings of "disguises and false surroundings." He is capable of using his enormous powers to stop threats with a single thought.
game_text: Nullifies all Event (except Shield) in play at any one spaceline location.

name: Kevin Uxbridge: Convergence
lore: A Douwd, a race of sentient energy beings of "disguises and false surroundings." He is capable of using his enormous powers to stop threats with a single thought.
game_text: Nullifies all Event (except Shield) in play at any one spaceline location.

name: Latinum Payoff
lore: Gold-pressed latinum, which cannot be replicated, is a valuable metal used as currency in many less-developed sectors, primarily outside Federation space.
game_text: Plays if Greed aboard your ship when it destroys another ship in battle (once per destroyed ship). X=3 for each OFFICER aboard destroyed ship.

name: Loss of Orbital Stability
lore: If a ship's orbit decays, it can be drawn toward a planet and burn out in its atmosphere.
game_text: Plays on any ship orbiting a planet. Ship has NO RANGE until end of turn, and is destroyed at end of its owner’s next turn unless SHIELDS>4; then discard interrupt.

name: Lure of the Nexus
lore: Though exiting the nexus is as simple as wishing it so, its temptations are so great that few desire to leave. Those pulled away against their will are forever changed by their experience.
game_text: Prevent a personnel from leaving The Nexus. OR Relocate all personnel under The Nexus aboard a ship about to be destroyed by it; relocate ship to adjacent location. Discard interrupt.

name: Oof!
lore: Surprised by Benjamin Sisko's rather unconventional response to Q's antagonism, the allegedly omnipotent being protested, "You hit me! Picard never hit me!"

name: Oof!
lore: Surprised by Benjamin Sisko's rather unconventional response to Q's antagonism, the allegedly omnipotent being protested, "You hit me! Picard never hit me!"
game_text: Once per game, opponent loses 5 points for each copy of Amanda Rogers, Kevin Uxbridge, and Q2 they have removed from this game. (Immune to Amanda Rogers.) OR Nullifies Fightin' Words.

name: Orb Experience
lore: In 2369, Benjamin Sisko encountered the Orb of Prophecy and Change. This contact caused him to experience a flashback to his first meeting with his wife-to-be, Jennifer.
game_text: Plays on any personnel with INTEGRITY>6. Adds Orb icon. OR Plays if your Orb personnel is present with an Orb. Examine any one card in the game (once per game per Orb).

name: Outgunned
lore: On a mission inside Dominion space, the U.S.S. Defiant was surrounded by Jem'Hadar vessels. In the face of superior firepower, Benjamin Sisko elected to surrender.
game_text: Plays at start of battle against opponent's only ship here. If undocked and your total WEAPONS involved > its SHIELDS x3: battle cancelled; ship commandeered and crew captured.

name: Palor Toff: Alien Trader
lore: Rich merchant and trader from an unknown race. Friend of Kivas Fajo. Snappy dresser.
game_text: Once each turn, remove this card from the game to take a card from your discard pile (except a personnel) into your hand.

name: Phaser Burns
lore: Even on stun settings, phased energy weapons can cause severe injuries and burns if not fired judiciously in bursts.
game_text: If you have phasers or disruptors present during a personnel battle, before a winner is determined randomly select two opposing stunned cards to die.

name: Prefix Code Transmission
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Each starship is assigned a unique security code to prevent remote access to its vital systems. With knowledge of the code, a ship can be ordered to lowers its own shields.
game_text: Plays on your ship when firing on a target that has a matching affiliation or faction icon or that your infiltrator is aboard. Opposing DEFENSE total reduced by half (round down).

name: Preparation
lore: Mission briefings with senior staff are important for information and planning. Lack of preparation can be costly in some instances.
game_text: Plays on your unexamined mission if you control personnel with four different classifications there. Examine bottom seed card. OR Nullifies Lack of Preparation (but still lose points).

name: Q2
lore: Member of the Q who observed Q's act of self-sacrifice and re-instated him in the Q continuum.

name: Q2
lore: Member of the Q who observed Q's act of self-sacrifice and re-instated him in the Q continuum.
game_text: Nullifies any Amanda Rogers OR Kevin Uxbridge just played, OR a Q icon dilemma OR a dilemma with the word "Q" in title.

name: Q2

game_text: Nullifies any Amanda Rogers OR Kevin Uxbridge just played, OR a Q icon dilemma OR a dilemma with the word "Q" in title.

name: Quinn
lore: Member of the Q who felt immortal life had become futile, meaningless, and unendurable. Lobbied to be made mortal so he could commit suicide and upset the Continuum's status quo.
game_text: Thrice per game, lose points to nullify an Interrupt or Event just played or activated, unless Shield or "immune" to Kevin Uxbridge or Amanda Rogers

name: Remodulation
lore: With Borg intruders overrunning every defensive checkpoint, Jean-Luc Picard struggled with modifications to make resources more effective.

name: Remodulation
lore: With Borg intruders overrunning every defensive checkpoint, Jean-Luc Picard struggled with modifications to make resources more effective.
game_text: Nullifies Adapt: Modulate Shields. OR Once each turn, discard one or two cards and draw an equal number from the bottom of your draw deck.

name: Remodulation

name: Scan
lore: Sensor instruments can detect life signs and molecular signatures at a distance with accuracy.

game_text: Plays at the start of your turn on your ship with at least two staffing icons at a Space mission. Stop your Computer Skill and Stellar Catrography aboard to examine the bottom seed card here.

name: Scorched Hand
lore: Plasma gas from the ruptured coolant tank liquified all the organic skin grafted onto Data's endoskeletal structure.
game_text: Plays to cause each player who has more than 12 cards in hand to shuffle all but 6 (random selection) and place beneath draw deck. (Immune to Amanda Rogers.)

name: Senior Staff Meeting
lore: Standard operating procedures on starships is to call a meeting of senior officers or department heads to help find solutions of paramount problems.
game_text: Plays on ship with OFFICER, ENGINEER, MEDICAL, SCIENCE and SECURITY aboard, just before the initial attempt of a space mission. First dilemma encountered is discarded. (Captain's Order.)

name: Sense the Borg
lore: "Yes, I know — the Borg."
game_text: Plays if a Borg ship, Borg personnel, Borg Ship dilemma or Rogue Borg just entered play. Download to hand Weak Spot OR Hugh OR Borg Neuroprocessor OR Ready Room Door.

name: Smooth As an Android's Bottom?
lore: Geordi once told Data that technological perfection can shave too close. That, of course, depends on the desired results.
game_text: Once each turn, plays to draw three cards from the bottom of your draw deck (may not be converted to downloads). Place each personnel card drawn out-of-play. OR Prevents the death of one Youth personnel.

name: Temporal Narcosis
lore: Debilitating disorientation caused by prolonged exposure to a temporal disturbance, similar to nitrogen narcosis ("the bends"). Jean-Luc Picard experienced this in 2369.
game_text: Plays to flip opponent's Revolving Door OR nullify Energy Vortex or Emergency Transporter Armbands OR use an opponent's Horga'hn on this turn as if earned.

name: Temporal Rift
lore: Time displacement caused by ultra high energy explosions such as that which affected the U.S.S. Enterprise-C at Narendra III.
game_text: Plays on your ship. Ship disappears. When countdown expires, ship reappears here.

name: Temporal Wake
lore: The Borg sphere used chronometric particles to create a temporal vortex. The pursuing U.S.S. Enterprise-E was pulled in when it flew through the wake of the anomaly.
game_text: Plays if any ship or Away Team just time traveled. Choose your other ship or Away Team which was present; it follows. OR Nullifies Anti-Time Anomaly.

name: The Juggler
lore: The Juggler hosted Lwaxana Troi and Alexander Rozhenko's visit to the Parallax Colony, all the time juggling his three worlds.
game_text: Choose any player to re-shuffle the cards in their draw deck.

name: The Needs of the Many...
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: "...outweigh...." "The needs of the few." "Or the one." Captain Spock made the ultimate sacrifice not because it was noble, but because it was logical.
game_text: Nullifies a dilemma or damage marker if it would destroy your ship. Discard one of that ship's crew members (opponent's choice).

name: The Wake of the Borg
lore: The New Providence colony on Jouret IV was scooped up by the Borg in 2366, just as Federation and Romulan outposts along the Neutral Zone had been destroyed in 2364.

name: The Wake of the Borg
lore: The New Providence colony on Jouret IV was scooped up by the Borg in 2366, just as Federation and Romulan outposts along the Neutral Zone had been destroyed in 2364.

name: The Wake of the Borg
lore: The New Providence colony on Jouret IV was scooped up by the Borg in 2366, just as Federation and Romulan outposts along the Neutral Zone had been destroyed in 2364.
game_text: Plays on opponent's Neutral Zone Region missionNeutral Zone Region mission if they seeded 4 or more. End of opponent's next turn, all non-Borg ships, facilities, and personnel there are returned to hand.

name: Thine Own Self
lore: Attempting a mission with only a few personnel is dangerous. Lt. Commander Data suffered amnesia while alone on Barkon IV. He was lost and eventually "killed."
game_text: Plays on opponent's one- or two person Away Team on a planet (unless in a facility). Away Team is "lost" (place under mission). Capture (or opponent rescues) by solving mission.

name: Victory Is Life
lore: "I am First Omet'iklan. And I am dead. As of this moment we are all dead. We go into battle to win back our lives. This we do gladly, because we are Jem'Hadar. Remember... victory is life."
game_text: Once every turn, download an Equipment card to your Jem'Hadar who just helped solve a mission or win a personnel battle against another player; score points.

name: Vulcan Mindmeld
lore: Ancient Vulcan ritual which telepathically links minds to intimately share each other's thoughts and knowledge.

name: Vulcan Mindmeld
lore: Ancient Vulcan ritual which telepathically links minds to intimately share each other's thoughts and knowledge.
game_text: Plays on your Mindmeld personnel. Personnel gains the skills of one of your other personnel present until end of turn. Discard interrupt.

name: Vulcan Nerve Pinch

Also, your Bajoran espionage cards may not be nullified. Once each turn, you may download a Bajoran espionage card to one of your unsolved missions (limit one per mission), then draw two cards if you have at least two Bajoran Resistance personnel in play.

name: Beware of Q

Once per mission location, if opponent just revealed your dilemma there, you may exchange it with a dilemma named Q from your Q's Tent or hand (discard original dilemma). OR Plays to download and seed a dilemma named Q under a mission; discard objective.

Your personnel may attempt it using these requirements:Any Son'a personnel + Injector Assembly One in orbit + Treachery x2 + no opposing ships or personnel hereWhen you solve, you may skip opponent's next turn and, for rest of game, all your personnel are STRENGTH +2, add Youth, and you may unstop them each once each turn.

name: Harness Particle 010
game_text: Plays on table. Target Omega Particle (download if needed; it is immune to Kevin Uxbridge) at your mission with no Borg Only objective on it. Your Borg may scout that location. After scouting complete, if your staffed Borg cube there, you may probe:Enigma, Incident, Objective : Perfection achieved. Place on location; discard Particle . Doubles point boxes of your subsequently completed Borg Only objectives.

name: HQ: Defensive Measures
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Your personnel with any Intelligence gain 1 Leadership and may initiate battle against their own affiliation. Also, opponent may not attempt any of your missions with more than one affiliation icon on each end unless opponent attempted to seed a copy of that mission OR opponent is using an appropriate Espionage card.

name: Navigate Plasma Storms
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. End of every player's turn, if any ship is in the Badlands Region (even Mirror Universe), that player must probe: Interrupt, Doorway : Flare-up. All ships and facilities in space in that region without 3 Navigation aboard are damaged. Objective : Maelstrom. All ships and facilities in that region without 5 Navigation aboard are destroyed. Event : Plasma storms subside. Discard objective.

name: Open Diplomatic Relations
game_text: Seeds on table during doorway phase; you may seed one Treaty during this phase (cumulative). At any time, you may exchange two cards in hand for a Treaty in your discard pile. OR Plays on opponent's ship. Your Away Teams which have a V.I.P. may beam to and from that ship, and it may not voluntarily move while your V.I.P. aboard. Discard objective if your personnel battle aboard that ship.

name: Operate Wormhole Relays
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Once each turn, your staffed ship with two or fewer staffing icons and SCIENCE, Physics x2, and Astrophysics aboard may move through Barzan or Bajoran Wormhole (or between two Transwarp Network Gateways) by using RANGE equal to twice the span of the destination location, and is not stopped.

name: Organ Theft
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Once each turn, stop your Vidiian using Vidiian Harvester to "steal organs" from any non-Hologram personnel present (except an android or shape-shifter). Discard victim; you may report two Universal Vidiians (or download one) and, until end of your next turn, your Vidiians may ignore The Phage. If victim belonged to opponent, you may discard objective (thrice per game) to score points.

name: Reflection Therapy
game_text: Plays on a personnel (except Suna) if your Treachery>Honor present. Replace one regular skill with one level of another regular skill (discard if skill lost). Any player may nullify with 3 Empathy present. OR Plays on an opponent's personnel affected by Frame of Mind; personnel is captured. Discard objective if rescued or (on a later turn) to download Brainwash or Interrogation to this captive.

name: Kira Nerys
lore: Outspoken Major in Bajoran Militia. Assigned as first officer of Deep Space 9. Former member of Shakaar resistance cell. Romantically involved with Odo.

name: Shakaar Edon
lore: Leader of Shakaar resistance cell. Farmer. He refused to return soil reclamators to provisional government in 2371. Old friend of Kira Nerys.

name: Gowron of Borg
lore: Assimilated counterpart who spoke to the Empire in a parallel universe. "The knowledge and experience of the Klingon - Gowron - is part of us now."

name: Gowron of Borg
lore: Assimilated counterpart who spoke to the Empire in a parallel universe. "The knowledge and experience of the Klingon - Gowron - is part of us now."

name: Six of Eleven
lore: IDENTIFICATION: QUANTUM DRONETASK: Investigate parallel space/time. Analyze.BIOLOGICAL DISTINCTIVENESS: Human species

name: Third of Five
lore: IDENTIFICATION: TACTIC DRONETASK: Survey. Compile tactical data. Encode. Report.BIOLOGICAL DISTINCTIVENESS: Humanoid.

name: Tomalak of Borg
lore: Assimilated counterpart who spoke to the Star Empire in a parallel universe. "The knowledge and experience of the Romulan - Tomalak - is part of us now."

name: Aamin Marritza
lore: Former file clerk. He served under and impersonated Gul Darhe'el, the infamous "Butcher of Gallitep," in an attempt to force Cardassia to atone for war crimes.

name: Garak
lore: Cardassian male. Virtual player in the Vorta scenario testing the resolve of Alpha Quadrant species. Risked his life in the defense of his comrades.

name: Hanok
lore: Karemma Commerce Minister. Helped to defuse a torpedo lodged in the hull of the U.S.S. Defiant. Learned of Ferengi business philosophy from Quark.

name: Admiral Cartwright
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Militant admiral opposed to Chancellor Gorkon's peace initiative. Used his covert contacts in mounting a conspiracy to assassinate the Klingon leader.

name: Admiral Kirk
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: While Captain Kirk regretted accepting promotion, he commanded the Starship Enterprise in later crises. Time away from the center seat did not diminish his ingenuity.

name: Admiral Riker
lore: Commander of Starbase 247 in an alternate future. At odds with Governor Worf. Battled Klingons near Devron.

name: Amanda Grayson
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: Human wife of Ambassador Sarek. Admires the Vulcan way, but taught her son Captain Spock that the capacity of human emotion is just as great.

name: Ambassador Sarek
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Vulcan ambassador. Sent Admiral Kirk to recover the body of his son Captain Spock. Reciprocated Kirk's effort by defending him to the Federation Council.

name: Captain Styles
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Overconfident captain of the Starship Excelsior for a failed transwarp test. Planned to break old Starship Enterprise speed records. Was really in for a shock.

name: Captain Sulu
lore: After moving through the ranks aboard the Starship Enterprise, Lt. Sulu earned a captaincy in 2290. Holds loyalty in high regard, his crew as dear as family.

name: Carol Marcus
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Molecular biologist. Head of Project Genesis. Once romantically involved with Admiral Kirk. Asked that he leave her to raise David Marcus in her world, not his.

name: Chief Engineer Scott
lore: Mr. Scott is chief engineer of the I.S.S. Enterprise. Scotty is a relentless taskmaster. His department has the highest rate of turnover on the ship.

name: Clark Terrell
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Captain of U.S.S. Reliant. Has a strong sense of duty. Has never met Admiral Kirk, but knows something of him from a few stories told by Commander Chekov.

name: Commander Rand
lore: After serving on the Starship Enterprise, Yeoman Rand desired greater duties. She rose to transporter chief and Starship Excelsior's communications officer.

name: Commander Uhura
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: While Lt. Uhura had promotions and transfers, she seized each chance to return to Starship Enterprise. Got to play for a captive audience on Nimbus III.

name: David Marcus
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Gifted scientist. Like his father, often bends the rules. His impatience was Project Genesis' breakthrough and downfall. Proud - very proud - to be Admiral Kirk's son.

name: Demora Sulu
lore: Daughter of Captain Sulu. Helmsman of the U.S.S. Enterprise-B. James T. Kirk declared: "It wouldn't be the Enterprise without a Sulu at the helm."

name: Dmitri Valtane
lore: Starship Excelsior science officer. Monitored the 2293 disaster on the Klingon moon Praxis. Host of a parasitic memory virus. Thinks Vulcans need to relax.

name: Donald Varley
lore: Human captain of the U.S.S. Yamato. He retrieved a "Galactic Rosetta Stone" from Denius III to search for – and unfortunately find – the mythical planet Iconia.

name: Dr. Chapel
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: After her first tour aboard the Starship Enterprise, Nurse Chapel earned a medical doctorate. She later accepted a post at Starfleet Command.

name: Dr. McCoy
lore: Leonard H. "Bones" McCoy. Chief medical officer of the starship Enterprise. Awarded the Legion of Honor.

name: Dr. McCoy
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Leonard H. "Bones" McCoy. Retired from Starfleet in 2270, but returned a year later on Admiral Kirk's request. Retired again in 2293. Would again return.

name: Ensign Tuvok
lore: 29-year-old Vulcan on first deep space assignment aboard Captain Sulu's Starship Excelsior in 2293. Joined Starfleet under pressure from his parents.

name: Ensign Tuvok
lore: 29-year-old Vulcan on first deep space assignment aboard Captain Sulu's Starship Excelsior in 2293. Joined Starfleet under pressure from his parents.

name: Giusti
lore: Ensign Giusti is representative of staff officers in Starfleet. Served at the Ops console aboard the U.S.S. Enterprise in 2370.

name: Henreid
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Typical first officer. Assigned to Starship Excelsior in 2285. Stood in for the helmsman, who was on leave when Admiral Kirk stole the Starship Enterprise.

name: Ilia
lore: Deltan navigator assigned to the Starship Enterprise. Her Oath of Celibacy is on record. Was romantically involved with Willard Decker while posted to Delta IV.

name: Jacobson
lore: Typical member of the medical staff aboard the Starship Enterprise, serving under Dr. McCoy and Dr. Chapel. Specialist in microcellular biology.

name: James T. Kirk
lore: Famous captain thought lost in 2293. Returned from the Nexus 78 years later to make a difference once more.

name: Lal
lore: Soong-type android and daughter of Data. Created through replication of Data's positronic pathways. Named for the Hindi word for imzadi or beloved.

name: Lwaxana Troi
lore: Betazoid mother of Deanna Troi. Daughter of the Fifth House, Holder of the Sacred Chalice of Rixx, Heir to the Holy Rings of Betazed.

name: Mendon
lore: Ensign Mendon is a Benzite male representative of science specialists within Starfleet. Served aboard the U.S.S. Enterprise in 2365. Looks like Mordock.

name: Mendon
lore: Ensign Mendon is a Benzite male representative of science specialists within Starfleet. Served aboard the U.S.S. Enterprise in 2365. Looks like Mordock.

name: Miles O'Brien
lore: Transporter chief. Conn and Tactical expert. Loathes "Cardies." Loves Keiko. Begat Molly. He plays cello.

name: Montgomery Scott
lore: Chief Engineer of the Starship Enterprise. Scotty was rescued by the U.S.S. Enterprise after he spent 75 years in the pattern buffer of the U.S.S. Jenolen.

name: Montgomery Scott
lore: Chief Engineer of the Starship Enterprise. Scotty was rescued by the U.S.S. Enterprise after he spent 75 years in the pattern buffer of the U.S.S. Jenolen.

name: Montgomery Scott
lore: Chief Engineer of the Starship Enterprise. Scotty was rescued by the U.S.S. Enterprise after he spent 75 years in the pattern buffer of the U.S.S. Jenolen.

name: Mr. Scott
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Scotty knows his ship like the back of his hand. With his help, a chimpanzee and two trainees could run her.

name: Mr. Scott
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Scotty knows his ship like the back of his hand. With his help, a chimpanzee and two trainees could run her.

name: Saavik
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Vulcan cadet mentored by Captain Spock. She prefers to do things "by the book." Was determined to learn how Admiral Kirk beat the Kobayashi Maru.

name: Sam Lavelle
lore: Typical Starfleet ensign eagerly chasing a promotion. Served aboard the U.S.S. Enterprise in 2370. Decent poker player. His grandfather was Canadian.

name: St. John Talbot
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Ambassador to the worthless lump of rock known as Nimbus III. Released the pain of his cynicism when Sybok enlisted his help in the search for Eden.

name: Tasha Yar-Alternate
lore: Traveled to 2344 and helped prevent a disastrous war. Survivor of the Battle of Narendra III. Consort of Romulan general. Mother of Sela.

name: T'Pan
lore: Vulcan female. Dr. T'Pan served as director of the prestigious Vulcan Science Academy. Preeminent expert in subspace morphology.

name: Valeris
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Vulcan protégé of Captain Spock whom he intended as his replacement. She made a choice to sabotage negotiations with the untrustworthy Klingon Empire.

name: Wesley Crusher
lore: Ensign Wesley Crusher was a child prodigy. Protégé of the Traveler. Son of Dr. Beverly Crusher. Saved the U.S.S. Enterprise 3½ times as a teenager.

name: Willard Decker
lore: Son of Commodore Decker. Succeeded Admiral Kirk as captain of the Starship Enterprise, at Kirk's recommendation. Personally oversaw its refit.

name: Icheb (AI)
lore: Borg rescued from the collective and his own people, the Brunali. Takes Starfleet Academy courses, taught by U.S.S. Voyager's crew. Protégé of Seven of Nine.

name: Seven of Nine
lore: Borg freed from the Collective. Slowly reclaiming her human past and individuality, guided by Kathryn Janeway, The Doctor, and the rest of the U.S.S. Voyager crew.

name: Gegis
lore: DaiMon who reprogrammed the Federation hologram intercepted by Nunk. "Mastermind" of a plan to return Voyager to the Delta Quadrant through a geodesic fold.

name: The Trois
lore: Tog abducted the Betazoid Lwaxana Troi and her half-human daughter Deanna Troi, beamed them out of their clothes, and planned to exploit their skills.

name: Brigadier Kerla
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Military advisor to the High Council leader. Loyally served both Chancellor Gorkon and Azetbur, though bitterly opposed to peace with the Federation.

name: Captain Kang
lore: Respected warrior. Named his firstborn son in honor of Curzon Dax. Watched the careers of the Starship Enterprise crew since encountering them in 2268.

name: Ch'dak
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Characteristic member of the I.K.S. Kla'Diyus crew. A pilot rated on many designs, he enjoyed the new tactics enabled by the ability to attack while cloaked.

name: Chancellor Gorkon
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Klingon leader who first embraced the notion of peace with the Federation. His vision mapped the way to the undiscovered country – the future.

name: Colonel Worf
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Warrior and father of Mogh. He represented Captain Kirk and Dr. McCoy at their trial. His low political standing improved once they were proved innocent.

name: General Chang
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Chief of staff of the High Council leader. Conspired to assassinate Chancellor Gorkon and ensure no peace. Likes Shakespeare, especially in the original Klingon.

name: General Korrd
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Once-renowned military strategist exiled to Nimbus III by the High Council. Released the pain of his dishonor when Sybok enlisted his help in the search for Qui'tu.

name: K'Temoc
lore: Captain of the sleeper ship I.K.S. T'Ong, on a crucial mission order by the High Command in the late 23rd century. Awoke 75 years later in a much-changed galaxy.

name: Kamarag
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: Ambassador to the Federation. Believed Admiral Kirk wanted Project Genesis as a weapon against Qo'noS. Predicted there would be no peace while Kirk lived.

name: Karnog
lore: Science officer aboard the I.K.S. Amar. Tried to analyze the sensor data from the intruder V'Ger. Unfortunately, his expertise was in the planetary sciences.

name: Klaa
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Aggressive captain. He hunted the U.S.S. Enterprise-A without authorization in 2287. Later demoted and assigned menial translation duties on Qo'noS.

name: Kor'choth
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Typical bodyguard of the High Council leader. Lost an arm defending Chancellor Gorkon. Refused prosthetic replacement. Gave evidence at the subsequent trial.

name: Krase
lore: Captain of the I.K.S. Amar. His tendency to rash behavior has earned him a ruthless reputation – even by Klingon standards.

name: Maltz
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Klingon serving under Kruge. Prefers the night shift. Captured when his ship was commandeered. Willing to die for this dishonor. Admiral Kirk saw otherwise.

name: Martok
lore: Highly decorated general and High Council member. Accepted Worf, Alexander and Jadzia into the House of Martok. Lost his left eye battling the Jem'Hadar.

name: Toral
lore: Illegitimate son of Duras. Claimed leadership position on the High Council at bidding of Duras' sisters, Lursa and B'Etor.

name: Torg
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Kruge's first officer. Led the boarding party sent to secure the Starship Enterprise. His promotions came slowly. Doesn't know when he's being spoken to.

name: Vixis
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Klaa's first officer. Tracked the U.S.S. Enterprise-A by intercepting their distress signal and impersonating Starfleet Command. She has wonderful muscles.

name: Quark Son of Keldar
lore: Quark wedded Grilka by brek'tal ritual to head the House of Kozak (as the House of Quark) on Qo'noS. The Ferengi saved his be'nal from financial ruin.

name: George and Gracie
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: Two humpback whales, male and female, raised in captivity on 20th-century Earth. Gracie is pregnant.

name: 10 and 01
lore: Paired genderless Bynars from the planet Bynaus. In the year 100100111100, they upgraded systems on the U.S.S. Enterprise at Starbase 01001010.

name: 10 and 01
lore: Paired genderless Bynars from the planet Bynaus. In the year 100100111100, they upgraded systems on the U.S.S. Enterprise at Starbase 01001010.

name: Ajur
lore: A female Vorgon criminal from the 27th century who ruthlessly sought artifacts with partner Boratus. Hunted the Tox Uthat by returning to 2366.

name: Arandis
lore: Chief facilitator of entire Temtibi Lagoon. Welcomes all to Risa. Curzon Dax's last romantic encounter.

name: Boratus
lore: Male Vorgon criminal from the future. Aims to steal artifacts with partner Ajur. Once hunted the Tox Uthat discovered by Jean-Luc Picard on Risa.

name: Cyrus Redblock
lore: Civil but dangerous gangster. Believes in killing when for a purpose. Is resolved to obtain "the item" he believes was entrusted to Dixon Hill by Jessica Bradley.

name: Cyrus Redblock
lore: Civil but dangerous gangster. Believes in killing when for a purpose. Is resolved to obtain "the item" he believes was entrusted to Dixon Hill by Jessica Bradley.

name: Dathon
lore: Tamarian captain of the Tama. He said: "Darmok and Jalad at Tanagra. The beast of Tanagra. Picard and Dathon at El-Adrel. Sokath, his eyes uncovered!"

name: Dathon
lore: Tamarian captain of the Tama. He said: "Darmok and Jalad at Tanagra. The beast of Tanagra. Picard and Dathon at El-Adrel. Sokath, his eyes uncovered!"

name: Dixon Hill
lore: Fictional private detective. Solved dozens of cases. Jean-Luc Picard is an aficionado of the original 1930s stories and the latest holonovels by Broht and Forrester.

name: Dr. Tolian Soran
lore: El-Aurian refugee "rescued" from the Nexus in 2293 by the U.S.S. Enterprise-B. Spent the next 78 years obsessed with returning there, no matter the cost.

name: J'Onn
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Humanoid settler of Nimbus III. Release the pain of his impoverishment when Sybok enlisted his help in the search for the knowledge sought by all since time began.

name: Joachim
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Khan's lieutenant and most trusted friend. Augment who acted as first officer on the U.S.S. Reliant when, after nearly two decades, they escaped Ceti Alpha V.

name: Khan
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Genetically engineered augment exiled to Ceti Alpha V by Admiral Kirk. Seeks to avenge his wife's death.

name: Lore
lore: Evil Soong-type android. Data's "elder brother."

name: Madred
lore: Gul Madred, Cardassian officer in the Obsidian Order. Specializes in prisoner interrogation. Tortured Jean-Luc Picard time after time in 2369.

name: Martia
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Chameloid prisoner on Rura Penthe. She helped set up Captain Kirk and Dr. McCoy to get a full pardon. Great shape-shifter, though it takes "a lot of effort."

name: Mas'ud
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Specimen of late 20th-century genetic engineering. Augment who swore loyalty to Khan. Studied the effects of the Ceti eel while trapped on Ceti Alpha V.

name: Mas'ud
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Specimen of late 20th-century genetic engineering. Augment who swore loyalty to Khan. Studied the effects of the Ceti eel while trapped on Ceti Alpha V.

name: Mortal Q
lore: Q was made human and evicted from the Continuum due to antics. Retained his other fine qualities.

name: Regina Barthalomew
lore: Fictional character inspired by the Sherlock Holmes stories. Romantically involved with Professor Moriarty.

name: Sarod
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Loyal augment follower of Khan. He served as the group's physician. With healthy "supermen" rarely taxing him, he knew of nothing to save Lt. McGivers.

name: Sherlock Holmes
lore: The role of Sir Arthur Conan Doyle's brilliant detective was often assumed by the Soong-type android Data.

name: Soong-type Android
lore: A recently produced Soong-type android ready to select its gender and appearance. Replicated using a method developed by Data.

name: Soong-type Android
lore: A recently produced Soong-type android ready to select its gender and appearance. Replicated using a method developed by Data.

name: Suna
lore: Military official of Tilonus IV. He twisted William T. Riker's mind using neurosomatic techniques. Typical of treacherous Tilonian government interrogators.

name: Sunad
lore: Zalkonian captain. Sought to capture criminals undergoing a dangerous mutation before they could further disrupt society.

name: Sybok
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Vulcan son of Ambassador Sarek and half-brother to Captain Spock. Banished for his belief in Sha Ka Ree.

name: Vic Fontaine
lore: Self-aware hologram of a 20th-century Las Vegas singer. His keen insights helped Bashir, Odo, Kira, Worf, Nog and others aboard Deep Space 9 through difficult times.

name: Wajahut
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Eugenics Wars augment. Escaped on the Botany Bay with Khan. With superior intellect and knowledge of that ship, she quickly adapted to the U.S.S. Reliant.

name: Zon
lore: Nausicaan officer who stabbed young Jean-Luc Picard through the heart in a brawl at Starbase Earhart in 2327. Dom-jot player.

name: Icheb
lore: Borg rescued from the collective and his own people, the Brunali. Takes Starfleet Academy courses, taught by U.S.S. Voyager's crew. Protégé of Seven of Nine.

name: Seven of Nine
lore: Borg freed from the Collective. Slowly reclaiming her human past and individuality, guided by Kathryn Janeway, The Doctor, and the rest of the U.S.S. Voyager crew.

name: Caithlin Dar
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Ambassador to Nimbus III. Hides disdain for the position with overeagerness. Released the pain of her deception when Sybok enlisted her help in the search for Vorta Vor.

name: Major Rakal
lore: Physically altered, the half-Betazoid, half-human Deanna Troi was coerced to assume the identity of a Tal Shiar major in the 2369 M'ret defection plot.

name: Taris
lore: Female subcommander. Captain of the warbird Haakona. Investigated the Federation incursion of the Neutral Zone in the vicinity of Iconia.

name: Jonathan Archer
lore: Captain of the Enterprise NX-01. Leaped into deep space to make the future quantifiably better for all mankind.

name: Ar-Q-ologist
lore: "How can you write about something that you've never seen? I know! Why don't I take you there?"
game_text: Opponent may place up to X cards from this discard pile on top of their draw deck, where X=total number of Skill dot and Download icons on lowest INTEGRITY personnel present. Nullify with Archaeology and Honor present.

name: Go Back Whence Thou Camest
lore: "Thou art notified that thy kind has infiltrated the galaxy too far already. Thou art directed to return to thy own solar system immediately."
game_text: If INTEGRITY < 10 OR INTEGRITY > 50, at the end of your turn opponent may relocate any one of your ships at this location to one of your facilities.

name: Guilty - Provisionally
lore: "You will now answer to the charge of being a grievously savage race... Soldiers, you will press those triggers if this criminal answers with any word other than 'guilty.'"
game_text: Randomly select one personnel present. If you say "guilty - provisionally," plays on table; opponent may cancel the next battle you initiate, then discard dilemma. Otherwise, personnel killed.

name: Hide and Seek
lore: "Why don't we play a little game? I'll hide.. you find me."
game_text: Shuffle Hide and Seek together with crew or Away Team. Randomly select cards until a Universal personnel or Hide and Seek selected. All selected personnel are stopped; discard dilemma. (May be seeded as a Q dilemma.

page_title: His Honor, The High Sheriff of Nottingham (Errata) (QC)
name: His Honor, The High Sheriff of Nottingham
base_name: His Honor, The High Sheriff of Nottingham
lore: "Yes, but what about your merry men? Are you willing to jeopardize their lives as well?"
game_text: If any of your personnel are held captive, you must either lose points OR return one such captive here (released). If, just after relocation, opponent shows SECURITY from hand, opponent captures two of your personnel present (random selection). (Immune to Miss Q.)

name: Mandarin Bailiff
lore: "Criminal! How plead you?"
game_text: Opponent captures one personnel present (random selection). You may prevent this by "posting bail": you lose points and opponent gains points. X = number of Skill Dot icons on that personnel.

name: Q-Type Android
lore: "Think fast, Commander Riker."
game_text: Opponent places dilemma on one non-Hologram Personnel at this location, then chooses: If android, all copies of that card become human (STRENGTH -4); otherwise, becomes Q-type androids (STRENGTH +4) OR if non-Borg, seed that personnel under an unsolved Q's Planet; discard dilemma. (May be nullified only by Mortal Q or any William T. Riker present.)

name: Aldebaran Serpent
lore: "You will abandon that mission, Captain. My business with you takes precedence."
game_text: If personnel are present, and the number of personnel in this crew or Away Team > lowest attribute present, discard event. Otherwise, place on mission; after this Q-Flash ends, crew or Away Team is stopped and you must attempt a different mission before attempting this one again.

name: Amanda's Parents
lore: "They had assumed human form... in vulgar human fashion they proceeded to conceive a child. And like mockish humans they became attached to it."
game_text: Plays on table until any Q-Flash. Each time you play an Amanda Rogers card (except to nullify a Q icon card), opponent may take that Amanda Rogers (and any two other cards) from your discard pile and place all three out-of-play.

name: Door-Net
lore: "Stay where thou art."
game_text: Plays on one of your non-Shield Doorway cards in play (your choice) until any Q-Flash; it is now closed. May be nullified by Alternate Universe Door OR by showing 2 Diplomacy from your hand during your turn.

name: Q's Fantasy Women
lore: "My good fortune is your good fortune."
game_text: Plays on a male present (opponent's choice) until any Q-Flash. If he helps you solve a mission, opponent scores points. Discard event.

name: Scottish Setter
lore: "Crusher gets more shrill with each passing year."
game_text: If no ANIMAL present, play on one personnel present (random selection) until any Q-Flash. That personnel's classification changes to ANIMAL. May be nullified by Amanda Rogers.

name: Incoming Message - The Continuum
lore: "Your progress, Q?""As anticipated, there are some problems. I Need time."
game_text: Opponent may end current Q-Flash now (no more Q icon cards are drawn) and immediately seed the card that started it under any other mission (it has no further effects now; mission continues).

name: The Higher... The Q-er
lore: "You want to review your rapid progress? to where humans learned to control their military with drugs?"
game_text: If no CIVILIAN present, add X additional Q icon cards to this Q-Flash, where X = number of personnel present with a Command icon.

name: The Issue is Patriotism
lore: "You slaughtered millions in silly arguments about how to divide the resources of your little world."
game_text: You must immediately initiate a battle at one location that has opposing ships or Away Teams (if any). Stopped cards are unstopped long enough to battle. No leaders are required and no affiliation restrictions apply. (Immune to Miss Q.)

name: The Naked Truth
lore: "Red Alert!"
game_text: Opponent may play a unique personnel from hand to your crew or Away Team. That personnel is under your control (compatible with your cards regardless of affiliation; assimilated if playing Borg) and is stopped. (Opponent may not report the same personnel more than once per game in this manner.)

name: Bajoran Raider
lore: Nimble fighter used by the Bajoran resistance during the occupation. Kira Nerys commanded one in 2370.
game_text: Once each turn, may report with 2 personnel, take off, or land. X=4 if moving within a region.

name: Borg Cube
lore: IDENTIFICATION: BORG CUBETASK: Explore galaxy for biological and technological distinctiveness. Assimilate.

name: Borg Cube
lore: IDENTIFICATION: BORG CUBETASK: Explore galaxy for biological and technological distinctiveness. Assimilate.

name: Borg Probe
lore: IDENTIFICATION: BORG PROBETASK: Explore unimatrices at the borders of Borg space. Locate biological and technological distinctiveness.
game_text: May report with up to 3 personnel to any Delta Quadrant location if your Borg Queen in play.

name: Borg Scout Vessel
lore: IDENTIFICATION: BORG SCOUT VESSELTASK: Search for assimilation targets. Establish transwarp connections.
game_text: May report with up to 4 personnel to a Transwarp Network Gateway (download doorway if necessary) at any spaceline end.

name: Locutus' Borg Cube
lore: IDENTIFICATION: BORG CUBETASK: Explore galaxy for biological and technological distinctiveness. Assimilate.

name: Locutus' Borg Cube (Foil)
lore: IDENTIFICATION: BORG CUBETASK: Explore galaxy for biological and technological distinctiveness. Assimilate.

name: Queen's Borg Cube
lore: IDENTIFICATION: BORG CUBETASK: Assimilate human home world by direct attack, Earth date 2373. Borg Queen commands.

name: Starship Constitution
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: With new modifications, ships of this class were built long after the original's launch. Starfleet continued this practice of refitting older designs into the 24th century.

name: Starship Excelsior
lore: Unsuccessful transwarp test ship later refitted as the prototype for one of Starfleet's most durable and ubiquitous classes of ship. Commanded by Captain Sulu.

name: Type 18 Shuttlepod
lore: Small shuttlecraft. One commanded by Benjamin Sisko guided a silithium comet through the Bajoran wormhole.
game_text: May report with up to 2 Navigation personnel to your Defiant-class ship.

name: U.S.S. Danube
lore: Class of runabout often named for Terran rivers. First commissioned in 2368. The following year, the U.S.S. Enterprise delivered three Danube-class vessels to DS9.

name: U.S.S. Enterprise-A
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: Specially commissioned in 2286 to replace the famous ship lost one year earlier. Proudly continued the mission of its predecessor under the command of James T. Kirk.
game_text: Any Federation Classic Films personnel OR James T. Kirk

name: U.S.S. Enterprise-B
lore: Third Federation ship so christened, launched on stardate 9715. Became fully operational the following Tuesday.
game_text: El-Aurians may report aboard.

name: U.S.S. Oberth
lore: Class of small ships often used for scientific missions. Named for 20th century rocket scientist Hermann Oberth.

name: Brunt's Shuttle
lore: Personal shuttle commanded by Brunt during his numerous liquidations. Transported Quark's rag-tag negotiation team to Empok Nor to rescue Ishka.
game_text: May report with up to 3 personnel to docking site of an Empok Nor you don’t control.

name: Kazon Warship
lore: Enormous Kazon vessel used as a mobile base of operations. Dwarfs even D'deridex‑class ships.
game_text: Has no transporters.

name: I.K.C. Bortas
lore: Flagship commanded by Gowron during the Klingon Civil War of 2367-68. Lieutenant Worf briefly served aboard as a weapons officer.

name: I.K.S. Negh'Var
lore: Flagship of the Klingon Defense Force. Commanded by Gowron when first commissioned, and then by Martok during the 2372 invasion of Cardassia.

name: I.K.S. Negh'Var
lore: Flagship of the Klingon Defense Force. Commanded by Gowron when first commissioned, and then by Martok during the 2372 invasion of Cardassia.

name: I.K.S. Amar
lore: One of the first K't'inga-class ships. Leader of the battle group dispatched to escort an unidentified intruder out of Klingon space in 2271.

name: I.K.S. Chang
lore: Patrolled the Devron system with sister ship I.K.S. Fek'Ihr. Formerly commanded by Governor Worf.
game_text: If your I.K.S. Fek'Ihr in play, it has a Nemesis Blue Left icon and both ships reduce staffing by one Alternate icon.

name: I.K.S. Chontay
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Bird-of-prey captained by Klaa. The highlight of its mission was shooting space garbage until its pursuit of the U.S.S. Enterprise-A through the Great Barrier.

name: I.K.S. K'elric
lore: One of three ships that ended The Albino's raids on Klingon colonies. Intercepted the Starship Excelsior in the Azure Nebula. Commanded by Captain Kang.

name: I.K.S. K't'inga
lore: Though the basic form of the Klingon cruiser had been the same since the 22nd century, this design introduced in the 2270s boasted upgrades to all major systems.
game_text: Any Universal Klingon Classic Films personnel

name: I.K.S. Kla'Diyus
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Unique vessel able to fire while cloaked. Commissioned and commanded by General Chang, who ordered the designers killed to preserve the secret of its existence.

name: I.K.S. T'Ong
lore: A Klingon sleeper ship from the 23th century, an era when Klingons despised humans and attacked them on sight. Commanded by K'Temoc.
game_text: Must report with up to 3 personnel at end of spaceline.

name: Kronos One
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
game_text: Any Klingon Classic Films personnel

name: Darmok
lore: Typical Tamarian vessel. "Picard and Dathon, trading knives at El-Adrel. Children at Tama's knee. Sokath, forging knives for his brothers."

name: Liberty
lore: Maquis ship commanded by Captain Chakotay in 2371. 30-year old vessel – with a 39-year old engine that has been rebuilt and modified many times over.

name: Phoenix
lore: Earth's first faster-than-light-ship. Launched via a Titan missile. Commanded by Zefram Cochrane.
game_text: May take off (score points) once and land once.

name: Enterprise
lore: Legendary prototype designed for deep space travel. Commanded by Jonathan Archer. First Starfleet vessel to bear the name that would symbolize Starfleet's elite.
game_text: Attributes all +1 for each Starfleet Command aboard (limit 5).

name: Docking Pads
game_text: Any ship with no staffing requirements may report, dock (land) and undock (take off) here if ship is compatible with station's affiliation OR Crew includes a V.I.P. OR player controlling ship has a Computer Skill personnel present at this site unopposed (just before undocking, that personnel may board ship). Player controlling station may, once per game, download Establish Landing Protocols.

name: Holosuite
game_text: This site must be placed adjacent to Quark's Bar (or another Holosuite). Has a Holodeck. Holoprogram cards may be played here (limit one; station controller may discard it during their turn). Hologram Equipment cards and compatible Hologram personnel may report here, and may be transferred directly to/from owner's ship docked at this station.

name: Breen Disruptor Burst
game_text: ATTACK bonus +3 if you have a Breen ship firing.Hit = Tactic Draw. Direct hit = Tactic Draw Tactic Draw.

name: Maximum Firepower
game_text: Hit = Tactic Draw (or Tactic Draw Tactic Draw if you have Future Enterprise, I.K.C. Chang, I.K.C. Fek'Ihr, Decius, any Alternate ship with the word "future" in its lore firing). Direct hit = Tactic Draw Tactic Draw.

name: Maximum Firepower
game_text: Hit = Tactic Draw (or Tactic Draw Tactic Draw if you have Future Enterprise, I.K.C. Chang, I.K.C. Fek'Ihr, Decius, any Alternate ship with the word "future" in its lore firing). Direct hit = Tactic Draw Tactic Draw.

name: Picard Maneuver
game_text: If you initiated ship battle with your matching commander aboard your ship, it appears to be in two places at once and has a 50/50 chance to avoid all damage this battle.Hit = Tactic Draw. Direct hit = Tactic Draw Tactic Draw.

name: T'Pol/Soong Maneuver
game_text: ATTACK bonus +3 and DEFENSE bonus +2 if you have a NX-class ship firing. Hit = Tactic Current Tactic Draw. Direct hit = Tactic Current Tactic Draw Tactic Draw

name: Cetacean Institute
lore: 1986 Earth: Marine biology research laboratory and public aquarium located in Sausolito, California.
game_text: Seeds or plays on table; download George and Gracie here. Native to this timeline: Dr. Gillian Taylor and George and Gracie.

name: Halkan Council
lore: 2267 Halkan Planet: Site of dilithium deposits and obstinate inhabitants.
game_text: Seeds or plays on table; any players may download one Mirror Quadrant Constitution-class ship here. Native to this timeline: all Alternate Mirror Quadrant Original Series cards, and all Original Series Equipment cards. Once per turn, one such card reporting at this location may report for free.

name: Locutus of Borg
lore: Assimilated counterpart who spoke to the Federation."The knowledge and experience of the human – Jean-Luc Picard '–' is part of us now."

name: Decaren
lore: Alpha-Hirogen who agreed to hunt alongside the crew of Voyager. A master in tracking, but overly prone to the fervor of an imminent kill. Commands a Hunting Vessel.

name: Two of Nine
lore: IDENTIFICATION: TRANSTATOR DRONETASK: Primary adjunct of unimatrix zero one.BIOLOGICAL DISTINCTIVENESS: Humanoid

name: Admiral Riker
lore: Commander of Starbase 247 in an alternate future. At odds with Governor Worf. Battled Klingons near Devron.

name: Betazoid Gift Box
lore: Traditional device for presenting important gifts. Its sculpted face comes to life boisterously presenting its contents to the recipient.
game_text: Immediately look through your draw deck for up to thirty seconds and choose three cards to place in your hand. Reshuffle draw deck and discard artifact.

name: Horga'hn
lore: Mysterious symbol of sexuality from the pleasure planet of Risa. To own one is to call forth its powers. To display one is to announce that the owner is seeking jamaharon.

name: Interphase Generator
lore: Experimental Romulan device that both cloaks and phases matter, allowing it to pass through normal matter.

name: Kurlan Naiskos
lore: Statues which open to reveal a multitude of similar but smaller figurines inside, representing the belief that each person is a community of individual voices and desires.
game_text: Place in hand until played on any ship as an Event card. If ship has all 7 personnel types aboard, its RANGE, WEAPONS and SHIELDS are all tripled. (Not cumulative.)

name: Thought Maker
lore: Outlawed Ferengi mind control device. Transmits signals that implant sensory experiences and triggers emotions and memories.
game_text: Place in hand until played once as an Interrupt card. Look at opponent's draw deck for ten seconds and rearrange as desired.

name: Time Travel Pod
lore: Craft from the future, stolen in the past by Berlinghoff Rasmussen for his own gain.
game_text: Place in hand until played once as an Interrupt card on any ship. That ship travels into the future (disappears for up to 5 turns). Pre-announce the return time.

name: Tox Uthat
lore: Dangerous quantum phase inhibitor invented in the future by Kal Dano who hid it in the 22nd century for safekeeping.
game_text: Place in hand until played on table as an event (supernova can be played on later turn) OR as an interrupt (prevents supernova). Discard after use.

name: Varon-T Disruptor
lore: Only five of these pistols were made before being banned by the Federation. These vicious weapons disrupt the body from the inside out, causing a slow and painful death.
game_text: Use as Equipment card. Doubles all of your personnel's STRENGTH where present. (Not cumulative.)

name: Vulcan Stone of Gol
lore: Ancient Vulcan telepathic weapon. Kills by magnifying aggressive and violent thoughts, but can be blocked by peaceful thoughts.
game_text: Plays in hand until played as an Event card. Kills everyone in an Away Team without Youth OR CUNNING>7. Discard artifact.

name: Alien Abduction
lore: Solanagen-based aliens, existing in a subspace domain, can access our universe and abduct humanoids for study.

name: Alien Parasites
lore: Intelligent parasites enter and take control of a humanoid. Their presence can be detected by a gill like protrusion on the back of a host's neck.
game_text: Unless INTEGRITY>32, Away Team infected. They beam back and opponent immediately controls ship and crew until "stopped." Then turn resumes.

name: Anaphasic Organism
lore: A male non-corporeal life-form that lives inside a female host which he enchants, as in the case of Dr. Beverly Crusher's late grandmother.
game_text: If Female(s) in Away Team, the one with highest total attribute numbers resigns (is discarded), unless SECURITY and MEDICAL present. Discard dilemma.

name: Ancient Computer
lore: Vital information can be retrieved from old or damaged computer systems like this one aboard a derelict Promellian battlecruiser.
game_text: Cannot get past unless 2 Computer Skill OR 3 SCIENCE OR 3 ENGINEER present.

name: Archer
lore: Indigenous inhabitants, such as this Mintakan bowman, often attack an Away Team out of fear.
game_text: Away Team member with highest total attribute numbers is shot and dies unless SECURITY and MEDICAL present. Discard dilemma.

name: Armus - Skin of Evil
game_text: Kills one Away Team member (random selection). Discard dilemma.

name: Barclay's Protomorphosis Disease
lore: Contagious affliction which causes animals to de-evolve into ancestral forms. Disease named for Lieutenant Reginald Barclay.
game_text: Entire crew or Away Team (except Androids) de-evolves (dies) unless MEDICAL, SCIENCE and SECURITY present. Discard dilemma.

name: Birth of "Junior"
lore: Large infant spaceborne life-form. Attached itself to the U.S.S. Enterprise in 2368, sucking energy from the ship.

name: Borg Ship
lore: Gigantic cubic ship of the Borg collective. Possesses powerful weapons and remarkable regenerative abilities.

name: Chalnoth
lore: Anarchistic lupine race of humanoids with the reputation of violent responses to a variety of situations.
game_text: Kills one Away Team member (opponent's choice) unless 3 SECURITY OR STRENGTH>40 present. Discard dilemma.

name: Cosmic String Fragment
lore: A long space object as thin as a proton but with the gravitational attraction of a hundred stars.
game_text: Ship is sucked in and destroyed unless Astrophysics OR Engineer OR Navigation aboard. Discard dilemma.

name: Crystalline Entity
lore: Spaceborne life-form strips biological energy from planets and ships. Sensitive to modulation much like crystal can shatter from a high pitch note.
game_text: Space mission: Kills all life on ship unless SHIELDS>6 OR Music aboard. Planet mission: Kills entire Away Team unless SCIENCE and MEDICAL present. Discard dilemma.

name: Cytherians
lore: Race which explores the galaxy by giving other species the temporary ability and strong compulsion to come to them.
game_text: Place on ship. Ship must do nothing but travel to far end of spaceline at normal speed. When reached, discard dilemma. Score points.

name: El-Adrel Creature
lore: Nearly invisible predatory electromagnetic creature. First encountered by Dathon and Captain Jean-Luc Picard on El-Adrel IV.
game_text: Attacks two strongest members in Away Team (owner's choice if tie). Kills one of them (random selection) unless their combined STRENGTH>16. Discard dilemma.

name: Female's Love Interest
lore: A genetically-engineered leader. Once romantically involved with Deanna Troi.

name: Firestorm
lore: With advanced technology, personnel can work together to survive natural phenomenon such as the firestorms on Bersallis III.

name: Gravitic Mine
lore: Free-floating weapon used against space vehicles. The U.S.S. Denver struck such a mine, which caused it to crash in the Mericor System.
game_text: Ship damaged unless SCIENCE and Navigation aboard. Discard dilemma.

name: Hologram Ruse
lore: Holograms can be used to create realistic fantasy worlds.

name: Hyper-Aging
lore: Disease created accidentally at the Darwin Genetic Research Station on Gagarin IV. Causes rapid aging and death.

name: Iconian Computer Weapon
lore: Highly destructive virus from the ancient extinct Iconians. Transmitted to target vessels via a probe.
game_text: Unless SCIENCE present, re-boot by discarding all non-personnel cards in hand and replenish from top of draw deck. Discard dilemma.

name: Impassable Door
lore: Forcefields across door or hallway openings are commonly used to bar entry.
game_text: To get through this door, Away Team must have Computer Skill present.

name: Ktarian Game
lore: Psychotropically, mesmerizingly addictive game device. One by one, its players are made susceptible to complete mental control.
game_text: Place on ship. Now and start of each of your turns, one person aboard (random selection) is disabled. Cured when non-disabled CUNNING>30 OR android aboard.

name: Male's Love Interest
lore: One of the many beautiful women who reside on the paradise planet of Risa.

name: Matriarchal Society
lore: The planet Angel One was dominated by its women who were intolerant of dealing with men.
game_text: Cannot get past unless at least two female Away Team members are present.

name: Menthar Booby Trap
lore: Relic from ancient Menthar-Promellian war. Aceton assimilators trap passing ships, drain power, then emit deadly radiation.

name: Microbiotic Colony
lore: Rare subatomic spaceborne life-form that can cause severe damage to a starship's hull.
game_text: Ship damaged unless SCIENCE, ENGINEER and OFFICER aboard. Discard dilemma.

name: Microvirus
lore: Genetic weapon designed to attack humanoids who have specific DNA sequences.
game_text: Kills one Away Team member (opponent's choice), unless MEDICAL and SECURITY present. Discard dilemma.

name: Nagilum
lore: Extra-dimensional entity willing to kill in order to understand the concept of mortality.
game_text: Half of crew is killed (random selection, round down) unless 3 Diplomacy OR STRENGTH>40 aboard. Discard dilemma.

name: Nanites
lore: Originally, submicroscopic robots used for medical therapy. Now, self-replicating sentient life-forms who can disable computer systems.
game_text: Damages afflicted ship unless 2 SCIENCE OR Diplomacy present. Discard Dilemma.

name: Nausicaans
lore: Tall humanoid species with a quick temper. A Nausicaan once stabbed Jean-Luc Picard through the heart with a knife.
game_text: Three Nausicaans pick a fight. One Away Team member is killed (random selection) unless STRENGTH>44. Discard dilemma.

name: Nitrium Metal Parasites
lore: Microscopic life-forms that normally live in asteroids but can infest and damage ships by ingesting nitrium.

name: Null Space
lore: A rare, invisible pocket of space caused by turbulence during star formation. Absorbs all energy.
game_text: Ship hits null space turbulence and is damaged unless 2 Navigation aboard. Discard dilemma.

name: Phased Matter
lore: Phased personnel vibrate out of sync with normal matter, rendering them undetectable. Phased people cannot interact with non-phased people.

name: Portal Guard
lore: Portal 63 is the last remaining protector of the Tkon Empire, which went extinct 600,000 years ago. Challenges those who awaken him.
game_text: Unless at least one Away Team member has CUNNING>7 OR Honor, the entire Away Team must abort mission and beam up or die.

name: Q
lore: Incorrigible, extra-dimensional member of the Q Continuum, a race of omnipotent beings. Q exhibits a child-like petulance and sense of playfulness.

name: Radioactive Garbage Scow
lore: Barges containing dangerous waste can be adrift for centuries. One such barge threatened Gamelon V in 2367.

name: Rebel Encounter
lore: Belligerent rebels from war-torn worlds often hide out on other planets and can endanger an Away Team.
game_text: Kills one Away Team member (random selection) unless STRENGTH>44 OR you bribe rebels first by discarding an Equipment card, if present. Discard dilemma.

name: REM Fatigue Hallucinations
lore: A crew can go insane from lack of REM (rapid eye movement) sleep.

name: Sarjenka
lore: Alien child from Drema IV. Her radio pleas for help were answered by Lt. Commander Data in violation of the Prime Directive.
game_text: Primitive alien begs for help. Ignore her (discard dilemma) OR help her and earn Bonus points, but all Away Teams here are "stopped."

name: Shaka, When the Walls Fell
lore: "Shaka, when the walls fell," means inability to understand. The incomprehensible Tamarians spoke entirely in metaphors.
game_text: Must have 2 Diplomacy and CUNNING>30 to communicate and proceed.

name: Tarellian Plague Ship
lore: Ship containing the survivors of a Tarellia war plague. Infected from biological weapons, they are now refused entry everywhere.

name: Temporal Causality Loop
lore: Localized distortion causes time to repeat ad infinitum. U.S.S. Bozeman was trapped for 90 years in a temporal loop that held the U.S.S. Enterprise for 17.4 days.
game_text: Unless SCIENCE and CUNNING>35, undo your last two actions of this turn and end turn. Discard dilemma.

name: Tsiolkovsky Infection
lore: Variety of water-based Psi 2000 virus. Passed by perspiration. Creates dangerous intoxication-like instability among a crew.

name: Two-Dimensional Creatures
lore: Perfectly flat spaceborne creatures from a two-dimensional spatial continuum. Ensnared the U.S.S. Enterprise in 2367 and impeded Counselor Deanna Troi's empathic abilities.

name: Wind Dancer
lore: Sentry of the Parallax Colony. Only allows those whose hearts are joyous to pass.

name: Engineering Kit
lore: Representative of specialized engineering instruments. Such equipment has been developed by many races.
game_text: Gives all of your OFFICER-classification personnel the extra skill of ENGINEER where present.

name: Engineering PADD
lore: Representative of Personal Access Display Devices designed specifically for engineering functions. Such equipment has been developed by many races.
game_text: Gives all of your SCIENCE-classification personnel the extra skill of ENGINEER where present.

name: Federation PADD
lore: Standard Federation Personnel Access Display Device for computerized information.
game_text: Federation use only. Each of your personnel CUNNING +2 where present. (Cumulative.)

name: Klingon Disruptor
lore: Phase-disruptor used by Klingons and other races. Similar to a phaser.
game_text: Klingon and Non-Aligned use only. Each of your personnel STRENGTH +2 where present. (Cumulative.)

name: Klingon PADD
lore: Standard Klingon Personnel Access Display Device for computerized information.
game_text: Klingon use only. Each of your personnel CUNNING +2 where present. (Cumulative.)

name: Medical Kit
lore: Representative of specialized medical equipment. Such equipment has been developed by many races.
game_text: Gives all of your OFFICER-classification personnel the extra skill of MEDICAL where present.

name: Medical Tricorder
lore: Representative of specialized tricorder optimized for medical use. Such equipment has been developed by many races.
game_text: Gives all of your SCIENCE-classification personnel the extra skill of MEDICAL where present.

name: Romulan Disruptor
lore: Directed-energy weapon used by Romulans and other races. Disruptor fire can be identified by a high residue of antriprotons that linger for several hours.
game_text: Romulan and Non-Aligned use only. Each of your personnel STRENGTH +2 where present. (Cumulative.)

name: Romulan PADD
lore: Standard Romulan Personnel Access Display Device for computerized information.
game_text: Romulan use only. Each of your personnel CUNNING +2 where present. (Cumulative.)

name: Starfleet Type II Phaser
lore: Handheld weapon can be set for stun, heat and disruption. PHASER is an acronym for PHASed Energy Rectification.

name: Tricorder
lore: Representative of multipurpose handheld device combining sensors, computers and recorders. Such equipment has been developed by many races.
game_text: Gives all of your ENGINEER-classification personnel the extra skill of SCIENCE where present.

name: Alien Probe
lore: Space probes of unknown origin are frequently encountered by starships. Often such probes seek information or contact.
game_text: Plays on table. Both players continue the game with their hands (cards) exposed, face up on table.

name: Anti-Time Anomaly
lore: Q-created phenomena. Rift caused by anti-time particles in the future. Anomaly grows backward in time endangering all life in the past.

name: Atmospheric Ionization
lore: Charged particles in the atmosphere of planets which can disrupt transporter beams.

name: Bynars Weapon Enhancement
lore: Binary race closely integrated with computers. Always work in pairs. Bynars have the ability to enhance specific computerized systems.

name: Distortion Field
lore: Atmospheric phenomena that inhibits use of transporters as on Nervala IV.

name: Espionage: Federation on Klingon
lore: Federation intelligence-gathering has often relied upon sympathetic informants and electronic surveillance.
game_text: Plays on any Klingon mission. Your Federation personnel may now attempt this mission. Discard after mission completed.

name: Espionage: Klingon on Federation
lore: Klingon espionage against the Federation has included data stolen from Relay Station 47 by Morag.
game_text: Plays on any Federation mission. Your Klingon personnel may now attempt this mission. Discard after mission completed.

name: Espionage: Romulan on Federation
lore: Romulan spies are everywhere.
game_text: Plays on any Federation mission. Your Romulan personnel may now attempt this mission. Discard after mission completed.

name: Espionage: Romulan on Klingon
lore: Romulan espionage against Klingons has included efforts to de-stabilize the Klingon government by programming assassins and supporting rebel forces.
game_text: Plays on any Klingon mission. Your Romulan personnel may now attempt this mission. Discard after mission completed.

name: Gaps in Normal Space
lore: Pockets of space, such as those in the Mar Oscura nebula, dangerously phase out when coming in contact with a ship.
game_text: Place between two Mission cards. Creates a gap with a span of 4. Ships stopping on the gap kill one personnel (random selection).

name: Genetronic Replicator
lore: Medical device invented by Dr. Toby Russell. Capable of growing replacements for damaged organs.

name: Goddess of Empathy
lore: Lt. Reginald Barclay created a fantasy holodeck simulation of Counselor Deanna Troi. Her empathic abilities help other personnel anticipate danger.
game_text: Plays on table until the end of your turn. Neither you nor your opponent can play Interrupt cards (except Kevin Uxbridge or Q2). Discard event after use.

name: Holo-Projectors
lore: The hologram projector on Minos is an example of planet-based interactive holographic technology.

name: Kivas Fajo - Collector
lore: Treacherous collector of rare one-of-a-kind antiquities. Once tried to add Lt. Commander Data to his collection.
game_text: Choose any player to immediately draw three new cards from the top of their draw deck. Discard event after use.

name: Lore Returns
lore: Data's charismatic android brother. Identical except has more emotional ability. Had a negative effect on Data. Became Borg leader known as The One.
game_text: Plays where Rogue Borg have eliminated a ship's crew. With Lore, your Rogue Borg may now use ship to attack ships and/or beam to battle Away Teams.

name: Lore's Fingernail
lore: Circuitry in Lore's finger was used to control and manipulate Lt. Commander Data with emotions.
game_text: Plays on table. While in play, all Soong-type androids (including Lt. Cmdr. Data) and Exocomps lose their affiliation and are non-aligned personnel.

name: Masaka Transformations
lore: Masaka attempted to transform the U.S.S. Enterprise into an ancient temple and grounds by rearranging its matter.
game_text: Plays on any player. That player must shuffle entire hand, place on bottom of draw deck, then draw the same number of cards from the top. Discard event after use.

name: Metaphasic Shields
lore: Revolutionary shields using overlapping subspace fields. Invented by Ferengi Dr. Reyga.

name: Neural Servo Device
lore: Device which can be used to control a crew by activating pain causing implants.
game_text: Plays on any non-aligned ship. Unless 2 SECURITY aboard, use ship and crew for one turn as your own. Discard event.

name: Nutational Shields
lore: Nutation adjusts the shield frequency phase rotation, thereby increasing shield efficiency. Used against the Borg in 2367.

name: Pattern Enhancers
lore: Devices which amplify transporter signals to enhance transporter beam power in hazardous areas.
game_text: Plays on table. Allows your personnel and equipment unlimited beaming through atmospheric ionization or distortion fields.

name: Plasma Fire
lore: Intensely hot combustion of ionized plasma gas. Dangerous fire which can destroy a ship.
game_text: Plays on any ship, except Borg ship. Fire damages ship at end of next turn and continues damaging each turn. SECURITY puts it out. Discard after use.

name: Q-Net
lore: Q used an enormous forcefield grid in space to stop the U.S.S. Enterprise in 2364.
game_text: Plays between two adjacent spaceline locations. No ship may pass the Q-Net unless 2 Diplomacy aboard.

name: Raise the Stakes
lore: Weekly poker game aboard the U.S.S. Enterprise honed the tactical and bluffing skills of many officers.
game_text: Your opponent must forfeit the game OR agree the eventual winner may randomly select and keep one card from loser's 60-card deck. (Cumulative.)

name: Red Alert!
lore: The state of maximum crew and systems readiness aboard starships.

name: Res-Q
lore: Q once saved Captain Jean-Luc Picard's life following an injury from a compressed teryon beam.
game_text: Regenerates a card. Exchange this event for any one card from your discard pile.

name: Spacedock
lore: Orbital repair and building facility for starships. Such facilities have been developed by many races.
game_text: Plays on outpost. Instantly repairs your damaged ships if they stop here. Also repairs non-aligned ships.

name: Static Warp Bubble
lore: Dr. Beverly Crusher experienced a shrinking universe, shaped by her own thoughts, inside a static warp bubble created by Ensign Wesley Crusher.
game_text: Plays on table. Opponent must discard one card before ending each turn. (Not cumulative.)

name: Subspace Warp Rift
lore: Dr. Serova proved in 2370 that disastrous rifts occur in the fabric of space due to the excessive use of warp drive. Discovery led to a Federation-wide speed limit of warp 5.
game_text: Plays crosswise on any spaceline location. Any ship passing over here without stopping incurs damage.

name: Supernova
lore: The explosion of a star, usually caused by natural processes toward the end of its life cycle.
game_text: You must have Tox Uthat on table. Place atop any mission. Everything there is destroyed (discarded), but leave Mission card underneath for span reference.

name: Telepathic Alien Kidnappers
lore: Unknown aliens abducted Captain Jean-Luc Picard for telepathic studies about authority in 2366.
game_text: Plays on table. At end of each turn, guess a card type and point to a card in your opponent's hand. Card must be shown. If guessed correctly, card is discarded.

name: Tetryon Field
lore: Intense masses of subspace particles, unstable in normal space, which require ships to route through safe corridors.
game_text: Plays crosswise on any spaceline location. All ships must stop here before proceeding on next turn, unless Navigation aboard.

name: The Traveler: Transcendence
lore: Benevolent humanoid from Tau Alpha C who could transcend space and time with thought.
game_text: '''Place beside any player's draw deck. That player must draw one extra card at the end of each turn. Also, while in play, nullifies Static Warp Bubble (Not cumulative.)

name: Treaty: Federation/Klingon
lore: Past treaties between these powers included the Treaty of Alliance creating mutual aide and defense without intervention.
game_text: Plays on table. Your Federation and Klingon affiliations recognize this treaty. They can now mix and cooperate.

name: Treaty: Federation/Romulan
lore: Past treaties between these powers included the Treaty of Algeron, which created a neutral zone and outlawed Federation cloaking devices.
game_text: Plays on table. Your Federation and Romulan affiliations recognize this treaty. They can now mix and cooperate.

name: Treaty: Romulan/Klingon
lore: Historically bitter enemies, these two powers had a brief, failed alliance to share technology around 2268.
game_text: Plays on table. Your Romulan and Klingon affiliations recognize this treaty. They can now mix and cooperate.

name: Warp Core Breach
lore: In warp propulsion systems, if the magnetic confinement field collapses, matter and antimatter collide causing the ship to explode.
game_text: Plays on any ship, except Borg ship. Ship explodes at end of owner's next turn, unless ENGINEER aboard by then. Discard after use.

page_title: Where No One Has Gone Before (PL)
name: Where No One Has Gone Before
base_name: Where No One Has Gone Before
lore: The Traveler transcends space with thought. Took the U.S.S. Enterprise to Galaxy M-33, then to an even greater extragalactic distance.
game_text: Plays on table. Allows all your ships to leave one end of the spaceline and enter the other end.

name: Federation Outpost
lore: Earth is a member of the United Federation of Planets. The Federation establishes outposts throughout its territory.

name: Klingon Outpost
lore: The Klingon Homeworld is Qo'noS. The Klingon Empire establishes outposts throughout its territory.

name: Romulan Outpost
lore: Romulus is one of the two homeworlds for the Romulans. The Romulan Star Empire establishes outposts throughout its territory

name: Alien Groupie
lore: Lanel, a Malcorian nurse, agreed to help Commander William T. Riker, but only if he would...
game_text: Plays on any Away Team which has just completed a planet mission. Female groupie delays beam up of one male (random selection) for one full turn.

name: Amanda Rogers
lore: Female Q raised as a human on Earth. Was taken to the Q continuum by Q after she could not resist the benevolent use of her powers.

name: Asteroid Sanctuary
lore: Hoping to avoid detection by a Romulan Warbird, the U.S.S. Enterprise entered a giant asteroid cavern in 2370.
game_text: Plays on any ship. If 2 Navigation aboard, hides ship to prevent any battle initiated against that ship for this turn.

name: Auto-Destruct Sequence
lore: Computer controlled self-destruct countdown which can be set by the senior officers aboard a ship.

name: Crosis
lore: Fanatical Borg lieutenant of Lore. Captured Lt. Commander Data with the lure of emotions.
game_text: Plays on Rogue Borg. Doubles their STRENGTH, including himself. Two Borg =4 STRENGTH each, three Borg =6 STRENGTH each, etc. (Not cumulative.)

name: Disruptor Overload
lore: A directed-energy weapon can be set on overload and left to explode like a bomb.

name: Distortion of Space/Time Continuum
lore: Time effects can be caused by the unusual warping or rifting of space.

name: Emergency Transporter Armbands
lore: Devices which allow quick remote activation of a transporter when in danger.

name: Energy Vortex
lore: Whirlpool-like space/time phenomena that can destroy a ship, as it nearly did the U.S.S. Enterprise in 2365.
game_text: Plays immediately after opponent plays any non-Interrupt card from hand. That card returns to their hand and a different one must be played instead.

name: Escape Pod
lore: Angosian escape pod used by Roga Danar in 2366. Escape pods can be used in an emergency to save a crew.
game_text: Plays on ship being destroyed . Escape pod saves entire crew. Unseen by enemy ships, crew remains in pod until personnel rescued. Discard after rescue.

name: Full Planet Scan
lore: Sensor instruments can make detailed scans of a planet surface and atmosphere.

name: Honor Challenge
lore: The call to glory inspires the Klingon warrior to maximum fierceness and honor, as symbolized by the Bat'telh (sic) championship trophy.
game_text: Plays just after an Away Team battle is initiated. Each Klingon with Honor immediately kills one opponent with Treachery. Battle continues.

name: Hugh
lore: The Federation named a rescued Borg, Hugh. When he returned, his newly acquired self-aware personality collapsed the Borg collective.
