lore: Chief of Starfleet Operations. Misguided paranoid. Faked evidence of impending Dominion invasion and urged Jaresh-Inyo to place Earth under martial law.

name: Admiral Riker
lore: Commander of Starbase 247 in an alternate future. At odds with Governor Worf. Battled Klingons near Devron.

name: Captain Kirk
lore: Legendary starship captain. In 2267, met "lieutenant" Sisko. 17 temporal violations. "The man was a menace."

name: Jaresh-Inyo
lore: Male Grazerite. President of the United Federation of Planets. Reluctantly imposed martial law on Earth in 2372 at the urging of Admiral Leyton.

name: Keogh
lore: Captain of the U.S.S. Odyssey. In 2370, ordered to investigate the Jem'Hadar threat and rescue Benjamin Sisko. Knew Jadzia Dax, but not on friendly terms.

name: Michael Eddington
lore: Lt. Commander Eddington. Security officer assigned to Deep Space 9 becuase of Starfleet concerns about Odo. Defected to the Maquis.

name: Atul
lore: Typical Klingon intelligence specialist. Dispatched to Deep Space 9 with Morka and Bo'rak to investigate Romulan activity.

name: Ch'Pok
lore: Klingon advocate. Skilled negotiator. Prosecuted a contrived hearing against Worf in 2372 to manipulate Federation involvement in the Klingon/Cardassian war.

name: Martok
lore: Highly decorated general and High Council member. Accepted Worf, Alexander and Jadzia Dax into the House of Martok. Lost his left eye battling the Jem'Hadar.

name: Worf Son of Mogh
lore: Worf resigned his Starfleet commission to join Gowron during the 2367-68 Klingon Civil War. Saved the I.K.C. Bortas from destruction by Duras forces.

name: Anya
lore: Female allasomorph. Shape-shifting guardian of Salia. Scouts ahead before declaring environment safe. Will do anything to protect Salia and the hope she represents.

name: Salia
lore: Allasomorph leader of Daled IV. Shape-shifter. Parents killed in civil war. Raised by Anya on Klavdia III. Expected to unite her people. Likes Wesley Crusher.

name: Soto
lore: Typical Lethean mercenary. Telepathically extracted Kor's knowledge of the Shroud of the Sword. Tried to help Toral steal the Sword of Kahless.

name: Lovok
lore: High-ranking colonel in the Tal Shiar. Proponent of a temporary alliance with the Obsidian Order to destroy the foundation of the Dominion.

name: Senator Vreenak
lore: Vice-Chairman of the Tal Shiar. Secretary of the War Plans Council. Key Romulan senator for over 14 years. Negotiated non-aggression pact with the Dominion.

name: T'Rul
lore: Romulan female assigned to install, safeguard and operate the cloaking device loaned to Starfleet for use aboard the U.S.S. Defiant.

name: Keldon Advanced
lore: Faster than standard Keldon-class vessels. Secretly upgraded by the Obsidian Order. Staged in Orias System.

name: Trager
lore: Commanded by Macet. Dispatched to intercept U.S.S. Phoenix, reportedly attacking Cardassian vessels in violation of the 2366 peace treaty.

name: Jem'Hadar Attack Ship
lore: Nimble attack fighter used by the Dominion. Has ion propulsion drive and ventral impellers. Virtual display technology. Polaron beam weapons.

name: Jem'Hadar Warship
lore: Mainstay battle cruiser of the Jem'Hadar fleets. Capable of serving as a mobile base for attack ships. Equipped with shield-penetrating transporters.

name: U.S.S. Defiant
lore: NX-74205. Built to battle Borg. Recommisioned to oppose the Dominion. First ship to test ablative armor and quantum torpedoes. Captain by Benjamin Sisko.

name: U.S.S. Odyssey
lore: NCC-71832. Starship sent into the Gamma Quadrant to investigate the Dominion. Victim of Jem'Hadar suicide tactics. Commanded by Keogh.

name: U.S.S. Rio Grande
lore: First runabout assigned to Deep Space 9. Towed the Prakesh through the Bajoran Wormhole. Commanded by Benjamin Sisko.

name: I.K.C. Rotarran
lore: Bird-of-Prey station at Deep Space 9 during the war against the Dominion. Commanded by Martok. Led many raids into Cardassian and Dominion space.

name: D'deridex Advanced
lore: Upgraded by the Tal Shiar near Orias III. Used in Tal Shiar/Obsidian Order attack of the Dominion of 2371.

name: We Are the Borg
lore: "Lower your shields and surrender your ships. We will add your biological and technological distinctivenes to our own. Your culture will adapt to service us. Resistance is futile."
game_text: Downloads two Defense drones; discard event. OR Plays on table. Each turn, report one of your Borg cards for free or make an additional end-of-turn draw (immune to Kevin Uxbridge).

name: Add Distinctiveness
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. X varies, where X = number of Skill Dot icons on personnel you've assimilated as drones. Also, if you are behind by 40 or more points, once per game you may open a sealed First Contact expansion pack. Play or place in hand any or all non-seed cards in that pack. (non-Borg cards are assimilated or stolen, as appropriate), then place others out-of-play).

name: Nightmare
game_text: Plays on non-Borg opponent if you have a Borg card or Borg Ship dilemma in play. Each turn, peek at one to three cards in opponent's hand (random selection) and store at least one of them beneath incident. Nullified only by Plexing or when stored cards exceed cards in opponent's hand. (When nullified, choose one stored card to place beneath opponent's draw deck; return others to opponent's hand.)

name: Population 9 Billion - All Borg
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. If your Borg have completed Stop First Contact (or Build Interplexing Beacon), place incident on Earth; you may download a Borg outpost there. Your Borg cards may subsequently report on Earth or to that outpost; and your subsequently completed Borg Only objectives targeting missions in the Alpha Quadrant score double points.

name: Service the Collective
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Whenever your current objective targets either a homeworld OR your mission that has an affiliation icon matching your counterpart there, your Borg are not restricted from probing on same turn they complete scouting. Also, while a personnel you've assimilated as a counterpart is on your ship, that ship is WEAPONS and SHIELDS +4 against counterpart's former affiliation(s).

name: Bareil of Borg
lore: Assimilated counterpart who spoke to the Bajorans. "The knowledge and experience of the Bajoran – Bareil Antos – is part of us now.

name: Dukat of Borg
lore: Assimilated counterpart who spoke to the Cardassians. "The knowledge and experience of the Cardassian – Dukat – is part of us now."

name: Eleven of Seventeen
lore: IDENTIFICATION: COMPLINK DRONETASK: Ensure network data continuity. Augment.BIOLOGICAL DISTINCTIVENESS: Humanoid.

name: Six of Nineteen
lore: IDENTIFICATION: REASSIMILATION DRONETASK: Repair and reintegrate defective drones.BIOLOGICAL DISTINCTIVENESS: Humanoid.

name: Assimilated Counterpart
lore: Assimilated counterpart who spoke for the Borg. "His knowledge and experience 'is part of us now.

name: Communication Drone
lore: IDENTIFICATION: COMMUNICATION DRONETASK: Service communication subcommand.

name: Defense Drone
lore: IDENTIFICATION: DEFENSE DRONETASK: Service defense subcommand.

name: Navigation Drone
lore: IDENTIFICATION: NAVIGATION DRONETASK: Service navigation subcommand.

name: Sword of Kahless
lore: Legendary first bat'leth. 1500-year-old blade weapon forged by Kahless the Unforgettable. Used to slay the tyrant Molor. Discovered by Worf, Kor and Jadzia Dax in 2372.
game_text: Use as Equipment card. Where present, your Klingons with Honor are attributes all +3; Kahless is STRENGTH +7 more and may not be killed in personnel battle. (Not duplicatable.)

name: Chula: The Abyss
lore: In shap six of chula, players can fall into a deep crevasse. Three Deep Space 9 senior officers fell in, but landed in Quark's bar and learned it was only part of an elaborate game.
game_text: To get past, three personnel present (random selection) must face the abyss. If their total CUNNING is odd, they are "stopped" and, if possible, relocated to Quark's Bar.

name: Chula: The Lights
lore: Players face several perils throughout the game of chula. In shap four of the game played in Quark's bar, Julian Bashir was singled out and "eliminated" by a burst of energy.
game_text: Crew or Away Team member with total attributes closest to 22 (your choice if tie) returns to hand. To get past requires CUNNING>24 remaining.

name: Drumhead
lore: In 2367, suspected sabotage to the warp core of the U.S.S. Enterprise led to an investigation of the crew. Suspicions ran rampant before Jean-Luc Picard put an end to the "witch hunt."
game_text: If present, discard a crew member of INTEGRITY<5 (Norah Satie's choice if in play, or random selection); otherwise, to get past requires Jean-Luc Picard OR Law. Nullify with Plexing.

name: Ferengi Ingenuity
lore: Quark's refusal to spend latinum resulted in some creative holosuite repairs. Rom once used a copper-ytterbium composite spatula as a spare part – the perfect plasma conductor.
game_text: If one personnel present has 2 Computer Skill, discard dilemma. Otherwise, to get past, place on most CUNNING Computer Skill present ("stopped" during countdown).

name: Gravimetric Distortion
lore: Gravimetric fluctuations sometimes accompany interruptions in the normal flow of space and time. Spatial distortion phenomena can cause a wide range of problems.
game_text: Ship damaged unless 4 ENGINEER OR 2 Astrophysics OR a personnel who has 2 Navigation OR Guinan aboard.

name: Hazardous Duty
lore: Jake Sisko was exposed to the horrors of war when caught in the Klingon attack on Ajilon Prime. Not a soldier, he was unprepared for the hazards he faced with the colonists.
game_text: To get past requires 2 OFFICER; then place on mission until solved. If any non-OFFICER dies here, its owner loses points (discard dilemma).

name: New Essentialists
lore: The New Essentialists Movement asserts that decadence and complacency are eroding the foundations of the Federation. Worf was temporarily swayed by this group while on Risa.
game_text: Unless INTEGRITY>40 and 2 Honor OR CUNNING>40 and 2 Treachery present, place one non-Borg Away Team member (random selection) atop draw deck. Nullify with Jamaharon.

name: Stellar Flare
lore: Stellar flares release tremendous amounts of energy and emit radiation across the entire electromagnetic spectrum. Large flares can cause severe damage throughout a star system.
game_text: Damages and "stops" all ships at this location except those that are docked, landed or carried OR have 2 Navigation and Astrophysics aboard OR have SHIELDS>11. Discard dilemma.

name: Under Fire
lore: While on a medical mission to Ajilon Prime in 2373, Julian Bashir found himself in the middle of a live combat situation.
game_text: Immediately probe (then place probe card atop draw deck}: Doorway, Interrupt, Download, Borg : Kills two personnel (random selection). Otherwise: "Stops" one personnel (random selection).

name: Battle Bridge Door
game_text: Place one atop Battle Bridge side deck during the seed phase. Battle Bridge is now open and in play (immune to cards which close doorways). OR Stock in deck and play at start of ship battle (even during opponent's turn) if you have Leadership in that battle. Allows you to draw two extra Tactic cards (cumulative) or enhances each of your ships' and facilities' WEAPONS +1; then discard doorway.

name: Holding Cell Door
game_text: Seeds (during facility phase) or plays on your ship or facility (except a Nor). Adds a Brig. OR Downloads Brainwash, Interrogation or Torture to a captive in your Brig, if you have Tal Shiar, Obsidian Order, Resistance or Section 31 (or a personnel who has SECURITY and Treachery) present; discard doorway or place atop draw deck. OR Nullifies any card closing another Holding Cell Door; discard doorway.

name: Bat'leth
lore: Traditional blade weapon of the Klingon warrior. According to legend, the first bat'leth, or "sword of honor," was forged by Kahless the Unforgettable some fifteen centuries ago.
game_text: Each of your Klingons present is STRENGTH +2, and in each battle one of them may mortally wound one adversary they just stunned. (Cumulative.)

name: D'k Tahg
lore: Fearsome, three-bladed weapon. Ubiquitous in Klingon society. Favored knife of the warrior. Has ceremonial, combat and culinary applications. Easily concealed.
game_text: Klingon use only. Reports for free. Each of your personnel present is STRENGTH +1. (Cumulative.) May report to a just-initiated personnel battle involving your Klingon card(s).

name: Kar'takin
lore: Blade weapon used by the Jem'Hadar and Dominion allies. Similar to the Klingon bat'leth in function and effectiveness.
game_text: Each of your Jem'Hadar, Breen and Dosi present is STRENGTH +2, and in each battle one of them may mortally wound one adversary they just stunned. (Cumulative.)

name: Klingon Disruptor Rifle
lore: Standard phase disruptor fitted with attachable shoulder stack. Rifle components include extended-charge capacitance cell, high-energy augmented accelerator and requisite induction coil.
game_text: Klingon and Non-Aligned use only. Each of your personnel present is STRENGTH +3, but loses 1 Diplomacy unless aboard your ship. (Cumualtive.)

name: Mek'leth
lore: Blade weapon favored by many Klingons for close-combat situations. Typically made of baakonite. The mek'leth's size and perfect balance make it an excellent offensive weapon.
game_text: May report wherever you have a Klingon present. Each of your Klingons present is STRENGTH +2. (Cumulative.)

name: Romulan Disruptor Rifle
lore: Enhanced energy rifle used throughout the Romulan Star Empire. Generates an elevated level of residual anti-protons which are detectable for several hours after firing.
game_text: Romulan and Non-Aligned use only. Each of your personnel present is STRENGTH +3, but loses 1 Diplomacy unless aboard your ship. (Cumulative.)

name: Starfleet Type I Phaser
lore: Least powerful of the standard hand-held Federation defensive weapons. Low profile favored by Starfleet captain. Smaller in size than the type II phaser, and easily concealed.
game_text: Federation use only. Reports for free. Each of your personnel present is STRENGTH +1. (Cumulative.) May report to a just-initiated personnel battle involving your Federation card(s).

name: Defense System Upgrade
lore: Wartime upgrades to Deep Space 9's defensive systems in 2372 included enhanced shield emitters, rotary phasers, microtorpedo launchers and 5,000 new torpedoes.
game_text: Plays on your space facility. WEAPONS=6 (or WEAPONS +4) and SHIELDS +6. (Cumulative.) OR Fully repairs a damaged facility if your compatible ENGINEER aboard; discard event.

name: Dial Martok for Murder
lore: While infiltrating the Klingon Empire, a changeling posing as Martok killed two guards in an isolated corridor. They never expected such treachery from an honorable warrior.
game_text: Plays to allow your infiltrator to initiate a battle, with +4 STRENGTH, against up to two opposing personnel present (your choice). Infiltrator is not exposed. Discard event.

name: E-Band Emissions
lore: Taibak and Kell used E-band emissions transmitted to Geordi La Forge's VISOR to influence the engineer's actions. La Forge was being programmed to assassinate Governor Vagh.
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. May not be nullified if Kell, Taibak or Entek in play. Brainwash is immune to Kevin Uxbridge and gives captive infiltration icons for its own affiliation(s).

name: Engage Shuttle Operations: Dominion
lore: Jem'Hadar warships are designed as mobile bases for attack ships, allowing the Dominion to quickly mobilize and maintain a massive strike fleet.
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Your shuttlecraft and Jem'Hadar attack ships may be loaded aboard and launched from your Dominion warships and battleships with Tractor Beam.

name: Fajo's Gallery
lore: Kidnapped by Kivas Fajo, Data became part of an impressive collection of rare and one-of-a-kind items. Fajo had no problem with the morality of Data's imprisonment.
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. You may draw two cards each time you capture a unique personnel, and one card each time one of your Fajo Collection cards or your Mona Lisa enters play.

name: The Big Picture
lore: Jean-Luc Picard has to convince Lily Sloane that she was on a starship orbiting Earth. To defeat the Borg, Captain Picard's crew had to succeed on the ship as well as on the planet.
game_text: Plays on table. Each player who has no solved (or scouted) at least two missions with point boxes (one Space and one Planet) needs an additional 40 points to win. (May not be nullified.)

name: Torture
lore: Jean-Luc Picard was captured by Cardassians in 2369. He was subjected to intense physiological and psychological torture in an effort to obtain strategic Federation information.

name: Intruder Alert!
game_text: Seeds or plays on table; nullifies all seeded Memory Wipe cards. At any time, you may capture a one- or two-person Away Team in your Ops or assimilate one personnel intruder on your Borg ship or facility if your Talon Drone is present (discard incident) OR download Intruder Force Field (place incident atop event to protect it from nullification and extend its effects to all intruders on your ships.

name: Long Live the Queen
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Reveal (then discard) incident to do one of the following: If your Borg Queen was just killed, download another Borg Queen. OR Prevent your Borg Queen present with your Defense drone from being captured (drone is captured instead). OR Suspend any Regenerate while you place out-of-play from targeted discard pile up to six cards without a Borg Only or Borg icon.

name: Prisoner Exchange
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. During your turn, you may release a personnel you hold captive (relocate to owner's ship or facility at same location). Release any or all of your own personnel held captive at that location (relocate them to your ship or facility there), or instead download any one personnel there; then discard incident.

name: Sniper
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. At start of each battle you initiate on a planet, if you have a phaser or disruptor present, target one personnel present. (Cumulative.) Immediately probe (then place probe card beneath draw deck):Staff, Ketracel-White, Equipment, Maquis : Hit. Target(s) mortally wounded. Objective, Interrupt, Doorway, Alternate : Glancing blow. Target(s) stunned. Federation, Ferengi, Borg, Command : Sniper spotted. Discard incident.

name: Attack Pattern Delta
lore: Upon encountering Dominion ships during a rescue attempt in 2370, Captain Keogh ordered the U.S.S. Odyssey and two runabouts to execute a predermined attack pattern.
game_text: Plays at start of ship battle. Doubles one Tactical Console until end of battle OR draw up to X additional Tactic cards, where X = the number of your ships in this battle.

name: Counterintelligence
lore: The Founder posing as Julian Bashir used his position as chief medical officer to gain valuable information for the Dominion, while secretly undermining the efforts of his enemies.
game_text: Plays on your infiltrator. Until end of turn, subtract (rather than add) infiltrator's classification, skills and attributes from infiltrated crew's or Away Team's totals.

name: Inside Operation
lore: The changeling impersonating Lovok compromised the mission to destroy the Founders' homeworld. His participation in the battle plans led the attacking fleet into a Jem'Hadar ambush.
game_text: Plays at start of ship battle. Each opposing ship and facility in this battle is WEAPONS and SHIELDS -3 if your personnel is infiltrating one of them. Infiltrator exposed.

name: Outgunned
lore: On a mission inside Dominion space, the U.S.S. Defiant was surrounded by Jem'Hadar vessels. In the face of superior firepower, Benjamin Sisko elected to surrender.

name: Phaser Array Power Cell
lore: In times of war, it is not unusual for a crew to adopt rituals recognizing its accomplishments in battle. In 2374, the crew of the U.S.S. Defiant ceremonially displayed used phaser cells.
game_text: Once per turn, plays to score points if your ship survived a battle in which it and an opponent's card both fired WEAPONS.

name: Prisoner Escort
lore: Captured by a Hunter, Tosk was led through the corridors of Deep Space 9 to show that he had been apprehended – the ultimate humiliation for a Tosk.
game_text: Plays on a personnel you just captured. If you place captive in your Brig, its owner lose points (once per persona per game).

name: The Guardian
lore: The allasomorphy Anya could appear in many forms. In 2365, while escorting Salia aboard the U.S.S. Enterprise, Anya took the form of a monstrous guardian to protect her charge.
game_text: Suspends play while you place interrupt on your shape-shifter . It morphs (STRENGTH +6; exposed if infiltrating). Discard interrupt if shape-shifter morphs again.

name: The Wake of the Borg
lore: The New Providence colony on Jouret IV was scooped up by the Borg in 2366, just as Federation and Romulan outposts along the Neutral Zone had been destroyed in 2364.

name: Victory Is Life
lore: "I am First Omet'iklan. And I am dead. As of this moment we are all dead. We go into battle to win back our lives. This we do gladly, because we are Jem'Hadar. Remember... victory is life."

name: A Good Day To Live
lore: Secarus IV: Seek revenge on notorious criminal who used a genetic virus to murder Klingon children.
game_text: *+5 for each Nemesis Red Right personnel in Away Team.

name: Bat'leth Tournament
lore: Klingon planet: Participate in bat'leth competition held at this Klingon settlement.
game_text: *+10 if bat'leth is Sword of Kahless.

name: Chart Stellar Cluster
lore: Edge of Denkiri Arm: Perform long-distance overview survey of this region in the Gamma Quadrant.

name: Examine Singularity
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Once each turn, your ship with SCIENCE , Astrophysics and CUNNING>30 in crew may close Black Hole where present. Relocate all ships there to one other location in any quadrant, place Black Hole out-of-play and score points (discard objective). Also, once each turn, you may download (even from discard pile) Bajoran Wormhole, Temporal Wake or Deactivation.

name: Impersonate Captive
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Place on your Founder present with a non-Borg personnel you've captured. Founder morphs to impersonate captive. Founder's classification, skills, staffing icon, infiltration icon, STRENGTH and CUNNING change to those of captive. Founder has 1 Treachery, loses all Honor and gains infiltration icon(s) for captive's affiliation(s). May morph back at any time (discard objective).

name: Prepare the Prisoner
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Captives you Brainwash are not required to relocate to an outpost. Opponent's Rescue Captives card affects only captives at one location where opponent has a crew or Away Team (rescued personnel relocate to that crew or Away Team). Each turn, you may draw one card by placing one capturing-related card from your hand beneath your draw deck or discard pile.

name: Furel
lore: Strong believer in the Prophets. While with Shakaar resistance cell, lost his left arm saving Kira Nerys from Cardassians. Refuses synthetic replacement.

name: Lupaza
lore: Friend of Kira Nerys. Romantically involved with Furel. Member of Shakaar resistance cell. Fought provisional government over soil reclamators.

name: Riker Wil
lore: In 2370, the human William T. Riker accompanied Ro Laren on a clandestine mission to investigate the Maquis. He posed as a Bajoran freedom fighter.

name: Ro Laren
lore: Former Starfleet officer. Defected to the Maquis in 2370. Used a low-intensity particle beam to expose a Federation attack force hiding in a nebula.

name: Boone Impersonator
lore: Cardassian surgically altered to resemble retired Starfleet officer Raymond Boone. Spied on the Federation. Attempted to frame Miles O'Brien.

name: Dolak
lore: Officer in the Cardassian militia, unit 41. First Gul to command the Kraxon. Tactical commander of task force sent to kill the Bajoran terrorist Orta.

name: Elim
lore: Elim Garak forced himself to interrogate Odo in an attempt to regain favor with his father, Enabran Tain.

name: Gul Madred
lore: Ruthless Obsidian Order officer. Madred's torture of Jean-Luc Picard quickly degenerated into a desperate attempt to break Picard's will. A pitiable man.

name: Duran'Adar
lore: Sixth. Typical Jem'Hadar alpha. Served under Kudak'Etan. Assisted with repairs to U.S.S. Defiant captured by his away team in 2364.

name: Gelnon
lore: Vorta who ordered an attack on the U.S.S. Defiant in 2374. Skeptical of using Kudak'Etan and other Jem'Hadar alphas. His suspicions were justified.

name: Ixtana'Rax
lore: Jem'Hadar Honored Elder. Became Second under Kudak'Etan when the alpha was promoted above him. Unsure about the new order of things.

name: Kudak'Etan
lore: Arrogant First under Gelnon. Commanded the captured U.S.S. Defiant in 2374. One of the first Jem'Hadar bred in Alpha Quadrant. Ignored his Second's advice.

name: Lamat'Ukan
lore: Jem'Hadar Third. Alpha. Realigned targeting sensors on U.S.S. Defiant captured by Dominion forces in 2374. His initiative pleased First Kudak'Etan.

name: Odo Founder
lore: Changeling who confused the crew of the U.S.S. Defiant by posing as Odo.

name: Oken'alak
lore: Fifth under Ikat'ika. Guard at Internment Camp 371. Representative of Jem'Hadar assigned to guard and escort Dominion prisoners.

name: Umat'Adan
lore: Fifth. Jem'Hadar alpha assigned to Kudak'Etan. Well versed in the Alpha Quadrant anomaly. Once guarded prisoners repairing the commandeered U.S.S. Defiant

name: Admiral Ross
lore: Starfleet veteran. Performed the wedding of Benjamin Sisko and Kassidy Yates. Reluctantly involved in Section 31 plot to discredit Senator Cretak.

name: Enrique Muñiz
lore: Highly valued assistant to Chief O'Brien. Called "Quigue" by his friends. Joked that he wants to grow up to be O'Brien – just not as old and grizzled.

name: Miles O'Brien
lore: Chief of operations on Deep Space 9. Friend of Julian. Father of Molly and Kirayoshi. Husband of Keiko. Likes kayaking, darts and historical battle simulations.

name: Sarita Carson
lore: Ensign Carson is one of the many talented navigators serving Starfleet. Former member of Nova Squadron. Assigned to bridge duty aboard U.S.S. Defiant.

name: Ilon Tandro
lore: Klaestron dignitary. Son of Enine and General Ardelon Tandro. In 2369, used Cardassian technology to gain access to Deep Space 9 in order to kidnap Jadzia Dax.

name: Hon'Tihl
lore: First officer and sole survivor of the I.K.C. Toh'Kaht. Briefly succeeded captain Kee'Bhor. Suffering from the influence of Saltah'na energy spheres.

name: Jadzia Dax
lore: Trill. Disregarded her commitments to both Starfleet and Trill custom in order to honor a Klingon blood oath sworn by her symbiont's previous host, Curzon Dax.

name: Kang
lore: Faced Kirk at Beta XII-A. Sword blood oath against the Albino with Kor, Koloth and Curzon Dax to avenge the death of his firstborn son.

name: Kavok
lore: Commanded U.S.S. Enterprise after hijacking it from Starbase 74. Intended to start a war with the Federation and die in glorious battle. Once captained I.K.C. Buruk.

name: Koloth
lore: Called d'akturak, "ice man," by Curzon Dax due to his negotiating prowess. Commanded the I.K.C. Gr'oth during the Sherman's Planet sabotage mission in 2267.

name: Kor
lore: Dahar master. Legendary warrior. Former ambassador to Vulcan. Victorious at Klach D'Kel Brakt. Swore blood oath against the Albino. Sought the Sword of Kahless.

name: N'Garen
lore: Typical of young Klingons serving the Empire. Daughter of Tse'Dek. Assigned to tactical/weapons station on I.K.C. Rotarran by General Martok.

name: Voktak
lore: Typical front-line Klingon officer. Engaged Federation forces on Ajilon Prime. Once commanded the I.K.C. K'Ratak while its captain recovered from war injuries.

name: Wo'Din
lore: Typical Klingon inspired by tales of glorious battle against the Dominion. Learned diplomatic skills from his father, a former Klingon negotiator.

name: Worf Son of Mogh
lore: Worf resigned his Starfleet commission to join Gowron during the 2367-68 Klingon Civil War. Saved the I.K.C. Bortas from destruction by Duras forces.

name: Zetal
lore: Typical skilled Klingon serving in the fleet during the war with Cardassia. Her ship took part in a raid which destroyed an outpost on Korma in 2372.

name: Quark Son of Keldar
lore: Quark wedded Grilka by brek'tal ritual to head the House of Kozak (as the House of Quark) on Qo'noS. The Ferengi saved his be'nal from financial ruin.

name: The Albino
lore: Infamous humanoid criminal. Mercenary captain of a spacefaring group of bandits. Engineered a genetic virus that killed firstborn sons of Kor, Kang and Koloth.

name: Ambassador Tomalak
lore: Romulan Ambassador in Barash's illusion. Key figure in securing a treaty with the Federation. Commander of the Decius.

name: Chief O'Brien
lore: Holographic re-creation of U.S.S. Enterprise transporter chief. Used to aid mental reprogramming. Taibak forced Geordi La Forge to "kill" the chief repeatedly.

name: D'Vin
lore: Typical graduate of Romulan Astrophysical Academy. Research assistant to Dr. Telok R'Mor during the doctor's last year at the academy.

name: Dr. Koramar
lore: Brilliant Romulan astro-archaeologist. Member of the Romulan underground. Works closely with Spock for reunification of the Vulcan and Romulan peoples.

name: La Forge Impersonator
lore: Surgically altered Romulan. In 2367, posed as Geordi La Forge so Taibak could brainwash the real La Forge without raising suspicions.

name: Mopak
lore: Representative of Romulan security personnel. Specializes in biohazard detection. In 2372, helped search the Romulan fleet for Dominion infiltration.

name: Navok
lore: Representative of security personnel in the Romulan Star Empire. His detachment accompanied Senator Vreenak to Deep Space 9 in 2374.

name: Parthok
lore: Technical advisor to Senator Vreenak. Trained by Tal Shiar. In 2374, counseled the senator during his mission to Deep Space 9.

name: R'Mal
lore: Typical Romulan scientist. Led team of archaeologists on an unsuccessful mission to locate an Iconian gateway in Romulan territory.

name: Senator Letant
lore: Romulan military strategist. He studied, and grudginly approved, Benjamin Sisko's plan for an attack on the Dominion shipyards at Chin'toka.

name: Tamarith
lore: Female nurse. Member of Romulan underground. Supported Ambassador's Spock efforts to reunify Romulus and Vulcan.

name: Tharket
lore: Associate of Taibak. Provided security services during the mental reprogramming of Geordi La Forge.

name: Locutus' Borg Cube
lore: IDENTIFICATION: BORG CUBETASK: Eliminate resistance at location designation Wolf 359. Locutus of Borg commands.

name: Keldon
lore: Cardassian warship. More powerful than Galor-class spacecraft. Design commissioned by the Central Command after war with Federation in 2366.

name: Kraxon
lore: Cardassian warship sent to intercept the U.S.S. Defiant and the renegade Thomas Riker in 2371.

name: Alpha Attack Ship
lore: Jem'Hadar attack ship produced at Chin'toka shipyard in Alpha Quadrant. Constructed after enemy forces restricted Dominion access to the Bajoran Wormhole.

name: U.S.S. Thunderchild
lore: NCC-63549. Helped lead Starfleet forces against invading Borg cube in 2373. Briefly commanded by Fleet Admiral Shanthi during its shakedown cruise.
game_text: SHIELDS +4 vs. Borg ships and Borg Ship dilemma.

name: I.K.C. Koraga
lore: Klingon Bird-of-Prey briefly commanded by Worf Son of Mogh in 2375. Along with the I.K.C. Rotarran, engaged a Dominion patrol near the Badlands.
game_text: If your I.K.C. Rotarran in play, both are RANGE +1.

name: I.K.C. Lukara
lore: Bird-of-Prey commanded by Kang. Transported its commander and his comrades to Secarus IV in 2370, to confront the Albino in his stronghold.

name: I.K.C. Negh'Var
lore: Flagship of the Klingon Defense Force. Commanded by Gowron when first commissioned, and then by Martok during the 2372 invasion of Cardassia.

name: Goraxus
lore: Warbird commanded by Sela. Used to intercept Geordi La Forge's shuttle en route to Risa in 2367, and to mentally reprogram the engineer.
game_text: Download Romulan Ambush

name: Romulan Shuttle
lore: Romulan shuttlecraft. Favored by the Tal Shiar. Senator Vreenak commanded one on his diplomatic mission to Deep Space 9.

name: Security Holding Cell
game_text: Has a Brig. Once each turn, player who controls station may download [[Brainwash#Star Trek 1st Edition>Brainwash]], Interrogation or Torture to a captive held in this Brig if that player has a Tal Shiar, Obsidian Order, Resistance or Section 31 personnel (or a personnel who has SECURITY and Treachery) unopposed here.

name: "Crimson Forcefield"
game_text: Harmless pyrotechnic ruse nullifies opponent's Tactic card unless opponent has an OFFICER with CUNNING>8 aboard a ship or facility on this battle.Hit = Tactic Draw. Direct hit = Tactic Draw.

name: Attack Wing
game_text: ATTACK bonus +1 for each of your ships firing. DEFENSE bonus +1 if you have a Jem'Hadar attack ship defending.Hit = Tactic Draw. Direct hit = Tactic Draw Tactic Draw.

name: Borg Cutting Beam
game_text: If you hit, you may relocate one of target's crew members (random selection; from any one site if on a Nor) to one of your ships in this battle and assimilate that personnel.Hit or Direct hit = Tactic Current.

name: Evasive Maneuvers
game_text: DEFENSE bonus +2 if you have a ship with no staffing requirements defending.Hit = Tactic Draw. Direct hit = Tactic Draw Tactic Draw.

name: Full Phaser Spread
game_text: ATTACK bonus +1 if you have a Galaxy-class ship firing.Hit = Tactic Draw. Direct hit = Tactic Draw Tactic Draw.

name: Phased Polaron Beam
game_text: ATTACK bonus +1 if you have a Dominion ship firing.Hit = Tactic Draw. Direct hit = Tactic Draw Tactic Draw.

name: Phaser Banks
game_text: ATTACK bonus +2 if you have a Federation ship firing.Hit = Tactic Draw. Direct hit = Tactic Draw Tactic Draw.

name: Photon Torpedo
game_text: ATTACK bonus +1 if you have an Akira-class ship firing.Hit = Tactic Draw. Direct hit = Tactic Draw Tactic Draw.

name: Plasma Torpedo
game_text: ATTACK bonus +2 if you have a Romulan ship firing.Hit = Tactic Draw. Direct hit = Tactic Draw Tactic Draw.

name: Primary Energy Weapon
game_text: ATTACK bonus +2 if you have a Borg ship firing.Hit = Tactic Draw. Direct hit = Tactic Draw Tactic Draw.

name: Pulse Disruptor
game_text: ATTACK bonus +2 if you have a Klingon ship firing.Hit = Tactic Draw. Direct hit = Tactic Draw Tactic Draw.

name: Pulse Phaser Cannons
game_text: ATTACK bonus +1 if you have a Defiant-class ship firing.Hit = Tactic Draw. Direct hit = Tactic Draw Tactic Draw.

name: Quantum Torpedo
game_text: ATTACK bonus +1 if you have a Sovereign-class ship firing.Hit = Tactic Draw. Direct hit = Tactic Draw Tactic Draw.

name: Spiral-Wave Disruptor
game_text: ATTACK bonus +2 if you have a Cardassian ship firing.Hit = Tactic Draw. Direct hit = Tactic Draw Tactic Draw.

name: Strafing Run
game_text: ATTACK bonus +1 if you have a Hideki-class ship firing.Hit = Tactic Current Tactic Draw. Direct hit = Tactic Current Tactic Draw Tactic Draw.

name: Target Engines
game_text: ATTACK bonus +2 if you have a Dominion ship firing.Hit = Tactic Current Tactic Draw. Direct hit = Tactic Current Tactic Draw Tactic Draw.

name: Target Shields
game_text: Hit = Tactic Current Tactic Draw. Direct hit = Tactic Current Tactic Draw Tactic Draw. Otherwise, drains target's SHIELDS (Tactic Current).

name: Target These Coordinates
game_text: Hit = Tactic Current Tactic Draw (or Tactic Current Tactic Draw if target is affected by Weak Spot).Direct hit = Tactic Current Tactic DrawTactic Draw.

name: Target Weapons
game_text: ATTACK bonus +2 if you have a Dominion ship firing.Hit = Tactic Current Tactic Draw. Direct hit = Tactic Current Tactic Draw Tactic Draw.

name: Sword of Kahless
lore: Legendary first bat'leth. 1500-year-old blade weapon forged by Kahless the Unforgettable. Used to slay the tyrant Molor. Discovered by Worf, Kor and Jadzia Dax in 2372.
game_text: Use as Equipment card. Where present, your Klingons with Honor are attributes all +3; Kahless is STRENGTH +7 more and may not be killed in personnel battle. (Not duplicatable.)

name: Fajo's Gallery
lore: Kidnapped by Kivas Fajo, Data became part of an impressive collection of rare and one-of-a-kind items. Fajo had no problem with the morality of Data's imprisonment.
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. You may draw two cards each time you capture a unique personnel, and one card each time one of your Fajo Collection cards or Mona Lisa enters play.

name: Inside Operation
lore: The changeling impersonating Lovok compromised the mission to destroy the Founders' homeworld. His participation in the battle plans led the attacking fleet into a Jem'Hadar ambush.
game_text: Plays at start of ship battle. Each opposing ship and facility in this battle is WEAPONS and SHIELDS -3 if your personnel is infiltrating one of them. Infiltrator exposed.

name: Riker Wil
lore: In 2370, the human William T. Riker accompanied Ro Laren on a clandestine mission to investigate the Maquis. He posed as a Bajoran freedom fighter.

name: Elim
lore: Elim Garak forced himself to interrogate Odo in an attempt to regain favor with his father, Enabran Tain.

name: Odo Founder
lore: Changeling who confused the crew of the U.S.S. Defiant by posing as Odo.

name: Jadzia Dax
lore: Trill. Disregarded her commitments to both Starfleet and Trill custom in order to honor a Klingon blood oath sworn by her symbiont's previous host, Curzon Dax.

name: Kang
lore: Faced Kirk at Beta XII-A. Sword blood oath against the Albino with Kor, Koloth and Curzon Dax to avenge the death of his firstborn son.

name: Koloth
lore: Called d'akturak, "ice man," by Curzon Dax due to his negotiating prowess. Commanded the I.K.C. Gr'oth during the Sherman's Planet sabotage mission in 2267.

name: Kor
lore: Dahar master. Legendary warrior. Former ambassador to Vulcan. Victorious at Klach D'Kel Brakt. Swore blood oath agains the Albino. Sought the Sword of Kahless.

name: La Forge Impersonator
lore: Surgically altered Romulan. In 2367, posed as Geordi La Forge so Taibak could brainwash the real La Forge without raising suspicions.

name: Locutus' Borg Cube
lore: IDENTIFICATION: BORG CUBETASK: Explore galaxy for biological and technological distinctiveness. Assimilate.

name: Kraxon
lore: Cardassian warship sent to intercept the U.S.S. Defiant and the renegade Thomas Riker in 2371.

name: U.S.S. Thunderchild
lore: NCC-63549. Helped lead Starfleet forces against invading Borg cube in 2373. Briefly commanded by Fleet Admiral Shanthi during its shakedown cruise.
game_text: SHIELDS +4 vs. Borg ships and Borg Ship dilemma.

name: I.K.C. Negh'Var
lore: Flagship of the Klingon Defense Force. Commanded by Gowron when first commissioned, and then by Martok during the 2372 invasion of Cardassia.

name: Goraxus
lore: Warbird commanded by Sela. Used to intercept Geordi La Forge's shuttle en route to Risa in 2367, and to mentally reprogram the engineer.
game_text: Download Romulan Ambush

name: Borg Cutting Beam
game_text: If you hit, you may relocate one of target's crew members (random selection; from any one site if on a Nor) to one of your ships in this battle and assimilate that personnel.Hit or Direct hit = Tactic Current.

name: Orb of Wisdom
lore: Acquired by Zek from one of his contacts on Cardassia III. The Grand Nagus used the Orb to contact the Prophets, then sold it to the Bajoran government at a substantial profit.
game_text: Use as Equipment card. Your personnel present are each INTEGRITY +3. Each turn, one of your cards played here plays for free if your Orb personnel present. (Not duplicatable.)

name: Phased Cloaking Device
lore: Phasing cloak prototype created in violation of the Treaty of Algeron, which forbids the Federation from developing cloaking technology. Salvaged from the U.S.S. Pegasus.
game_text: May seed under Pegasus Search. Use as Equipment card. While aboard your ship, that ship has a Phasing Cloak (RANGE +4 while phased).

name: Starry Night
lore: Famous painting by Dutch impressionist Vincent van Gogh. Painted at Saint‑Rémy in 1889. Dubiously owned by Kivas Fajo 477 years later. A highly prized commodity.
game_text: If earned at same location as Quark's Bar, a Trading Post or a homeworld, immediately download here (earn) up to two "use as Equipment card" artifacts. Discard Starry Night.

name: Center of Attention
lore: After Morn faked his own death, Quark "inherited" the Lurian's stolen latinum fortune. Naturally, this made him quite a hit with Morn's former partners in crime.
game_text: Unless 4 SECURITY OR hand weapon and CUNNING>36 OR any Quark present, kills one personnel present (opponent's choice) who has Treachery or Greed. Discard dilemma.

name: Chula: Crossroads
lore: Caught in a game of chula, Deep Space 9 senior officers divided up to explore different paths. Some paths were dead ends, while others led to the next step.
game_text: Immediately probe (then draw probe card):Referee, Barash, Gamma Quadrant, Ferengi: "Stops" two personnel (your choice).Otherwise: "Stops" one personnel (opponent's choice).

name: Chula: The Door
lore: In the Wadi game of chula, participants are confronted with a virtual labyrinth of doorways. A few seem to permit passage arbitrarily, but most remain closed.
game_text: To get past, two personnel must each contribute any one of their attributes to equal a total of 5 or 21. Nullify by placing any doorway out-of-play from hand.

name: Dangerous Liaisons
lore: Quark agreed to provide mercenaries for Rao Vantika's attempted theft of a deuridium shipment. Failure to complete his contract would have been a fatal mistake.
game_text: To get past requires 3 Treachery and Acquisition OR 2 SCIENCE and 2 SECURITY OR Ty Kajada. Nullify by discarding Recruit Mercenaries from hand.

name: Ferengi Bug
lore: Quark attempted to use a Ferengi eavesdropping device to gather information on Shakaar Edon in 2372. He wanted to sell high-level Bajoran political information.
game_text: Unless 3 SECURITY (or Odo) and any tricorder OR 2 FCA present, place atop mission. While in play, your hand is exposed, face up on table.

name: In the Pale Moonlight
lore: In a desperate attempt to spark Romulan participation in the defense of the Alpha Quadrant, Benjamin Sisko enlisted Elim Garak's effective, but questionable, methods.

name: Orion Syndicate Bomb
lore: Typical explosive device. One was hidden in a floor panel of a runabout carrying Quark to testify before a Federation Grand Jury. Odo's attempt to beam it out accelerated its detonation.
game_text: Damages ship unless Transporter Skill OR any Orion Syndicate personnel present. Discard dilemma.

name: Scientific Method
lore: Beverly Crusher scanned Jo'Bril's body for tetryon traces during her 2369 "murder" investigation. Her scientific approach eventually revealed that Jo'Bril had faked his own death.
game_text: To get past requires MEDICAL and 3 SCIENCE.

name: Strange Bedfellows
lore: Dukat's disguise as a Bajoran farmer and seer named Anjohl allowed him to forge an alliance with Winn Adami that was both dangerous and disgusting.
game_text: If a male and female present, lowest INTEGRITY male and lowest INTEGRITY female are "stopped" (discarded if their INTEGRITY numbers are the same).

name: Breen CRM114
lore: Powerful disruptor often brokered by Hagath. Guaranteed to cut through reactive armor up to 15 centimeters and shields up to 4.6 gigajoules. Quick recharge. Expensive, but well worth it.
game_text: Reports to your Breen or arms dealer. At start of battle, kills up to 5 Rogue Borg present. Once each turn, this Away Team may attack a landed ship or facility on same planet (damaged=Tactic Draw).

name: Ferengi Disruptor
lore: Standard-issue hand weapon used by military personnel in the Ferengi Alliance. Provides accuracy and energy output comparable to those of the Starfleet hand phaser.
game_text: Ferengi and Non-Aligned use only. Each of your personnel present is STRENGTH +2. (Cumulative.)

name: Ferengi Disruptor Rifle
lore: Powerful energy weapon. Essential protection for particularly dangerous or unusual missions – such as when rescuing one's moogie from the Dominion.
game_text: Ferengi and Non-Aligned use only. Each of your personnel present is STRENGTH +3, but loses 1 Diplomacy unless aboard your ship. (Cumulative.)

name: Ferengi PADD
lore: Standard Ferengi Personal Access Display Device for computerized information.
game_text: Ferengi use only. Each of your personnel present is CUNNING+2. (Cumulative.)

name: Gold-Pressed Latinum
lore: Valuable liquid latinum encased in relatively worthless gold dust. Standard of exchange throughout the Ferengi Alliance. Typically traded in bars, strips and slips; 1 bar = 20 strips = 2,000 slips.
game_text: Once each turn, on a Trading Post, homeworld or Quark's Bar, you may discard two Latinum (one if your Acquisition present) to download a non-Latinum Equipment card there.

name: Kukalaka
lore: Beloved childhood companion (and first surgical patient) of Julian Bashir. Loaned to, and especially treasured by, Leeta. A timeless symbol of innocence and security.
game_text: Your non-Borg personnel present are each INTEGRITY +2, or +3 if Leeta present. Also, each player is limited to one Brain Drain OR one Going to the Top every turn. (Unique).

name: Scepter of the Grand Nagus
lore: Traditional cane of the Grand Nagus of the Ferengi Alliance. Symbol of his power and authority. The gnarled hardwood shaft is crowned by a nagus head made of gold-pressed latinum.
game_text: Your Nagus present may allow one Rule card to play for free each turn, prevent opponent from nullifying Rule cards here and stun one adversary he just engaged per turn. (Unique.)

name: Small Cloaking Device
lore: Device obtained by Quark. Illegal under Bajoran law. Quark gave it to Natima Lang so she could elude Cardassian authorities, but warned her it would work only for a short time.
game_text: Reports for free if your Smuggling or Acquisition present. While aboard your ship with no staffing requirements, ship has a Cloaking Device. Counts down only when engaged.

name: The Ferengi Rules of Acquisition
lore: Ornate book of 285 sayings, attributed to Grand Nagus Gint, which guide Ferengi commerce. They're really only guidelines; calling them "rules" was just a clever marketing play.
game_text: Once each turn, you may place a Rule card beneath draw deck from hand to draw a card (if your Ferengi is present) or to download a Rule card to hand (if your Nagus is present).

name: 1st Rule of Acquisition
lore: "Once you have their money, you never give it back."
game_text: Seeds or plays on your freighter, transport or Ferengi facility or ship. Gold-Pressed Latinum you download may come from your discard pile. Once per game, you may download to hand one Gold-Pressed Latinum and/or one Ferengi V.I.P.

name: 211th Rule of Acquisition
lore: "Employees are the rungs on the ladder of success – don't hesitate to step on them."

name: 33rd Rule of Acquisition
lore: "It never hurts to suck up to the boss."
game_text: Plays on your Greed personnel at a mission or Borg Only objective opponent completed. Compliment opponent's score. If they say "thank you," score points. If not, draw up to four cards. Discard event. (Limit two per location.)

name: 34th Rule of Acquisition
lore: "War is good for business."
game_text: Plays on your arms dealer or Acquisition personnel. Once every turn, if a non-Rogue-Borg battle was just initiated or opponent's ship was just damaged, download two Gold-Pressed Latinum here (three if an arms dealer) OR draw two cards.

name: 47th Rule of Acquisition
lore: "Don't trust a man wearing a better suit than your own."
game_text: Plays on your Acquisition or Greed personnel. Nullifies all Palor Toff cards. Whenever at same location as any Garak or a personnel who has more Skill Dot icons than this one, may place that personnel atop owner's draw deck; discard event.

name: 59th Rule of Acquisition
lore: "Free advice is seldom cheap."
game_text: Plays on your Nagus. At any time, advise opponent to attempt a specific mission. If opponent does so voluntarily, opponent must first discard two cards from hand and/or top of draw deck and you may draw up to two; discard event.

name: 6th Rule of Acquisition
lore: "Never allow family to stand in the way of opportunity."
game_text: Plays on your Ferengi who has Greed or Treachery; place beneath draw deck another Ferengi present who names (or is named by) this one in lore. Download to Equipment cards or one Ferengi ship here OR draw up to three cards. Discard event.

name: 75th Rule of Acquisition
lore: "Home is where the heart is, but the stars are made of latinum."
game_text: Plays on your Acquisition personnel in their native quadrant. If that personnel helps solve a mission in another quadrant, score points OR download up to five Gold-Pressed Latinum there; discard event. (Once per mission.)

name: Ferengi Outpost
lore: Ferenginar is a rainy, soggy homeworld of the highly capitalistic Ferengi people. The Ferengi Alliance establishes outposts throughout its territory.

name: Tower of Commerce
lore: The Grand Nagus enjoys absolute control over Ferengi business affairs from his Chamber of Petitioners.
game_text: Seeds or plays on Ferenginar. Once per turn, one Ferengi V.I.P., CIVILIAN or Hupyrian OR one HQ card may play for free here. (Not duplicatable.)

name: Continuing Committee
lore: Praetor Neral presides over the Continuing Committee of the Romulan People, the final authority on Romulus.
game_text: Seeds or plays on Romulus. May coexist with Office of the Proconsul. Once per turn, one Tal Shiar personnel OR any Neral may report for free here. (Not duplicatable.)

name: Bodyguards
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. At start of any personnel battle, each of your bodyguards and leaders who has SECURITY in that battle may exclude from battle one of your V.I.P. personnel or CIVILIAN personnel. If you have a non-Borg Leadership personnel or a Defense drone remaining in battle, instead of shuffling your combat pile you may pre-arrange the order in which your personnel will fight. Discard incident.

name: Bribery
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Once each turn, your Smuggling or Greed personnel may discard one of your Gold-Pressed Latinum present to add Ferengi mission icon to your mission there (except Ferenginar) until end of your next turn OR to prevent one entire point loss of up to 9 points just incurred there (discard incident) OR to release (and relocate to that personnel) one of your personnel held captive there.

name: Dabo
game_text: Plays on Quark's Bar. Any player who has a personnel here (except any Quark) may "wager" 1 to 3 cards from discard pile (except Kevin Uxbridge/Amanda Rogers) and probe:Equipment, Event, Skill Dot: Place wager in point area (2 points per card).Otherwise: Place wager out-of-play; if station's controller has any Quark here, for each dabo girl here that player may draw one card OR download one Gold-Pressed Latinum here.

name: Emergency Evacuation
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. If your ship or facility is being destroyed or just encountered Abandon Ship, you may place entire crew under that Abandon Ship dilemma OR download Escape Pod (ignoring Computer Crash ) to save entire crew of ship or facility OR relocate entire crew to a planet at that location. Discard incident after use.

name: HQ: Ferengi Credit Exchange
game_text: Seeds or plays on Ferenginar, Ferengi Trading Post or Quark's Bar. Any player who has Acquisition present may, once each turn, discard up to three Gold-Pressed Latinum cards present. For each one discarded, score 2 points (place that Latinum card in point area), draw one card or place any one card from discard pile beneath draw deck. May be nullified by Subspace Interference.

name: It's Only a Game
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Limits each non-Borg report with crew action to four total personnel/equipment. Limits Red Alert to one Personnel, one Ship and one Equipment card per turn. Limits probing and doubling for Visit Cochrane Memorial to once per game per persona. Also, whenever opponent draws three or more cards in one turn, you may download (even from discard pile) Scorched Hand, ignoring Computer Crash.

name: Protection Racket
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Once each turn, your Ferengi who has Treachery (or your non-Ferengi who has Treachery x2) may "threaten" (place incident on) any non-Borg personnel at this location. Make any request of opponent. Incident nullified if opponent complies. Threatened personnel loses first-listed skill and opponent must probe each turn:'Doorway, Skill Dot: Assassin strikes''. Threated personnel killed.]]]

name: Quark's Isolinear Rods
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. You may ignore each opponent's Computer Crash. Also you may nullify any or all cards preventing you from playing Q's Tent (discard incident after card taken from tent). Once per game, you may download to hand Intermix Ratio, The Big Picture or a non-OFFICER who has Computer Skill x2 (discard incident). Does not count down while you have any Quark in play.

name: Incoming Message - Ferengi
lore: Messages and directives are sent, faster than light, on subspace radio signals amplified by networks of relay stations.

name: Vacuum-Desiccated Remains
lore: When a Ferengi dies, his body is desiccated and apportioned into flat, circular containers to be sold as collectibles. The remains of noteworthy individuals can become quite valuable.
game_text: Once per turn, place out-of-play any Ferengi just killed by your opponent's card. Draw cards and/or download Gold-Pressed Latinum: up to three total if a V.I.P., two otherwise.

name: Collect Sample
lore: Gaseous cloud: Beam volatile sample aboard ship for possible use as a weapon component.

name: Deliver Message
lore: Ferenginar: Convey documents to Grand Nagus Zek on the Ferengi homeworld; beware enemy patrols.

name: Gunrunning
lore: Military checkpoint: Get lethal cargo past patrol ship to conclude lucrative arms deal with local interests.

name: Market Research
lore: Undercommercialized system: Survey remote region; seek out new life and new civilizations to exploit.

name: Runabout Search
lore: Class-L planet: Track distress signal; locate survivors of ship sabotaged by Orion Syndicate.
game_text: If you solve, may download Odo or Quark here.

name: Tulaberry Wine Negotiations
lore: Dosi planet: Meet with aggressive Dosi negotiators to discuss lucrative wine contract and distribution rights.

name: Establish Trade Route
game_text: Seeds or plays on a space mission with a point box that you seeded. You may attempt it used these requirements: Greed + (freighter OR transport OR Ferengi ship + Acquisition x3 + CUNNING>(mission points x2) When you solve mission, you may download Ferengi Trading Post (plus up to two Equipment cards) here; discard objective.

name: Ferengi Conference
game_text: Seeds or plays on Quark's Bar. When you have a Nagus here, you may download up one copy of the 75th Rule of Acquisition to each of your other Ferengi here who has Acquisition. Discard objective. OR Plays on your Nagus at Quark's Bar or aboard a Ferengi facility. Download to that Nagus one Hupyrian or any number of Ferengi CIVILIANs with up to 11 total Skill Dot icons. Discard objective.

name: Forced-Labor Camp
game_text: Seeds or plays on Cardassia IV, Ligos VII or your planet that has Geology or Archaeology as a requirement. Your Cardassian and Ferengi personnel may attempt mission. On Cardassia IV or Ligos VII, changes your mission requirements to these: SECURITY + Geology + STRENGTH>(mission points x2) After you solve, while you escort a captive on this planet, you may draw one additional card at end of each turn.

name: Leeta
lore: Bajoran dabo girl. Formed the Guild of Restaurant and Casino Employees with Rom. Amateur sociologist. Was formerly separated from Julian Bashir on Risa in 2373.

name: Mardah
lore: Bajoran entomology student. Dabo girl. Orphaned by Cardassians. Romantically involved with Jake Sisko. Accepted to the science academy on Regulus III.

name: Benil
lore: Cardassian Gul of the Eighth Order. Intercepted the U.S.S. Defiant en route to Cardassia Prime. Covert arms dealer with suspected Kressari connections.

name: Lemec
lore: Gul in command of the Reklar. Clashed with Captain Edward Jellico over troop and ship movements along the Federation-Cardassian border.

name: Deyos
lore: Vorta in charge of Internment Camp 371. Responsible for training and equipping Jem'Hadar troops. Accepts nothing less than perfect obedience.

name: Edan'Atal
lore: Representative of Jem'Hadar assigned to guard Dominion operations on Cardassia Prime. Fourth. Bred in the Alpha Quadrant.

name: Ikat'ika
lore: Jem'Hadar First under Deyos. Leader of detachment assigned to Internment Camp 371. Fought Worf as part of training exercise. Skilled combatant.

name: Inglatu
lore: Typical male Dosi. Violent and impatient negotiator. Threatened to kill Quark because of the Ferengi's annoying tenacity.

name: Krajensky Founder
lore: The changeling appearing as Ambassador Krajensky seized the U.S.S. Defiant in an effort to start a war between the Federation and the Tzenkethi.

name: Ambassador Krajensky
lore: Starfleet dignitary. Scoffs at rumors of his inability to form lasting relationships. Spends much of his free time on Risa.

name: Elizabeth Lense
lore: Female chief medical officer of the U.S.S. Lexington. Julian Bashir's medical school rival. Able to distinguish a preganglionic fiber from a postganglionic nerve.

name: George Primmin
lore: Starfleet security officer assigned to Deep Space 9. Annoyed Odo. Discovered a subspace crossover shunt placed on station by the criminal Rao Vantika in 2369.

name: Nog
lore: Dedicated, hardworking ensign. The first Ferengi in Starfleet. Friend of Jake. Briefly served as chief engineer of U.S.S. Valiant under Captain Watters.

name: Berik
lore: Officer serving Lurin. Participated in the failed takeover attempt of the U.S.S. Enterprise. Blamed Morta for failing to seize control of the main computer.

name: Birta
lore: Ferengi bureaucrat stationed on Ferenginar. Point of contact for offworlders. Informed Jean-Luc Picard that Bok had bought his way out of Rog Prison.

name: Bractor
lore: DaiMon in command of the Kreechta. Observed war games between the U.S.S. Enterprise and the U.S.S. Hathaway. Attempted to claim the latter as salvage.

name: Brunt
lore: Liquidator with the Ferengi Commerce Authority. Rude. Arrogant. Corrupt. Despised and envied by Ferengi everywhere. Strives to ruin Quark.

name: Dr. Borts
lore: Representative Ferengi scientist. Helped Lurin invade the U.S.S. Enterprise. Paid more attention to Dr. Crusher's molecular models than to his guard duties.

name: Frool
lore: Typical Ferengi waiter. Serves his employees as well as can be expected for a young, impatient, aspiring opportunist.

name: Gaila
lore: Arms dealer. Owed his cousin Quark a shuttle. Made good on his debt, but booby-trapped the ship. Involved with Hagath. Helped rescue Ishka from the Dominion.

name: Goss
lore: Uninvited participant in the 2366 Barzan wormhole negotiations. DaiMon. Conspired with Devinoni Ral to deceive. Preoccupied with getting his own chair.

name: Gral
lore: Aggressive Ferengi opportunist. Diplomatically, but insistently, threatened Quark with a protection racket while Quark was briefly serving as the Grand Nagus.

name: Grand Nagus Gint
lore: The first Grand Nagus. Credited with the Rules of Acquisition. Appeared in Quark's dream; looked a lot like Rom. Told Quark the Rules were a marketing play.

name: Grand Nagus Zek
lore: Aging financial and political leader of the Ferengi Alliance. Romantically – and secretly – involved with Ishka. Admits he's not as greedy as he used to be.

name: Ishka
lore: "Moogie" to Quark and Rom. Financial genius. Wears clothes. Earns profit. Secretly helps Zek run his empire.

name: Kazago
lore: First officer. Shocked by DaiMon Bok's free gift of the derelict U.S.S. Stargazer to the human Picard. Placed Bok under arrest for using an illegal thought maker.

name: Krax
lore: Son of Grand Nagus Zek. Missed his chance to show his father he could be a good nagus when he tried to seize power quickly, rather than accumulate it quietly.

name: Krunk
lore: Transporter technician under the command of Lurin. Guarded a U.S.S. Enterprise transporter room during his DaiMon's unsuccessful takeover attempt.

name: Leck
lore: Professional assassin called an "eliminator." Doesn't crave latinum, but doesn't like being cheated. Brunt called him a psychopath during the 2374 Ishka rescue.

name: Letek
lore: Typical first officer in the Ferengi Alliance. Serves under Taar. Tried to find favor with Portal 63 on an ancient Tkon planet.

name: Lurin
lore: DaiMon who illegally mined vendarite on Ligos VII. Tried to take over the U.S.S. Enterprise. Would've succeeded, too, if it weren't for those meddling kids.

name: Maihar'du
lore: Hupyrian servant. Grand Nagus Zek's bodyguard, pilot and handkerchief valet. Took a vow to speak only to his master. As loyal as he is silent.

name: Morta
lore: Security officer. Led an assault team that boarded the U.S.S. Enterprise on Lurin's order. Befuddled by Commander Riker's bogus computer lesson.

name: Nava
lore: Typical Ferengi entrepreneur. Took over the Arcybite gouge-mining refineries in the Clarius system. Plans to introduce synthehol to the Gamma Quadrant.

name: Nibor
lore: Security guard aboard the Krayton. Served with Tog during the Lwaxana Troi incident. Played chess with William Riker. Isn't bragging about the outcome.

name: Nilva
lore: Typical member of Ferengi Commerce Authority. One of 432 FCA commissioners. Chairman of Slug-o-Cola, "the slimiest cola in the galaxy." Lusts after Lumba.

name: Omag
lore: Ferengi arms dealer. DaiMon. Glutton. Always requests that Amarie play Melor Famagal. Referred to as "the fat Ferengi" by the Qualor II locals.

name: Par Lenor
lore: Emissary of the Ferengi Trade Mission. Sabotaged his own ship to force a rescue by the U.S.S. Enterprise, creating the opportunity to bribe Ambassador Briam.

name: Pel
lore: Waiter. Female. Used synthetic lobes to appear male. Ware clothes and sought profit in violation of Ferengi law. Romantically involved with Quark – briefly.

name: Prak
lore: Representative DaiMon in the Ferengi Alliance. In exchange for repairs to his ship, provided sensor log readings on missing U.S.S. Fleming to Jean-Luc Picard.

name: Qol
lore: Assistant to Par Lenor. Sneaked into a cargo bay on the U.S.S. Enterprise to scan an empathic metamorph. Accidentally triggered premature emergence.

name: Quark
lore: Bartender and proprietor of Quark's Bar, Grill, Gaming House and Holosuite Arcade. Longtime nuisance to Odo.

name: Solok
lore: Typical DaiMon. Like most Ferengi, easily manipulated by any female who tickles his lobes. Smuggled humans to the Cardassian planet Celtris III in 2369.

name: Sovak
lore: DaiMon who sought the Tox Uthat. Followed Vash to Risa, only to be deceived by the treacherous human female and facially assaulted by Jean-Luc Picard.

name: Taar
lore: Representative Ferengi DaiMon. First member of the Ferengi Alliance to make visual contact with humans. Claimed he sought "only what is equitable."

name: Tog
lore: DaiMon. Presented flowers to Lwaxana Troi. Abducted her from Betazed, hoping to exploit her empathic skills during negotiations. She called him a "toad-faced troll."

name: Tol
lore: Unusually calm and intelligent Ferengi. Science officer aboard Bok's marauder. Questioned his commander's actions in the Jason Vigo incident.

name: Rom
lore: Brilliant yet befuddled Ferengi engineer. Works for the Bajorans aboard Deep Space 9. Quark's brother. Nog's father. Gaila's cousin. Has a crush on Leeta.

name: Margh
lore: Veteran Klingon warrior. Achieved many glorious victories. Trained in battlefield medicine. Former member of Gowron's elite High Council honor guards.

name: Arandis
lore: Chief facilitator of entire Temtibi Lagoon. Welcomes all to Risa. Curzon Dax's last romantic encounter.

name: Calandra
lore: Attractive young vocalist and part-time nurse. Known as one of "Omag's girls." Overlooks the fat Ferengi's disgusting behavior because of his generosity to her.

name: Hagath
lore: Humanoid arms dealer. Associate of Quark's cousin Gaila. Ruthless. Treats his business associates like family – until they cross him.

name: Krozh
lore: Typical Nausicaan bodyguard. Protects FCA liquidator Brunt. Doesn't mind working for Ferengi cowards as long as the money is good.

name: Morn
lore: Lurian. Freighter captain. Frequent patron of Quark's. Part of the infamous Lissepian Mother's Day Heist. Hides a small fortune in latinum in his second stomach.

name: Kasidy Yates
lore: Freighter captain for Bajoran Ministry of Commerce. Smuggled weapons for the Maquis in 2372. Loves baseball. Romantically involved with Benjamin Sisko.

name: Aluura
lore: Humanoid dabo girl. In three months she didn't spill a drink, mix up a food order or short-change a bill. Actually liked by other dabo girls – and even the Ferengi waiters.

name: Patahk
lore: Commander of the Pi. Rescued from Galorndon Core by the U.S.S. Enterprise crew. Refused to "pollute his body" with an infusion of Worf's Klingon ribosomes.

name: Senator Cretak
lore: Female Romulan. Kimara Cretak was liaison to Deep Space 9 in 2375. Coordinated a fleet of warbirds attempting to deliver weapons to a Bajoran moon.

name: Naprem
lore: Bird-of-Prey commanded by Dukat. Commandeered near the Cardassian outpost on Korma. Named for Tora Ziyal's mother. Carried Jodmos to Ty'Gokor in 2373.

name: Patrol Ship
lore: Common patrol vessel of the Cardassian Union. Uses the same hull as the Cardassian shuttlecraft, but boosts a much higher performance profile.

name: Karemman Vessel
lore: The Karemma conduct trade operations for the Dominion. Their vessels can be found throughout the Gamma Quadrant. Hanok commanded one.

name: U.S.S. Sao Paulo
lore: Replacement for the U.S.S. Defiant. NCC-75633. Briefly commanded by Admiral Ross during delivery to Deep Space 9. Captained by Benjamin Sisko.

name: B'rel
lore: Old surplus Klingon Bird-of-Prey. Much smaller than K'Vort-class ships. Ferengi bought this one to support a covert vendorite mining operation on Ligos VII.

name: D'Kora Marauder
lore: Ferengi military vessel. Standard D'Kora spaceframe optimized for battle readiness. Most DaiMons enjoy the raw power but lament the minimal cargo space.

name: D'Kora Transport
lore: Ferengi trade vessel. Same spaceframe as the D'Kora-class marauder, but has a smaller crew complement and devotes for more internal volume to cargo capacity.

name: Ferengi Shuttle
lore: Common shuttlecraft of Ferengi design. Dr. Arridor commanded one.

name: Krayton
lore: Marauder commanded by Tog. Briefly imprisoned Lwaxana Troi, whom Tog had abducted from Betazed following the 2366 Trade Agreements Conference.

name: Kreechta
lore: Ferengi marauder. Under the command of Bractor in 2365, interrupted a mysterious battle between the Federation starships Enterprise and Hathaway.

name: Quark's Treasure
lore: Briefly captained by Quark. Faster than a Romulan interceptor. A belated delivery from its former captain, Gaila, who had owed Quark a ship for some time.

name: Jovis
lore: Zibalian transport and merchant vessel commanded by Kivas Fajo. Houses his collection of rare and one-of-a-kind objects. Used to imprison Data in 2366.
game_text: Once per game, may capture an Android on an undocked ship here.Download Kivas Fajo

name: Apnex
lore: Named for a sea on Romulus. Has a cloaking device prototype based on a phase inverter. Commanded by Mirok after the death of the ship's captain.

name: Cargo Bay
game_text: Smuggling, Acquisition and Non-Aligned Navigation personnel may report here (or download here in place of a normal card play; player draws no cards that turn). Once each turn, if a freighter, transport or Ferengi ship's crew member completes a "cargo run" (brings a non-weapon Equipment card here from another facility), for each mission passed (except starting and ending locations) owner may draw a card or download a Gold-Pressed Latinum here. (Once per game per Equipment card title.)

name: Quark's Bar
game_text: Morn and Ferengi may report here. Once each turn, a bartender, a dabo girl, a waiter, any Quark or any Rom may report here for free (or download here in place of a normal card play; player draws no cards that turn). Any player who has Morn unopposed here may draw an additional card at end of each turn. Any player who kills any waiters or dabo girls here in battle must discard two cards for each. Ferengi ships may report, dock, undock and repair at this Nor.

name: Ferengi Energy Weapon
game_text: ATTACK bonus +1 if you have a Ferengi ship firing.Hit = Tactic Draw. Direct hit = Tactic Draw Tactic Draw.

name: Plasma Energy Burst
game_text: ATTACK bonus +4 and DEFENSE bonus +2 if you have a D'Kora-class ship firing.Hit = Tactic Current Tactic Draw. Direct hit = Tactic Current Tactic Draw Tactic Draw. Otherwise, causes electromagnetic disruptions (Tactic Current).

name: U.S.S. Jupiter
lore: Captained by Satelk. Helped U.S.S. Enterprise defend timeship Premonition from a Borg attack in 2376. Armed with experimental Chain Reaction Pulsar weapon.

name: Vedek Dax
lore: Trill with symbiont. Jadzia Dax posed as a Vedek to sneak Kira Nerys past members of the Circle and into the Chamber of Ministers. Joked about keeping the nose.

name: Legate Damar
lore: Damar became legate in 2374. Weary of Dominion rule, he led the resistance effort to free Cardassia in 2375. Rumored to have secret mountain stronghold.

name: Bashir Founder
lore: Changeling posing as Julian Bashir. Tried to destroy an entire fleet by causing the Bajoran sun to go nova.

name: Luther Sloan
lore: Section 31 operative. Secretive man with seemingly limitless access. Attempted to recruit Julian Bashir. Involved in infecting Odo with the changeling virus.

name: Jodmos
lore: The human Benjamin Sisko assumed the identity of Jodmos, son of Kobor, to help rid the Klingon Empire of a suspected changeling at Ty'Gokor.

name: Koval
lore: Chairman of the Tal Shiar. Seeks appointment to the Continuing Committee. Suffers from Tuvan Syndrome. Conspired with Sloan to bring down Senator Cretak.

name: Orb of Time
lore: Bajoran Orb. Transported U.S.S. Defiant across time and space to encounter starship Enterprise. Also used by Kira Nerys to travel back to the Cardassian occupation to learn of her mother's fate.
game_text: Use as Equipment card. Once each turn, your ship or Away Team (if this Orb and your Orb personnel present) may time travel (except to board opponent's ship or outpost).

name: Chula: The Drink
lore: One chula puzzle places the players in a cocktail party filled with poison gas. The antidote awaits the one who is clever (or foolish) enough to take a chance on a mysterious beverage.
game_text: To get past, four personnel present (random selection) must be "tested". All four are "stopped" unless one has CUNNING<6 OR CUNNING>9.

name: Chula: The Way Home
lore: Near the end of their chula experience, three Deep Space 9 senior staff members were enticed to follow an image of Julian Bashir. He claimed to have found the way home.
game_text: To get past, three personnel present (random selection) are chosen. Opponent may relocate one to Quark's Bar or your facility if the other two have combined INTEGRITY<15.

name: Executive Authorization
lore: Before Benjamin Sisko and Admiral Leyton could implement extreme security measures on Earth in 2372, they had to obtain authorization from Federation president Jaresh-Inyo.
game_text: To get past requires a President, High Council Leader, General, Legate, Chancellor, Proconsul, Chairman, Intendant, Minister, Kai, Founder, Nagus, Governor, Queen, counterpart, or PADD.

name: Ferengi Infestation
lore: In anticipation of a prisoner exchange, a Dominion delegation boarded Empok Nor in 2374. They found that Ferengi were already entrenched there.
game_text: Opponent may download up to two male Ferengi to a facility at this location (or up to six if facility is Empok Nor). To get past requires 2 SECURITY and CUNNING>50.

name: Lineup
lore: After a bar fight with Klingons on Station K-7, Captain Kirk ordered a lineup. No crewman claimed responsibility for starting the brawl, but none pointed the finger at Mr. Scott, either.
game_text: To get past requires four personnel present (random selection) to "form a lineup." All four are "stopped" unless one has INTEGRITY<5 OR INTEGRITY>8.

name: Oops!
lore: In 2374, an ill-prepared band of Ferengi arranged a prisoner exchange aboard Empok Nor. Their profound lack of competence made the process even more difficult than they had expected.
game_text: Unless Leadership present, kills one personnel (random selection) and "stops" all other present. To get past requires three Staff OR three Defense drones OR Nog.

name: Palukoo
lore: Large spider-like creature inhabiting the Bajoran moors. One-time food source for Resistance Fighters. Caused Dax concern, since Trill/symbiont biochemistry cannot tolerate insect bites.
game_text: Unless Resistance OR ANIMAL present, "bites" a non-android (random selection). If Trill with symbiont, dies now (discard dilemma); otherwise, disabled until countdown expires.

name: Q Gets the Point
lore: Q, stripped of his powers, helped the U.S.S. Enterprise crew develop a plan to save Bre'el IV from destruction. Guinan used a simple serving fork to verify his claim of mortality.
game_text: To get past requires 2 Treachery or Mortal Q, but one such personnel (opponent's choice) is "forked" ("stopped") if opponent has any Guinan in play. Nullified by any Guinan.

name: Storage Compartment Door
game_text: Place one atop Tribble side deck during the seed phase. Side deck is now open and in play. Once each turn, you may draw up to 3 cards from side deck, then play or discard each. OR Stock in deck and play (once each turn) to download from your Tribble side deck one Trouble or Tribble card , or to nullify any card that is closing another Storage Compartment Door; then discard doorway.

name: Classic Communicator
lore: Typical 23rd century personal communications device. Features flip-up antenna grid and multi-band tuning. Such equipment was developed by many races.

name: Classic Medical Tricorder
lore: General-purpose medical reference and diagnostic tool. Representative of devices used in the latter half of the 23rd century. Such equipment was developed by many races.

name: Classic Tricorder
lore: Multipurpose hand-held device typical of those employed by many races in the late 23rd century. Jadzia Dax said of this one, "I love classic 23rd century design."
game_text: Your Original Series personnel present who have ENGINEER or SCIENCE classification all add ENGINEER OR SCIENCE OR Geology OR Physics. (May re-select once each turn.)

name: Classic Type II Phaser
lore: Starfleet personal defense and security weapon. Styling is typical of those used in the late 23rd and early 24th centuries. The pistol grip cradles and amplifies a Type I Phaser.
game_text: Federation use only. Each of your Original Series personnel present is STRENGTH +2 (cumulative). Each of your Original Series leaders present adds SECURITY.

name: VR Headset
lore: Standard visual interface used by the Dominion. Virtual-reality eyepiece facilitates face-to-face communications and provides an unobstructed 360-by-360 view outside the ship.
game_text: Each VR Headset aboard your Dominion ship allows one Vorta, Jem'Hadar or Cardassian present to enhance WEAPONS and SHIELDS +1 and (if Vorta) to serve as matching commander.

name: 62nd Rule of Acquisition
lore: "The riskier the road, the greater the profit."
game_text: Plays on your unattempted mission. Nullified if you begin an attempt with <3 (or >7) personnel, or if you play (or have played) Scan or Full Planet Scan. If you solve, score points; opponent loses points (discard event).

name: Organian Peace Treaty
lore: Pacifistic energy beings known as Organians imposed upon the United Federation of Planets and the Klingon Empire the treaty that those warring factions were unable to forge themselves.
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Your Federation- and Klingon-affiliation cards that have Original Series icons may mix and cooperate. (Immune to The Devil.)

name: Subspace Transporter
lore: Bok beamed to and from the U.S.S. Enterprise using a subspace transporter that forced his body into a state of quantum flux. Though dangerous, such devices have greatly extended range.
game_text: Plays on your ship. Each turn, ship may beam one of your Treachery personnel to and/or from anywhere at same or adjacent location. Nullified only by Subspace Interference.

name: Temporal Investigations
lore: The Federation Department of Temporal Investigations regulates and assesses possible damage to the timeline caused by time travel. They're never short of work.
game_text: Plays on table. Once every turn, if opponent reports an Alternate personnel or ship to Alpha Quadrant spaceline, you may draw one card OR download Lucsly and/or Dulmer.

name: Treaty: Cardassian/Bajoran
lore: In 2371, the Bajoran and Cardassian peoples finally began to put their long conflict behind them, with the signing of a peace treaty between Legate Turrel and the newly elected Kai Winn.
game_text: Plays on table (for free if you have Bareil Antos, Kai Winn, or Turrel in play). Your Cardassian and Bajoran affiliations recognize this treaty. They can now mix and cooperate.

name: Treaty: Romulan/Bajoran
lore: After the Romulan Star Empire's entry into the Dominion war in 2374, Senator Cretak established a Romulan military presence on Deep Space 9 – and a fragile trust with Colonel Kira Nerys.
game_text: Plays on table (for free if you have Colonel Kira or Senator Cretak in play). Your Romulan and Bajoran affiliations recognize this treaty. They can now mix and cooperate.

name: Deep Space Station K-7
lore: Federation frontier station, circa mid-2260s. Consists mostly of fabrication facilities and storage units.
game_text: Plays at 2267 Sherman's Planet; may be used by all players' compatible cards. Once per turn, one Original Series card reporting at this location may report for free. (Not duplicatable.)

name: Chain Reaction Ricochet
game_text: '''Seeds or plays on table. When your Chain Reaction Pulsar hits (but does not destroy) a ship, after applying damage it "ricochets" to other opposing ships present (except those already damaged this battle) in the order of your choice. Second ship's damage = Tactic Draw, third = Tactic Draw Tactic Draw, and so on, until one is destroyed. Discard incident.

name: Homefront
game_text: Seeds or plays on homeworld. In place of a normal card play, a SECURITY personnel matching homeworld's affiliation may download here (owner draws no cards that turn). No player may attempt mission or use headquarters game text here unless they have 4 SECURITY on planet. OR Plays on table. Your personnel who have infiltration icons may report (for free) on homeworlds those icons match.

name: HQ: Orbital Weapons Platform
game_text: Plays on any homeworld. Each time opponent initiates battle here against your ship or facility matching this homeworld's affiliation, just after it is targeted each of your Orbital Weapons Platforms here may "fire upon" an opposing ship present.
