lore: Prototype Starfleet vessel, NX-59650. Boasts ablative armor, regenerative shielding, and multivector assault mode. Captured by Romulans during a test flight.
game_text: May download Multivector Assault Mode when in battle.

name: U.S.S. Prometheus
lore: Prototype Starfleet vessel, NX-59650. Boasts ablative armor, regenerative shielding, and multivector assault mode. Captured by Romulans during a test flight.
game_text: May download Multivector Assault Mode when in battle.

name: Hunting Vessel
lore: Small ship usually manned by a hunting pair. Often travels in groups like that which subdued Voyager in 2374. Its monotanium armor scatters enemy targeting scanners.
game_text: X=7+number of your other staffed Hirogen ships here.

name: Venatic Hunter
lore: Large ship shunned by most hunters – there is a blind spot in its engines' ion wake, and its heavy armaments reduce the challenge of a hunt. Netek commanded one.

name: Kazon Fighter
lore: Small fighter based on same design as the larger Raider. Karden commanded one when battling to earn his name.
game_text: May report for free aboard your Kazon Raider if no ships aboard.

name: I.K.C. Voq'leng
lore: 23th-century battle cruiser. Believing the Empire had lost its way, the original crew set out over a century ago from the Alpha Quadrant on a quest to find the Kuvah'Magh.

name: Liberty
lore: Maquis ship commanded by Captain Chakotay in 2371. 30-year-old vessel – with a 39-year-old engine that has been rebuilt and modified many times over.
game_text: Your Maquis may report aboard. May be your seed at Caretaker's Array.

name: The Think Tank's Ship
lore: Advanced ship boasting technology designed by its crew, including a neutronium alloy hull, isomorphic projectors, and subspace cloaking device. Commanded by Kurros.

name: U.S.S. Dauntless
lore: Unique ship constructed and commanded by Arturis. Equipped with an operational quantum slipstream drive. Designed to appear as an experimental Starfleet vessel.
game_text: May be fully staffed by Arturis.

name: U.S.S. Dauntless
lore: Unique ship constructed and commanded by Arturis. Equipped with an operational quantum slipstream drive. Designed to appear as an experimental Starfleet vessel.
game_text: May be fully staffed by Arturis.

name: The City of B'hala
lore: 20,000-year-old depiction of an ancient Bajoran city. Among the most revered icons of their faith. Some thought B'hala a legend until this painting helped The Emissary find its underground ruins.
game_text: May seed only at Bajor. Use as Equipment card. If present where attempting a Bajoran mission, encounter seed cards in reverse order. (Immune to Disruptor Overload.)

name: Alice
lore: Alien shuttle with an interface that restructures its pilot's neural pathways. Manifested in Tom Paris' mind as an Academy crush, forcing him to take the ship to her particle fountain "home."
game_text: Unless 2 Computer Skill and Biology present, personnel with most Navigation (opponent's choice if tie or none) is captured. Discard dilemma.

name: Chula: Echoes
lore: The echoing voice of the "fallen" Julian Bashir attempted to separate Sisko, Dax, and Kira before they reached the final challenge in their game of chula.
game_text: To get past, three personnel present (random selection) are chosen. If the highest CUNNING among them is odd, all three are "stopped."

name: Chula: Trickery
lore: Most chula puzzles play upon a participant's initial instincts – open doors are not always to be taken. Those who remember lessons from earlier shaps will fare better in the endgame.
game_text: Opponent conceals your personnel, randomly selects one, and recites their attribute numbers. Unless you can name the selected personnel, all are "stopped." Discard dilemma.

name: Cytoplasmic Life-Form
lore: Even a knowledge as vast as The Doctor's has limitations. In 2375, he called upon a holographic "consultant" to assist in removing a parasitic alien that had attacked B'Elanna Torres.
game_text: Unless 3 Exobiology present, place on mission. Each of its skill requirements must be met by a different personnel when solving it.

name: Dejaren
lore: Alien hologram with a deranged hatred of organic life. Murdered all the filthy animals aboard his ship, then attacked The Doctor and B'Elanna Torres when they responded to his distress call.
game_text: Two personnel (one Hologram and one non-Hologram) are killed (random selection) if their individual CUNNING<9. To get past requires 2 Computer Skill remaining.

name: Emergent Life-Form
lore: An emerging intelligence seized control of the Enterprise in 2370 to seek out particles it needed to evolve. The crew interacted with it on the holodeck, helping to find this nourishment more quickly.
game_text: Place on ship. Now and start of each turn, opponent may move ship to another location (using its RANGE). If ship has Holodeck, cure with 2 ENGINEER and Astrophysics aboard.

name: Primitive Humanoids
lore: Humanoids inhabiting a desolate planet captured Neelix and Kes while the two crewmen were searching for food. The cave-dwellers particularly like Kes' golden locks.
game_text: Unless 2 Leadership and Anthropology present, place two Away Team members (random selection) with dilemma atop mission until solved (or planet assimilated).

name: Talosian Cage
lore: Telepathic aliens with the power to create illusory worlds, often based on the memories of life-forms they've captured. Starfleet General Order 7 forbids contact with their homeworld, Talos IV.
game_text: Unless 3 Empathy OR Christopher Pike present, opponent may choose to discard two females (random selection) OR male with most Skill Dot icons. Discard dilemma.

name: The Clown: Guillotine
lore: Though The Clown existed only through the minds linked to his system, he was willing to execute one to ensure the obedience of the others, perpetuating his role as fear personified.
game_text: Unless 2 Diplomacy present, kills one personnel (random selection) and "stops" each personnel whose total attributes are lower than killed personnel until end of your next turn.

name: The Clown: Playing Doctor
lore: Linked directly to the minds of his "guests," The Clown could use their deepest fears to torment them. The Doctor's timely arrival spared Harry Kim a violent reenactment of a childhood trauma.
game_text: One personnel (random selection) and all others present who have the same first-listed skill are killed (only "stopped" if a Hologram personnel present).

name: Your Galaxy Is Impure
lore: The genetic density of Species 8472 is superior to all known forms of life. Any wound inflicted by them will spread infection throughout a victim's body, consuming it from the inside out.

name: '45 Dom Perignon
lore: Champagne of a respected 20th-century vintage. Traditionally used to christen new ships. In the holographic world of Secret Agent Julian Bashir, also serves as an effective hand weapon.
game_text: May discard to download a unique ship to replace (discard) your Universal ship of same class here. Once per battle, your personnel present may stun an adversary they just engaged.

name: Ablative Armor
lore: Early 25th-century technology brought from an alternate future to the 2377 by Admiral Janeway. Quickly adapted for use on Voyager, enabling it to withstand the attack of a Borg cube.
game_text: While aboard your ship or facility, opponent's ATTACK total must be more than double that ship or facility's DEFENSE total to score a hit, and more than triple to score a direct hit.

name: Satan's Robot
lore: Robotic minion of Chaotica. Warns of invaders and deals with intruders. Nearly conquered the world in the final chapter of one of The Adventures of Captain Proton.
game_text: Participates in battle like a personnel; has NO STRENGTH vs. a Borg or android adversary, otherwise STRENGTH=8. May capture any female or Hologram adversary it stuns. (Unique.)

name: Bynars Data Transfer
lore: A star in the Bynars' system went nova in 2364. Only their expertise with computers allowed them to transfer information from their main computer in time to save their world.
game_text: Plays on table. Glance at the top five cards of your draw deck. Place them in any order on top of and/or beneath your draw deck, then place event beneath draw deck.

name: Dominion War Efforts
lore: The Dominion has the ability to produce Jem'Hadar in massive numbers with incredible ease. Losses taken in their war with the Alpha Quadrant meant as little to them as their Cardassian allies.
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Your Assign Support Personnel card is not discarded when used to download a Dominion or Cardassian "support personnel." (Immune to Kevin Uxbridge.)

name: Ferengi Financial Data Net
lore: Galactic service providing up-to-the-second reports on market fluctuations, currency values, and commodity prices – all for a reasonable usage fee. Essential for any serious entrepreneur.
game_text: Plays to discard your hand. Draw a card for each unique Ferengi Greed personnel you have in play. Discard event.

name: Holo-Projectors
lore: Technology which the escaped Hirogen holograms hoped to use to establish a permanent home planet. B'Elanna Torres helped Kejal bring the device online.

name: Oo-mox
lore: The bestseller Oo-mox for Fun and Profit guides a female around the highly erogenous Ferengi ear, from the tympanic tickle and eustachian tube rub to the infamous auditory canal nibble.
game_text: Plays on table, "stopping" all male Ferengi in play. Until countdown expires, doubles regular skills of all male Ferengi in play, and they are attributes all +2.

name: Transwarp Hub
lore: Identification: TRANSWARP HUBTask: Dispatch Borg vessels throughout the galaxy.
game_text: Seeds or plays at any nebula. Once each turn, your ship may move from here to any Transwarp Network Gateway, or vice versa.

name: Holoprogram: 221B Baker Street
game_text: Seeds or plays on your ship or facility with a Holodeck. In place of your normal card play, you may download Sherlock Holmes (or any personnel with his name in lore) aboard. OR Seeds or plays on table. Once each turn, you may place a personnel here from hand. Personnel placed here add Hologram icon to your copies of same personnel in play. You may discard any cards placed here at any time.

name: Holoprogram: Deadwood
game_text: Seeds or plays on your ship with a Holodeck. Sheriff Worf and Deputy Rozhenko may report aboard. If both aboard: location here is span+X for opponent (where X=number of your SECURITY personnel aboard, maximum 4), opponent must have more SECURITY here than you to initiate battle here, and, once each turn, Sheriff Worf may nullify any dilemma requiring SECURITY he just encountered here.

name: Holoprogram: Noah's Mountain Retreat
game_text: Seeds or plays on any ship or facility with a Holodeck. You may report Secret Agent Julian Bashir (or any personnel with his name in lore) aboard. In place of your normal card play, you may download such a personnel aboard. Also, if your Transporter Skill aboard, at start of your turn you may replace (discard) your Dr. Noah (or personnel with his name in lore) present by downloading a version of same persona.

page_title: Holoprogram: The Office of Dixon Hill (HA)
name: Holoprogram: The Office of Dixon Hill
base_name: Holoprogram: The Office of Dixon Hill
game_text: Seeds or plays on your ship with a Holodeck. In place of a card draw, you may download Felix Leech aboard. Also, your Cyrus Redblock may report aboard and, if he is aboard, once each turn you may request "the item." Place a card from hand face down on table. Opponent must choose: you may play it for free and draw a card OR you must place it out-of-play and score 5 points.

name: In the Zone
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. If a non-Borg player scores more than 50 points during a single turn (including this turn), those points in excess of 50 do not count toward winning. While your score is exactly 50 points, each of your ships has double RANGE and SHIELDS. Also, nullifies End Transmission and Preparation, and each player may call "Devidian Door" only during their turn (and only once per turn).

name: Jem'Hadar Shrouding
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. During your turn, you may place here one or two Jem'Hadar from hand or in play, then draw a card. (These Jem'Hadar are not in play.) OR Plays once every turn (for free) on an opponent's Away Team (unless it is on a homeworld). Initiate battle against that Away Team by playing up to an equal number of personnel to it from your Jem'Hadar Shrouding on table. Discard incident.

name: Tongo
game_text: Plays on table. Once each turn, you may declare a move from the list below. Each player simultaneously reveals a bet from hand (a personnel card; yours must be Ferengi). Player with highest total attributes on bet is winner.Acquire. Winner: discard bet, then draw up to two cards.''Confront. Winner: report bet. Loser: place bet on draw deck.Evade.'' Winner: place bet under draw deck. Loser: discard bet.

name: White Deprivation
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. At start of every player's turn, all of that player's Ketracel White personnel present together must battle (and stun or mortally wound when able) opposing non-changelings present, or (if none) any non-changelings present, or (if none) each other (split randomly into two equal groups). Also, one Ketracel White personnel in each of that player's crews and Away Teams dies (random selection).

name: All Threes
lore: While trapped in a temporal causality loop, Data's dealing at the regular poker game was influenced by a posthypnotic suggestion sent from an earlier repetition of events.
game_text: Plays once each turn to reveal two sets of three cards from top of your draw deck. Take one set into hand; discard the other (opponent's choice unless you have any Data in play).

name: Data, Keep Dealing
lore: Data could shuffle playing cards as if they were isolinear chips removed by an intoxicated engineer. Will Riker often quipped, "Sometimes I wonder if he's stacking the deck."

page_title: I'm a Doctor, Not a Bartender (HA)
name: I'm a Doctor, Not a Bartender
base_name: I'm a Doctor, Not a Bartender
lore: Though happy to celebrate Kes' second birthday, The Doctor's mood soured when he became trapped in the Chez Sandrine holoprogram during an encounter with a spatial distortion ring.
game_text: Adds Anthropology to one MEDICAL personnel until end of turn. OR Downloads a bartender to replace (discard) your MEDICAL personnel in play (or vice versa).

name: I've Been Waiting for You
lore: Upon learning of Quark's plan to feature her in a lascivious holoscenario, Kira Nerys enlisted Odo's help in making a small change to the program. The client got far more than he paid for.

name: Remember the Alamo
lore: Miles O'Brien's fascination with the famous 1836 battle led him to create this massive scale model. Kira and Worf teased him about his toy. Molly noted she let him play with her toys.
game_text: Randomly kills an opposing personnel in a personnel battle you just lost (limit once per battle). OR Once per game, plays on a planet to randomly kill a SECURITY personnel.

name: Small Oversight
lore: Holographic technology is notoriously finicky. Before The Doctor acquired his mobile emitter, attempts to project him outside of sickbay or the holodeck invariably met with problems.
game_text: Plays on a Hologram personnel who is not wearing a Mobile Holo-Emitter. Hologram and Command personnel present are each attributes all -3 and lose first-listed skill for rest of turn.

name: Establish Home Planet
lore: Ha'Dara: Help found a new "Home of Light" for holograms liberated from Hirogen training facilities.
game_text: * +25 if all personnel in Away Team are Hologram.

name: Mine Gallicite
lore: Sakari colony: Collect valuable material from the tunnels beneath this apparently abandoned world.

name: Repair Memorial
lore: Tarakis: Recharge power cells of a monument built to commemorate a Nakan massacre.
game_text: Personnel here are each attributes all -2.

name: Seal Rift
lore: Near Grid 986: Use an anti-tychon pulse to implode this artificially-created temporal phenomenon.
game_text: Until solved, Alternate ships may report here.

name: Transport Colonists
lore: Enara Prime: Convey members of a telepathic species from the Fima system to their home planet.
game_text: *+5 if Empathy or Mindmeld present.

name: Hunting Group
game_text: Seeds or plays on table on your non-Hirogen mission space mission with a point box. You may attempt it using these requirements:Alpha Hirogen + Hirogen ship + (CUNNING + STRENGTH) > mission points x3When you solve mission, you may commandeer an opposing ship present (capturing opposing personnel aboard) if your total WEAPONS there > twice its SHIELDS. Discard objective.'''

name: Orbital Bombardment
game_text: Plays on your non-Federation ship. It is WEAPONS +4 against planet facilities, and may target landed ships in battle (those ships may not return fire). Also, if this ship is at a planet location at end of your turn (and has not battled this turn), you may probe: Skill Dot : Targets hit. Kills up to two opposing personnel on planet (random selection). Opponent may counter-attack next turn.

name: Els Renora
lore: Wry, 100-year-old judge who presided over Jadzia Dax's Klaestron extradition hearing in 2369. Shows no signs of slowing down, despite her advanced age.

name: Iden
lore: Charismatic but megalomaniacal hologram. Escaped the Hirogen. Seeks to create a new religion based on his deliverance of holograms from oppression and slavery.

name: Iden
lore: Charismatic but megalomaniacal hologram. Escaped the Hirogen. Seeks to create a new religion based on his deliverance of holograms from oppression and slavery.

name: Teero Anaydis
lore: Excommunicated Vedek. Worked in counterintelligence for the Maquis. Experimented with using mind control to recruit agents. Honed his techniques on Tuvok.

name: Crell Moset
lore: Re-creation of notorious exobiologist. Cured the Fostossa virus through cruel experiments on Bajoran prisoners.

name: Doran
lore: Typical Hirogen hologram based on information taken from Voyager. His memories of the hunt were transferred to The Doctor in the hopes of gaining his understanding.

name: Doran
lore: Typical Hirogen hologram based on information taken from Voyager. His memories of the hunt were transferred to The Doctor in the hopes of gaining his understanding.

name: Ekoor
lore: Former soldier in a Jem'Hadar security detail. Outraged by the destruction of Lakarian City, he pledged his life to the resistance against the Dominion.

name: Harath
lore: Representative of the Hirogen's holographic prey. The Cardassians' deceptive nature – and unpredictability when cornered – made them a worthy challenge.

name: Harath
lore: Representative of the Hirogen's holographic prey. The Cardassians' deceptive nature – and unpredictability when cornered – made them a worthy challenge.

name: Kejal
lore: Cardassian hologram created by the Hirogen. Self-taught engineer of advanced skill. Her name, the Bajoran word for "freedom,," was given to her by Iden.

name: Kejal
lore: Cardassian hologram created by the Hirogen. Self-taught engineer of advanced skill. Her name, the Bajoran word for "freedom,," was given to her by Iden.

name: Mila
lore: Former housekeeper and confidante of Enabran Tain. Hid members of Damar's resistance in her basement. Procured a com unit and other equipment for their use.

name: Rusot
lore: Arrogant Gul. Gathered support in the early stages of the anti-Dominion resistance, despite his disdain for covert tactics. His Cardassia's dead, and won't be coming back.

name: Seskal
lore: Abrasive Gul. Loyal to Damar, though he believes the resistance movement would do better without the interference of the former terrorist, Kira Nerys.

name: Vornar
lore: Guard stationed at a facility in the Kelvas system. Characteristic of the many Cardassians, resentful of the Dominion, who embraced Damar's resistance effort.

name: Dar
lore: The Hirogen created relatively few Breen holograms, given the limited and conflicting information about their species gleaned from the Voyager databanks.

name: Dar
lore: The Hirogen created relatively few Breen holograms, given the limited and conflicting information about their species gleaned from the Voyager databanks.

name: Wodek'idan
lore: One of dozens of holograms freed by Iden. The Jem'Hadar reputation for raw prowess in battle made re-creations of them favorites among Hirogen hunters.

name: Wodek'idan
lore: One of dozens of holograms freed by Iden. The Jem'Hadar reputation for raw prowess in battle made re-creations of them favorites among Hirogen hunters.

name: Admiral J.P. Hanson
lore: Head of Borg research and strategic planning at Starfleet Tactical. Friend of Jean-Luc Picard for over 40 years. Amassed an armada to face a Borg cube at Wolf 359.

name: Boothby
lore: Groundskeeper at Starfleet Academy for more than 50 years. Has mentored countless cadets. Half the captains in Starfleet wouldn't be where they are without him.

name: E.M.H. - Mark II
lore: Emergency Medical Hologram. More sophisticated – and more eccentric – than the earlier Mark I version.

name: Edward Jellico
lore: Take-charge captain of U.S.S. Enterprise during Picard's Celtris III mission. Negotiated first Cardassian armistice. When he gives an order, expects his crew to get it done.

name: Ezri Dax
lore: Trill. Ship's counselor. Succeeded Jadzia Dax as ninth symbiont host. Unprepared for her emergency joining. Romantically involved with Julian Bashir. Gets spacesick.

name: Lewis Zimmerman
lore: Father of modern holography. Designed the E.M.H. series. Was briefly romantically involved with Leeta in 2373. Suffering from acute subcellular degradation.

name: Naomi Wildman
lore: ½ Ktarian, ½ human born on Voyager; raised by its crew. Daughter of Samantha. Goddaughter of Neelix. Mentored by Seven of Nine. Official captain's assistant.

name: Sumek
lore: Initially produced en masse for their logic and strength, Vulcan holograms were soon abandoned by the Hirogen for showing no lust for the hunt or fear of being hunted.

name: Sumek
lore: Initially produced en masse for their logic and strength, Vulcan holograms were soon abandoned by the Hirogen for showing no lust for the hunt or fear of being hunted.

name: The E.C.H.
lore: Emergency Command Hologram. At his request, The Doctor was granted the privilege in 2376 to command U.S.S. Voyager in emergencies like the Quarren incident.

name: Weiss
lore: Bloodthirsty hologram programmed to be Hirogen prey. Turned the tables, leading the slaughter of 43 hunters during his escape. Became Iden's tactical officer.

name: Weiss
lore: Bloodthirsty hologram programmed to be Hirogen prey. Turned the tables, leading the slaughter of 43 hunters during his escape. Became Iden's tactical officer.

name: Rulat
lore: Kazon-Nistrim bodyguard reporting directly to Seska. Instrumental in planning the assault to take Voyager in 2372.

name: B'Elanna Daughter of Miral
lore: The half-human B'Elanna Torres embraced her Klingon heritage in dealing with the Voq'leng crew. With Kohlar's help, she convinced them her child was the Kuvah'Magh.

name: Chancellor Gowron
lore: Beginning with his invasion of Cardassia in 2372, Gowron became increasingly prideful and paranoid. Nearly destroyed the Empire in his quest for glory.

name: Kar'meth
lore: One of the secondary bridge officers on I.K.C. Voq'leng. Has already begun training his successor; the Nehret has been known to claim his family quickly.

name: Nirok
lore: Chief of security aboard I.K.C. Voq'leng. His great-grandfather was the ship's original captain when it first set out over 100 years ago.

name: Ah-Kel and Ro-Kel
lore: Miradorn twins, bonded as if two halves of one being. Attacked and plundered transports for valuable objets d'art. Negotiated with Quark to sell one such item.

name: Anastasia Komananov
lore: KGB agent. Kira Nerys, with a Russian accent. Brought orders to pursue Dr. Noah. Romantically involved with Secret Agent Julian Bashir. Wears exploding earrings.

name: Arachnia
lore: Impetuous Queen of the Spider People, as portrayed by Kathryn Janeway. Forced Chaotica to lower his lightning shield after uncorking her pheromones on his henchman.

name: Barash
lore: Humanoid child orphaned by his homeworld's invasion. Secreted on Alpha Onias III in a cavern equipped with advanced holotechnology. Bonded with William T. Riker.

name: Buster Kincaid
lore: Harry Kim played the role of Captain Proton's trusty sidekick through fiery volcanoes, crash landings, killer robots, alien invasions, and the Den of Crocodiles.

name: Captain Proton
lore: Spaceman First Class, Protector of Earth, Scourge of Intergalactic Evil. Tom Paris played the adventurous hero in his re-creation of the original 1930s sci-fi serials.

name: Carlos
lore: Identity adapted by the Soong-type android Data in the fictional world of Dixon Hill. Snappy dresser with a nice tan. From South America. "Can't you tell?"

name: Chaotica
lore: Evil Ruler of Planet X, enemy of Captain Proton. Lusts after Arachnia. In 2375, waged war on photonic aliens from "the Fifth Dimension" with his fiendish Death Ray.

name: Cravic Unit 122
lore: Standard Automated Commander built by the Cravic to wage war on the Pralor. It is among the oldest of their androids still in operation. Commands a Cravic Warship.

name: Cyrus Redblock
lore: Civil but dangerous gangster. Believes in killing when for a purpose. Is resolved to obtain "the item" he believes was entrusted to Dixon Hill by Jessica Bradley.

name: Deputy Rozhenko
lore: With some help from Reginald Barclay, the ¾ Klingon, ¼ human Alexander Rozhenko created a holodeck program of the Ancient West for himself and his father.

name: Dixon Hill
lore: Fictional private detective. Solved dozens of cases. Jean-Luc Picard is an aficionado of the original 1930s stories and the latest holonovels by Broht and Forrester.

name: Dr. Noah
lore: Archenemy of Secret Agent Julian Bashir, replaced by the transporter pattern of Benjamin Sisko. Gathered the world's finest minds to start a new human race.

name: Duchamps
lore: Dr. Noah's associate. Skilled baccarat player, but less so than Secret Agent Julian Bashir. Carries a cigar rigged with a knockout agent. Transformed to appear as Worf.

name: Durango
lore: While most in touch with her Betazoid heritage, Deanna Troi loved her human father's tales of the Ancient West. She always wanted to play the "mysterious stranger."

name: Eli Hollander
lore: The Butcher of Bozeman, meanest gunslinger in the West. Frank's boy. Assumed Data's traits in a holodeck glitch – including his dexterity with a deck of cards.

name: Falcon
lore: Deadly assassin hired by Dr. Noah to deal with problems like Secret Agent Julian Bashir. The character took the appearance of Miles O'Brien after an accident in 2372.

name: Felix Leech
lore: Hit man from the Dixon Hill series. Never strays far from his boss, Cyrus Redblock. Held several Enterprise crew members at gunpoint during a holodeck malfunction.

name: Frank Hollander
lore: Main "bad guy" in Alexander's Deadwood program. Eli's pa. A computer malfunction caused the character to take on the appearance and physical abilities of Data.

name: John Watson
lore: London physician and companion of Sherlock Holmes. Recounted a full five dozen of the sleuth's cases. On the holodeck, Geordi La Forge was Data's Watson.

name: Leonardo da Vinci
lore: Renaissance man whose accomplishments as a scientist, artist, mathematician, philosopher, astronomer, inventor, anatomist, and geologist dwarfed all his contemporaries.

name: Lily
lore: In her time aboard U.S.S. Enterprise-E, Lily Sloane adjusted admirably to rayguns, force fields, bionic zombies, and the holographic world of Dixon Hill.

name: Lonzak
lore: Inferior serving as bodyguard to Chaotica. Enforces his liege's rule, imprisoning infidels in the Dungeon of Pain or Mines of Mercury. Often seizes Constance Goodheart.

name: Madam Pulaski
lore: Katherine Pulaski entered the holodeck on a bet that Data could not solve a Sherlock Holmes-style mystery without already knowing the outcome.

name: Minuet
lore: Knockout brunette in a computer-generated gin joint. Programmed by the Bynars to distract William T. Riker. His feelings for her remained quite passionate for years.

name: Mona Luvsitt
lore: Capable valet to Secret Agent Julian Bashir. She speaks seven languages, has degrees in biology, chemistry, and physics, and can fly anything from a jet to a helicopter.

name: Mr. Garak
lore: The Cardassian Elim Garak taught Secret Agent Julian Bashir: "There comes a point when the odds are against you and the only reasonable cause of action is to quit."

name: Nicki the Nose
lore: Nefarious gangster and arms dealer. Infrequent patron of a highbrow San Francisco restaurant. Featured in several Dixon Hill stores, including The Big Goodbye.

name: Pralor Unit 3947
lore: Automated Personnel Unit built by the Pralor. Found adrift in space by Voyager. Abducted B'Elanna Torres in the hopes she could build more androids of its kind.

name: Pralor Unit 6263
lore: Standard Automated Personnel Unit built by the Pralor. Its creators were annihilated when they tried to shut the androids down after reaching peace with the Cravic.

name: Professor Honey Bare
lore: Seismologist replaced by an image of Jadzia Dax. Built the lasers Dr. Noah planned to use to destroy the world. Romantically involved with Secret Agent Julian Bashir.

name: Professor Moriarty
lore: Sherlock Holmes' enemy. Accidentally made sentient in 2365. Built a simulation of the Enterprise and its crew.

name: Secret Agent Julian Bashir
lore: Bashir... Julian Bashir. Role in a holoprogram created by his friend Felix, of a spy for Great Britain in the Cold War of 20th-century Earth. Has escaped countless traps.

name: Sheriff Worf
lore: Sheriff of Deadwood, South Dakota, as played by Worf. Though initially reluctant to spend time with his son, the Klingon soon saw the appeal of Alexander's scenario.

name: Sherlock Holmes
lore: The role of Sir Arthur Conan Doyle's brilliant detective was often assumed by the Soong-type android Data.

name: Sigmund Freud
lore: Neurologist who founded the science of psychoanalysis on Earth in the late 19th century. Data looked to his re-creation for interpretations of his first nightmares.

name: The President of Earth
lore: The Doctor gave an unimpeachable performance on the holodeck in 2375, negotiating with transdimensional aliens who mistook a Captain Proton program for reality.

name: The Twin Mistresses of Evil
lore: Captain Proton villains portrayed by the Delaney sisters, Megan and Jenny. Threatened to use their Brain Probe to make Buster Kincaid their slave. He didn't mind.

name: Vic Fontaine
lore: Self-aware hologram of a 20th-century Las Vegas singer. His keen insights helped Bashir, Odo, Kira, Worf, Nog, and others aboard Deep Space 9 through difficult times.

name: Garren
lore: Because of their cloaking technology and precise strategic planning, re-creations of Romulans were often used by the Hirogen in ship-to-ship hunting simulations.

name: Garren
lore: Because of their cloaking technology and precise strategic planning, re-creations of Romulans were often used by the Hirogen in ship-to-ship hunting simulations.

name: Praetor Neral
lore: Neral is the president of the Continuing Committee and Praetor of the glorious Romulan Star Empire. Has not aged well under the mantle of leadership.

name: Maleth
lore: Typical chief of security for large Vidiian bases. Head of perimeter defense for the Avery III installation. Captured Tom Paris, B'Elanna Torres, and Peter Durst in 2371.

name: Ar-Q-ologist
lore: "How can you write about something that you've never seen? I know! Why don't I take you there?"

name: Q's Fantasy Women
lore: "My good fortune is your good fortune."
game_text: Plays on a male present (opponent's choice) until any Q-Flash. If he helps you solve a mission, opponent scores bonus points. Discard event.

name: Quandary
lore: "It's so unlike you, Jean-Luc, to have a sense of humor. Especially about getting stabbed through the back... So if you had to do it all over again... ?"
game_text: "Restore" one personnel from your discard pile (there may not be a version of the same persona in play) and shuffle into crew or Away Team. Opponent then selects one personnel (random selection). If it is not "restored" personnel, discard it and lose points.

name: Trullux
lore: Modified transport commanded by Gegis, who planned to use his profit from stolen Borg nanoprobes to install multiphasic shielding and a gold-pressed latinum hull.

name: Baxial
lore: Small ship owned and commanded by Neelix. Ugliest thing he ever saw, though its appearance grew on him.
game_text: May report for free to Neelix's location.

name: Cravic Warship
lore: Powerful ship built decades ago by the Cravic. Still used by their androids to continue war on the Pralor Units.
game_text: Your Cravic Units may report aboard.

name: Olarra
lore: Stolen Hirogen ship. Commanded by Iden on his quest to free "Children of Light" from the Hirogen, Nuu'bari and other Delta Quadrant civilizations.
game_text: Your Hologram cards may report aboard.

name: Olarra
lore: Stolen Hirogen ship. Commanded by Iden on his quest to free "Children of Light" from the Hirogen, Nuu'bari and other Delta Quadrant civilizations.
game_text: Your Hologram cards may report aboard.

name: Pralor Warship
lore: Part of the large armada left behind by the now-extinct Pralor. Commanded by Pralor Unit 6263.
game_text: Your Pralor Unit may report aboard.

name: Holosuite
game_text: This site must be placed adjacent to Quark's Bar (or another Holosuite). Has a Holodeck . Holoprogram cards may be played here (limit one); station controller may discard it during their turn). Hologram Equipment cards and compatible Hologram personnel may report here, and may be transferred directly to/from owner's ship docked at this station.

name: Holosuite
game_text: This site must be placed adjacent to Quark's Bar (or another Holosuite). Has a Holodeck . Holoprogram cards may be played here (limit one); station controller may discard it during their turn). Hologram Equipment cards and compatible Hologram personnel may report here, and may be transferred directly to/from owner's ship docked at this station.

name: The Genesis Device
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Torpedo created by Project Genesis. Reorganizes matter at the subatomic level to achieve rapid terraforming on a planetary scale. Its matrix utilizes dangerously unstable protomatter.

name: Engine Imbalance
lore: An improperly balanced warp drive system poses a serious hazard. Even a minor misalignment can propel a ship into an artificial wormhole.

name: "God"
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: "This starship. Could it carry my wisdom beyond the Barrier? ...Then I shall make use of this starship... bring it closer, so that I might... join with it.
game_text: Unless two Away Team members each have INTEGRITY>7, place on mission; destroys one ship here (opponent's choice). You must have a ship here to attempt mission.

name: Hero Worship
lore: "Doctor Cochrane, I know this sounds silly, but can I shake your hand?"

name: I Hate You
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: "The sins of all our fathers, is being dumped on us – The sons. The only choice we're given is HOW MANY MEGATONS? And I eschew you! And I say SCREW YOU! And I hope you're blue too."
game_text: To get past requires Anthropology, Youth, and no Music present. Nullified by Vulcan Nerve Pinch.

name: Linguistic Legerdemain
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered County
lore: "We must respond personally. The universal translator would be recognized."
game_text: Unless Anthropology and Exobiology present, X=1+number of affiliation icons on this mission with no matching personnel present; place on mission; it cannot be attempted.

page_title: Now Would Be A Good Time (TMP)
name: Now Would Be A Good Time
base_name: Now Would Be A Good Time
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: With insufficient transporter power for Scotty to beam him off the aircraft carrier Enterprise, Chekov was captured and interrogated by the U.S. Navy. Being Russian didn't help him.

name: Subspace Shock Wave
lore: Dangerous aftermath of a stellar, planetary, or lunar explosion. The shock wave created by the "incident" on Praxis was felt even beyond the boundaries of Klingon space.

name: The Whale Probe
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: Alien space probe of unknown origin. Traveled to Earth to contact the extinct humpback whale. Its powerful transmission caused total power loss aboard nearby ships and starbases.

name: V'Ger
lore: Massive living machine created by an unknown race around the lost NASA space probe Voyager VI. Left a trail of destruction during its return to Earth in search of its creator.
game_text: Ship is destroyed unless 2 Empathy OR Diplomacy, Anthropology, and Computer Skill present. Discard dilemma.

name: Transport Inhibitor
lore: Device that emits an energy field preventing the operation of transporters within a radius of several meters. Used by the Enterprise crew in their defense against the Son'a.

name: Transporter Drones
lore: Typical reconnaissance devices modified by the Son'a to fire isolinear tags. Transporters can lock onto a tagged object, overcoming any interference with normal targeting scanners.

name: Duj Saq
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Klingon for "land the ship." Though K'Vort-class ships were larger and more heavily armed than the B'rel design they were based upon, only the 23rd-century original had this ability.

name: Fal-tor-pan
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Vulcan refusion of the body and katra. The ritual was performed successfully for the first time since ancient legend between Leonard H. McCoy, son of David, and Spock, son of Sarek.

page_title: I Just Love Scanning for Life-forms (TMP)
name: I Just Love Scanning for Life-forms
base_name: I Just Love Scanning for Life-forms
lore: "Life-forms... you tiny little life-forms... you precious little life-forms... where are you?"
game_text: Plays to reveal up to three cards from the top of any draw deck (six if your own). Discard all non-personnel cards; replace remaining cards in any order. Discard event.

name: Isomagnetic Disintegrator
lore: Don't give an isomagnetic disintegrator to a Klingon showing signs of jak'tahla unless you want him to use it.
game_text: Plays on table. Shuffle your hand into your discard pile, then exchange your discard pile for your draw deck. Draw four cards (may not be converted to downloads). Discard event.

property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan

property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier

page_title: I Do Not Take Orders from You! (TMP)
name: I Do Not Take Orders from You!
base_name: I Do Not Take Orders from You!
lore: Admiral Dougherty knew the Son'a were devious and dangerous, but never imagined how far Ru'afo would go until it was too late. "The Federation will never know what happened here."
game_text: Plays at start of a personnel battle you initiated (once per battle). Each of your personnel who has Treachery x2 may kill an opposing personnel who has lower CUNNING.

name: Lure of the Nexus
lore: Though exiting the nexus is as simple as wishing it so, its temptations are so great that few desire to leave. Those pulled away against their will are forever changed by their experience.

page_title: No, Kirk... The Game's Not Over (TMP)
name: No, Kirk... The Game's Not Over
base_name: No, Kirk... The Game's Not Over
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: "From hell's heart, I stab at thee! For hate's sake... I spit my last breath at thee!"
game_text: Plays if you just changed a mission's point value using The Genesis Device. Discard all planet facilities, landed ships, and ships in orbit there, and all personnel on planet.

name: Prefix Code Transmission
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Each starship is assigned a unique security code to prevent remote access to its vital systems. With knowledge of the code, a ship can be ordered to lowers its own shields.

name: Smooth As an Android's Bottom?
lore: Geordi once told Data that technological perfection can shave too close. That, of course, depends on the desired results.

name: The Needs of the Many...
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan

page_title: What Does God Need With a Starship? (TMP)
name: What Does God Need With a Starship?
base_name: What Does God Need With a Starship?
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: "Excuse me. I'd... just like to ask a question."

name: Analyze Radiation
lore: Briar Patch Region ● Sector 441: Conduct analysis of the metaphasic particles in this nebula.
game_text: Span -2 for all Son'a ships.

name: Insurrection
lore: Briar Patch Region ● Ba'ku planet: Prevent the Son'a attempt to forcibly relocate the Ba'ku race.
game_text: Ba'ku may report on planet (for free).

name: Observe Ritual
game_text: Vulcans and Amanda Grayson may report on planet.

property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country

name: Admiral Kirk
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: While Captain Kirk regretted accepting promotion, he commanded the Starship Enterprise in later crises. Time away from the center seat did not diminish his ingenuity.

name: Amanda Grayson
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home

property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock

name: Captain Spock
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: ½ Vulcan, ½ human. Mr. Spock was restored from death by the Genesis wave – and his friends' resolve.

property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan

name: Clark Terrell
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan

name: Commander Chekov
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Over the years, Ensign Chekov's distinguished career would include many promotions, and positions as acting science officer, security chief, navigator, and first officer.

name: Commander Uhura
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country

name: David Marcus
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Gifted scientist. Like his father, often bends the rules. His impatience was Project Genesis' breakthrough and downfall. Proud – very proud – to be Admiral Kirk's son.

name: Dr. Chapel
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home

name: Dr. McCoy
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country

name: Henreid
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock

name: J. T. Esteban
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Captain of the U.S.S. Grissom. Has served as such for over four years without serious incident, due largely to his cautious, "by the book" command style.

name: John Harriman
lore: Son of a respected Federation official. Captain of U.S.S. Enterprise-B. Usually confident in dealing with reporters, but on the ship's maiden voyage was having an off day.

name: Lojur
lore: Conservative helmsman of the Starship Excelsior. Serves adequately in the position, but is less knowledgeable about the ship and its limitations than Captain Sulu.

name: Mark Tobiaston
lore: Communications officer, fully rated on Excelsior-class ships. Linguistics expert who has authored an analysis on similarities of the Vulcan and Romulan languages.

name: Matthew Dougherty
lore: Conflicted admiral under orders from the Federation Council to oversee the Ba'ku relocation. Dislikes working with Ru'afo, but will do it for the Federation.

name: Mr. Scott
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country

name: Saavik
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan

name: St. John Talbot
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Ambassador to the worthless lump of rock known as Nimbus III. Released the pain of his cynicism when Sybok enlisted his help in the search for Eden.

name: T'Lar
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Revered elder. High priestess of the ancient temple at Mount Seleya. The only Vulcan known to have actually performed a successful fal-tor-pan ceremony.

name: Tahglio
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Typical guard for Federation Security. Given a low-priority post on Earth after a poor performance review at his last assignment. His next review showed no improvement.

name: Valeris
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country

name: Voight
lore: Science officer aboard U.S.S. Enterprise-B. Joined Starfleet to pursue her interest in alien environments. Has Irish lineage dating back nearly four centuries.

name: Azetbur
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Daughter of Chancellor Gorkon; became chancellor herself in 2293. Pursued his dream of peace with the Federation, signing the historic Khitomer Accords.

name: Brigadier Kerla
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country

name: Ch'dak
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country

name: Chancellor Gorkon
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Klingon leader who first embraced the notion of peace with the Federation. His vision mapped the way to the undiscovered country – the future.

name: Colonel Worf
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country

name: General Chang
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country

name: General Korrd
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Once-renowned military strategist exiled to Nimbus III by the High Council. Released the pain of his dishonor when Sybok enlisted his help in the search for Qui'tu.

name: Kamarag
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home

name: Klaa
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier

name: Komal
lore: Typical chief surgeon of a K't'inga-class ship. Friend of Krase. Strongly opinionated, he often provides his captain with advice, whether asked to or not.

name: Kor'choth
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country

name: Koth
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Warden of the penal asteroid Rura Penthe. His greatest pleasures are watching fights among his inmates and delivering his welcoming speech to new prisoners.

name: Kruge
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Klingon commander with a festering hatred of the Federation. Attempted to seize the secret of the Genesis weapon – the secret of ultimate power.

name: Maltz
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock

name: Regnor
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Trained medic serving under Kruge. Like most serving aboard smaller Klingon vessels, is more often called upon as a soldier.

name: Torg
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock

name: Valkris
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Klingon operative romantically involved with Kruge. Obtained top secret documents on Project Genesis. It was the pinnacle of her career in espionage.

name: Vixis
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier

name: Woteln
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Technican at the Morska listening post. Representative of those performing less glorious duties in service of the Klingon Empire. "Dujvetlh'e' nuq? ...rIn."

name: George and Gracie
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: Two humpback whales, male and female, raised in captivity on 20th-century Earth. Gracie is pregnant.

name: Dr. Gillian Taylor
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: 20th-century marine biologist. Helped Admiral Kirk safely bring George and Gracie to the 23rd-century, where she then signed on aboard a Starfleet vessel.

name: Dr. Gillian Taylor
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: 20th-century marine biologist. Helped Admiral Kirk safely bring George and Gracie to the 23rd-century, where she then signed on aboard a Starfleet vessel.

name: Gallatin
lore: Ru'afo's first officer. Once the most vengeance-minded of the Son'a, recent time with the Ba'ku – and a persuasive Federation captain – has softened his hatred.

name: J'Onn
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Humanoid settler of Nimbus III. Release the pain of his impoverishment when Sybok enlisted his help in the search for the knowledge sought by all since time began.

name: Joachim
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan

name: Khan
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan

name: Martia
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country

name: Mas'ud
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan

name: Pa'rena
lore: Son'a female. Chief science officer of the Li'seria. Part of the team that perfected mass production of ketracel-white for trade with the Dominion.

name: Rae'alin
lore: One of the Son'a assigned to the Ba'ku duck blind operation. Has been secretly looking for opportunities to steal technology from the Federation installation.

name: Ru'afo
lore: Leader of the Son'a, a people banished from their home planet by the Ba'ku. Will let nothing stand in the way of his revenge upon them, least of all his Federation allies.

name: Sam'po
lore: Tactical officer aboard the Li'seria. Among the most far gone of the Son'a – will likely die within a few months unless he receives metaphasic treatment.

name: Sarod
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan

name: Sharic
lore: Typical Tarlac, born into indentured servitude of the Son'a. Ru'afo's personal body sculpture attendant. Very good at what she does.

name: Sybok
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier

name: Wajahut
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan

name: Caithlin Dar
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Ambassador to Nimbus III. Hides disdain for the position with overeagerness. Released the pain of her deception when Sybok enlisted her help in the search for Vorta Vor.

name: Nanclus
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Romulan Ambassador to the Federation in 2293. Conspired with Admiral Cartwright and General Chang in the assassination of Chancellor Gorkon.

name: H.M.S. Bounty
property_logo: Star Trek IV; The Voyage Home
lore: Bird-of-prey captained by Kruge on a covert mission to the Genesis Planet. Stolen and commanded by Admiral Kirk; re-christened with historical irony by Dr. McCoy.

name: H.M.S. Bounty
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: Bird-of-prey captained by Kruge on a covert mission to the Genesis Planet. Stolen and commanded by Admiral Kirk; re-christened with historical irony by Dr. McCoy.

name: Starship Constitution
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: With new modifications, ships of this class were built long after the original's launch. Starfleet continued this practice of refitting older designs into the 24th century.

name: Starship Enterprise
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Venerable Starfleet ship refit in 2270. Completed many successful missions before being transferred to Captain Spock's command and retired for use as a training vessel.

name: Starship Excelsior
lore: Unsuccessful transwarp test ship later refitted as the prototype for one of Starfleet's most durable and ubiquitous classes of ship. Commanded by Captain Sulu.

name: U.S.S. Enterprise-A
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: Specially commissioned in 2286 to replace the famous ship lost one year earlier. Proudly continued the mission of its predecessor under the command of James T. Kirk.

name: U.S.S. Enterprise-B
lore: Third Federation ship so christened, launched on stardate 9715. Became fully operational the following Tuesday.
game_text: El-Aurians may report aboard.

name: I.K.C. Amar
lore: One of the first K't'inga-class ships. Leader of the battle group dispatched to escort an unidentified intruder out of Klingon space in 2271.

name: I.K.C. Chontay
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier

name: I.K.C. K't'inga
lore: Though the basic form of the Klingon cruiser had been the same since the 22nd century, this design introduced in the 2270s boasted upgrades to all major systems.

name: I.K.C. Kla'Diyus
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Unique vessel able to fire while cloaked. Commissioned and commanded by General Chang, who ordered the designers killed to preserve the secret of its existence.

name: Kronos One
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country

name: Injector Assembly One
lore: Specialized ship designed to collect metaphasic radiation particles from the ring system of the Ba'ku planet – a procedure tested extensively by Ru'afo in simulations.
game_text: May report to location of your Son'a ship . Download Collect Metaphasic Particles

name: Li'seria
lore: Flagship of the small Son'a fleet and base of operations for their entire race. Commanded by Ru'afo.
game_text: Son'a shuttlecraft may report, be carried, and launch aboard.

name: Son'a Battleship
lore: Fast and deadly, the largest of Son'a ships carry isolytic subspace weapons banned by the Khitomer Accord.
game_text: Son'a shuttlecraft may report, be carried, and launch aboard.

name: Son'a Shuttle
lore: Small craft capable of atmospheric flight. Used to strafe the Ba'ku village and launch Son'a transporter drones.
game_text: Transporter Drones may report aboard (for free, once each turn).

name: U.S.S. Reliant
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: NCC-1864. Placed at the disposal of Project Genesis to locate a suitable Stage Three testing site. Captured at Ceti Alpha V and subsequently commanded by Khan.

name: U.S.S. Reliant
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: NCC-1864. Placed at the disposal of Project Genesis to locate a suitable Stage Three testing site. Captured at Ceti Alpha V and subsequently commanded by Khan.

name: Isolytic Burst
game_text: Requires a Son'a Battleship or Li'seria firing. If you hit, randomly kills one additional personnel (on a Nor, one personnel at site of opponent's choice). Hit = Tactic Current Tactic Draw. Direct hit = Tactic Draw Tactic Draw.

name: Riker Maneuver
game_text: Requires ship at a nebula firing; ATTACK bonus +3 if William T. Riker aboard. Hit = Tactic Current Tactic Draw. Direct hit = Tactic Draw Tactic Draw, and another opposing ship present (your choice) is also hit = Tactic Draw.

name: Target Warp Field Coils
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
game_text: May not be used to fire upon a facility. Hit = Tactic Current Tactic Draw. Direct hit = Tactic Current Tactic Draw Tactic Draw.

name: Camp Khitomer
lore: 2293 Khitomer: Site of the ground-breaking peace talks between the Federation and the Klingon Empire.
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Native to this timeline: all cards with both Classic Films and Alternate icon. Once per turn, one such card reporting at this location may report for free.

name: Cetacean Institute
lore: 1986 Earth: Marine biology research laboratory and public aquarium located in Sausolito, California.

name: Environmental Suit
lore: Self-contained garment for protecting personnel in a hostile environment. A variable magnetic field can be activated in the boots when working in zero-gravity.
game_text: You may discard this equipment to prevent a personnel present from being killed by a dilemma or a Tactic card (that personnel is stopped instead).

name: Espionage: Bajoran on Dominion
lore: No strangers to oppression, many Bajorans fought the 2374 Dominion occupation from within. With Odo's help, Kira's small "resistance cell" paved the way for the Dominion withdrawal.
game_text: Plays on any Dominion mission (for free if you have Odo there). Your Bajoran personnel may now attempt this mission. Discard after mission completed.

name: Shape-Shift Inhibitor
lore: Prototype device developed by the Obsidian Order. Emits a quantum stasis field that prevents a changeling from altering its biomolecular structure.
game_text: Plays on table. Each player must first discard a personnel card in order to download a non-Borg personnel. (Immune to Kevin Uxbridge.)

name: Timepod Ring
lore: Small device used to monitor the auto-timer on the time travel pod appropriated by Berlinghoff Rasmussen. As he was uncertain how to reprogram the timer, the ring was very precious to him.
game_text: Plays on table. Once each turn, you may peek at the top card of your deck. Also, you may discard this event and the top card of your draw deck to nullify an Alternate dilemma.

name: Treacherous Advice
lore: For many months, a changeling posing as General Martok manipulated the Klingon Empire through choice lies whispered in the ear of Chancellor Gowron.
game_text: Peek at an opponent's hand. You may discard one of those cards for each Leadership personnel present with one of your infiltrators who is infiltrating. Discard event after use.

name: Bluegill Infestation
game_text: Seeds on table; place up to seven unique personnel face up beneath here from outside the game. Your copies of those personnel in play are STRENGTH +5, considered Bluegills, and may not be stunned. Also, when one of your Bluegills is killed, you must randomly select a personnel from here; if it matches one who was killed, that personnel was considered to be the Bluegill Queen. (Unique.)

name: Kobayashi Maru Scenario
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan

name: Changeling Sweep
lore: Changelings will be forced into a gelatinous state by a mid-level phaser stun. In 2372, special units were placed in many Starfleet facilities to ensure that empty rooms were in fact truly so.
game_text: Plays to "sweep" an opponent's discard pile: examine it and place any interrupt cards (except Borg or Referee cards) out-of-play.

name: Dimensional Shifting
lore: Powerful form of folded space transport, capable of penetrating all known shields and forcefields. Repeated use of the technology causes a fatal degradation of the subject's cellular chemistry.
game_text: During your turn, discard a random card from hand to place any number of your personnel and equipment at one mission aboard any ship at the same mission.

name: Empathic Touch
lore: "It's accelerating. You have no more time for games."
game_text: When your personnel is about to be killed, if your Empathy personnel is present, stop both personnel to prevent that.

name: In for a Trim
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Barber Pole and Mot's Advice play for free. Once each turn, if you have Barber Pole in play, you may "take a little off the top": peek at the top X cards of opponent's draw deck, where X is the number of your non-Borg Barbering personnel in play. You may discard any events, incidents, or interrupts (except Borg Only and Referee cards), then replace the rest in any order.

name: Colonel Kira
lore: During Captain Sisko's absence after the death of Jadzia Dax, Kira Nerys was promoted to command DS9. She soon learned the responsibilities of the captain's chair.

name: Shandor
lore: Prylar representative of members of the Bajoran clergy. Maintains the shrine aboard Deep Space 9.

name: Admiral Janeway
lore: In an alternate future where Voyager had remained lost for 23 years, Kathryn Janeway decided to travel back in time and guide her younger self to a faster route home.

name: Admiral Riker
lore: Commander of Starbase 247 in an alternate future. At odds with Governor Worf. Battled Klingons near Devron.

name: Christopher Pike
lore: Noted captain. Succeeded Robert April and commanded the Starship Enterprise for 13 years. Accepted promotion in 2263 and relinquished command to James T. Kirk.

name: Gideon Seyetik
lore: Gifted terraformer who in 2370 planned to crown his career by reigniting the burned-out star Epsilon 119. Failure – and modesty – do not agree well with him.

name: Lt. Palmer
lore: Representative of relief officers on Federation starships. Such officers routinely fill in for crewmembers on shore leave or restricted duty.

name: Miral Paris
lore: ¼ Klingon, ¾ human daughter of B'Elanna Torres and Tom Paris. Has her father's charm and mother's temper. In a possible future, helped Janeway negotiate with Korath.

name: Miral Paris
lore: ¼ Klingon, ¾ human daughter of B'Elanna Torres and Tom Paris. Has her father's charm and mother's temper. In a possible future, helped Janeway negotiate with Korath.

name: Raymond Boone
lore: Starfleet officer who served on the U.S.S. Rutledge in the Federation/Cardassian war. Captured at Setlik III in 2347 and subsequently killed while in captivity.

name: Robert DeSoto
lore: Captain of the U.S.S. Hood and former commanding officer of William T. Riker. Years ago, he and Jean-Luc Picard served together as lieutenants on the same ship

name: Yeoman Rand
lore: Janice Rand is yeoman to Captain Kirk aboard the Enterprise. Captain of the Academy Diving Team in 2264-65. Student of horticulture and xenobotany.

name: Uri'lash
lore: Typical Hupyrian. Hired by Brunt as a bodyguard during his brief stint as Grand Nagus in 2374.

name: Anij
lore: Ba'ku female who became romantically involved with Jean-Luc Picard. In her 300 years, learned to sustain a perfect moment in time – but never learned to swim.

name: Artim
lore: Twelve-year old Ba'ku child. Son of Sojef. Taught Data the importance of play and having a little fun every day.

name: Raimus
lore: Farian crime lord and thief. Oversees a significant Orion Syndicate operation based on Farius Prime. When he tells you to do something, you just do it.

name: Sojef
lore: Leader of the small community of Ba'ku that settled a new world in the Briar Patch. Ardent supporter of a simple way of life, free of advanced technology.

name: Sunad
lore: Typical Zalkonian captain. Sought to capture criminals undergoing a dangerous mutation before they could further disrupt society.

name: Tournel
lore: Chief engineer of the ship that first brought the Ba'ku to their new home in 2066. Now one of the more respected "elders" in their idyllic community.

name: Weyoun 6
lore: Activated after his predecessor's suspicious death, this clone of the Vorta Weyoun had subtle errors. He hoped to end the Dominion War by defecting to Odo's side.

name: Reklar
lore: In response to tensions along the Cardassian/Federation border, this ship was sent to attend diplomatic talks with the U.S.S. Enterprise.
game_text: WEAPONS +2 and SHIELDS +1 while you have a captive.

name: U.S.S. Drake
lore: Starfleet vessel, registry NCC-20381. In 2364, was assigned to a routine mission of exploration in and around the Lorenze Cluster under the command of Paul Rice.

name: U.S.S. Grissom
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Science vessel assigned to survey and investigate the Genesis Planet in 2285. Named for one of Earth's earliest space explorers.

name: U.S.S. Pegasus
lore: Modified prototype on which an experimental cloak was secretly tested in 2358. Some of the crew mutinied against Captain Erik Pressman for this violation of treaty.
game_text: Download Phased Cloaking Device

name: Calondon
lore: Independent freighter commanded by Zef'No. In 2370, ran weapons supplied by the Cardassianss to the Bajoran isolationists of the Circle.
game_text: Smuggling personnel in crew may use hand weapons to complete "cargo runs."

name: Lokirrim Vessel
lore: The Lokirrim, at war with photonic insurgents, forbid the use of holograms in their space. Their ships can emit a disruption field that decompiles holographic matrices.
game_text: All Hologram cards here are deactivated.

name: Tsunkatse Ship
lore: Formidable vessel commanded by Penk, from which he broadcasts his popular fighting circuit. Heavily shielded to prevent anyone from abducting his competitors.
game_text: Your personnel with "Tsunkatse" in lore may report aboard.

name: Starfleet Phaser Pistol
lore: There are only two settings. Stun, and kill. Make sure to not get them mixed up.

name: Revisionist History
lore: One might meet an unfortunate end if the timeline were to be altered.

name: Temporal Shifting
lore: Time Travel can afford the user certain abilities that might not be available to those native to the current time.
game_text: Plays on a player. That player must choose to either discard three cards from hand or discard one Alternate card. If that player discards a Alternate card, he/she may draw up to four cards. Discard event.

name: Seat of Starfleet
lore: The place that started it all. Changed the galaxy as we know it.

name: Charles Tucker III
lore: Self taught Chief Engineer of Enterprise. Best friend and confidant to Jonathan Archer.

name: Elizabeth Cutler
lore: Hard working scientist, gourmet cook, and amateur bartender. Always eager to be selected for special assignments.

name: Emory Erickson
lore: Inventor of the Transporter and father figure to Jonathan Archer. Dreams big. Honorary President of the Association of Transporter Technicians.

name: Ethan Novakovich
lore: Tends to leave jobs quickly. Tried working as a cook, bartender, waiter, fan club president and event student senator before joining Starfleet.

name: Hoshi Sato
lore: Communications officer on board the Enterprise NX-01. Didn't want to come along, but after listening to some Klingon, she felt motiviated. (sic)

name: Jeremy Lucas
lore: Chairman of research at Cold Station 12. Close friend of Dr. Phlox. His optimism sometimes leads him to jump to dangerous conclusions.

name: Jonathan Archer
lore: Captain of the Enterprise NX-01. Leaped into deep space to make the future quantifiably better for all mankind.

name: Malcolm Reed
lore: Head of Security aboard Enterprise. Experienced weapons expert, qualified bodyguard and crack shot.

name: Maxwell Forrest
lore: Respected Admiral. Friend of Soval. Sent the crew of Enterprise out into the final frontier to go where no man had gone before.

name: Phlox
lore: Medical miracle worker. Former chairman of immunology at his alma mater. Has a great smile.

name: T'Pol
lore: Female Vulcan first officer of the Enterprise NX-01. Finds humans to be fascinating. Dislikes the smell of dogs.

name: Travis Mayweather
lore: Crack pilot aboard the Enterprise NX-01. Itching to get into deep space. Loves the sweet spot.

name: Enterprise
lore: Legendary prototype designed for deep space travel. Commanded by Jonathan Archer. First Starfleet vessel to bear the name that would symbolize Starfleet's elite.

name: T'Pol/Soong Maneuver
game_text: ATTACK bonus +3 and DEFENSE bonus +2 if you have a NX-class ship firing. Hit = Tactic Current Tactic Draw. Direct hit = Tactic Current Tactic Draw Tactic Draw.

name: Worf
lore: Klingon chief of security aboard the U.S.S. Enterprise-E. Returned to Starfleet after a hiatus as the Federation Ambassador to Qo'noS.

name: Odo
lore: The Great Link's savior, the changeling Odo became a Founder to save his people and secure peace at the close of the Dominion War.

name: Borg Queen
lore: "I am the beginning; the end; the one who is many. I am the Borg.... I am the collective."

name: Administrator Weyoun
lore: Stalwartly loyal Vorta. Third incarnation of Weyoun. Dutifully directed the destruction of the New Bajor colony in 2370, as ordered by the Founders.

name: Comm Officer Sato
lore: Hoshi Sato seized command of the Starship Defiant and declared herself Empress of the Terran Empire.

name: Centurion Kirk
lore: Surgically-altered human thief. Captain Kirk was under secret orders from Starfleet Intelligence.

name: Centurion Kirk (AI)
lore: Surgically-altered human thief. Captain Kirk was under secret orders from Starfleet Intelligence.

name: Persistent Individuality
lore: The Borg Queen uses deadly force and extreme measures to protect the hive mind. The sense of identity found in residents of Unimatrix Zero was both a threat and a means to resist.
game_text: Kills 7 - X personnel (random selection), where X = the number of different classifications present. To get past requires ENGINEER.

name: Worf
lore: Klingon chief of security aboard the U.S.S. Enterprise-E. Returned to Starfleet after a hiatus as the Federation Ambassador to Qo'noS.

name: Odo
lore: The Great Link's savior, the changeling Odo became a Founder to save his people and secure peace at the close of the Dominion War.

name: Borg Queen
lore: "I am the beginning; the end; the one who is many. I am the Borg.... I am the collective."

name: Administrator Weyoun
lore: Stalwartly loyal Vorta. Third incarnation of Weyoun. Dutifully directed the destruction of the New Bajor colony in 2370, as ordered by the Founders.

name: Comm Officer Sato
lore: Hoshi Sato seized command of the Starship Defiant and declared herself Empress of the Terran Empire.

name: Centurion Kirk
lore: Surgically-altered human thief. Captain Kirk was under secret orders from Starfleet Intelligence.

name: Centurion Kirk (AI)
lore: Surgically-altered human thief. Captain Kirk was under secret orders from Starfleet Intelligence.

name: Derran Tal
lore: Varro dissident who became romantically involved with Harry Kim. She designed a synthetic parasite to attack and dismantle the Varro's generational ship.

name: Dala
lore: Humanoid con artist, thief, and liar who impersonated Kathryn Janeway. She took advantage of the Federation's trustworthy reputation for personal gain.

name: Spock
lore: ½ Vulcan, ½ Human son of Sarek and Amanda Grayson. Over 140-year-old ambassador. On private mission to Romulus. Mindmelded with Picard.

name: Tribunal of Q
game_text: Seeds on table. You may download Referee cards from your discard pile. While you are downloading or playing a Referee card, you may ignore any effect and no action may suspend play. In place of a card draw you may download a Referee card (once per game per card title) OR Q the Referee (limit once every turn). At the start of the first turn, if it is not your turn, you may download a Referee card.

name: Bajoran Wormhole
game_text: Requires two Bajoran Wormhole cards; each inserts into a spaceline to create a location (span 1). Play one in Alpha Quadrant (Bajor Region); download the other to Gamma Quadrant . Limit one per quadrant. While in play, any ship may move from one end to the other, then is "stopped." OR Plays at any time to nullify any card which is closing or destroying Bajoran Wormhole (discard doorway).

name: Slar
lore: Vicious Gorn Slavemaster of the Tholian Assembly who was assigned to gut the Starship Defiant in the Mirror Universe. He does not trust Terrans.

name: Handshake
game_text: Plays once each turn (for free) if you have played no cards this turn and have fewer in hand than opponent; they must choose to discard three cards or allow you to draw three. OR Plays to look at top five cards in any draw deck or discard pile for ten seconds; rearrange as desired. OR Plays if you have at least three other cards in hand; discard entire hand and draw seven cards. Discard incident after any use.

name: Jean-Luc Picard
lore: Rescued Borg counterpart. After returning to his command of the U.S.S. Enterprise, Picard developed a violent vendetta against the Borg.

name: Porthos
lore: Captain Archer's pet beagle. Likes cheese. T'Pol thinks he smells worse than even the humans do.

name: Antaak
lore: Physician responsible, albeit accidentally, for creating the disfiguring Klingon augment virus. Found a future in cranial reconstruction. Had a knack for diplomacy.

name: Rotation Damage Marker
game_text: Unprepared and naive of the dangers that they would encounter, the Enterprise took its share of damage in those first few years. The ship and crew held up remarkably well under pressure.

name: Rotation Damage Marker
game_text: The U.S.S. Constellation took heavy damage from the Doomsday Machine as it past through system L-374. The planet killer proved to be quite formidable in battle against two Federation starships.

name: Rotation Damage Marker
game_text: The Future Enterprise was more advanced after its refit. With more powerful engines and advanced firepower, it was able to dispense two Klingon attack cruisers while only taking minimal damage.

name: Rotation Damage Marker
game_text: The damage was heavy on both sides of the war between the Federation and the Dominion. While the Dominion held little regard for their fallen, the Alpha Quadrant species did not share that sentiment.

name: Rotation Damage Marker
game_text: With some help from the future, the U.S.S. Voyager was able to get past a Borg armada. One transphasic torpedo would damage a Borg cube, and two is enough to destroy it.

name: Rotation Damage Marker
game_text: When V'Ger came to Earth in search of its creator, it destroyed the Klingon vessels that penetrated the massive energy cloud. It viewed carbon based units aboard as a damaging infestation to be elimintated.

name: Rotation Damage Marker
game_text: While in command of the Reliant, Khan was able to damage the flagship of the Federation. Only by hiding in the Mutara Nebula was the Enterprise able to evade him long enough to destroy the Reliant.

name: Rotation Damage Marker
game_text: Unfortunately for James T. Kirk, the U.S.S. Enterprise 1701-B left spacedock without many of its key components installed. It was thus ill equipped to deal with the effects of the Nexus and was damaged.

name: Rotation Damage Marker
game_text: Only with the combined efforts of Earth's entire defenses and the return of the U.S.S. Enterprise-E, was Starfleet able to destroy the Borg cube that attacked at Sector 001. But by then, the damage was done.

name: Personal Duty
lore: Commodore Decker, driven to the edge of madness by the loss of his entire crew, sacrificed himself in a vain attempt to destroy the "Planet Killer."
game_text: To get past requires Leadership OR OFFICER. All such personnel are "stopped," but if two or more present, one must continue (random selection).

name: Tactical Disadvantage
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Khan's battle experience was significant but limited to terrestrial combat. Three-dimensional thinking gave Captain Kirk and the Enterprise a clear advantage.
game_text: Players show their hands and examine revealed ships. Unless your total SHIELDS > opponent's total WEAPONS, kill one personnel (random selection). Discard dilemma.

name: The Caretaker's "Guests"
lore: Harry Kim and B'Elanna Torres were abducted by the Caretaker and exiled to the subterranean Ocampan society.
game_text: One personnel present (opponent's choice) is placed atop draw deck. You may place a different personnel of the same affiliation from your discard pile with this crew or Away Team.

name: The Clown: Bitter Medicine
lore: Linked into the Kohl mental preservation network, Harry Kim endured searing confrontations of his deepest fears.
game_text: Place on mission. Now and start of each mission or scouting attempt here, opponent names a skill. All your personnel with that skill are attributes -2 until end of turn.

name: Friction
lore: The steadfast obedience of the Jem'Hadar to their leaders often made working with other species difficult.
game_text: Plays on table if you control three Dominion personnel. Each non-Jem'Hadar personnel enters play "stopped."

name: Getting Under Your Skin
lore: When it comes to logic and emotions, Romulan women may differ from Vulcan women, but that is not the only thing Spock finds distracting about Commander Charvanek.
game_text: Plays on table if you control three Romulan personnel. Once each turn, when you play an event on table, opponent reveals top card of deck. If it is a personnel, score 5 points. (Unique.)

name: Prison Compound
lore: Often housing political prisoners, clandestine Cardassian camps use hard labor as punishment.
game_text: Plays if you control three Cardassian personnel to score points. X= the total number of Skill Dot on all your captives.

name: Solbor
lore: The Bajoran Prylar worried about Kai Winn's interest in the Pah-Wraiths but remained a faithful attendant.

name: Rusot
lore: A proud nationalist, Gul Rusot joined Damar's underground resistance movement. Served on Terok Nor. Dissident.

name: Founder Architect
lore: Male Shape-shifter serving as a representative of the Founder population. Greeted Odo when he returned to the Great Link.

name: Dukat
lore: Treacherous, scheming Cardassian. Closed the Bajoran Wormhole as a Pah-Wraith puppet.

name: Malik
lore: Devious augment from the time of Khan. Kept as a frozen human embryo until grown by Arik Soong.

name: Data
lore: Soong-type android in disguise as a Dissident and member of the Romulan underground. Claimed to be from the city of Rateg.

name: Dominion Battleship
lore: Twice the size of a Galaxy-class starship, battleships of this design served in the Alpha Quadrant war.
game_text: Attributes all +3 if Founder, Vorta and Jem'Hadar aboard.

name: Betazoid Gift Box
lore: Traditional device for presenting important gifts. Its sculpted face comes to life boisterously presenting its content to the recipient.

name: The Guardian of Forever
game_text: Plays on planet Gateway (limit one). Once per turn, one or more personnel present may time travel to a time location in this quadrant, or may return here from there (with any of owner's other personnel present). OR Plays once each turn to nullify any card that is closing Guardian, or to draw up to four cards if your Archaeology or Anthropology personnel just time traveled back to Guardian; place doorway out-of-play.

name: Temporal Shifting
lore: Time Travel can afford the user certain abilities that might not be available to those native to the current time.

name: Deep Space 9
lore: Formerly known as Terok Nor. Now a Bajoran trading center and administrative facility run by the Federation.

name: HQ: Secure Homeworld
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
game_text: Seeds or plays on a homeworld. Your Away Teams which include a personnel who matches homeworld's affiliation may attempt the mission using these requirements: Leadership x2 + SECURITY + (Honor OR Treachery) + any one attribute total > point value of mission When you solve mission, capture all opposing personnel on planet who do not match affiliation of homeworld.

name: Agent Garak
lore: Elim Garak joined the Federation in its fight against the Dominion. Served as a code breaker in spite of his fear he was betraying his homeworld.

name: Captain Nog
lore: In an alternate timeline, Nog served as captain of the U.S.S. Defiant. Aided Jake Sisko in an effort to reverse a time-altering subspace inversion.

name: George and Gracie
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: Two humpback whales, male and female, raised in captivity on 20th-century Earth. Gracie is pregnant.

name: U.S.S. Voyager
lore: NCC-74656. Commanded by Kathryn Janeway. Pulled 70,000 light years from the Alpha Quadrant. Its crew has spent nearly seven years on a long trek home.
game_text: Download Bio-Neural Gel Pack Download Blue Alert

name: Sternenflotten Phaserpistole
lore: There are only two settings. Stun, and kill. Make sure to not get them mixed up.
game_text: Starfleet use only. Each of your personnel present is STRENGTH +2 (or +3 if that personnel has Security). (Cumulative).

page_title: A Fast Ship Would Be Nice (VP)
name: A Fast Ship Would Be Nice
base_name: A Fast Ship Would Be Nice
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: After beaming Kirk and Spock aboard the Qel'Poh to escape the destruction of Genesis, Maltz told Kirk he didn't deserve to live. Kirk replied, "Fine, I'll kill you later."
game_text: Kills one personnel (opponent's choice). You may substitute a bodyguard or Guard Drone present OR any empty ship here (moved to opponent's side of spaceline; commandeered).

name: Espionage: Bajoran on Dominion
