game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Once per game, at the start of your turn, for every two missions an opponent seeded where you have TNG Romulanpersonnel, you may download to hand one TNG Romulan ship and one TNG Romulan Command personnel. Discard objective.

name: Corak
lore: Representative of Cardassians researching new means of interrogation. Glinn. Visited the U.S.S. Enterprise in 2369 as Gul Lemec's aide.

name: Gollek
lore: Female chief engineer on the Vetar. Believes females make better engineers. Injured in a Maquis attack in 2370. Tactful manager.

name: Joret Dal
lore: Cardassian informant who provided military secrets to the Federation for the good of the Cardassian Union. Commanded a Type VI Shuttlecraft.

name: Joret Dal
lore: Cardassian informant who provided military secrets to the Federation for the good of the Cardassian Union. Commanded a Type VI Shuttlecraft.

name: Joret Dal (with TCC watermark)
lore: Cardassian informant who provided military secrets to the Federation for the good of the Cardassian Union. Commanded a Type VI Shuttlecraft.

name: Harcourt Fenton Mudd
lore: Smuggler, entrepreneur, starship thief, peddler of the Venus drug and emperor of androids. Just an "honest businessman." Married to Stella Mudd.

name: Rybak
lore: Human thief working for Baran during the hunt for the Stone of Gol. Served as cook, occasional bodyguard, and boarding party member.

name: Agyer
lore: Expert in shield and cloak technology serving on the Apnex in 2368. Invited to Dr. Reyga's metaphasic shield test but refused permission by his government.

name: Ambassador Spock
lore: Legendary ½ Vulcan, ½ human head of the Romulan underground. An advocate of reunification, Spock was betrayed by his friend Senator Pardek.

name: D'Lors
lore: Typical political aide. Dissident who defected to the Federation in stasis with Vice-Proconsul M'ret in 2369. Former senator in the youth diplomatic corps.

name: Jean-Luc Picard
lore: Human captain disguised as a Romulan. Worked with the Romulan underground movement. Shared his memories of Sarek through a mindmeld with Spock.

name: Kell
lore: High Council emissary. Klingon who conspired with Romulans to assassinate Governor Vagh and thereby disrupt the Klingon-Federation alliance.

name: Kharic
lore: Typical member of the Romulan underground. Female colleague of Tamarith. Pleased by Spock's decision to stay on Romulus after Pardek's betrayal.

name: Khev
lore: Representative of non-military personnel guarding the Carraya system prison camp for Khitomer survivors. Sometimes serves as Tokath's bodyguard.

name: Mareth
lore: Typical Romulan engineer who became trapped in a temporal fragment in 2369. Did not realize the cause was life-form incubation in the engine core.

name: Parem
lore: Special security officer aboard the Apnex. Assigned to guard the prototype phase-inverting cloaking device. Worked as a bartender before joining the military.

name: Proconsul Neral
lore: Neral deceived Ambassador Spock by pretending he supported a reunification of Romulus with Vulcan.

name: T'Jev
lore: Typical field nurse assigned to a damage control team on the Haakona in 2365. Was tending injured crew members when Jean-Luc Picard appeared.

name: Tacil
lore: One of many female officers serving aboard Romulan warbirds. Former engineering technician who got caught in a temporal fragment in 2369.

name: Toraan
lore: Tal Shiar officer assigned to the Office of the Proconsul in 2368. Often works alongside his twin brother Telak. Likes viinerine with Romulan ale.

name: U.S.S. Excalibur
lore: Refitted vessel captained by William T. Riker during Starfleet's blockade of the Klingon-Romulan border in 2368. Underwent further refit in 2373.

name: Voyager
lore: In 2372, Culluh and Seska took command of the Alpha Quadrant vessel U.S.S. Voyager and its technology for the benefit of the Kazon-Nistrim sect.
game_text: Download Home Away From Home

name: Deranas
lore: Warbird commanded by Tomalak. Often assigned to the Neutral Zone. Encountered the U.S.S. Enterprise twice in 2366.
game_text: Attributes all +2 in Neutral Zone.

name: Assimilated Vessel
lore: Revived Borg drones found in Earth's Arctic Circle assimilated the nearest ship in an attempt to rejoin the Collective.
game_text: End of every turn: Attacks one ship (random selection), then moves. Opponent scores points if dilemma moves off spaceline (even if Borg).

name: Cybernetic Homing Device
lore: Data and his brother Lore each contained a homing device. When Dr. Soong activated them in 2367, Data took control of the U.S.S. Enterprise to reach his creator.
game_text: If android or non-Borg aboard, opponent may move ship up to printed RANGE (ship is "stopped"), then discard dilemma. Otherwise, to get past requires CUNNING>36.

name: Data Has Some Issues
lore: Under Lore's emotional influence, Data felt a sense of brutal pleasure after killing a Borg on Ohniaka III. He pursued those feelings until his ethical subroutines were reinitialized.
game_text: Place on ("stops") a personnel present (random selection). End of each turn, they kill another personnel present with lower STRENGTH (opponent's choice). Cure with 3 ENGINEER.

name: Hunter Probe
lore: Silaran Prin used hunter probes to exact vengeance against several Shakaar resistance cell members, including Latha Mabrin, Furel, and Lupaza.
game_text: Unless 2 SECURITY and 2 Anthropology present, opponent chooses two personnel. Both die at end of turn. Mission continues.

name: Irrational Commander
lore: After Worf's suggestion to activate the U.S.S. Enterprise-E's self-destruct sequence, Jean-Luc Picard's outburst surprised his crew. They carried out his orders nonetheless.
game_text: Unless you have two leaders with Honor OR two leaders with Treachery, place on mission. Crew must have any attribute>double mission points to solve. (Unique.)

name: Murasaki Effect
lore: Electromagnetic phenomenon that surrounded Taurus II in 2267. Damaged the shuttlecraft Galileo and left transporters temporarily unreliable.
game_text: Damages all unstaffed ships in orbit. Place on mission. Each time transporters used here, one just-beamed personnel is killed (random selection).

name: Osaarian Pirates
lore: Heavily armed Osaarian merchant ship. Its crew turned to piracy after being stranded in the Delphic Expanse.
game_text: End of every turn: Destroys one equipment (random selection) on each facility (except a Nor) and ship here without Smuggling aboard, then moves.

name: Paralyzed by Fear
lore: The untested junior engineers assigned to salvage Empok Nor were frozen with terror after Cardassian killers gradually began eliminating them.
game_text: "Stops" each personnel in crew or Away Team with printed CUNNING+INTEGRITY<13. Nullify with Miles O'Brien#Star Trek CCG 1st Edition"Miles O'Brien.

name: Regime Change
lore: Shinzon's elimination of the Romulan Senate using a thalaron radiation device ensured his ascension to the pinnacle of power in the Star Empire.
game_text: Opponent chooses: kills three personnel (random selection) who report for free using game text on planet (or planet facility here) OR kills one V.I.P. (random selection).

name: Remat Detonator
lore: Black market device of Romulan origin which scrambles transporter beams on rematerialization. Silaran Prin used one to kill Shakaar resistance cell informant Trentin Fala in 2373.
game_text: Unless 2 Transporter Skill present, place on table. Whenever your personnel have just beamed, opponent may discard dilemma to kill one (opponent's choice).

name: Spaceborne Entity
lore: Angry life-form transformed into a massive and powerful vessel. Nothing like it in Starfleet records – not even close.
game_text: No personnel may report "for free" at this location.End of every turn: Attacks all ships matching mission's affiliation icons, then moves.

name: Brace for Impact
lore: In 2371, a warp core breach forced the crew of the U.S.S. Enterprise to land the saucer section on Veridian III, bringing the ship's mission to an end.
game_text: Plays to land your damaged ship at a planet location. If Galaxy-class, X=landed ship's lowest printed attribute. Otherwise, X=0.

name: Stone Knives and Bearskins
lore: Stranded on Earth in the 1930s, Spock struggled to construct a mnemonic memory circuit using the comparatively primitive equipment of the era.
game_text: Plays on any planet mission. Suspends gametext of all non-unique Equipment present (except blade weapons, Rule cards, Ketracel-White, and Gold-Pressed Latinum).

name: Repurposed Outpost
lore: As the power of a spacefaring culture declines, outposts established throughout its former territory are often occupied by independent groups.
game_text: Seed one OR build where you have a Non-Aligned ENGINEER. Does not allow aligned cards to report.

name: Taken Prisoner
game_text: Plays on table. Once each turn, you may report a TNG Cardassian personnel (for free) to your Cardassian outpost or to your TNGCardassian ship at a mission an opponent seeded or that is worth 40 or more points. Once each turn (thrice per game), if an opponent's personnel present with your TNGCardassian personnel is about to be killed, you may capture that personnel instead.

name: A Missing Day
lore: The isolationist Paxan race hid their existence by erasing explorers' memories. The Paxans failed to remove all clues of their encounter with the U.S.S. Enterprise in 2367.
game_text: Plays once each turn to count down an opponent's dilemma, interrupt, or event (except Omega Particle).

name: Fitting In
lore: To prevent the assassination of Captain Kirk in 2268, the crew of the U.S.S. Defiant needed to blend into the background of daily life aboard the Starship Enterprise.
game_text: Plays once each turn to give your non-Alternate personnel a skill from an Alternate personnel present until end of turn.

page_title: Your Place is on the Bridge (TStL)
name: Your Place is on the Bridge
base_name: Your Place is on the Bridge
lore: In times of a crisis, a captain needs to be able to coordinate crew activities. James T. Kirk reminded John Harriman of this during the maiden voyage of the U.S.S. Enterprise-B.
game_text: Plays on your damaged ship OR your ship just targeted in a battle you did not initiate. Download its matching commander aboard. Discard interrupt.

name: Evade Borg Vessel
lore: Paulson Nebula: Hide from pursuing Borg cube in dense, hazardous nebula.
game_text: Only one of your ships may battle here every turn.

name: Install Emotion Chip
lore: Terlina III: Install new android hardware at remote laboratory.
game_text: *+5 for each unique Soong-type android present, up to three.

name: Locate Terrorist Leader
lore: Valo Region ● Third moon of Valo I: Find Bajoran terrorist's resistance cell.

name: Redirect Energy Ribbon
game_text: Seeds on Veridian III. Your El-Aurian personnel may attempt it using these requirements: Treachery + Astrophysics + Trilithium Weapon + Trilithium Weapon Control PADD When you solve, download or relocate The Nexus (even from on table) to any of your planet missions and you may convert Veridian III to a space mission.

name: Twelve of Thirteen
lore: IDENTIFICATION: TOPOLOGY DRONETASK: Analyze planetary surface features. Secure.BIOLOGICAL DISTINCTIVENESS: Humanoid.

name: Goran
lore: Representative of espionage specialists serving in the Cardassian military. Posed as a monk to attack a Maquis cell at the Juhraya colony in 2370.

name: Nador
lore: Elder gul encountered by the U.S.S. Enterprise in multiple realities. Commanded the Rakassa. Investigated espionage uses of the Argus Array.

name: Captain Spock
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Trainee instructor of Starfleet Academy, Mr. Spock supervised the Kobayashi Maru scenario, ½ Vulcan, ½ human mentor of Saavik.

name: D.C. Franklin
lore: Human tactical officer typical of those serving in the late 23rd century. Directed efforts to transport the S.S. Lakul survivors aboard the U.S.S. Enterprise-B.

name: Kathryn Janeway
lore: Promoted to vice-admiral after seven years in the Delta Quadrant. Dispatched the U.S.S. Enterprise-E to Romulus on an "easy" diplomatic assignment.

name: Marruu
lore: Human navigator of U.S.S. Enterprise-B staff officers. Befriended Demora Sulu. Enjoys strategy games and tales of the ancient American West.

name: Martinez
lore: Typical nurse who served under Beverly Crusher for many years. Helped evacuate sickbay when the Borg boarded the U.S.S. Enterprise-E.

name: William T. Riker
lore: Experienced officer who often commanded the U.S.S. Enterprise. Defeated the Sisters of Duras at Veridian III. Well versed in saucer separations.

name: Dr. Farek
lore: Typical Ferengi physician. Served aboard the Krayton in 2366. Distrusted Lwaxana Troi. Tried to study her empathic powers with a mind probe.

name: Lwaxana Troi
lore: Betazoid ambassador held captive by Tog. Misled him about her willingness to cooperate. Later described Tog as slightly repulsive, but with a certain charm.

name: B'Etor
lore: Since failing to seize control of the Klingon Empire, B'Etor, sister of Duras, has been trying to acquire powerful weapons. Still the prettier sister.

name: Dokar
lore: Characteristic of male Klingon warriors supporting attempts by the House of Duras to regain power after their defeat in the Klingon Civil War.

name: K'Vit
lore: Klingon helmsman serving the sisters of Duras. Briefly worked as a bounty hunter. Warrior at heart. Surprised when his ship began to cloak at Veridian III.

name: Lursa
lore: Ambitious sister of Duras and B'Etor. Working to restore her family's previous position of power. Named her newborn son after her father, Ja'rod.

name: Bosus
lore: Typical disconnected Borg disciple of The One. Participated in the raid on Ohniaka III. Swore to avenge the death of his friend Torsus.

name: Data
lore: Loyal brother of Lore. The Soong-type android was swayed by emotions to join The One's cause.

name: Goval
lore: Representative of lost Borg who found a new sense of purpose with The One. Temporarily separated himself from his new collective.

name: Kamala
lore: The perfect mate, an empathic metamorph. Kriosian mutant romantically involved with Jean-Luc Picard. Dutifully married Alrik despite her bond to Jean-Luc.

name: Lieutenant Crosis
lore: Renegade Borg who commanded the initial phase of raids on Federation outposts. Loyal aide to The One. Recruited Data to their cause.

name: Millin
lore: Male El-Aurian representative of refugees rescued by the U.S.S. Enterprise-B from the S.S. Lakul before it was destroyed by the Nexus.

name: Morik
lore: One of many Borg disconnected from the Collective who became loyal to The One. Guarded the Federation prisoners, but was easily tricked by them.

name: The One
lore: The Soong-type android Lore found his calling giving purpose to the disconnected Borg drones.

name: Third of Five
lore: Borg befriended by Geordi La Forge. Became an individual, "Hugh," fracturing his hive's link to the Collective. Led those resisting Lore's leadership.

name: Relam
lore: Complex strategist affected by temporal irregularities in 2369. Once captained a D'deridex. Has a family tradition of military service.

name: Tarvang
lore: Typical Romulan pilot. Beamed aboard the U.S.S. Enterprise during an encounter with quantum singularity lifeforms in 2369. Enjoys chess.

name: Supply Ship
lore: Typical Cardassian freighter. Carries anything from research equipment to disruptors to taspar eggs. Uses high-energy subspace fields to mask its cargo.

name: Cha'Joh
lore: Bird-of-Prey commanded by Lursa and B'Etor, the Sisters of Duras. Fought at Veridian III.
game_text: May report to location of Cha'Joh.

name: Assimilator
lore: Large Borg ship operated by a group of renegade Borg. First encountered the U.S.S. Enterprise while raiding the Federation outpost on Ohniaka III.
game_text: Download Transwarp Conduit

name: Stolen Ship
lore: One of many decommissioned Vulcan merchant vessels. Several were stolen by the Romulans in a ploy to conquer Vulcan for the Star Empire.

name: Stolen Ship
lore: One of many decommissioned Vulcan merchant vessels. Several were stolen by the Romulans in a play to conquer Vulcan for the Star Empire.

name: Stolen Ship (with TCC watermark)
lore: One of many decommissioned Vulcan merchant vessels. Several were stolen by the Romulans in a play to conquer Vulcan for the Star Empire.

name: Starting Over
lore: Kathryn Janeway offered the disconnected drone Seven of Nine a new life free from the Borg Collective and the chance to rediscover her humanity as Annika Hansen.
game_text: Discard your hand, then draw the same number of cards. If you have a Borg personnel in play, draw two extra cards. (No draws may be converted to downloads.) Discard event.

name: Unstable Matrix
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: David Marcus used dangerously unpredictable protomatter to build the Genesis Device, inadvertently dooming the Genesis Planet.
game_text: Seeds on Genesis. If mission complete, you may lose points (discard event) to convert to a space mission. (Immune to Kevin Uxbridge.)

name: Access Relay Station
lore: Callinon VII: Analyze automated subspace relay station for information on the Dominion.

name: Acquire Illicit Explosives
lore: Bajor Region ● Bajor System: Purchase bilitrium from Klingon outcasts for delivery to Bajoran insurgents.

name: Attack at Rare Phenomenon
lore: Compression anomaly: Ambush enemy ship while it conducts delicate research.

name: Battle Reconnaissance
lore: Northwest Passage Region ● Borg wreckage: Investigate unusual bio-readings.

name: Clash at Chin'toka
lore: Chin'toka Region ● Defense perimeter: Battle over strategically significant system.

name: Collect Omicron Particles
lore: Nucleogenic cloud: Harvest rare substance for use as replacement power source.
game_text: Adjacent missions are span -1.

name: Destroy Iconian Gateway
lore: Vandros IV: Permanenty close ancient portal held by renegade Jem'Hadar.

name: Eliminate Virus
lore: T'Lani III: Return to analyze and destroy last traces of deadly nanobiogenic weapon accidentally re-released.
game_text: *Points do not count when Harvester Virus in play.

name: Evade Dominion Squadron
lore: Kuiper belt: Maneuver among icy comet fragments during hot pursuit.

name: Genesis Planet
lore: Mutara Region ● Genesis: Study final collapse of unstable and formerly forbidden planet.

name: Investigate Derelict
lore: Delphic Expanse Region ● Wrecked D'Kyr: Study remains of antique Vulcan ship.
game_text: When you solve, restores RANGE of all ships in region.

name: Investigate Maquis Activity
lore: Demilitarized Zone Region ● Volan III: Confer with colonial leaders about recent tensions.
game_text: *+5 if this is your first completed mission.

name: Navigate Argolis Cluster
lore: Argolis Cluster Region ● Protostar cluster: Engage enemy near vital sensor array.

name: Protect the Escapees
lore: Olmerak rendezvous point: Defend civilian government from Klingon patrols.
game_text: Solving player may initiate battle against Klingon.

name: Renovate Starbase
lore: Berengaria VII: Refurbish outpost established in the earliest days of space exploration.
game_text: When you solve, download a facility here.

name: Resupply Marauder
lore: Clandestine base: Restock Ferengi vessels for operations in adjacent sectors.
game_text: Solving player's D'Kora-class ships are RANGE +1.

name: Search and Rescue
lore: Badlands Region ● Class-M Planetoid: Search for officer kidnapped from Deep Space 9 by Maquis.

name: Signal for Rescue
lore: Desolate world: Quickly repair damaged communication system; call for help.

name: Study Badlands
lore: Badlands Region ● Plasma Storms: Chart region of intense plasma activity.

name: Study Rare Phenomenon
lore: Compression anomaly: Evaluate subspace abnormality for possible transwarp applications.

name: Surgery Under Fire
lore: Ajilon Prime: Assist with triage of heavy combat casualties.

name: Survey Star System
lore: Planetary system: Scan uncharted system for inhabited, habitable, and resource-rich worlds.

name: The Siege of AR-558
lore: Chin'toka Region ● AR-558: Fight for control of critical communications array.

name: Verify Evidence
lore: Badlands Region ● Rendezvous point: Substantiate reports of information broker working here.

name: Back Room Dealings
lore: Conducting illicit negotiations with a pair of volatile Klingons requires an experienced eye and careful haggling, much like the day-to-day life of a tailor.
game_text: One personnel (random selection) is killed unless you "stop" a personnel with Treachery or INTEGRITY<4. To get past requires STRENGTH<24 remaining.

name: Chula: Unfortunate Roll
lore: In the game of chula, even choosing the less profitable but safer path does not guarantee that all of your players will continue to the next shap.'''
game_text: '''To get past, three personnel present (random selection) are chosen. If their total INTEGRITY is odd, all three are "stopped." Otherwise, discard dilemma.

name: Cultural Differences
lore: Klingon honor and Ferengi greed are not a natural match. To win the heart of Grilka, Quark had to dispel many Klingon prejudices against the Ferengi.
game_text: One personnel (random selection) is killed unless you "stop" a personnel with Acquisition or Anthropology. To get past requires CUNNING>24 remaining.

name: Difficult Disposal
lore: Julian Bashir found the harvester virus remarkably resistant to most forms of radiation, making the disease difficult to destroy. It only took 375 attempts.
game_text: To get past requires 2 ENGINEER and MEDICAL OR ENGINEER and 2 MEDICAL.

name: Encased in Crystal
lore: With Kira Nerys' life seemingly in danger from an expanding crystal, Odo tried everything from brute force to harmonic vibrations in an attempt to free his friend.
game_text: To get past requires 2 Geology and SECURITY OR Geology and 2 SECURITY OR 2 Music.

name: Ferengi Locator Bomb
lore: Pheromone-guided assassination device used unsuccessfully against Grand Nagus Quark in 2369. Very difficult to avoid. Can be identified by the telltale solarium and argine traces.
game_text: Unless Computer Skill, Navigation, and Physics OR Acquisition, Treachery, and CUNNING>32 present, one personnel (random selection) is placed on bottom of draw deck.

page_title: Fly by the Seat of Your Pants (EM)
name: Fly by the Seat of Your Pants
base_name: Fly by the Seat of Your Pants
lore: With limited resources and outdated technology, the Bajoran resistance had to rely on their instincts rather than navigational sensors to pilot their vessels.
game_text: To get past requires 2 Navigation and OFFICER OR Navigation and 2 OFFICER.

name: Hard Time
lore: Argrathi criminal remediation relies on false memories of imprisonment. After being accused of espionage, Miles O'Brien received a memory of a 20-year incarnation.
game_text: One personnel (random selection) is returned to hand; X = the number of Skill Dot icons on that personnel. To get past requires at least X personnel remaining.

name: More of Your Kind
lore: The Prophets living in the Bajoran wormhole found their existence was disrupted each time a vessel entered the Celestial Temple. The Sisko negotiated for safe passage.
game_text: Randomly stop half of your crew (round down). Nullify with any Orb personnel.

name: Precision Piloting
lore: Jadzia Dax and Arjin had to maneuver carefully while transporting a protouniverse, avoiding any verteron nodes that could destabilize their delicate cargo.
game_text: To get past requires Navigation with Command or Staff. All such personnel are "stopped", but if two or more present, one must continue (your choice).

name: Secret Identity
lore: Pel posed as a male waiter in order to bypass Ferengi commerce laws and earn profit. Rom exposed her secret, jealous that she had usurped his position at Quark's side.
game_text: One personnel (opponent's choice) is discarded. If you did not seed this dilemma, you may download a personnel of the same affiliation to join crew or Away Team.

name: Socializing with the Staff
lore: Julian Bashir made sure to meet all of the dabo girls working at Quark's Bar. Jadzia Dax took perverse pleasure in making sure those meetings were awkward.
game_text: To get past requires a female. All female personnel are "stopped," but if two or more present, one must continue (random selection).

name: Too Many Chiefs
lore: The assignment of two chiefs of security aboard Deep Space 9 inevitably muddled the chain of command. Benjamin Sisko reassured Odo that George Primmin was not in charge.
game_text: One SECURITY-classification personnel (random selection) is "stopped." If that personnel has Leadership, two additional SECURITY personnel are "stopped" (random selection).

name: Unlikely Pair
lore: The bombing of Garak's tailor shop led Odo and Garak to investigate the whereabouts of Enabran Tain. However, their investigation also caught the eye of the Tal Shiar.
game_text: Choose to "stop" until countdown expires: two personnel not of the same species (your choice) OR two personnel (random selection).

name: Bajor for Bajorans
lore: After the Cardassian occupation, many Bajorans wished to rid themselves of all alien influence. The Circle's isolationist attitude led to acts of violence against non-Bajorans.
game_text: Plays on table (for free if you have Jaro Essa in play). At the end of each of your turns, if you have no non-Bajoran personnel in play, you may draw an extra card.

name: Internment
lore: Julian Bashir was captured by Dominion operatives at a conference. Like General Martok, he was imprisoned in the Gamma Quadrant and replaced by a changeling.
game_text: Plays to relocate a captive held by your trap card to your brig (in same quadrant or Alpha Quadrant). OR Plays to download a capturing-related card to hand. Discard event.

name: New Frontiers
lore: The discovery of the Bajoran wormhole created new opportunities for inter-quadrant exploration, commerce, and colonization.
game_text: Plays to draw two cards. If you have four DS9 personnel at a mission not in their native quadrant, draw two additional cards. Discard event.

name: Raktajino
lore: The stimulating Klingon coffee is a staple of Benjamin Sisko's morning routine. He isn't awake until he's had his first cup.
game_text: Plays to make a unique personnel attributes +2 until end of turn OR shuffle the bottom three personnel and/or ships from your discard pile into your draw deck. Discard event.

name: Shipwright
lore: In 2371, Benjamin Sisko used an ancient Bajoran spacecraft to prove Bajorans were capable of interstellar travel before many other races.
game_text: Plays on table. Your Bajoran ships are RANGE +1. (Cumulative.) OR Lose points to make your ship with Solar Sail RANGE +10 this turn.

name: Articles of Jurisprudence
game_text: Plays on your escorted captive on Cardassia Prime; you may discard captive at any time. (Unique.) Each of your Cardassian Law personnel add captive's skill. Cardassian personnel without Honor are each attributes all +2. OR Plays once each turn to draw a card for each captive you are escorting or have in your brig (limit four).

name: Call for Reinforcements
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Once per game, in place of your normal card play, you may download a Universal ship. Once per game, in place of your normal card play, you may fully repair your ship if you have a matching facility (or compatible Nor) in play.

name: Gagh Tek Or?
game_text: Plays to download Lursa and B'Etor OR Yeto and T'Kar OR Quark Son of Keldar and Grilka OR once per game, download Klingon Restaurant and one DS9 Klingon (may report to that site); when reporting and for rest of game, personnel downloaded with this incident may mix and cooperate with your DS9 cards regardless of affiliation. Draw no cards this turn. Discard incident.

name: Labor Camp
game_text: Plays on an Ore Processing Unit or on your non-Homeworld planet mission (for free if Forced-Labor Camp present). Start of each turn, if your Cardassian personnel or Ferengi personnel present is escorting a captive, score 5 points. (Unique.)

name: Nano-Biogenic Disarmament
game_text: Seeds or plays on T'Lani III. Your cards with "harvester virus" in lore may report here; once each turn, one such personnel may do so for free if you do not have a facility here. When you solve, you may download and seed a dilemma with "harvester virus" in lore beneath any mission OR discard incident to score points.

name: New Arrivals
game_text: Seeds on table. Once each turn, you may place a Universal personnel you do not already have in play for free. End of each turn, you may draw an extra card. Discard incident if you play more than one personnel for free on any turn.

name: Reshape the Quadrant
game_text: Seed one on table. You may download one Reactor Core card. Your Nors, personnel, and ships that have a Star Trek: Deep Space Nine property logo gain DS9 (even if not in play). Discard incident if your play (or have played) a non-DS9 personnel or ship.

name: Establish Interquadrant Communications
lore: Wormhole terminus near Idran: Set up subspace communications array.

name: Host Tournament
lore: Wadi planet: Facilitate high stakes gaming event.
game_text: Gamma Quadrant Non-Aligned cards may report on planet.

name: Pacify Warring Factions
lore: Alien penal colony: End centuries of warfare and rescue crash survivors.

name: Reopen Trade Discussions
lore: Karemman space: Renegotiate contract in exchange for information.

name: Salvage Wrecked Ship
lore: Unknown wreckage: Recover scrap from crashed vessel.
game_text: When you solve, may download Jem'Hadar Birthing Chamber here.

name: Verify Legendary Journey
lore: Intersystem tachyon eddies: Recreate ancient spacefarers' "impossible" journey.
game_text: May insert adjacent to Bajor Region OR Cardassia Region.

name: Anneli
lore: Representative of female Bajorans serving in the militia. Dispatched by General Krim to help the Circle secure Deep Space 9.

name: Ben Sisko
lore: Shipwright Benjamin Sisko built and commanded the Baraka, a replica Bajoran lightship. Human. Recreated a legendary interstellar journey.

name: Ben Sisko
lore: Shipwright Benjamin Sisko built and commanded the Baraka, a replica Bajoran lightship. Human. Recreated a legendary interstellar journey.

name: Ben Sisko (with TCC watermark)
lore: Shipwright Benjamin Sisko built and commanded the Baraka, a replica Bajoran lightship. Human. Recreated a legendary interstellar journey.

name: Beyor
lore: Representative of Bajoran political aides. Worked with Jaro Essa and, despite her connections to the Circle, later rose to become a minister.

name: Borum
lore: Selfless hero held prisoner on Cardassia IV. Bajoran willing to sacrifice himself to rescue Li Nalas. Never gave up hope of returning him to Bajor.

name: Deputy Quark
lore: Ferengi merchant Quark was deputized by Odo to get information on Kressari weapons movements. Keen participant in the Bajoran gratitude festival.

name: Deputy Quark
lore: Ferengi merchant Quark was deputized by Odo to get information on Kressari weapons movements. Keen participant in the Bajoran gratitude festival.

name: Deputy Quark (with TCC watermark)
lore: Ferengi merchant Quark was deputized by Odo to get information on Kressari weapons movements. Keen participant in the Bajoran gratitude festival.

name: Dohlem
lore: Typical Bajoran vedek. He collects antique Bajoran mandalas. Tried to acquire one in an auction at Quark's Bar in 2373. Interested in human culture.

name: Kira Meru
lore: Comfort woman aboard Terok Nor in 2346. Romantically involved with Dukat. Worked all hours in hope of a better life for her family.

name: Kira Meru
lore: Comfort woman aboard Terok Nor in 2346. Romantically involved with Dukat. Worked all hours in hope of a better life for her family.

name: Kira Meru (with TCC watermark)
lore: Comfort woman aboard Terok Nor in 2346. Romantically involved with Dukat. Worked all hours in hope of a better life for her family.

name: Kira Taban
lore: Husband and father who lived in the Singha refugee camp in 2346. Married to Kira Meru, who he called the bravest woman he'd ever known.

name: Minister Toran
lore: Planetary geologist in charge of the Jeraddo energy project in 2369. He ordered the forced relocation of the moon's last three residents.

name: Murjo
lore: Representative of male Bajorans who became disillusioned with the provisional government and joined the Circle. Helped kidnap Kira Nerys.

name: Vedek Kira
lore: Hero of Bajor Kira Nerys posed as a vedek to enter the Chamber of Ministers. Exposed Cardassian connections to the Circle.

name: Yarka
lore: Former vedek who lost his position in 2371 for protesting against peace with the Cardassians. Misinterpreted Trakor's third prophecy.

name: Belva
lore: Typical Cardassian dissident. Works at the central medical center on Cardassia Prime. She befriended Legate Damar to obtain information on the Dominion.

name: Danar
lore: Irascible Gul assigned to pursue Tahna Los. Captain of the Aldara. Has mapped Klingon, Romulan, and Starfleet-patrolled space for the Cardassian Union.

name: Darhe'el
lore: The Butcher of Gallitep. Gul and labor camp commandant during the occupation of Bajor. Later impersonated by former file clerk Aamin Marritza.

name: Dukat
lore: Gul of the Second Order. Abducted by the Maquis from Deep Space 9 in 2370. He easily resisted their interrogation attempts.

name: Investigator Odo
lore: Impartial changeling. Served on Terok Nor during the occupation of Bajor. An observer by necessity.

name: Jasad
lore: Representative Gul of the Cardassian Guard, Seventh Order. AttackED Deep Space 9 in 2369. Eager to stake a claim in the Gamma Quadrant.

name: Jerax
lore: Typical Glinn of the Third Battalion. Psychotropic drug test subject. Revived from stasis on Empok Nor when a Starfleet salvage team arrived in 2373.

name: Makbar
lore: Chief Archon. She believes efficient execution of Cardassian jurisprudence makes good viewing and is uplifting for the public.

name: Oran
lore: irritable Gul posted on Bajor during the occupation. Took leave on Terok Nor in 2346. Staged an incident to help Dukat win the favor of Kira Meru.

name: Quark
lore: Ferengi bartender romantically involved with Natima Lang. Former dissident who illicitly sold discounted food to oppressed Bajorans on Terok Nor.

name: Quark
lore: Ferengi bartender romantically involved with Natima Lang. Former dissident who illicitly sold discounted food to oppressed Bajorans on Terok Nor.

name: Quark (with TCC watermark)
lore: Ferengi bartender romantically involved with Natima Lang. Former dissident who illicitly sold discounted food to oppressed Bajorans on Terok Nor.

name: Rogesh
lore: Typical low-level member of the Obsidian Order. Captured during Enabran Tain's attack on the Founder homeworld and held at Internment Camp 371.

name: Tadim
lore: Representative of senior Cardassian security experts. Advised the Detapa Council. Became a dissident after observing the trial of Miles O'Brien.

name: Arjin
lore: Young Trill initiate seeking to be joined with a symbiont. Level five pilot who helped his field docent, Jadzia Dax, transport a protouniverse.

name: Benjamin Sisko
lore: Officer who reluctantly took command of Deep Space 9 in 2369. Named Emissary of the Prophets by Kai Opaka. Expert cook. Friend of Cal Hudson.

name: Hoya
lore: Benzite female. One of many runabout pilots stationed on DS9. Transported a survey team to Torga IV in 2373. Was married by Benjamin Sisko.

name: Jadzia Dax
lore: Science officer who reported to Deep Space 9 in 2369. Female Trill joined with the Dax symbiont in 2367. Very different from Curzon.

name: Jake Sisko
lore: Son of Benjamin Sisko. Apprenticed under Miles O'Brien. Helped save Deep Space 9 from its counterinsurgency program. Friend of Nog.

name: Julian Bashir
lore: Genetically enhanced chief medical officer of DS9. Helped destroy the harvester virus. Once mistook a preganglionic fiber for a postganglionic nerve.

name: Melora Pazlar
lore: Female Elaysian stellar cartographer. Visited DS9 in 2370. Romantically involved with Julian Bashir, the doctor who helped her walk in standard gravity.

name: Paulson
lore: One of many human astrophysicists aboard Deep Space 9 who studies the Bajoran wormhole. Stayed with her crew during the siege of 2370.

name: Chef Kaga
lore: Owner and cook of the Klingon restaurant aboard Deep Space 9. Often serenades his customers with Klingon folk songs. Makes excellent rokeg blood pie.

name: Altovar
lore: Vindictive criminal and Lethean thief who assaulted Julian Bashir while stealing bio-mimetic gel in 2371. He was later arrested by Odo.

name: Bhaduri
lore: Typical female Kellerun technician. Learned all she could about the harvester virus. Eagerly worked to destroy the devastating weapon in 2370.

name: Jakin
lore: Representative of male T'Lani who worked together with their former Kellerun enemies to destroy the weapon known as the harvester virus.

name: Javed
lore: Male Kellerun bodyguard of E'Tyshra and Sharat. Representative of those who intended to eliminate all knowledge of the harvester virus. Crack shot.

name: Tosk
lore: The hunted species known as Tosk had no identity outside of the hunt. He befriended Miles O'Brien after traveling through the wormhole in 2369.

name: Baraka
lore: Lightship built by Ben Sisko in 2371 from ancient Bajoran designs. Has artificial gravity. Unexpectedly traveled beyond Bajor's Denorios Belt.
game_text: Download Shipwright

name: U.S.S. Ganges
lore: One of three runabouts delivered to DS9 by the U.S.S. Enterprise. Often commanded by Miles O'Brien. Carried the harvester virus team in 2370.
game_text: Download Magnetic North

name: U.S.S. Orinoco
lore: Runabout fitted with an advanced sensor module to serve as a scientific scout vessel. Often commanded by Jadzia Dax. Registry number NCC‑72905.
game_text: Download Explore Gamma Quadrant

name: T'Lani Cruiser
lore: Munitions ship originally designed to deploy biological weapons. Used as a laboratory for the obliteration of the harvester virus in 2370.

name: Klingon Restaurant
game_text: Klingons may report here. Once each turn, any cook may report here for free (or download here in place of a normal card play; players draws no cards that turn). Klingon ships may report, dock, undock and repair at this Nor.

name: The Celestial Temple
lore: Infinity symbol Bajoran Wormhole: The Prophets of Bajor live outside of linear time.
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. At any time, any player may relocate their unique non-Treachery personnel between here and their ship or facility at the Alpha Quadrant Bajoran Wormhole. Any player with an Orb personnel here may draw an additional card at the end of each turn unless total WEAPONS>9 at any Bajoran Wormhole. No capturing or battles allowed here.

name: Angry Mob
lore: When Odo was under suspicion for murder, Bajoran nationals led by Zayra demanded that the changeling be handed over to them. Benjamin Sisko spared the constable from their "justice."
game_text: Kills a SECURITY or shape-shifter present (random selection) unless remaining Away Team has INTEGRITY>27 from up to four personnel OR STRENGTH>50. Discard dilemma.

name: Arms Deal
lore: In 2370, Quark was approached by Sakonna to arrange a covert arms deal o deliver weapons to the Maquis.
game_text: Unless Acquisition OR Vulcan with Treachery OR Smuggling OR Maquis personnel present, crew or Away Team "stopped." Discard dilemma.

name: Brief Romance
lore: Jadzia Dax became romantically involved with Meridian native Deral. Dax was so enamored she attempted to follow Deral when Meridian returned to its non-corporeal state.
game_text: Opponent specifies "male" or "female." Place on one personnel present of that gender (random selection). That personnel is "stopped" until countdown expires.

name: Chula: The Dice
lore: The throw of the dice is the foundation of chula. Each combination of Wadi symbols determines which challenge next awaits the game's participants.
game_text: To get past requires one personnel with INTEGRITY>6, another with CUNNING>7 and a third with STRENGTH>8.

name: Flaxian Assassin
lore: Valued for their professionalism, Flaxian assassins are often employed by the Tal Shiar. Retaya was sent to eliminate Garak using a combinant poison disguised as perfumes.
game_text: Unless 2 SECURITY and Biology present, kills one personnel (two if opponent has Tal Shiar in play) with three or more Skill Dot icons (random selection).

name: Lethean Telepathic Attack
lore: Altovar tried to steal biomimetic gel from the Deep Space 9 infirmary. When interrupted by Julian Bashir, he assaulted the doctor telepathically. Such attacks are usual fatal.
game_text: Unless 2 Empathy present, place on one personnel (Julian Bashir if present, otherwise random selection). Personnel is disabled (killed if CUNNING+STRENGTH>16).

name: Lockbox
lore: Quark's greed led him to critical evidence in a lockbox which ultimately solved a five-year-old murder case.
game_text: Unless Greed present, Away Team "stopped" (discard dilemma). Otherwise, score points if you solve mission this turn.

name: Oops!
lore: In 2374, an ill-prepared band of Ferengi arranged a prisoner exchange aboard Empok Nor. Their profound lack of competence made the process event more difficult than they had expected.
game_text: Unless Leadership present, kills one personnel (random selection) and "stops" all others present. To get past requires three Staff OR three Defense drones OR Nog.

name: Palukoo
lore: Large spider-like creature inhabiting the Bajoran moons. One-time food source for Resistance fighters. Caused Dax concern, since Trill/symbiont biochemistry cannot tolerate insect bites.
game_text: Unless Resistance OR ANIMAL present, "bites" a non-android (random selection). If Trill with symbiont, dies now (discard dilemma); otherwise, disabled until countdown expires.

name: Seismic Quake
lore: While on a scientific mission to planet L-S VII, Dr. Mora Pol's away team experienced a volcanic disturbance. The quake released noxious gases which cut short their research.
game_text: One Away Team member (random selection) is "stopped" if opponent's score is odd, killed otherwise. Cannot get past (shuffle back into seed cards here) unless Geology present.

name: The Three Vipers
lore: A shattered comet created a danger to ships and the Bajoran wormhole. The three silithium-laden "vipers" had to be guided through to the other side, fulfilling a Bajoran prophecy.
game_text: Ship damaged unless ENGINEER and 2 Navigation present. Even if not damaged, crew "stopped" unless SCIENCE, OFFICER and Astrophysics present. Discard dilemma.

name: Bajoran Wormhole
game_text: Requires two Bajoran Wormhole cards; each inserts into a spaceline to create a location (span 1). Play one in Alpha Quadrant (Bajor Region); download the other to Gamma Quadrant. Limit one per quadrant. While in play, any ship may move from one end to the other, then is "stopped." OR Plays at any time to nullify any card which is closing or destroying Bajoran Wormhole (discard doorway).

name: Establish Landing Protocols
lore: Diligent adherence to landing procedures is crucial to the successful operation of runabouts, shuttles and other small spacecraft.
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Each of your ships which has no staffing requirements may use 1 RANGE to land or take off once each turn. (Captain's Order.)

name: Renewal Scroll
lore: During the Bajoran Gratitude Festival, participants inscribe their troubles on small scrolls. Burning the renewal scrolls in a special brazier symbolically turns their problems to ash.
game_text: Plays if you have three or more Bajorans in play. "Burn" (discard from hand) any number of cards and "renew" (draw) an equal amount, plus two more. Discard event.

name: Sisko 197 Subroutine
lore: In anticipation of a Cardassian takeover in 2373, Benjamin Sisko sabotaged the Deep Space 9 central computer. The resulting damage hampered Terok Nor for quite some time.
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Plays on your Nor's Ops. Nor may not be moved or commandeered. Any player may nullify with 4 Computer Skill present. (Immune to Kevin Uxbridge.)

name: Treaty: Federation/Bajoran
lore: In 2369, the Bajoran provisional government applied for Federation membership. That same year, Bajor invited Starfleet to administer the recently acquired space station Terok Nor.
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Your Federation and Bajoran affiliations recognize this treaty. They can now mix and cooperate.

name: Bajoran Outpost
lore: The Bajoran homeworld is Bajor. The Bajorans establish outposts throughout their territory.
game_text: Seed one OR build where you have a Bajoran ENGINEER.

name: Deep Space 9
lore: Formerly known as Terok Nor. Now a Bajoran trading center and administrative facility run by the Federation.

name: Cardassian Outpost
lore: Cardassia Prime is the homeworld of the Cardassians. The Cardassian Union establishes outposts throughout its territory.
game_text: Seed one OR build where you have a Cardassian ENGINEER.

name: Hidden Fighter
lore: The resistance concealed small spacecraft throughout the Bajor system during the occupation. A decade later, Kira Nerys and Jadzia Dax recovered one from the abandoned Lunar V base.
game_text: Downloads one ship with no staffing requirements to your Away Team on a planet. (You may also download Establish Landing Protocols or Engage Shuttle Operations.)

name: Magnetic North
lore: Miles O'Brien used the polar magnetic field of Parada IV to shield his runabout from the sensors of pursuing ships.
game_text: Plays on your ship that has no staffing requirements if it is orbiting a planet. Prevents battles from being initiated against that ship. Discard interrupt when ship moves.

name: Wormhole Navigation Schematic
lore: The Bajoran Wormhole is the only one known to be stable. One terminus is in the Alpha Quadrant near Bajor; the other, in the Gamma Quadrant near the Idran system.
game_text: Allows your ship with SCIENCE and Navigation aboard to travel through Bajoran Wormhole without being "stopped." (Immune to Amanda Rogers) OR Nullifies The Three Vipers.

name: Characterize Neutrino Emissions
lore: Bajor Region ● Denorios Belt: Study and catalog neutrino discharge from charged plasma field.
game_text: Any number of Orb artifacts may seed here.

name: Search for Survivors
lore: Dozaria: Investigate possible crash location of Cardassian prisoner transport Ravinok.
game_text: May seed Universal Cardassian and Universal Bajoran under here.

name: Security Briefing
lore: Korma: Attend joint intelligence exchange on this Cardassian world regarding Klingon military movements.
game_text: You may play System 5 Disruptors for free here.

name: Assign Support Personnel
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. (Unique). Your "support personnel" (those who have exactly two skills, but no special skills) may report aboard your compatible ships that have two or more staffing icons. Once each turn, you may discard objective to download a "support personnel" (once per game per Personnel card title) to your matching ship that has two or more staffing icons, or to your matching facility.

name: Explore Gamma Quadrant
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. At any time, place on your ship docked at a facility in the Alpha Quadrant. If ship's crew or Away Team solves a Gamma Quadrant mission, then ship returns and docks at that facility, draw three cards and score points (discard objective).

name: File Mission Report
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. When one of your personnel has used a classification or skill to meet a mission requirement, and you have not yet attempted another mission, that personnel may "file a mission report" if unopposed at a site which allows this. Score points (discard objective). Limit one per mission.

name: Forced-Labor Camp
game_text: Seeds or plays on Cardassia IV, Ligos VII or your planet that has Geology or Archaeology as a requirement. Your Cardassian and Ferengi personnel may attempt mission. On Cardassia IV or Ligos VII, changes your mission requirements to these:SECURITY + Geology + STRENGTH>(mission points x2)After you solve, while you escort a captive on this planet, you may draw one additional card at end of each turn.

name: HQ: Secure Homeworld
game_text: Seeds or plays on a homeworld. Your Away Teams which include a personnel who matches homeworld's affiliation may attempt the mission using these requirements:Leadership x2 + SECURITY + (Honor OR Treachery) + any one attribute total > point value of missionWhen you solve mission, capture all opposing personnel on planet who do not match affiliation of homeworld.

name: Process Ore
game_text: Plays on an Ore Processing Unit. Start of each turn, if you control this Nor at a planet location and you have a matching ENGINEER or SECURITY personnel unopposed here, you may "process ore." Discard one card from hand, place bottom card of discard pile beneath draw deck or out-of-play, then draw up to two cards.

name: Rescue Personnel
game_text: Plays on your ship docked at a facility in the Alpha Quadrant. Target your Away Team on a planet which is either in a different quadrant or at a time location. If ship travels there, beams up Away Team and returns to facility, draw one card per personnel "rescued" (up to 5) and score points (discard objective). Limit one such "rescue" per location. (Unique).

name: Anara
lore: Representative of Bajoran engineering apprentices serving on Deep Space 9. Assisted Miles O'Brien with computer "pup" in 2369.

name: Bareil Antos
lore: Vedek. Follows springball religiously. Romantically involved with Kira Nerys. Began spiritual service as a gardener; still enjoys tending the grounds.

name: Colonel Day
lore: Member of Bajoran Militia and the Circle. Participated in DS9 siege of 2370. Deceived General Krim, under orders from Jaro Essa. Tried to kill Benjamin Sisko.

name: General Krim
lore: High-ranking Bajoran Militia leader. Member of the Circle. Took over Deep Space 9 in 2370, but returned the station when informed of Cardassian involvement.

name: Jaro Essa
lore: Ambitious member of Chamber of Ministers. Leader of Alliance for Global Unity, a.k.a. the Circle. Minister Jaro was allied with Vedek Winn until exposed as a traitor.

name: Minister Rozahn
lore: Typical member of the Chamber of Ministers. Has background in the sciences. Led Bajoran delegates in talks with Skrreean refugees.

name: Vedek Sorad
lore: Bajoran Vedek. Typical member of Vedek Assembly. Accompanied Minister Rozahn to Deep Space 9 in 2370 to deny Skrreean request to settle on Bajor.

name: Ari
lore: Dissident. Typical member of Cardassian underground. Loyal to Ghemor. Helped Kira Nerys escape Obsidian Order in 2371. Has hopes for a better Cardassia.

name: Borad
lore: Male trained in science and exoarchaeology. Studied the effects of stolen Bajoran orbs on the Cardassian nervous system. Had an unpleasant Orb experience.

name: Gilora Rejal
lore: Cardassian Ministry of Science member. Worked on the 2371 subspace relay project. Mistook Miles O'Brien's irritation with her as a Cardassian mating ritual.

name: Hogue
lore: Student of Natima Lang. Dissident. Member of Cardassian underground sentenced to death by Central Command. Sought refuge at Deep Space 9.

name: Kovat
lore: One of the finest public conservators on Cardassia. Assigned to defend Miles O'Brien. Deeply disturbed when he "won" the case and O'Brien was freed.

name: Parn
lore: Legate. Member of Central Command. Tried to conceal Cardassian effort to supply weapons to Demilitarized Zone colonists in 2370.

name: Plain, Simple Garak
lore: Tailor. Merchant. Elim Garak is suspected of being a spy by his friend Julian Bashir. Raises Edosian orchids as a hobby. Haggled with the Sisters of Duras.

name: Rekelen
lore: Young dissident. Forced to flee Cardassia with Natima Lang and Hogue because of her political views. Member of Cardassian underground.

name: Eris
lore: Duplicitous female agent. First Vorta to contact the Federation. Posed as an oppressed fugitive in order to win sympathy – and opportunities for espionage.

name: Founder
lore: Female member of the Dominion. Changeling. Characteristic of the members of the Great Link. Adept at mimicking the solids.

name: Inglatu
lore: Typical male Dosi. Violent and impatient negotiator. Threatened to kill Quark because of the Ferengi's annoying tenacity.

name: Ornithar
lore: Typical male Karemma official. Broker of tulaberry wine for the Dominion. Well versed in valuable metals. One-time business partner of Quark.

name: Umat'Adan
lore: Fifth. Jem'Hadar alpha assigned to Kudak'Etan. Well versed in the Alpha Quadrant anomaly. Once guarded prisoners repairing the commandeered U.S.S. Defiant.

name: Zyree
lore: Representative female member of the Dosi, a physically aggressive merchant race aligned with the Dominion. Tulaberry wine expert.

name: Enrique Muñiz
lore: Highly valued assistant to Chief O'Brien. Called "Quique" by his friends. Joked that he wants to grow up to be O'Brien – just not as old and grizzled.

name: Gideon Seyetik
lore: Gifted terraformer who in 2370 planned to crown his career by reigniting the burned-out star Epsilon 119. Failure – and modesty – do not agree well with him.

name: Ilon Tandro
lore: Klaestron dignitary. Son of Enina and General Ardelon Tandro. In 2369, used Cardassian technology to gain access to Deep Space 9 in order to kidnap Jadzia Dax.

name: Jace Michaels
lore: Representative of first officers serving in Starfleet. Assigned to the U.S.S. Odyssey. Courageously fought against the Jem'Hadar in 2370.

name: Keogh
lore: Captain of the U.S.S. Odyssey. In 2370, ordered to investigate the Jem'Hadar threat and rescue Benjamin Sisko. Knew Jadzia Dax, but not on friendly terms.

name: Michael Eddington
lore: Lt. Commander Eddington. Security officer assigned to Deep Space 9 because of Starfleet concerns about Odo. Defected to the Maquis.

name: Sarita Carson
lore: Ensign Carson is one of the many talented navigators serving Starfleet. Former member of Nova Squadron. Assigned to bridge duty aboard U.S.S. Defiant.

name: Gral
lore: Aggressive Ferengi opportunist. Diplomatically, but insistently, threatened Quark with a protection racket while Quark was briefly serving as the Grand Nagus.

name: Grand Nagus Zek
lore: Aging financial and political leader of the Ferengi Alliance. Romantically – and secretly – involved with Ishka. Admits he's not as greedy as he used to be.

name: Maihar'du
lore: Hupyrian servant. Grand Nagus Zek's bodyguard, pilot, and handkerchief valet. Took a vow to speak only to his master. As loyal as he is silent.

name: Nava
lore: Typical Ferengi entrepreneur. Took over the Arcybite gouge-mining refineries in the Clarius system. Plans to introduce synthehol to the Gamma Quadrant.

name: Pel
lore: Waiter. Female. Used synthetic lobes to appear male. Ware clothes and sought profit in violation of Ferengi law. Romantically involved with Quark – briefly.

name: T'Kar
lore: Klingon mercenary used by Verad. Helped capture Jadzia in an attempt to steal the Dax symbiont.

name: Yeto
lore: Particularly brusque Klingon who aided Verad's takeover of Deep Space 9 in 2370. Immobilized Odo in containment device.

name: Amaros
lore: Maquis terrorist. Cal Hudson's co-pilot. Helped abduct Gul Dukat, blaming him for supplying illegal weapons to Cardassians in the Demilitarized Zone.

name: E'Tyshra
lore: Female T'Lani ambassador. Worked with Sharat to end the war with the Kellerun. Schemed to eliminate everyone with knowledge of the harvester virus.

name: Kalita
lore: Longtime Maquis member. Helped Thomas Riker commandeer the U.S.S. Defiant. Helped Ro Laren steal medical supplies from the U.S.S. Enterprise.

name: Sakonna
lore: Female Vulcan. Gunrunner. Bought weapons from Quark in 2370. Helped the Maquis abduct Gul Dukat, but failed to establish a forced mindmeld with him.

name: Sharat
lore: Kellerun ambassador. Helped negotiate cease fire with the T'Lani. Worked on project to eliminate harvester virus and associated technology in 2370.

name: Ty Kajada
lore: Female Kobliad security officer. Representative of law enforcement agents found on non-aligned worlds. Pursued the criminal Rao Vantika for 20 years.

name: Assault Vessel
lore: Mainstay of the Bajoran Militia. During the 2370 coup attempted by the Circle, assault vessels commanded by General Krim and Colonel Day invaded Deep Space 9.

name: Galor
lore: Military spacecraft used by the Cardassian Union. The type-3 Galor-class warship is the backbone of the Cardassian fleet.

name: Patrol Ship
lore: Common patrol vessel of the Cardassian Union. Uses the same hull as the Cardassian shuttlecraft, but boasts a much higher performance profile.

name: Karemman Vessel
lore: The Karemma conduct trade operations for the Dominion. Their vessels can be found throughout the Gamma Quadrant. Hanok commanded one.

name: U.S.S. Danube
lore: Class of runabout often named for Terran rivers. First commissioned in 2368. The following years, the U.S.S. Enterprise delivered three Danube-class vessels to DS9.
game_text: Reports for free to Docking Pads.

name: U.S.S. Defiant
lore: NX-74205. Built to battle Borg. Recommissioned to oppose the Dominion. First ship to test ablative armor and quantum torpedoes. Captained by Benjamin Sisko.

name: Bajoran Shrine
game_text: Prylars, Vedeks and Kais may report here. Once each turn, any player who has a Prylar, Vedek, or Kai unopposed here with any other Bajoran may "conduct services": discard one card from hand, place bottom card of discard pile beneath draw deck or out-of-play, then draw one card (or two if any Orb artifact is present). Unless station is under Bajoran or Federation control, Shrine is suspended and may be destroyed by any personnel using a disruptor at an adjacent site.

name: Cargo Bay
game_text: Smuggling, Acquisition and Non-Aligned Navigation personnel may report here (or download here in place of a normal card play; player draws no cards that turn). Once each turn, if a freighter, transport or Ferengi ship's crew member completes a "cargo run" (brings a non-weapon Equipment card here from another facility), for each mission passed (except starting and ending locations) owner may draw a card or download a Gold-Pressed Latinum here. (Once per game per Equipment card title.)

name: Commander's Office
game_text: Once each turn, any player who has a matching Command OFFICER unopposed here, may in place of one card draw, download to hand one Captain's Order card. Matching OFFICER personnel may file mission reports here. This site is always the "innermost" site of any Nor (may not separate Ops from any other site.

name: Docking Pads
game_text: Any ship with no staffing requirements may report, dock (land) and undock (take off) here if ship is compatible with station's affiliation OR crew includes a V.I.P. OR player controlling ship has a Computer Skill personnel present at this site unopposed (just before undocking, that personnel may board ship). Player controlling station may, once per game, download Establish Landing Protocols. Capacity:6 ships, Tractor Beam.

name: Docking Ports
game_text: Any ship with fewer than three staffing icons may report, dock and undock here if ship is compatible with station's affiliation OR crew includes a V.I.P. OR player controlling ship has a Computer Skill personnel present at this site unopposed (just before undocking, that personnel may board ship). Freighters and transports report for free here.Capacity: 9 ships, Tractor Beam.

name: Docking Pylons
game_text: Any ship with fewer than five staffing icons may dock and undock here if ship is compatible with station's affiliation OR crew includes a V.I.P. OR player controlling ship has a Computer Skill personnel present at this site unopposed (just before undocking, that personnel may board ship). Ships may not report here but may repair here.Capacity: 6 ships, Tractor Beam.

name: Garak's Tailor Shop
game_text: Obsidian Order personnel may report here (for free if any Garak). Once each turn, any player who has a personnel unopposed here who has both Obsidian Order and Treachery may glance at top card of opponent's draw deck. Also, any player who doesn't control station but has Obsidian Order unopposed here may report Cardassian personnel and Cardassian-compatible Equipment cards here.

name: Guest Quarters
game_text: If unoccupied, any non-Borg V.I.P. may report here regardless of affiliation. Once each turn, any player who has V.I.P. unopposed here may, in place of one card draw, draw two cards and place on of them beneath draw deck. (Not cumulative.)

name: Holosuite
game_text: This site must be placed adjacent to Quark's Bar (or another Holosuite. Has a Holodeck. Holoprogram cards may be played here (limit one; station controller may discard it during their turn). Hologram Equipment cards and compatible Hologram personnel may report here, and may be transferred directly to/from owner's ship docked at this station.

name: Infirmary
game_text: Compatible MEDICAL-classification personnel, MEDICAL-related Equipment cards and I.P. Scanner may report here. Once each turn, any MEDICAL personnel unopposed here may "revive" a personnel present who was disabled by a Hypospray (revived personnel is no longer disabled). Matching MEDICAL personnel may file mission reports here.

name: Ops
game_text: Compatible OFFICER-classification personnel may report here. Any player may, in place of their normal card play, download to an unopposed site on this station one card which may play there (if reporting a ship or personnel, must be of matching affiliation); player draws no cards that turn. Any Computer Skill personnel unopposed here may commandeer station.

name: Ops: Mirror Universe
game_text: Cards with same Klingon Cardassian Alliance or Terran Empire icon as this Nor are considered to match its affiliation for purposes related to its sites. Compatible OFFICER-classification personnel may report here. Any player may, in place of their normal card play, download to an unopposed site on this station one card which may play there (if reporting a ship or personnel, must be of matching affiliation); player draws no cards that turn. Any Computer Skill personnel unopposed here may commandeer station.

name: Ore Processing Unit
game_text: Compatible ENGINEER-classification personnel and ENGINEER-related Equipment cards may report here. If Automated Security System on Ops at this station, personnel may not move to here from an adjacent site, or vice versa.This unit does not process ore when station is under Federation or Bajoran control.

name: Promenade Shops
game_text: Non-Borg CIVILIAN personnel may report here regardless of affiliation. Any player who has a non-Borg personnel present may probe:Event, Interrupt, Equipment : Shopping. Draw probe card.Objective, Cardassian, Klingon : Brawl. Must immediately initiate a personnel battle (if opposed by non-Borg) at this site.

name: Quark's Bar
game_text: Morn and Ferengi may report here. Once each turn, a bartender, a dabo girl, a waiter, any Quark or any Rom may report here for free (or download here in place of a normal card play; player draws no cards that turn). Any player who has Morn unopposed here may draw an additional card at end of each turn. Any player who kills any waiters or dabo girls here in battle must discard two cards for each. Ferengi ships may report, dock, undock and repair at this Nor.

name: Science Lab
game_text: Compatible SCIENCE-classification personnel, SCIENCE-related Equipment cards, I.P. Scanner and any PADDs may report here. Once each turn, if station at a Space mission and player who controls station has a SCIENCE personnel unopposed here, that player may scan bottom seed card under mission. Matching SCIENCE personnel may file mission reports here.

name: Security Holding Cell
game_text: Has a Brig. Once each turn, player who controls station may download Brainwash, Interrogation or Torture to a captive held in this Brig if that player has a Tal Shiar, Obsidian Order, Resistance or Section 31 personnel (or a personnel who has SECURITY and Treachery) unopposed here.

name: Security Office
game_text: Compatible SECURITY-classification personnel and hand weapons may report here. Whenever a personnel battle was just initiated on this station, any player's personnel here, if one has SECURITY, may move there (if possible) and join the battle. Matching SECURITY personnel may file mission reports here.

name: Contain Boarding Parties
game_text: Seeds or plays on Deep Space 9 ; you may download Sisko 197 Subroutine . Twice per game, when opponent voluntarily initiates battle aboard, you may download up to six DS9 personnel (each must be Federation or Bajoran), and/or one hand weapon to sites aboard where those cards may report. Does not count down during the first turn of the game.

name: Trust the Prophets
game_text: Seeds on table; you may download The Celestial Temple. The Celestial Temple ignores WEAPONS of Deep Space 9 (and any ships docked there). Compatible DS9 Federation except (Original Series) cards are considered to match Deep Space 9's affiliation for purposes related to its sites.

name: We Need You Here
game_text: Seeds or plays on Commander's Office. If your Reshape the Quadrant is in play, you may ignore restrictions of site(s) on this station which instruct you to "draw no cards that turn." Once each turn, in place of a card draw, you may download a site to this station. (Captain's Order.)

name: Herbert
lore: Representative transporter officer aboard the U.S.S. Enterprise. He held the rank of ensign in the early years of the flagship's mission.

name: Lieutenant Ballard
lore: Typical scientist and teacher in the U.S.S. Enterprise's primary school. She expressed concern to Data about Lal's ability to fit in.

name: Riva
lore: Respected mediator. Deaf and mute Ramatin male. Taught sign language to warring factions on Solais V. Gave the Klingons a word for "peacemaker."

name: A Pleasant Surprise
lore: Brothers Krit and Nahsk were Morn's co-conspirators in the Lissepian Mother's Day Heist. Their run-in with Quark could have been much less pleasant.
game_text: To get past, "stop" a personnel with CUNNING>6 and either Diplomacy or Treachery (random selection).

name: Deliberate Tactical Error
lore: Keevan ensured his own survival by betraying Remata'Klan and his fellow Jem'Hadar, sending them into a deadly trap.
game_text: Half of all Universal personnel in Away Team (random selection, round down) are killed (erased if Hologram). To get past requires two leaders OR two Command OR two Defense.

name: Dramatis Personae
lore: Soltah'na energy spheres caused the crew of DS9 to play out an ancient power struggle: scheming, maneuvering, and plotting to eliminate their former friends.
game_text: "Stops" all personnel in crew or Away Team named in lore by another personnel present. Discard dilemma.

name: Maquis Vendetta
lore: As hard to catch as a Norpin falcon, crafty and cunning Maquis leader Michael Eddington was able to stay one step ahead of the dogged pursuit of his former commanding officer.
game_text: To get past, "stop" a Leadership personnel (random selection). If that personnel has OFFICER or SECURITY, randomly select two additional personnel to be "stopped."

name: Protestations of Innocence
lore: After years of conflict and military aggression, colonists near the Cardassian-Federation border often doubted the sincerity of Cardassian negotiators
game_text: To get past requires INTEGRITY>28 (INTEGRITY>42 if you initiated battle this game; INTEGRITY>63 if you voluntarily initiated battle).

name: Recurring Injury
lore: While playing to maintain his darts winning streak at Quark's, Miles O'Brien aggravated an old kayaking injury, necessitating shoulder surgery and forfeiting his darts game.
game_text: To get past, one personnel with Biology OR MEDICAL (opponent's choice) must be "stopped." Nullify with a personnel who has either 2 Biology OR 3 MEDICAL.

name: Sabotaged Plasma Conduit
lore: To resist her Maquis captors, Kira Nerys blew out two plasma conduits, forcing the U.S.S. Defiant to seek refuge in a nebula until the cloaking device could be repaired.
game_text: To get past requires 2 Computer Skill and Physics OR Computer Skill and 2 Physics.

name: Scapegoat
lore: To avoid escalating violence between Cardassian and Federation settlers, Cardassian Central Command blamed Gul Dukat for supplying weapons to the Demilitarized Zone.
game_text: One personnel (random selection) is killed unless you "stop" a personnel with V.I.P. or Anthropology. To get past requires INTEGRITY>24 remaining.

name: Unscheduled "Assistance"
lore: The unexpected arrival of a Klingon fleet to defend DS9 against the changeling threat led to issues with docking schedules, shore leave, and unauthorized "inspections."
game_text: Opponent chooses two locations. To get past requires CUNNING>X, where X=15 times the number of your ships at those locations.

name: Determined to Stay
lore: Many colonists living in the Demilitarized Zone refused to abandon the worlds they had made their homes, despite pressure from the Federation and Cardassian governments.
game_text: Plays on your unattempted Demilitarized Zone Region mission. When your Maquis personnel solve, if no opposing ship is at this mission, you may draw up to five cards.

name: Organized Terrorist Activities
lore: In 2370, the Maquis blew up the Cardassian freighter Bok'Nor to prevent the transportation of additional weapons to Cardassian colonists in the Demilitarized Zone.
game_text: Plays if you have eight DS9 Maquis personnel in play. Damage an undamaged ship in (or adjacent to) a region (once per game per Ship card title). Discard event.

name: Bleed Resources
game_text: Plays on your Maquis, TNG Romulan, or DS9 Cardassian personnel. When this personnel helps solve a mission, you may choose one: Examine opponent's hand and choose two of those cards to be discarded OR Opponent places three cards (random selection) from hand on top of his or her draw deck OR Opponent discards the top four cards of his or her draw deck.

name: Defending Their Homes
game_text: Plays on table; you may download They Call Themselves the Maquis. Once each turn, one TNG Maquis personnel may report for free OR you may download For the Cause to your Demilitarized Zone Region mission. Discard if you have a Treaty in play.

name: Learning Curve
game_text: Plays on table. At the end of each of your turns, if you played two or more Maquis personnel this turn, you may place two cards from the top of your draw deck face down on this incident. You may play Maquis cards from this incident as though they were in your hand. At any time, you may place this card and each card atop it beneath your draw deck to draw that many cards. (Unique.)

name: Not so Demilitarized
game_text: Plays on table; you may download They Call Themselves the Maquis. Once each turn, while all your facilities are Maquis one DS9Maquis personnel may report for free OR you may download For the Cause to your Badlands or Demilitarized Zone Region mission. You may not play Espionage cards.

name: They Call Themselves the Maquis
game_text: Seeds or plays on table; you may download The Art of Diplomacy. Your Maquis cards may mix and, if ever attacked, have no affiliation attack restrictions. Your Maquis ships are immune to Navigate Plasma Storms. Your equipment, Maquis personnel, and Maquis ships may report to your Liberty or to a Badlands or Demilitarized Zone Region Planet mission; once each turn, one such unique personnel may do so for free.

name: Used to Being Outnumbered
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Condor-class ships may be used by Bajoran or Federation. In the Badlands or Demilitarized Zone Regions, opponent's ATTACK total must be more than double your Condor-class ship's DEFENSE total to score a hit, and more than triple to score a direct hit. While your Condor-class ship is moving within a region, it is RANGE +2.

name: You Could be Invaluable
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. At the start of a mission attempt involving only your DS9 Maquis personnel, you may reveal the top card of opponent's draw deck. If it is a personnel neither player has in play, opponent reports them to your attempting crew or Away Team (under your control; they gain Maquis). Return personnel to opponent's hand (if still in play) at end of mission attempt. (Unique.)

name: Stalling for Time
lore: Ro Laren was able to maintain Jean-Luc Picard's confidence in her loyalty just long enough to conceal her defection to the Maquis and help her new allies evade Starfleet's trap.
game_text: Plays once each turn on any location if you have three TNG Maquis personnel in play. Opponent chooses one of their personnel here to return to hand.

name: Divert Attention
lore: Badlands Region ● Rendezvous Point: Distract adversary to allow equipment theft.
game_text: Span -2 for Maquis ships.

name: Expose Secret Buildup
lore: Orias System: Reveal military construction at unsanctioned facility.

name: Supply Terrorists
lore: Demilitarized Zone Region ● Portas V: Broker sale of biogenic storage containers.

name: For the Cause
game_text: Plays on your Badlands or Demilitarized Zone Region mission. Your Maquis personnel may attempt this mission and may replace all levels of one requirement with:Leadership + SECURITY + CUNNING>30

name: The Only Way Home
game_text: Seeds on table. When your Maquis personnel solve a Delta Quadrant Planet mission, relocate your Maquis personnel to your Maquis ship there, then relocate ship to any Alpha Quadrant mission. For the rest of the game, your Non-Aligned Delta Quadrant personnel are attributes all +2 and may report to your Maquis ships.

name: Ro Laren
lore: Maquis sympathizer and Bajoran officer aboard the U.S.S. Enterprise. Found a new father figure in Macias. Betrayed Jean-Luc Picard's trust in her.

name: Ro Laren
lore: Maquis sympathizer and Bajoran officer aboard the U.S.S. Enterprise. Found a new father figure in Macias. Betrayed Jean-Luc Picard's trust in her.

name: Ro Laren (with TCC watermark)
lore: Maquis sympathizer and Bajoran officer aboard the U.S.S. Enterprise. Found a new father figure in Macias. Betrayed Jean-Luc Picard's trust in her.

name: Tabor
lore: Apoplectic Bajoran haunted by the screams of Crell Moset's victims. Chakotay helped him focus his rage. Skilled holoprogrammer. Friend of Jor.

name: Tabor
lore: Apoplectic Bajoran haunted by the screams of Crell Moset's victims. Chakotay helped him focus his rage. Skilled holoprogrammer. Friend of Jor.

name: Tabor (with TCC watermark)
lore: Apoplectic Bajoran haunted by the screams of Crell Moset's victims. Chakotay helped him focus his rage. Skilled holoprogrammer. Friend of Jor.

name: Cal Hudson
lore: Starfleet's attaché to the Federation's Demilitarized Zone colonies. Friend of Benjamin Sisko. Widower who found new purpose as leader of a Maquis cell.

name: George Sanders
lore: Captain dispatched to apprehend Michael Eddington. Asked Benjamin Sisko to save him a seat at Eddington's court-martial. Calls San Francisco home.

name: Niles
lore: Pilot and security officer typical of those who secretly support the Maquis. Captured Gul Dukat on Deep Space 9 on Cal Hudson's orders. Drinks lattes.

name: Tamal
lore: Technician and former petty officer aboard the U.S.S. Gandhi. Recruited into the Maquis by Thomas Riker. Enjoys studying early Earth warp technology.

name: Thomas Riker
lore: Defiant leader and starship thief. Poses as William T. Riker. Commanded the Stolen Defiant on raids in Cardassian space. Resents his transporter double.

name: Tom Paris
lore: "Starfleet observer" who helped U.S.S. Voyager track his former Maquis comrades in the Badlands. Talented pilot. Has a mercenary spirit.

name: Tuvok
lore: Undercover Vulcan who infiltrated Chakotay's Maquis cell. Former archery teacher at the Vulcan Institute for Defensive Arts. Has three sons and a daughter.

name: Bill Samuels
lore: Maquis saboteur William Patrick Samuels was a farmer from Volan II. Covertly planted a protomatter implosion device aboard the Bok'Nor.

name: Brathaw
lore: Male Bolian engineer. Helped smuggle goods to the Maquis. First officer who often commanded the freighter S.S. Xhosa in Kasidy Yates' absence.

name: Kalita
lore: Typical pilot in Macias' Maquis cell. Suspicious of everyone at first, but impressed by Ro Laren during a supply raid. Later worked with Thomas Riker.

name: Kasidy Yates
lore: Conflicted captain romantically involved with Benjamin Sisko. Served prison time for transporting medical supplies to the Maquis.

name: Kobb
lore: Representative of female colonists living on Volan III in 2370. Skilled administrator and colonial leader. Unlucky in love.

name: M'vil
lore: One of many Klingon seeking glory outside the Klingon Empire. She sympathized with the grievances of the Maquis.

name: M'vil
lore: One of many Klingon seeking glory outside the Klingon Empire. She sympathized with the grievances of the Maquis.

name: M'vil (with TCC watermark)
lore: One of many Klingon seeking glory outside the Klingon Empire. She sympathized with the grievances of the Maquis.

name: Macias
lore: Grizzled leader of a Maquis cell. Former resident of Juhraya. Trusted Ro Laren despite Kalita's caution. Knows someone will take his place. Likes hasperat.

name: Quark
lore: Intriguing Ferengi eager to please Sakonna. Became a temporary arms dealer to the Maquis.

name: Quark
lore: Intriguing Ferengi eager to please Sakonna. Became a temporary arms dealer to the Maquis.

name: Quark (with TCC watermark)
lore: Intriguing Ferengi eager to please Sakonna. Became a temporary arms dealer to the Maquis.

name: Rebecca Sullivan
lore: Resistance fighter. One of the few Maquis to survive Jem'Hadar attacks in 2373. Wife of Michael Eddington. Bluffed about a cloaked missile strike.

name: Reide
lore: Demilitarized Zone colonist typical of those who joined the Maquis. Enjoys fishing. Believes his family has bad luck.

name: Santos
lore: Freedom fighter who kidnapped and then recruited Ro Laren into the Maquis. Led his squadron in an attack on a Yridian convoy. Friend of Macias.

name: Sark
lore: One of many colonists living on Volan III in the Demilitarized Zone. Bolian member of Cal Hudson's Maquis cell. He helped plan Dukat's kidnapping.

name: Shankar
lore: Maquis soldier always prepared to defend against Cardassian attacks. Assigned by Amaros to stand guard over Dukat after the Gul's abduction.

name: Stolen Defiant
lore: The U.S.S. Defiant was commandeered by the Maquis in 2371 to attack Cardassian forces.
game_text: WEAPONS and SHIELDS +3 vs. Cardassian

name: Cosette
lore: Commanded by Ro Laren under the watchful eye of Kalita. Participated in the theft of medical supplies from the U.S.S. Enterprise in 2370.
game_text: Attributes all +2 in Demilitarized Zone Region.

name: Guingouin
lore: Maquis raider commanded by Michael Eddington in retaliatory strikes against Cardassian colonies. Uses many components salvaged from ambushed ships.
game_text: Once each turn, may land or take off using 1 RANGE.

name: Maquis Raider
lore: Versatile class of ship designed early in the 24th century by the Federation. Crew complement can vary widely.

name: S.S. Xhosa
lore: Independent freighter commanded by Kasidy Yates. Operated under contract for Bajor's Ministry of Commerce in 2372. Smuggled Maquis supplies.

name: Val Jean
lore: 30-year old vessel commanded by Captain Chakotay. Like many Maquis ships, has become many names. Also known as the Liberty.
game_text: Attributes all +2 in Badlands Region.

name: Close Quarters Combat
