lore: Typical Terran security guard often assigned to the phaser control room on the I.S.S. Enterprise. Loyal to Security Chief Sulu. Confronted Mr. Scott in 2267.

name: Farrell
lore: Trusted bodyguard of James Tiberius Kirk. Terran who helped identify plundered alien artifacts. Has an uncle who works in espionage. Wary of Haadok.

name: Haadok
lore: First Officer Spock's Vulcan bodyguard aboard the I.S.S. Enterprise. Perplexed by his captain's aberrant, illogical behavior in 2267. Tolerates Farrell.

name: Julian Bashir
lore: Genetically enhanced doctor from DS9. Put to work as a slave by Overseer Odo in the mirror universe.

name: Lt. Uhura
lore: Linguist quick to learn the rules of the game in the mirror universe. She distracted Security Chief Sulu.

name: Mr. Scott
lore: Wry Scotsman. Mirror universe technology variations were nothing Scotty couldn't handle.

name: Yeoman Vaughn
lore: Typical Terran yeoman aboard the I.S.S. Enterprise. Aspires to become a "captain's woman." Organizes shipboard social activities to cultivate allies.

name: Grand Nagus Zek
lore: Ferengi who sought new opportunities in the mirror universe. Briefly romantically involved with the Intendant. Counted on Quark to help him.

name: Quark
lore: Bartender who traveled with Ezri and Rom to the mirror universe in 2375 to rescue Grand Nagus Zek.

name: Rom
lore: Former waiter on DS9. Husband of Leeta. Worked with Quark to rescue Grand Nagus Zek from the mirror universe. Sabotaged a stolen cloaking device.

name: Baze
lore: Halkan council representative in the mirror universe. Derives his wisdom from his people's history of total peace.

name: Minister Tharn
lore: Halkan ethically compelled to preserve the pacifist ways of his people by refusing Terran demands to mine their dilithium. Tharn led the Halkan Council.

name: A Passionate Vulcan
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Banished from Vulcan, Sybok urged people to face their pain and draw strength from it.
game_text: Unless Mindmeld and Anthropology present, opponent may download (or relocate) Sybok here and may download Release This Pain onto one of your personnel present (random selection). Discard dilemma.

name: Attack of the Drones
lore: The Son'a used transporter drones to forcibly relocate anyone interfering with their harvest of metaphasic radiation.
game_text: Opponent may download up to three Transporter Drones to this planet. Three personnel (random selection) face the Drones as if in personnel battle, then are stopped; lose 3 points for each personnel captured.

name: Exact Change
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: Admiral Kirk and Captain Spock found their progress on 20th-century Earth slowed by obscure and archaic financial practices.
game_text: To get past requires exactly 50 CUNNING from all Away Team members. May nullify by stopping two personnel (opponent's choice) until end of next turn.

name: Jol Yichu'!
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: With the Genesis Planet collapsing, Admiral Kirk impersonated Kruge in order to secure his and Captain Spock's escape aboard a Klingon Bird-of-Prey. "Activate beam!"
game_text: Unless Anthropology in Away Team and Transporter Skill on your staffed ship in orbit, two personnel (opponent's choice) are killed.

name: Amargosa Observatory
lore: Solar research post. Secretly housed Dr. Tolian Soran's trilithium missile project.
game_text: Plays at Amargosa. Once per game, if your Dr. Tolian Soran is aboard, you may change the direction of The Nexus, then download Trilithium Weapon (as if earned).

name: Combined Task Force
game_text: Plays on table; you may download Treaty: Federation/Klingon. Your DS9 cards may initiate battle against any non-Federation and non-Klingon target. You may only report ships or personnel that are Federation or Klingon. Once each turn, one DS9 (except TOS or Mirror Universe) personnel may report for free OR you may nullify Homefront present with your V.I.P. Nullified if you control a Nor.

name: The Warp Five Program
game_text: Seeds or plays on Seat of Starfleet. Mission specialists you download may download here. Just after your Starfleet personnel reports here, you may relocate them to your NX-class ship in the Alpha Quadrant. If the first mission you solve is Space mission, score 10 points. Nullified if you have more than one ship (except shuttlepods) in play.

name: Khan!
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: "...KHAN!"
game_text: ''''Just after an opponent scores bonus points, nullify those points. OR Nullfies The Genesis Effect.

name: Vanquish Enemy
lore: Mutara Region • Mutara Nebula: Defeat nemesis among starship-debilitating ionized gases.
game_text: Once per game, may Tactic Draw opponent's ship here.

name: Facilitate Peace Talks
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
game_text: Seeds or plays on Khitomer; download Treaty: Federation/Klingon. Your TOS Classic Films personnel may attempt mission with the following requirements: Dipomacy x2 + Leadership x2 + INTEGRITY>40 When you solve, you may download up to two TOS Classic Films personnel of different affiliations here.

name: Set a Course for Home
game_text: Seeds or plays on Earth. If you have solved two Delta Quadrant missions, your U.S.S. Voyager may move between any spaceline end and this mission using its full RANGE. Your Away Team of only Delta Quadrant Federation personnel may attempt this mission with the following requirements: Navigation x2 + OFFICER x2 + CUNNING>40

name: Alien Conspiracy
lore: After years of oppression by their Terran colleagues, the powerful threat of the Starship Defiant incited many within the Empire to rise up.
game_text: Choose one personnel in crew or Away Team for each Dissident your opponent has in play. Your opponent chooses up to two of those personnel to be killed.

name: Archaic Ritual
lore: Many cultures have elaborate ceremonies. Jean-Luc Picard used the ja'chuq, a length recitation of victories, to delay the selection of a new Klingon High Council leader.
game_text: To get past, two personnel in crew or Away Team with the highest STRENGTH and one additional personnel with highest remaining CUNNING are stopped.

name: Multitronic Menace
lore: Reliance on automation can be dangerous. In 2268, shipboard tests of the M-5 multitronic unit with a skeleton crew resulted in the unit defending itself with deadly force.
game_text: If ship has any attribute > number of personnel in crew, kills a unique personnel (random selection) for each of this ship's staffing icons. Mission continues.

name: Quality of Life
lore: While Dr. Farallon`s exocomps proved useful as tools, their potential sentience led to conflict over whether they should be sacrificed to save humanoid lives.
game_text: Opponent may draw a card for each Equipment present. To get past requires an Equipment (your choice, discarded) OR Cybernetics and 2 Law OR 4 ENGINEER OR Exocomp.

name: Reflections
lore: Faced with time-consuming repairs, Chief Engineer Tucker was initially unaware that the sabotage was due to a suggestion implanted in his mind by Commander T'Pol.
game_text: Randomly stops half of crew (round down). If opponent has no cards in hand, those personnel are killed instead. Nullify with a personnel with Mindmeld and Treachery.

name: Suliban Cloaking Device
lore: In the 22nd century, cloaking devices were rare. The Suliban were one of the few sources of such technology.
game_text: May report to your 22nd Century ship (for free if Suliban). While aboard your ship, that ship has a Cloaking Device. Counts down only if you have any cards in hand.

name: A Real Game
lore: What constitutes a winning hand in fizzbin depends on the day of the week and whether it's dark outside. It's one of the few card games that requires its own glossary.
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Players need an additional 10 points to win the game. Nullified if any player has solved or scouted three or more missions. (Cumulative.)

name: Amanda Rogers: Protector
lore: Keeping her powers secret, Amanda Rogers protected the crew of the U.S.S. Enterprise from minor mishaps. A crisis in engineering ultimately forced her to reveal herself.

name: Captain's Perogative
lore: Although Starfleet regulations normally prohibit a starship commander from leading away missions, a captain can ignore such directives if it suits their interests or experience.
game_text: Plays on table. While you have no cards in hand, if the matching commander of a ship you have in play helps solve a mission, score 5 points. (Captain's Order.)

name: Loyal Subordinate
lore: Although junior officers can be impulsive and exuberant, a commanding officer relies on their quick reactions for timely protection.
game_text: Plays on table. While you have no cards in hand, your Command personnel cannot be captured or killed by opponent's dilemmas; stopped instead. (Captain's Order.)

name: Security Drills
lore: In times of crisis, those who wear the uniform have to be prepared for any contingency.
game_text: Plays on table. Name a skill (or two skills if you have no cards in hand). Your Deep Space NineFederation and MACO personnel may use 2 SECURITY as the named skill(s).

name: Technical Wizardry
lore: With help from Geordi La Forge, Jean-Luc Picard was able to steal Ardra's magic tricks, revealing her fraud and rendering the "mythical being" powerless.
game_text: Plays on table. While you have no cards in hand, your events are immune to Kevin Uxbridge.

name: Terran Flagship: Predator
lore: The capture of the technologically sophisticated Starship Defiant significantly advanced the Terran Empire.
game_text: Plays on your unique, non-Mirror Quadrant ship at a Mirror Quadrant location. Ship gains Mirror Quadrant and Terran Empire, is attributes all +4, replaces each staffing icon with Terran Empire, and once per game may nullify a Planet dilemma here (if at a Mirror Quadrant mission).

name: Tyranny
lore: Powerful dictatorships like the Terran Empire have traditionally gained additional manpower by creating a pervasive climate of fear.
game_text: Plays on table. At the start of your turn, if you had no cards in hand when your turn began, you may download to hand a Mirror Quadrant 22nd Century card or an Alternate Universe event. (Cumulative.)

name: Will You Kindly Die?
lore: Denying the Tholian "visitor" the extreme environmental conditions it required to survive proved to be an effective way of extracting information - and killing the troublesome guest.
game_text: Plays on table. Once each turn, if you have no cards in hand, you may make your opponent choose and discard one of their universal personnel in play.

name: Imperial Outpost
lore: In the mirror universe, the Terran system is the heart of the Terran Empire. The Terran Empire establishes outposts throughout its territory.
game_text: Seed one OR build where you have a Starfleet Terran Empire ENGINEER. Download One Small Step

name: Imperial Palace
lore: The seat of the Terran Empire has been located in numerous places including San Francisco and Kyoto.
game_text: Seeds or plays on Mirror Quadrant 2155 Earth. Once per turn, one Starfleet personnel may report for free here. (Not duplicatable.)

name: Starfleet Outpost
lore: As humanity explored further into deep space, Starfleet established outposts throughout its expanding territory.
game_text: Seed one OR build where you have a Starfleet ENGINEER. Download UFP: One Small Step

name: Radiation Monitoring
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Discard a card from hand to make your Starfleet Terran Empire ship attributes +1 until the start of your next turn (limit +3). Also, while you have no cards in hand, you may ignore your opponent's Containment Field when using a Download on your Starfleet Terran Empire personnel.

name: UFP: One Small Step
game_text: Plays on table. Your Starfleet personnel may attempt non-homeworld Federation missions. While all your personnel are Alternate Universe and the same affiliation, each of your personnel (and ships) are CUNNING (or RANGE) +1. OR Seeds or plays on a time location. Any ship may move between this time location and another time location in the same quadrant with a matching year by using 4 RANGE.

name: Watch Dog
game_text: Plays on table if you have three Starfleet Terran Empire personnel in play. Once each turn, you may play an Event with a countdown for free. Place any cards drawn at the end of your turn face down beneath this incident. At the start of your turn, take all cards from beneath this incident into hand. While you have cards in hand, your personnel lose their first-listed skill. (Unique.)

name: Deliver Ancient Artifact
lore: Vulcan: Repatriate historic object to reliquary on the Vulcan homeworld.
game_text: None

name: Incapacitate Inhabitants
lore: Janus VI: Subdue menacing life-forms disrupting mining operations on resource-rich planet.
game_text: * -5 points if opponent's 3 MEDICAL here.

name: Monitor Population
lore: Sector 001 Region • Earth: Conduct covert cultural research on former Starfleet homeworld.
game_text: None

name: Observe Spatial Coordinates
lore: Spatial Interphase: Covertly monitor former incursion site for further transdimensional incidents.
game_text: * +5 points if ship has Cloaking Device.

name: Sabotage Biosphere
lore: Moab IV: Destabilize independent Terran colony reliant on artificial habitat.
game_text: * +5 points if opponent's objective in play.

name: Unsanctioned Attack
lore: Dissident-controlled space: Bypass chain of command to coordinate strike on subversives.
game_text: None

name: Assert Authority
game_text: Seeds on table. If, at the end of your turn, your staffed ship with a unique Mirror Quadrant 22nd Century personnel aboard is at a mission opponent seeded (or a Universal mission), objective complete (once per game): Place objective in point area, place a copy of the unique personnel (the Contender) beneath objective from outside the game, draw a card, and you may download Betray Captain.

name: Betray Captain
game_text: Plays on table if your Assert Authority complete. If, at the end of your turn, your ship is at your unique mission with its matching commander and the Contender aboard, kill that commander; objective complete (once per game): Place objective in point area, the Contender is now the matching commander of that ship, draw two cards, and you may download Consolidate Power.

name: Consolidate Power
game_text: Plays on table if your Betray Captain complete. If you just won a battle involving at least two of your ships and the Contender, objective complete (once per game): Place objective in point area, the Contender is now an Admiral, your ship the Contender is aboard is attributes all +2, draw three cards, and you may download Declare New Sovereign.

name: Declare New Sovereign
game_text: Plays on table if your Consolidate Power complete. When the Contender helps solve a matching homeworld, objective complete (once per game): Place objective in point area, the Contender is now an Emperor (or Empress), and once each turn you may stop that personnel to either draw four cards OR download a personnel.

name: Carri
lore: Self-taught Terran biochemist serving in Mr. Sisko's crew. Typical female mercenary. Cook who often mediates shipboard conflicts. Plays the flute.

name: Dr. Cochrane
lore: First Terran to make contact with an alien species. Zefram Cochrane likes rum, country music, guns, and women in uniform. Demanded a statue.

name: Haon Obst
lore: Typical humanoid slave laborer reporting to Slar. His knowledge of alien cultures and anatomy did little to aid the reverse-engineering of the Starship Defiant.

name: Admiral Black
lore: Typical military leader. Briefly served as president of the Imperial Commission for Loyalty. Terran commander of the I.S.S. Avenger.

name: Captain Forrest
lore: Confident captain in the Terran Empire. Maxwell Forrest has friends in high places. Romantically involved with Comm Officer Sato.

name: Chief Engineer Tucker
lore: Talented Terran engineer recommended for his position by Admiral Black. Charles Tucker III has absorbed dangerously high levels of delta radiation.

name: Chief Surgeon Phlox
lore: Sadistic physiologist whose finesse was useful to the Empire. The Denobulan doctor Phlox was courted by the rebels and became a reluctant dissident.

name: Comm Officer Sato
lore: Hoshi Sato seized command of the Starship Defiant and declared herself Empress of the Terran Empire.

name: Commander Archer
lore: Covetous commander of the Starship Defiant. A soldier all his life, Jonathan Archer was romantically involved with Comm Officer Sato.

name: Commander T'Pol
lore: Dutiful commander. Vulcan dissident loyal to Captain Forrest. T'Pol was romantically involved with Chief Engineer Tucker during her last Pon farr.

name: Commander T'Pol (AI)
lore: Dutiful commander. Vulcan dissident loyal to Captain Forrest. T'Pol was romantically involved with Chief Engineer Tucker during her last Pon farr.

name: Corporal Scott
lore: Typical Terran MACO. Defended Commander Archer from a Gorn attack aboard the Starship Defiant.

name: Crewman Biggs
lore: Representative of Terran engineers. An expert in radiation effects on physiology. From Tosche Station, Luna. He likes to tinker with power converters.

name: Crewman D'Vela
lore: One of many subjugated Orion slave girls serving on Imperial Starfleet vessels. Dissident who is popular among her crewmates.

name: Crewman Gham
lore: Typical Andorian dissident serving aboard the I.S.S. Avenger. Sensor specialist and aspiring pilot. He enjoys old stories of the Andorian Imperial Guard.

name: Crewman Terev
lore: Typical Tellarite once suspected of being late for his duty shift. Became a dissident after spending time in the agony booth. Misses singing in the mud bath.

name: Crewman Soval
lore: Idealist and mentor to Commander T'Pol. Soval thought he was too old to become a revolutionary. Vulcan dissident. Commanded the I.S.S. Avenger.

name: Crewman Soval (AI)
lore: Idealist and mentor to Commander T'Pol. Soval thought he was too old to become a revolutionary. Vulcan dissident. Commanded the I.S.S. Avenger.

name: Ensign Guerrero
lore: Representative of junior science officers seeking out new worlds and civilizations to conquer. Obsessive collector of rare gemstones.

name: Ensign Kelby
lore: Terran who helped repair the Starship Defiant. Kelby covets Chief Engineer Tucker's position. Fascinated by methods of achieving enlightenment.

name: Major Reed
lore: Enthusiastic major, MACO, and opportunistic assassin. Second officer Malcolm Reed is largely credited with the creation of the agony booth.

name: Private Brown
lore: One of many Terran soldiers. Considered a career in the sciences before becoming a MACO. Distrusts his non-Terran crewmates, particularly Vulcans.

name: Private Palmer
lore: Representative of female MACO soldiers who worked closely with Major Reed and Sergeant Mayweather.

name: Sergeant Mayweather
lore: Opportunistic sergeant romantically involved with Comm Officer Sato. Travis Mayweather is a MACO and bodyguard to Commander Archer.

name: Sergeant Moreno
lore: Typical Terran tasked with procuring specimens for the medical bay. MACO interrogator entrusted by Major Reed to oversee the agony booth.

name: Starship Defiant
lore: NCC-1764. Responded to a Tholian distress call in 2268 and entered an area of spatial interphase. Emerged in the 22nd century mirror universe.
game_text: Terran Flagship

name: I.S.S. Avenger
lore: Admiral's ship, NX-09. Captained by Admiral Black in the Empire's fight against the rebellion and later commanded by Crewman Soval in the strike back.
game_text: Radiation MonitoringX=2 in Mirror Universe

name: I.S.S. Enterprise NX-01
lore: Prototype Terran flagship commanded by Captain Forrest. Later captained by Commander Archer.
game_text: Attributes all +1 for each Starfleet Terran Empire aboard (limit 4). Suliban Cloaking Device

name: Imperial Interceptor
lore: Destroyer used by the Terran Empire. Backbone of the fleet. Frequently used as support for the larger NX-class battle cruisers.
game_text: X = 3 at a Planet mission.

name: 22nd-Century Japan
lore: 2151 Earth: After attacking San Francisco, Empress Soto moved her throne to Kyoto.
game_text: Seeds or plays on table; download Imperial Palace here; any players may download UFP: One Small Step. Native to this timeline: all Mirror Universe Starfleet cards, Mirror Universe Non-Aligned 22nd Century personnel, Mirror Universe Neutral 22nd Century cards, and 22nd Century equipment. Non-22nd Century cards are excluded from battle here.

name: Vintaak Drydock Station
lore: 2151 Spatial Interphase: Site of concealed Tholian base used to study mysterious vessel.
game_text: Seeds on table; download Starship Defiant here from outside the game, uncontrolled. Any player may beam personnel from their ship here aboard Starship Defiant; may be commandeered by unopposed Away Team with 2 ENGINEER, OFFICER, SECURITY and STRENGTH>50 aboard. At the end of each of your turns, flip this card over.

name: A Miner Confrontation
lore: Harassed by marauding Klingons, deuterium miners found they needed both guts and guile to protect their assets.
game_text: To get past requires three personnel with Leadership OR three personnel with ENGINEER classification.

name: Authorized Access Only
lore: Many ships have secure areas to store valuable or dangerous materials. Only trusted officers can access such places. In 2151, unknown privateers searched for a vault on Enterprise.
game_text: To get past requires three personnel with Acquisition OR three personnel with OFFICER classification.

name: Contaminating a Culture
lore: Misplacing advanced technology can endanger both the development of pre-warp societies and those studying them.
game_text: To get past requires 2 Anthropology; then place on mission until solved. If any equipment is discarded here, its owner loses points (discard dilemma).

name: Defrosted Menace
lore: Preserved in the Arctic ice for 90 years, two cybernetic bodies posed more of a threat than initially suspected.
game_text: Unless 2 Biology, 2 Archaeology, and 2 SCIENCE present, place on mission. Now and start of every player's turn, their opponent (if playing Borg) assimilates their lowest CUNNING personnel here.

name: Faux Pas
lore: The Kreetassans were deeply insulted when Porthos urinated on an alvera tree. Considering the plants cultural treasures, they demanded a ritualistic apology from Jonathan Archer.
game_text: To get past requires three personnel with Diplomacy OR three personnel with V.I.P. classification.

name: MACO Encounter
lore: During the Earth-Romulan War, MACO soldiers served on the front lines as ground troops. Some later found it hard to find a role in peacetime.
game_text: Opponent may download up to two MACOs and/or one MACO Assault Rifle to planet. Any MACOs on planet may (if possible) initiate personnel battle. Discard dilemma.

name: Preoccupied
lore: While exploring a trinary system containing a black hole, unusual radiation caused the Enterprise crew to exhibit erratic and obsessive behavior.
game_text: Place on ship. Double first and second listed skill and removes all other skills on each non-Vulcan personnel aboard.

name: Quantum Leap
lore: After sabotaging the Xindi weapon, Jonathan Archer was caught in the explosion and vanished. He awoke, trapped in the past, striving to put right what had gone wrong.
game_text: One OFFICER (opponent's choice) is relocated to a time location (your choice); "disappears" (discarded) if none in play. To get past requires SECURITY and 2 Archaeology.

name: Rock People
lore: An Enterprise away team was exposed to a psychotropic compound in 2151. Experiencing intense anxiety and hallucinations, they claimed to see beings inside solid rock.
game_text: To get past requires three personnel with Geology OR three personnel with SCIENCE classification.

name: Silent Enemy
lore: Unidentified hostile vessel. Delayed Enterprise in 2151 until its phase cannon upgrades were completed.
game_text: Immediately battles attempting ship when encountered. End of every turn: Stops each ship here without CUNNING>30 aboard until end of owner's next turn, then moves.

name: Stand-off
lore: After the Eugenics Wars of the 20th century, human genetic engineering was outlawed. An encounter with hostile augments in 2154 reaffirmed the need for the ban.
game_text: To get past requires three personnel with Anthropology OR three personnel with SECURITY classification.

name: Symbalene Blood Burn
lore: A highly contagious disease which kills its victims through increased body temperature and destruction of blood vessel walls. Samples were kept at Cold Station 12 in 2154.
game_text: Kills one personnel (random selection). Place on facility here (your choice, quarantined). Now and start of each turn, kills one personnel aboard (your choice).

name: The Ghost of Cyrus Ramsey
lore: Trapped in the transporter pattern buffer, Hoshi Sato had an elaborate hallucination about a fictional transporter test subject, alien saboteurs, and her own disappearance.
game_text: To get past requires three personnel with Transporter Skill OR three personnel with MEDICAL classification.

name: Xindi Test Strike
lore: Even the small-scale test of the Xindi weapon in 2153 caused massive destruction.
game_text: Kills two personnel (random selection), and discards one personnel or empty ship (opponent's choice) at a corresponding time location. Nullify with 3 SECURITY OR a Xindi.

name: MACO Assault Rifle
lore: Generic phaser rifle developed for use by United Earth military forces. Produces rapid-fire discharges of energy ideal for combating multiple assailants.
game_text: MACO use only. Each of your personnel present is STRENGTH +3, but loses 1 Diplomacy unless aboard your ship. (Cumulative.)

name: Combat-Ready: Solidarity
lore: Knowing death is around every corner, soldiers often form close bonds with each other. The sense of camaraderie leads to improved teamwork and increased confidence.
game_text: Plays on table. MACOs cannot be killed by dilemmas (stopped instead) when present with two other unstopped MACOs.

name: Combat-Ready: Tense Situation
lore: The resilient MACOs were keen to volunteer for a unified assault team with their Starfleet colleagues and stop the Xindi weapon, even after the tragic loss of Jeremiah Hayes.
game_text: Plays on your MACO or your bodyguard; they gain Leadership. Each of your other leaders present gains SECURITY and is attributes all +1.

name: Decontamination
lore: Prior to the invention of the transporter biofilter, Starfleet away teams routinely spent several minutes in decontamination chambers after returning from missions.
game_text: Plays on table (for free). Once per game, if your Starfleet personnel have faced dilemmas at three different missions, you may discard event to score points.

name: Grappler: Shuttlepod Retrieval
lore: The grappler technology used on Starfleet vessels in the 22nd century aided docking and loading procedures but also had more unorthodox applications.
game_text: Plays on table. Your ships with at least one staffing icon gain Tractor Beam. (Immune to Kevin Uxbridge if all your personnel are 22nd Century).

name: Military Assault Command Operations
lore: Part of the United Earth military with technology two and three years more advanced than that of Starfleet. MACO troops were assigned to Enterprise in 2153.
game_text: Reveal the top three cards of your deck. You may report for free any MACO personnel revealed; place all other cards revealed beneath draw deck. Discard event.

name: Polarized Hull Plating
lore: In the 22nd century, Starfleet vessels used electromagnetic stiffening mechanisms to mitigate damage from enemy weapons.
game_text: Plays on table. Discard event to nullify one damage marker about to be placed on your 22nd Century ship. (Captain's Order.)

name: Gold!
game_text: Seeds on table. Once every turn, when one of your personnel is eligible for random selection, you may ask "Where's the Vault?" to pass this card to opponent (they now control it). If you do not, selection is instead opponent's choice. (May also be passed to opponent at start of your turn.) Worth points; X varies, where X=number of times passed. (Not duplicatable.)

name: Klingon Imperial Court
game_text: Plays on Hall of Magistrates. Adds a Brig to each of your Klingon outposts. Once each turn, your Klingon personnel (and any captives present) may relocate from here to Rura Penthe (and vice-versa) or to your Klingon 22nd Century ship in the Alpha Quadrant. Worth points while you have three or more captives on Rura Penthe.

name: Launch Bay
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. In place of a card draw, you may download one Starfleet shuttlepod to hand. Once per game, you may download Grappler and/or Emergency Evacuation. Your Starfleet shuttlepods may be loaded aboard (limit 4) and launched from your NX-class ships with Tractor Beam. Your Starfleet shuttlepods may land on or take off from planets using 1 RANGE.

name: Reed Alert!
game_text: Plays to download to your 22nd Century ship its matching commander OR to download any two of the following: Straight and Steady OR Explore New World OR Polarized Hull Plating OR Expert Pilot. (Captain's Order.)

name: Sickbay: Menagerie
game_text: Plays on your 22nd Century ship with at least one staffing icon. Thrice per game, you may stop your 22nd Century MEDICAL personnel aboard to prevent one personnel present from being assimilated, controlled by Ceti Eel, or killed by a dilemma; personnel is stopped instead. May be nullified by Plasma Fire.

name: Combat-Ready: Jury-Rig
lore: Soldiers are trained to quickly assess and handle a variety of technological obstacles, even under pressure.
game_text: Plays on your MACO or Miracle Worker. Until end of turn, that personnel is attributes all +2 and gains ENGINEER, Transporter Skill, and Computer Skill.

name: Combat-Ready: Tactical Reserve
lore: Military officers can quickly redeploy forces to where thy can be of the most use.
game_text: Plays on your Command personnel. Relocate one of your unstopped matching SECURITY-classification personnel from a mission in same quadrant to this personnel.

name: Klingon Border Patrol
lore: Klingons are extremely territorial. There is no such thing as an insignificant corner of Klingon space.
game_text: Plays on your Klingon 22nd Century ship present with an opponent's ship. If this ship is present with an opponent's ship at end of your next turn, score points.

name: Klingon Bounty
lore: Victims of the Klingon justice system, such as Jonathan Archer, soon learned that Klingons had little tolerance for escapees.
game_text: Once per game, plays on an opponent's ship at same location as your 2 Klingon 22nd Century SECURITY. One personnel aboard (random selection) is captured (relocated to those SECURITY).

name: Extract Rare Mineral
lore: Archer’s Comet: Drill into giant comet and collect sample of scarce eisilium.

name: Police Trade Route
lore: Near Nausicaan Space: Protect civilian transports along vital shipping lane.

name: Research Devastating Attack
lore: Sector 001 Region • Earth: Examine site of unprovoked assault on the Starfleet homeworld.

name: Retrieve Materiel
lore: Pre-industrial world: Recover technology previously lost on less-advanced planet.

name: Study Neutronic Storm
lore: Takret System: Examine plasma phenomena traveling at high warp.

name: Survey New World
lore: Minshara-class planet: Study habitable planet with novel ecosystems.

name: Survival Training
lore: Sector 001 Region • Luna: Attend survival school on the surface of Earth's moon.

name: Explore New World
game_text: Plays on your unexamined planet mission. You may not voluntarily use transporters here. If your entire Away Team (containing three or more Starfleet personnel) was just stopped by a dilemma here, you may download one equipment here. When mission solved by your Starfleet Away Team, you may unstop all your Away Teams here, restore full RANGE to one of your Starfleet ships in orbit and/or download Diverse Experiences.

name: Operate Dilithium Gulag
game_text: Seeds or plays on Rura Penthe; rotate mission so that your side now faces opponent. Once per game, at the start of your turn, you may download one personnel with "Rura Penthe" in lore to hand. While you have a captive (or any personnel with "Prisoner" in title) here, you may draw one additional card at the end of each turn. Once solved, each of your Klingon ships is RANGE +2.

name: Search and Seize
game_text: Plays on your unexamined Klingon mission Space mission. Each time your crew of only Klingon 22nd Century personnel overcomes a dilemma here, reveal top card of opponent's draw deck. If it is a personnel, opponent reports that personnel (if possible) to Rura Penthe (captured); discard otherwise. Once solved , increases point box of Rura Penthe by 10 points while a captive is there. (Unique).

name: Four of Fifty
lore: Identification: Harvest Drone Task: Identify targets in Sector 001. Engage. Biological Distinctiveness: Humanoid.

name: Ten of Fifty
lore: Identification: Synergy Drone Task: Recognize optimum performance. Coordinate. Biological Distinctiveness: Human species.

name: Advocate Kolos
lore: Courageous Klingon who won over 200 cases in 50 years of legal practice. Defended Prisoner Archer in court on Narendra III. Lost an eye on Rura Penthe.

name: Aklam
lore: Typical of helm officers on smaller Klingon ships. Served under Duras Son of Toral in 2153. Pilot particularly practiced at orbital maneuvers.

name: Bu'kaH
lore: Chief engineer of the I.K.S. Somraw who survived Xarantine ale poisoning. Sought to avoid a dishonorable death for herself and her crewmates.

name: Captain Goroth
lore: Klingon thief who hired bounty hunters to recapture Prisoner Archer. Initially agreed to pay nine thousand darseks but only gave Skalaar six thousand.

name: Captain Korok
lore: Klingon freighter captain. Thief who used intimidation to take deuterium from mining colonies. Ancestor of General Korok. Former pilot.

name: Captain Monak
lore: Representative of 22nd-century Klingon captains. Raided a Xarantine outpost in 2151. Got more than he bargained for.

name: Captain Vorok
lore: Commander of a prototype Klingon vessel. Spared a Xyrillian ship in 2151 in exchange for holographic technology.

name: Chancellor M'Rek
lore: Typical Klingon High Council Leader of the mid-22nd century. Encountered Jonathan Archer in 2151. Rumored to have exotic taste in women.

name: Duras Son of Toral
lore: Former captain demoted for failing to locate rebels harbored by Jonathan Archer. Given another chance by the High Council. Ancestor of Ja'rod.

name: Gonik
lore: Representative of soldiers aboard Klingon ships in the 22nd century. Cook who excels at preparing pipius claw, Captain Korok's favorite dish.

name: J'Met
lore: Typical Klingon female stationed aboard the Battle Cruiser Bortas. Served as yaS wa'DIch, executive officer, under Duras Son of Toral.

name: Klaang
lore: Seven foot tall High Council courier. Met with Sarin on Rigel X. Crashed on Earth in 2151. First Klingon encountered by humans. Treated by Phlox.

name: Magistrate Gorvil
lore: Typical Klingon magistrate overseeing the courts on Narendra III. Retired general who sentenced Prisoner Archer to a life of hard labor on Rura Penthe.

name: Morga
lore: Representative of Klingon bridge officers. Trustworthy member of the I.K.S. Nguq'Yab crew. Bodyguard who often takes the fall for his superiors.

name: P'Mokh
lore: Representative of Klingon mercenaries engaged in less honorable pursuits. Served with Captain Korok in 2152. A competent field nurse.

name: Prisoner Archer
lore: Human captain well-known in the Klingon Empire. Jonathan Archer was convicted of conspiracy and sentenced to a life of hard labor on Rura Penthe.

name: Prosecutor Orak
lore: Klingon lawyer with the ferocity of a warrior. Pursued the death penalty in the Klingon Empire's case against Prisoner Archer.

name: Osmotic Eel
lore: Aquatic member of Phlox's menagerie. Female osmotic eel with wound-sealing capabilities.

name: Darrit
lore: One of several Denobulan researchers working on Cold Station 12. He served with Jeremy Lucas in 2154 as a doctor and anatomist.

name: Shobbi-Har
lore: Giant Orion slaver. Runs the slave market on Verex III. Processed T'Pol and Jeffrey Pierce for auction in 2154. Likes to put on a big show.

name: Skalaar
lore: Bounty hunter. Tellarite freighter captain. Brother of Gaavrin. Captured Jonathan Archer in 2153 but gave him the means to escape the Klingons.

name: Trevix
lore: Typical Denobulan geologist. She studied unusual speleothems on Xantoras with Dr. Yolen. Tried to find clues to prevent seismic disasters on Denobula.

name: Amanda Cole
lore: Typical MACO corporal. Holds the team sharpshooting record. She once received Vulcan neuro-pressure treatment from Charles Tucker III.

name: Callaghan
lore: Typical Starfleet petty officer. She manned the bridge engineering station during Enterprise's battle with a group of augments in 2154.

name: Fiona McKenzie
lore: Experienced corporal who trained with gravity boots at Jupiter Station. MACO assigned to Enterprise in 2153. Goes by her middle name. Always alert.

name: Hideaki Chang
lore: Conscientious corporal from Hawaii. MACO who joined Enterprise for a crusade into the Delphic Expanse. Feared getting lost. Likes fast motorcycles.

name: Jeremiah Hayes
lore: Diligent major and MACO commander. Expert at both armed and unarmed combat. Found a sparring partner in Malcolm Reed. Likes consistency.

name: John Frederick Paxton
lore: Fanatic who served as chief administrator of the Orpheus Mining Facility. Leader of Terra Prime. Demanded aliens comply with evacuation orders.

name: Jonathan Archer
lore: Heroic diplomat and greatest explorer of the 22nd century. Captained Enterprise in the 2150s. Saved Earth from the Xindi. Friend of Charles Tucker III.

name: Kelby
lore: Arrogant engineer. Believed his promotion to chief engineer of Enterprise was endangered by Charles Tucker III's continued presence.

name: Markus Forbes
lore: Extraction specialist quick to volunteer for dangerous missions. MACO soldier assigned to Enterprise in 2153 under the command of Jeremiah Hayes.

name: Maxwell Forrest
lore: Starfleet executive who authorized the early launch of Enterprise during the Broken Bow incident. Admiral who worked closely with the Vulcans.

name: Nathan Samuels
lore: High-ranking government minister. Ex-mayor who climbed to the top. Former member of Terra Prime. Underestimated Jonathan Archer.

name: Nelson Kemper
lore: Representative of MACO sergeants assigned to Enterprise in 2153. Unaccustomed to life in space, he still visits Phlox every morning.

name: Phlox
lore: Alien physiologist who keeps an exotic menagerie. Denobulan doctor and occasional counselor. Has three wives, adhering to his world's polyamorous customs.

name: Sascha Money
lore: Typical MACO who serves aboard Enterprise with distinction, despite having been injured more than once. She sometimes picks up the wrong uniform.

name: Sean Hawkins
lore: Typical of aggressive MACOs often assigned to boarding parties. Has received extensive EV combat training. Always ready to stretch his legs.

name: Stewart Rivers
lore: Typical Starfleet engineer. Human from Cleveland, Ohio. His humor helped the crew bear the perils of the various alien quagmires they encountered.

name: Battle Cruiser Bortas
lore: Warship commanded by Duras Son of Toral. Pursued rebels from Raatooras. Once engaged Enterprise in combat.
game_text: Attributes all +1 for each Klingon 22nd Century Command aboard (limit 5).

name: I.K.S. Raptor
lore: Small scout vessel used by the Klingon Empire in the 22nd century. Equipped with photon torpedoes and a hull reinforced with a coherent molecular alloy.
game_text: Download Klingon Bounty

name: Intrepid
lore: Typical early starship design. Routinely stationed near the Sol system. The Intrepid-type variant became the standard design for this class of vessel.
game_text: X =2 if moving within a region. Download Grappler

name: Shuttlepod One
lore: Enterprise shuttlecraft. With transporter technology in its infancy, officers relied on shuttles instead.
game_text: Has no transporters. May report (for free) to your NX-class ship. Download Explore New World

name: Shuttlepod Two
lore: Typical Starfleet shuttlecraft of the mid-22nd century. Has plasma weapons and a ditanium hull.Has no transporters.

name: Hall of Magistrates
lore: 2154 Narendra III: Klingon sector judicial authority. Site of several historic trials.
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. In place of a normal card play, any player may download a Klingon 22nd Century Law personnel here. Native to this timeline: all Klingon 22nd Century cards, all Non-Aligned 22nd Century personnel, and all 22nd Century equipment (except Mirror Universe cards). Once per turn, one such personnel reporting at this location may do so for free (if all of that player's Time Locations are 2154).

name: MACO Training Camp
lore: 2154 Luna: Military Assault Command Operations established a training facility on Earth's moon.

name: Vulcan PADD
lore: Standard Vulcan Personal Access Display Device for computerized information.

name: Vulcan Phaser
lore: Handheld phased energy weapon from the 22nd century. Standard issue amongst Vulcan security, although many prefer to use the traditional lirpa.
game_text: Vulcan use only. Each of your personnel present is STRENGTH +2. (Cumulative.)

name: Espionage: Vulcan on Klingon
lore: The Vulcan High Command maintained a watchful eye on the military capabilities of the aggressive and adversarial Klingon Empire.

name: Espionage: Vulcan on Starfleet
lore: The Vulcan High Command uses its influence with other governments to gather intelligence on them, as with its advisory role in the Starfleet Warp Five Program.

name: Treaty: Starfleet/Vulcan
lore: Prior to the formation of the Federation, the Vulcan High Command allied with Starfleet to advise on its tentative early footsteps into deep space.

name: Vulcan Outpost
lore: Vulcan is the homeworld of the highly logical Vulcan people. The Vulcan High Command established outposts throughout its territory.
game_text: Seed one OR build where you have a Vulcan ENGINEER.

name: Kolinahr
game_text: Seeds or plays on Vulcan. Your Vulcan cards may mix and cooperate (regardless of affiliation) and may use Vulcan ships and Federation facilities. Once each turn, if you do not have Protect the Timeline in play, one personnel may report for free. Twice each turn, your personnel and ships may move between here and 2154 Vulcan. Discard incident if you play (or have played) any non-Vulcan personnel.

name: Vulcan Database
game_text: Plays on your 22nd Century ship or Vulcan Lander; ship gains one of the following skills as special equipment: ENGINEER, MEDICAL, Anthropology, Biology, Computer Skill, Exobiology, Geology, Physics, or Stellar Cartography. If a Vulcan aboard, may re-select skill once each turn. OR Plays to draw 2 cards (limit 4) for each of your ships in play with a skill as special equipment.

name: Excite Dark Matter
lore: Robinson Nebula: Illuminate concentrated dark matter using metreon particle bombardment.
game_text: None

name: Delvok
lore: Representative of Syrranite dissidents. Part-time bodyguard. Struggled to maintain emotional control while performing his own musical compositions.

name: Sanye
lore: One of many Vulcans trained in the field of science. Served on the D'Kyr in 2152. Worked as a cook in his family's plomeek soup kitchen.

name: Sopek
lore: Typical Vulcan captain. V'Shar agent working for the High Command. Spied on by Shran. Led a rescue mission on Coridan. Often patrols the Klaestron sector.

name: Soval
lore: Vulcan ambassador to Earth. Has liaised between the High Command and many alien nations. Thought it was "a mistake" to return Klaang to Qo'noS alive.

name: Strom
lore: Typical Vulcan doctor. Attended an Interspecies Medical Exchange conference on Dekendi III. Diagnosed T'Pol from residue on a PADD.

name: T'Lam
lore: Typical Vulcan High Command security advisor. She contacted T'Pol in 2152 regarding the fugitive Menos. Expert in the Vulcan martial art suus mahna.

name: T'Pol
lore: Vulcan aide to Soval. She thinks humans are not yet ready for space exploration. Tasked by the High Command to act as Jonathan Archer's first officer.

name: Valrik
lore: Representative of subspace geometry consultants. Vulcan who observed the early NX Program tests on Earth. He later joined the Syrranites as a dissident.

name: D'kyr
lore: 22nd-century mainstay of the Vulcan fleet. Combat cruiser tasked to ferry Phlox and T'Pol home after Enterprise was temporarily recalled in 2152.
game_text: SCIENCE

name: Kir'Shara
lore: Legendary Vulcan artifact containing Surak's original writings. Thought lost for centuries, its rediscovery led to the Vulcan Reformation and a new period of enlightenment.

name: T'Pol Has Some Issues
lore: Exposure to large concentrations of Trellium-D in the Delphic Expanse disrupted T'Pol's synaptic pathways. Her loss of emotional control endangered other crew members.
game_text: Place on (stops) a personnel present (random selection). End of each turn, they kill another personnel present with lower INTEGRITY (opponent's choice). Cure with 3 SCIENCE.

name: Espionage: Romulan on Vulcan
lore: Romulan spies were everywhere.

name: Espionage: Starfleet on Vulcan
lore: Starfleet routinely gathered intelligence on neighboring civilizations, even ostensibly friendly ones such as the Vulcans.

name: Espionage: Vulcan on Andorian
lore: The Vulcan High Command routinely monitored the activity of more emotional and aggressive neighboring species, such as the Andorians, from hidden listening posts.
game_text: Plays on any Non-Aligned mission (or any mission with "Andorian" in lore). Your Vulcan personnel may now attempt this mission. Discard after mission completed.

name: Neuropressure Massage
lore: Vulcan discipline for relaxing the mind and muscles by stimulating neural nodes and pressure points. Charles Tucker III was one of the few outsiders to experience it.
game_text: Plays on table. At the end of each of your turns, if all your personnel are Vulcan, you may draw two cards and place one of them beneath draw deck.

name: Strange New Worlds
lore: The Vulcans approached exploration of other cultures through passive observation and impassionate logic. The High Command encouraged other cultures to adopt similar policies.
game_text: Plays on a mission. (Unique.) Opponent's mission attempts here must use the following requirements:Anthropology + Diplomacy + Law + INTEGRITY>32

name: Temper Advancements
lore: Alarmed by the rapid pace at which Starfleet was venturing into deep space, the Vulcan High Command sought to curb humanity's potentially dangerous progress.
game_text: Once per game, seeds or plays on table. Each non-Vulcan personnel or ship enters play stopped.

name: Cautionary Tale
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. If you have three Vulcan personnel in play, your Abandon Mission, Gaps in Normal Space, Q-Net, and Subspace Warp Rift gain Scheme and are unique (even if not in play; if you have multiple in play, discard down to one copy of each). OR Plays to download a Scheme card (once per game per card title), then discard incident.

name: IDIC: Courage of the V'Shar
game_text: Plays on table. Your Vulcan personnel may attempt Alpha Quadrant missions requiring SECURITY. When you play (but not download) a Vulcan espionage card, you may draw up to two cards. Once each turn, you may place an Espionage card from hand beneath your deck to download a different Espionage card to hand.

page_title: IDIC: Power of the High Command (LLaP)
name: IDIC: Power of the High Command
base_name: IDIC: Power of the High Command

name: Only Logical
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
game_text: Plays on your mission (lose points). When attempting this mission, while at least four Vulcans are in crew or Away Team, name a card before each unexamined seed card is revealed. If it is the card you named, nullify it. (Unique.)

name: The Katra of Surak
game_text: Plays on your Vulcan personnel. (Unique.) This personnel gains Archaeology. Your Vulcan personnel present gain Honor, are attributes all +1, and may ignore their Treachery. At the start of your turn (or when this personnel is killed), if Mindmeld present, may transfer to your other personnel present.

name: The Secret of P'Jem
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Your Espionage: Vulcan on Andorian may target Federation missions (except Vulcan). Your Espionage cards targeting a mission you seeded may not be nullified by opponent's cards. Once each turn, when you complete a mission targeted by an Espionage card, you may download File Mission Report.

name: Thorough Debriefing
game_text: Plays between two adjacent missions if you have three Vulcan personnel in play. Just after an opponent's personnel at an adjacent mission uses a regular skill to solve a mission, overcome a dilemma, or cure a dilemma, they are stopped. (Unique.)

name: You're Not Ready
game_text: Plays between two adjacent missions if you have three Vulcan personnel in play. Opponent may not begin mission attempts at adjacent missions with fewer than nine personnel. (Unique.)

name: Accept Ambassadorial Invitation
lore: Tholia: Seize rare opportunity to study xenophobic race and their silk production process.
game_text: None

name: Assemble Fleet
lore: Regulus: Coordinate forces at staging ground beyond the range of Andorian listening posts.
game_text: None

name: Attend Ambassadorial Banquet
lore: Tellar Prime: Accept invitation to visit Tellarite capital for annual dinner at Andorian embassy.
game_text: Solving player may download Ambassador Gral here.

name: Cultural Observation II
lore: Mintaka III: Aid observation of primitive society.
game_text: WORMHOLE: You may move your staffed ship between here and any other location if that location is a Wormhole mission OR by playing one Wormhole interrupt there. Then flip this mission over.

name: Explore Delphic Expanse
lore: Delphic Expanse Region • Thermobaric clouds: Study remnants of old regional barrier.
game_text: None

name: Locate Telepaths
lore: Andoria: Seek out secretive Andorian subspecies living in the Northern Wastes.
game_text: +5 if an Aenar, a Breen, or Shran present.

name: Medical Conference
lore: Dekendi III: Present research at annual Interspecies Medical Exchange convention.
game_text: None

name: Rebuild Monastery
lore: P'Jem: Restore ancient Vulcan sanctuary destroyed during Andorian espionage incident.
game_text: None

name: Repatriate Citizen
lore: Qo'noS: Return warrior found at distant crash site to the Klingon homeworld.
game_text: None

name: Study Xenophobic Tendencies
lore: Tandar Prime: Observe shift in government policies towards anti-immigration stance.
game_text: None

name: Menos
lore: Surgically altered Vulcan. Former V'Shar operative turned smuggler after prolonged exposure to criminal activities. Has an air of mystique about him.
characteristics: style="text-align:left;width:500px;"[[{Category:Dual affiliation personnel (Star Trek CCG 1E)|Dual affiliation personnel]]

name: Menos (AI)
lore: Surgically altered Vulcan. Former V'Shar operative turned smuggler after prolonged exposure to criminal activities. Has an air of mystique about him.

name: Ambassador V'Lar
lore: Noted dignitary with a distinguished career. Gathered evidence against Mazarite criminals who later pursued her. Dissident against the V'Las regime.

name: Charles Tucker III
lore: Human engineer. Guest at the wedding of T'Pol and Koss, despite being romantically involved with T'Pol. Experienced in Vulcan neuropressure massage.

name: Charles Tucker III (AI)
lore: Human engineer. Guest at the wedding of T'Pol and Koss, despite being romantically involved with T'Pol. Experienced in Vulcan neuropressure massage.

name: Jonathan Archer
lore: Human captain who accompanied T'Pol into The Forge. Became embroiled in Vulcan politics and mysticism when he carried the katra of Surak.

name: Jonathan Archer (AI)
lore: Human captain who accompanied T'Pol into The Forge. Became embroiled in Vulcan politics and mysticism when he carried the katra of Surak.

name: Koss
lore: Vulcan architect briefly married to T'Pol. Helped to reinstate T'Les to her academy position. He aided Jonathan Archer's quest to return the Kir'Shara.

name: Minister Kuvak
lore: Member of the High Command. He questioned the aggressive policies towards Syrranites and Andorians. Deposed V'Las after the recovery of the Kir'Shara.

name: Minister T'Pau
lore: Former dissident and Syrranite leader. Found the Kir'Shara with Jonathan Archer. In her hands, it was used to initiate reform of the Vulcan government.

name: Oratt
lore: Senior physician working for the Vulcan High Command. Refused to share data on Pa'nar Syndrome. Suspended Yuris for his revelations.

name: Sedis
lore: Characteristic of Vulcan officers serving the High Command. He commanded the Sh'Raan during an encounter with Mazarite forces in 2152.

name: Sinam
lore: High priest at the P'Jem Sanctuary. He was recruited by the Vulcan High Command to keep the secret monitoring station there concealed from visitors.

name: Smolek
lore: Typical Vulcan commando. He was ordered by the Vulcan High Command to hunt down and exterminate "criminals" hiding in The Forge.

name: Sodor
lore: Typical junior academic. Former assistant to V'Las. He now studies ancient texts under V'Tal. Dissident who attended Koss and T'Pol's wedding.

name: Soval
lore: Former Vulcan ambassador turned dissident. Lost his position after using a mindmeld to investigate the 2154 embassy bombing. Friend of Maxwell Forrest.

name: Stel
lore: Chief investigator working for the High Command. Assassin favored by V'Las. He framed the Syrranites for the United Earth Embassy bombing in 2154.

name: Sulok
lore: Archivist and novice priest at the P'Jem Sanctuary. He sought to attain kolinahr. One of the few Vulcans aware of the concealed monitoring station there.

name: Surak
lore: Legendary 4th century Vulcan philosopher, scientist, and logician. Father of modern Vulcan civilization. Founded the T'Karath sanctuary. His katra survives.

name: Syrran
lore: Meaning Desert Wind, the Syrranite leader assumed the name Arev to travel incognito. Pacifist Vulcan dissident, he carried the katra of Surak.

name: T'Les
lore: Mother of T'Pol. Former instructor at the Vulcan Science Academy, forcibly retired following T'Pol's actions at P'Jem. Dissident who became a Syrranite.

name: T'Mer
lore: Representative of Vulcan medical assistants. Nurse and dissident who became a Syrranite. She dislikes the harsh conditions in The Forge. Has a pet sehlat.

name: T'Mik
lore: Captain of the D'kyr. Dutiful servant of the Vulcan High Command. She ordered her ship to rendezvous with Enterprise in 2152.

name: Talma
lore: Typical Vulcan warp theorist. Assigned by the High Command to observe the NX Program. He considered the human engine design to be unsound.

name: Tavek
lore: Captain of the Nyran. Sent by the High Command to take custody of the prisoner Menos. He delivered a water polo result to the "captain" of Enterprise.

name: V'Las
lore: Vulcan minister and High Command administrator. He conspired with Talok to eliminate the Syrranites.

name: V'Las (AI)
lore: Vulcan minister and High Command administrator. He conspired with Talok to eliminate the Syrranites.

name: V'Tal
lore: Elderly Vulcan priest. Secret expert on melding techniques. He relieved Jonathan Archer of Surak's katra. Officiated at the wedding of Koss and T'Pol.

name: Vanik
lore: Long-serving officer reporting to the Vulcan High Command. Captain of the Ti'Mur. Logistics expert. He helped rescue two Enterprise crewmen in 2151.

name: Yuris
lore: Junior physician and former nurse. Lost his standing in Vulcan medical circles after he exposed his mindmeld abilities. Later became a dissident.

name: Ni'Var
lore: Vulcan combat cruiser commanded by Sopek. Assigned to return T'Pol to Vulcan in 2151. Landed troops on Coridan as part of a rescue attempt.
game_text: Download Launch Portal

name: Sh'Raan
lore: Vulcan combat cruiser dispatched to rendezvous with Enterprise. Efficiently disabled Mazarite attackers attempting to capture Ambassador V'Lar.

name: Ti'Mur
lore: Cruiser that conveyed a message to T'Pol about her marriage. Observed Enterprise studying a comet. Rescued a shuttlepod with its tractor beam.
game_text: Activate Tractor Beam

name: Vulcan Frigate
lore: Large shuttlecraft in use by the High Command. Outfitted with particle beam armament for orbital defense of Vulcan. Often repurposed as a scout ship.
game_text: none

name: Vulcan Particle Beam
game_text: ATTACK bonus +2 if you have a Vulcan ship firing..Hit = Tactic Draw. Direct hit = Tactic Draw Tactic Draw.

name: 22nd-Century ShiKahr
lore: 2154 Vulcan: Desert metropolis located near The Forge. Birthplace of many famous Vulcans.
game_text: Seeds or plays on table; any player may download IDIC. Native to this timeline: all Vulcan 22nd Century cards, Non-Aligned 22nd Century personnel, and 22nd Century equipment (except Mirror Universe cards). Once each turn, one such personnel reporting at this location may do so for free. Non-22nd Century cards are excluded from battle here.

name: P'Jem Sanctuary
lore: 2151 P'Jem: Ancient Vulcan monastery. Concealed a secret V'Shar monitoring post.
game_text: Seeds or plays on table; any player may download The Secret of P'Jem and/or a V'Shar personnel here. Native to this timeline: all Vulcan 22nd Century cards and 22nd Century equipment (except Mirror Quadrant cards). V'Shar personnel may file mission reports here. When a player solves a mission, any V'Shar personnel there may relocate here.

name: Planet of Galactic Peace
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Founded in 2267 after the Federation-Klingon War, Nimbus III was a dream given form. Located deep in neutral space, it was considered the last, best hope for peace. It failed.
game_text: Plays on your non-homeworld mission. Your cards here may mix and cooperate regardless of affiliation. (Immune to Kevin Uxbridge.)

name: HQ: Executive Orders
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
game_text: Seeds or plays on any headquarters. Once each turn, if you report a matching personnel here that has a property logo not on any of your other personnel in play, you may draw a card. Your matching V.I.P.-classification personnel here gain SECURITY.

name: Colonel Kira
lore: Blockade commander Kira Nerys opposed the Romulans at Derna. She commanded DS9 in 2375.

name: Five of Fourteen
lore: Identification: Deployment DroneTask: Assess inter-hive resourcing. Optimize.Biological Distinctiveness: Humanoid.

name: Hiram Roth
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: Human president of the United Federation of Planets during the 2286 whale probe incident. He demoted Admiral Kirk for disobeying Starfleet regulations.

name: Mellis
lore: Typical Alpha-Hirogen in training. Refined his skills leading several successful hunts against holographic prey. Eager to test himself against a real opponent.

name: Mo'Lak
lore: First officer of the I.K.S. Amar during the V'Ger incident. Normally a calming influence on his commanding officer, Krase.

name: Karyn Berlin
lore: One of many humans descended from The 37's. Her ancestors were kidnapped and relocated to the Delta Quadrant. Protects her colony from invaders.

name: Dr. Pel
lore: Hologram created in 2372 with the intelligence and consciousness of the Vidiian female Danara Pel. Romantically involved with The Doctor.

name: Dr. Pel (AI)
lore: Hologram created in 2372 with the intelligence and consciousness of the Vidiian female Danara Pel. Romantically involved with The Doctor.

name: A Crime of Passion
lore: Manipulated by D'Nesh and her Orion pheromones, Kelby sabotaged the electro-plasma system aboard Enterprise as part of Harrad-Sar's attempt to capture the vessel.
game_text: Unless a female ENGINEER OR a unique male with printed INTEGRITY>7 present, opponent may choose a ship here to . Discard dilemma.

name: No Mention of Crime
lore: In 2152, Charles Tucker III and Malcolm Reed were deceived by con artists posing as alluring females on Risa. The Vulcan database hadn't warned them of potential criminal activity.
game_text: Opponent chooses to capture male with most icons OR stop any two males present. Nullify with four females.

name: Pawns of the Military
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: In the wrong hands, a new discovery or scientific advancement can be perverted into a dreadful weapon.
game_text: If T'Lani III or a biolab in play, opponent may download and seed here up to two of the following: Hyper-Aging, Aphasia Device or any virus-related dilemma; then place on mission: add 2 SCIENCE to requirements of all such dilemmas here.

name: Bigger on the Inside
lore: The secrets of a small futuristic ship and the corpse of a presumed temporal agent led Starfleet, Suliban, and Tholian forces to abandon all other priorities in an attempt to secure it.
game_text: Plays on a mission if your temporal agent is here or adjacent. Mission may not be attempted or scouted unless 4 Command OR any Intelligence in crew or Away Team. (Unique.)

name: Disrupted Continuum
lore: When temporal agent Daniels pulled Jonathan Archer out of a dangerous situation with the Suliban in the 22nd century, it resulted in devastating alterations to the timeline.
game_text: Plays on table. Once per game, discard event to nullify a non-Q dilemma your opponent just revealed; may download and seed a replacement Space or Planet dilemma.

name: Empress
lore: With the firepower of the Starship Defiant at her disposal, the former communications officer quickly assumed a new position of power. "You are speaking to Empress Sato."
game_text: Plays on your Contender (for free if any Hoshi). Once per game, at the start of your turn, discard event to complete a Contender-related objective (but draw no cards).

name: Revolutionaries
lore: Damar rallied the civilian population of Cardassia, knowing that failure to oppose an enemy as evil and powerful as the Dominion would condemn them all to eternal submission.
game_text: Plays on table. Your dissidents may initiate battle against their own affiliation. OR Download two Universal dissident personnel. Discard event.

name: Romulan Minefield
lore: Many species use mines to deny access to particular areas of space. Cloaked Romulan mines caused significant damage to Enterprise in 2152.
game_text: Plays between two missions (for free if both are Romulan). Creates a location (span 2). Passing non-Romulan ships must stop here for rest of turn or incur damage.

name: The Unrelenting Lust for Profit
lore: Outraged by the taxes and social reforms on Ferenginar, Quark declared that his bar would be the last outpost of what had once made Ferenginar great.
game_text: Seeds on Quark's Bar or a Trading Post; download 1st Rule of Acquisition or The Ferengi Rules of Acquisition. You may use them at any time on your turn.

name: Treaty: Romulan/Vulcan
lore: Under the administration of V'Las, a covert alliance existed in 2154 between the Vulcan High Command and Romulan agents with the aim of "reunifying" the two cultures.

name: "We Are the Metrons"
lore: Having pursued their Gorn adversaries into Metron-controlled space, the crew of the Starship Enterprise was forced to resolve their conflict on the Metrons' terms.
game_text: Seeds on your mission. If each of your missions has exactly one affiliation icon and all match, all non-Borg cards at this mission have attack restrictions of that affiliation.

name: Cold Station 12
lore: 22nd-century biolab built by Earth and Denobula. Stored hazardous pathogens and genetically enhanced embryos. Commandeered by augments.
game_text: Seed one at a Starfleet or Starfleet Space mission. Your Non-Aligned cards with "Khan" in title or lore may report here; one may seed here.

name: Tellarite Trading Post
lore: 22nd-century depot operated by the Tellarite Mining Consortium. Home away from home for diplomats, hustlers, entrepreneurs, and wanderers.
game_text: Seeds or plays at a 2154 Space location. Ships may dock and repair here (as if an outpost). UFP: One Small Step.

name: Ferengi Gas Trap
game_text: Plays on a Space location. Opponent's ship here must "bring this card aboard" (place on ship; limit once per game per ship title). Counts down only while on a ship. While on opponent's ship: crew disabled, and ship (if non-Borg) may be targeted by Secondary Market. Nullified if Decontamination is in play, by Disruptor Overload, or with CUNNING>103 here. (Unique.)

name: Holographic Camouflage
game_text: Seeds on table; place here from outside the game up to 7 different non-Borg ships. At the start of your turn, you may place a ship here out-of-play; until start of your next turn: your ships with Holographic Skin have that ship's WEAPONS and add its special equipment, use tactics as if that ship, and damage is replaced with Flip for all hits (score 5 points per hit). Your Outgunned is nullified.

name: One with the Borg
game_text: Plays on table. Once per game, when you assimilate an opponent's personnel, place your drone present beneath your draw deck and discard incident to assimilate another of opponent's personnel present (random selection). OR Plays on a ship you have assimilated. While your Communications aboard, worth points equal to ship's highest printed attribute.

name: The Spires of Romulus
game_text: Seeds on 2154 Romulus. Your UniversalRomulan personnel and Remans are considered native, and your downloaded mission specialists may download to here. When your staffed ship's crew solves a Space mission or wins a battle at a Neutral Zone location, you may relocate that ship to here.

name: Reman Sacrifice
lore: Oppressed by the Romulans for centuries, Reman troops made a vicious and expendable fighting force. They were frequently used as cannon fodder during the Dominion War.
game_text: Plays on your Reman. They are sacrificed (die) to draw three cards (once each turn) OR to substitute for a Romulan personnel present who is about to die.

name: Temporal Almanac
lore: Jonathan Archer had access to a database of future events and details, left behind by temporal agent Daniels. He rarely used it, fearing the consequences could be disastrous.
game_text: Once each turn, if you have a temporal agent at a time location, you may draw two cards OR immediately play an event on table for free.

name: Distant Control
game_text: Seeds on table. While your Leadership, Empathy, and Treachery present at Drone Control Room, your all-native Away Team present may attempt Space missions as the crew of your empty Romulan Drone-class ship (may not die unless they have Empathy, and may not relocate to spaceline). At the end of any dilemma, if no Empathy remains, attempt ends. You may not re-attempt this turn.

name: Hinder Progress
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. When opponent's crew or Away Team fails a mission attempt, if you have a personnel at that mission OR a dissident in play with affiliation matching any personnel in the attempt, you may place objective on that mission (limit once per mission): discard objective at end of turn, and score points if mission not solved.

name: Chef
lore: William T. Riker had a crisis of conscience over the search for the U.S.S. Pegasus. The cook sought guidance from recreations of Starfleet legends.

name: Data
lore: Captain of the U.S.S. Sutherland during the Klingon Civil War. Soong-type android who was romantically involved with Tasha Yar and Jenna D'Sora.

name: Ezri Dax
lore: Trill successor to Jadzia Dax. Counselor who drew on Joran Dax's memories from her symbiont to profile and apprehend a murderer aboard DS9.

name: Boshar
lore: Targ kept by Antaak since childhood. An early patient of the aspiring surgeon. Faithful pet who would recognize his master even without cranial ridges.

name: Korath
lore: Scientist and temporal agent. In an alternate future, he conspired with Admiral Janeway to gain a seat on the High Council. Invented the chrono deflector.

name: Arik Soong
lore: "Father" of many augment embryos from the time of Khan. Skilled doctor and geneticist. Human who traded goods and data with the Orion Syndicate.

name: Arik Soong (AI)
lore: "Father" of many augment embryos from the time of Khan. Skilled doctor and geneticist. Human who traded goods and data with the Orion Syndicate.

name: E'Lis
lore: Typical 22nd-century colonist. Humanoid nurse living on a deuterium mining colony. She helped fight off marauding Klingons in 2152.

name: Feezal Phlox
lore: Denobulan quantum optics expert. Second wife of Phlox. Made advances towards Charles Tucker III, in keeping with the polyamorous customs of her race.

name: Jaya
lore: Typical augment from the time of Khan. She sided with Malik to overthrow Raakin. Helped to rescue her "father" Arik Soong from his Starfleet captors.

name: Jonathan Archer
lore: Human captain recruited as a temporal agent by Daniels. Experienced time traveller. Visited 2004 Detroit with T'Pol to destroy a Xindi bioweapon.

name: Lissan
lore: Aenar leader and "speaker." Pacifist who refused to aid in destroying the Romulan drones. Later became a minister in a unified Andorian government.

name: N'Rana
lore: Typical Tarkalean navigator. She encountered an unknown race in 2153 and was partially assimilated as a Borg. Felt compelled to assimilate Enterprise.

name: Parrec-Sut
lore: Typical Orion serving under Harrad-Sar. Systems specialist aboard the Devna-Lev. Overexposure to slave girl pheromones has left him easy to fool.

name: Raakin
lore: Elder augment from the time of Khan. Kept his siblings alive after Arik Soong's arrest. Romantically involved with Persis prior to her and Malik's betrayal.

name: Riaan
lore: Talented Akaali apothecary, even by pre-industrial standards. She discovered the truth about Malurian pollution. Romantically involved with Jonathan Archer.

name: Sarin
lore: Suliban dissident and former Cabal member turned temporal agent. Genetically-enhanced shape-shifter. She worked with Klaang to expose Silik's plans.

name: Admiral Mendak
lore: Strategist and student of history. Mendak helped retrieve Selok from deep cover. Strives to emulate military icons like Admiral Valdore, Keras, and Talok.

name: Devanha
lore: Representative of Romulan technicians working for the Tal Shiar. Served under Admiral Valdore. He gathered holographic specifications on alien vessels.

name: Leodis
lore: Physician and bodyguard typical of Reman conscripts. Like many of his race, possesses telepathic abilities and extreme sensitivity to light.

name: Olicana
lore: Typical 22nd-century Romulan officer. Worked with Nijil in 2154. Specialist in remote astrometric navigation. He disliked their reliance on an Aenar.

name: Talok
lore: Romulan operative. Spent years undercover on Vulcan. Served under T'Pol on the Tomed mission. Devious major who conspired with V'Las.

name: Venoxis
lore: Typical Reman soldier. Aide and bodyguard to Senator Vrax in 2154. Dissident who secretly plotted independence from his Romulan masters.

name: Escort Vessel
lore: Federation warship. Mass produced after Miles O'Brien had resolved the kinks in the U.S.S. Defiant.
game_text: Training Cruise

name: Cargo Vessel
lore: Ferengi merchant vessel from the 22nd century. The large cargo capacity resulted in numerous trading partners adopting the design - for a modest fee.
game_text: Non-Aligned cards have standard attack restrictions here.

name: Cargo Vessel (AI)
lore: Ferengi merchant vessel from the 22nd century. The large cargo capacity resulted in numerous trading partners adopting the design - for a modest fee.
game_text: Non-Aligned cards have standard attack restrictions here.

name: Devna-Lev
lore: One of many vessels operated as a privateer and slave transport by the Orion Syndicate. Commanded by Harrad-Sar. Battled Enterprise in 2154.
game_text: Grappler (may use as if Starfleet NX-class).

name: Bird-of-Prey
lore: Typical cruiser used by the Romulan Star Empire in the 22nd century to patrol the edges of its territory. Mainstay used during the Earth-Romulan War.
game_text: X=3 if all crew are 22nd Century or Universal.

name: Raptor Two
lore: Second of two prototypes created from modified warbirds. Controlled remotely via telepresence. Carried an advanced multispatial sensor platform.
game_text: May move to Raptor One using full RANGE.

name: Smuggler's Rendezvous
lore: 2154 Near Nausicaan space: Lawless shipping lane frequented by scum and villainy.
game_text: Seeds on table; any player may download Tellarite Trading Post here. Native to this timeline: All 22nd Century cards (except Mirror Quadrant cards). Once per turn, one native personnel reporting here may do so for free. Any player may seed one native Universal ship here. Any player who seeds or reports cards here may not report cards at other time locations for rest of game.

name: Command Decisions
lore: Although there are many command styles, the best leaders share the ability to make difficult decisions and take swift action in a crisis.
game_text: One personnel (random selection) is killed unless you stop a personnel with Leadership or OFFICER. To get past requires STRENGTH>24.

name: The Clown: On His Throne
lore: Leader of a band of torturous performers, The Clown could easily tap into the fears of his victims and manipulate the artificial environment in which they resided.
game_text: Place on mission. Opponent chooses INTEGRITY, CUNNING, or STRENGTH. Replace other personnel attributes in dilemma and mission text here with the named attribute.

name: Awaiting Trial
lore: On Cardassia Prime, no crime goes unsolved and all criminals are punished. With conviction guaranteed before trial, the people's faith in Cardassian justice is assured.
game_text: Plays on table (for free if you have three Cardassian personnel in play). At the end of each of your turns, if you have a captive, draw an extra card. (Cumulative.).

name: Biosphere Toxin
lore: In 2369, to prevent the collection of further DNA samples from Indri VIII, Nu'Daq destroyed all life on the planet.
game_text: Plays on an unsolved planet mission if you have a ship there with 4 Treachery aboard. Mission worth -5 points. At the end of each turn, kills an opponent's personnel present (random selection). (Cumulative.)

name: Earn Your Rank!
lore: In a 31st-century Kyrian recreation, Starfleet officers were portrayed as belligerent and undisciplined, brawling with each other to settle their differences.
game_text: Plays on table. Your Hologram leaders gain Command; your other Hologram non-CIVILIAN personnel gain Staff . When you play Holodeck Door, draw a card.

name: Esteemed Vedek
lore: Bajorans often seek guidance from their religious leaders. Members of the Vedek Assembly help many fellow Bajorans explore their pagh and gain enlightenment.
game_text: Plays on table; download a Vedek personnel. Also, while in play, each Bajoran personnel is INTEGRITY +2. (Cumulative.)

name: Life's Simple Pleasures
lore: While Samuel Clemens lamented the loss of opening a door for a lady, the 24th century's gains in eliminating poverty, prejudice, sexism, and intolerance far outweighed any losses.
game_text: Plays on your non-Borg crew of at least six personnel. If more males than females, download a female personnel; otherwise, draw three cards. Discard event.

name: Patient Schemer
lore: Many individuals have faked their own death to conduct illicit activities with impunity. In 2369, Jo'Bril used such a ploy in an attempt to steal Dr. Reyga's metaphasic shield technology.
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. When your assassin, thief, or Jo'Bril is about to be killed by a dilemma, return them to your hand instead.

name: Psychological Pressure
lore: In 2369, the Cardassian Union used the capture of Jean-Luc Picard to gain leverage in its negotiations with Starfleet.
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. For each different regular skill in dilemma or mission requirements that is also on your captive, opponent must discard a card from hand to use that skill to meet those requirements (or choose not to).

name: Quite a Coincidence
lore: In 2371, Odo was informed that three former agents of the Obsidian Order had died the previous day from "natural causes," while two more perished in "accidents."

name: Sleeper Ship
lore: Ships like the I.K.S. T'Ong could be deployed with their crew in cryogenic suspension. Once awakened, such ships could attack - unaware of changes in the political situation.
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. When your ship wins a battle and its matching commander is aboard, you may report a personnel aboard. (Captain's Order.)

name: Condition Red
game_text: Plays on table. While aboard your ships, each of your Staff personnel gains Command. At the start of each of your turns, if opponent has more ships in play than you (including any cloaked, phased, or landed ships), you may discard a card from hand to download a ship to hand, then discard incident (unless ship is Universal). (Captain's Order.)

name: Holoprogram: The Voyager Encounter
game_text: Plays on Museum of Kyrian Heritage; Hologram cards may exist here. At the start of your turn, your native Hologram personnel may exchange (from hand to in play, or vice versa) with your personnel named in their printed lore (limit once each turn per lore reference). When a native personnel leaves play this way, draw a card. When a native personnel enters play this way, their Download is considered unused.

name: Intuition
game_text: Seeds or plays on table (for free if Deanna Troi in play). Once each turn, if you have a dabo girl, counselor, El-Aurian, or genetically enhanced personnel in play, you may name a card type and reveal a random card from opponent's hand. If it is the named card type, draw a card.

name: Training Cruise
game_text: Plays on your ship. Compatible cadets may report aboard; once each turn, one such personnel may report aboard for free. Ship is attributes all +1 for each cadet aboard (limit 4). If crew has no more than one non-cadet, ship and crew may ignore affiliation attack restrictions.

name: Souls of the Dead
lore: Many Bajorans believe that what remains after death is just a shell, with the pagh leaving the body to begin a new journey: to walk with the Prophets in the Celestial Temple.
game_text: Plays once each turn if you have three Bajoran personnel in play. Place a card from your discard pile on top of your deck.

name: That's a Stupid Question!
lore: Jack, Lauren, and Patrick impersonated Starfleet officers to escape the Institute and bring Sarina to DS9 for treatment. Admiral Patrick had the perfect reply to any challenges.
game_text: Suspends play to make all opponent's OFFICER-classification personnel attributes -2 until end of turn. OR Nullifies any card with "question" or "?" in title.

name: Conduct Perilous Trade
lore: Kyrian-Vaskan planet: Negotiate exchange of goods amid geo-political conflict.
game_text: None

name: Eleven of Ninety
lore: IDENTIFICATION: CALIBRATION DRONETASK: Track hive resource usage. Optimize.BIOLOGICAL DISTINCTIVENESS: Humanoid

name: Thorel
lore: Representative of Cardassian technicians stationed on Terok Nor in 2374. Assigned to analyze the changes to the repurposed ore processing facilities.

name: Imat'Korex
