Any player may nullify with 3 Empathy present. OR Plays on an opponent's personnel affected by Frame of Mind; personnel is captured. Discard objective if rescued or (on a later turn) to download Brainwash or Interrogation to this captive.

name: Suna
lore: Military official of Tilonus IV. He twisted William T. Riker's mind using neurosomatic techniques. Typical of treacherous Tilonian government interrogators.

name: Hide and Seek
lore: "Why don't we play a little game? I'll hide.. you find me."
game_text: Shuffle Hide and Seek together with crew or Away Team. Randomly select cards until a Universal personnel or Hide and Seek selected. All selected personnel are stopped; discard dilemma. (May be seeded as a Q dilemma.

name: Darmok
lore: Typical Tamarian vessel. "Picard and Dathon, trading knives at El-Adrel. Children at Tama's knee. Sokath, forging knives for his brothers."

name: Q: A Dazzling Flash
lore: One of many Q conflicts encountered during their voyage home, a furious chase between Q and Quinn threw the U.S.S. Voyager from the birth of the universe to a Christmas tree.
game_text: Crew or Away Team has a Q-Flash with X cards from opponent's Q-Continuum, where X = number of personnel present. Discard dilemma. (Immune to Q2.)

name: Q: Enter the Supernova
lore: A civil war between the Q resulted in the implosion of multiple stars. Each one created a negative density false vacuum, sucking the surrounding matter into the Continuum.
game_text: Crew has a Q-Flash with X cards from opponent's Q-Continuum, where X = the lowest attribute of attempting ship. Discard dilemma. (Immune to Q2.)

name: Miss Q
lore: Female Q. Has an eternal association with Q. Relied on a rickety barge and its half witted crew to stop Q from mating with a human. Mother of Q Junior. Admires Klingon females.
game_text: Once per Q-Flash, just before a card is drawn from your Q-Continuum, download a Q card (once per game per card title) and place it atop that deck. OR Nullifies a Q card.

name: Mortal Quinn
lore: Controversial Q philosopher. Granted mortality, he was able to live the rest of his life as a human.

name: An Absence of Manners
lore: "At some point along the way, I guess we just stopped thinking about the little niceties."
game_text: Plays on table until any Q-Flash. Play with your hand revealed. If, at the start of opponent's turn, you have drawn exactly one card since end of opponent's last turn (including card draws converted to downloads), discard event. May be nullified only by Plexing or Wolf.

name: It's a Party!
lore: "One dance, B'Elanna, that's all I ask."
game_text: If crew or Away Team began attempt with more than 9 or fewer than 4 personnel, plays on table until any Q-Flash. Opponent may play one additional card each turn.

name: Don't Provoke the Borg!
lore: "If the Continuum has told you once, they've told you a thousand times..."
game_text: If any Borg ship or Borg ship dilemma is on this spaceline, opponent (even if playing Borg) scores points (once per game), and you may relocate one such card up to 20 span away from its current location on same spaceline.

name: Futile Attempt
lore: "If you're attempting to embarrass me, you won't succeed."
game_text: Reveal the top card of your draw deck. If it is a personnel, it is placed beneath draw deck; opponent scores 1 point for each • and you lose 2 points for each ∇ . May be nullified by any Seven of Nine.

name: I Will Not Promise...
lore: "...never to appear again."
game_text: ''If played during a Q-Flash: Opponent may end current Q-Flash now (no more Q cards are drawn) and immediately seed this interrupt beneath any other mission like a Space/Planet dilemma.If encountered seeded beneath a mission: Crew or Away team has a Q-Flash with three Q cards.'

name: Hello Computer?
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: Any technology, if sufficiently advanced, seems indistinguishable from magic. Obsolete machinery, however, also poses certain challenges. "Just use the keyboard."
game_text: Unless Archaeology, Physics, and Computer Skill present, place on table. All your personnel are attributes all -2.

name: Nuclear Wessels
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: Searching in an unfamiliar environment can be challenging. Commander Uhura and Commander Chekov struggled to locate a naval base in ancient San Francisco.
game_text: Place on planet. Now and start of each attempt here, cannot get past unless one SECURITY OR Anthropology is stopped (random selection). (Unique.)

name: Slingshot Effect
game_text: Seeds on table. Your Alternate Classic Films personnel, ships and facilities (and Alternate cards of other card types) may seed and play. Once each turn, your Classic Films ship may time travel between a time location and its corresponding spaceline location. Temporal Investigations is nullified.

name: Earth Spacedock
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: Large starship service facility commanded by Fleet Admiral Morrow. On a clear night, visible from Earth.
game_text: Seeds at a Federation mission Sector 001 mission; you may not play cards to Camp Khitomer. Once each turn, if all your personnel are Classic Films, one Federation Classic Films personnel may play for free here.

name: Guess Who’s Coming to Dinner
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
game_text: Seeds on The Great Hall; discard if you have another headquarters in play. Once each turn, your Klingon affiliation Classic Films personnel reporting here may do so for free. You may play personnel for free only at Qo'noS. In place of your normal card draw, you may download to hand one Classic Films personnel with "High Council" in lore OR on HQ card.

name: Take Us Out!
lore: The late 23rd century saw many scientific and technological advancements. New ships were launched and older ships refurbished, each one worthy of celebration.
game_text: Seeds on table. If all your ships in play are Classic Films, they are RANGE and SHIELDS +2 while uncloaked. Nullified if you have in play both Camp Khitomer and a headquarters.

name: The Undiscovered Country
game_text: Seeds on table. While all your personnel in play are Classic Films, you may draw an extra card at the end of your turn. Once per game, in place of your normal card play, you may nullify Homefront. Nullified if you have in play both Camp Khitomer and a headquarters.

name: We Surrender!
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: To avoid instigating full scale war on the eve of universal peace, Captain Kirk ordered his crew to yield to the Klingon flagship.
game_text: Plays at start of a battle opponent initiated against your card. Cancels and prevents battles there. Up to two of your personnel involved (opponent's choice) are captured.

name: Overhaul Starship Systems
lore: Sector 001 Region ● Near Earth: Enhance, repair, and upgrade vessel to latest specifications.

name: GIVE ME GENESIS!
property_logo: StarTrek III: The Search for Spock
game_text: Seeds on any Federation mission Planet mission that requires SCIENCE OR Geology. No player may use The Genesis Device on a mission they seeded. In place of your normal card play, you may download Kruge here; lose 5 points. When you solve mission, you may download The Genesis Device here. (Unique.)

name: Reserve Activation Clause
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Once each turn, just after the end of a mission attempt, you may "retire" one Federation Classic Films personnel who was involved in that attempt when it ended (place atop objective; in play for uniqueness only) and play a different Classic Films personnel there (from hand) instead. Once per game, you may play one personnel from here to your crew or Away Team.

name: Admiral S’rrel
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: Typical Caitian diplomat and ambassador serving in Starfleet. Mentor to Lt. M'Ress. Attended the inquiry following the controversial events at Genesis.

name: Bill Toddman
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Fleet admiral and Chief in Command in 2293. Agreed to open negotiations with the Klingon Empire.

name: Bob Bennett
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Starfleet Chief of Staff. Admiral who sent the U.S.S. Enterprise-A to Nimbus III. Helped write and produce leadership textbooks used at Starfleet Academy.

name: Captain Alexander
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: Decorated Starfleet captain. She commanded the Starship Saratoga in 2286 when it encountered the whale probe. Previously served under Admiral Kirk.

name: Captain Kirk
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Demoted admiral who became captain of the U.S.S. Enterprise-A. Father of David Marcus. His efforts at Khitomer helped build an alliance with the Klingons.

name: Commander Sonak
lore: Typical Vulcan science officer. Newly appointed to the refitted Starship Enterprise. He expressed gratitude to Admiral Kirk for the assignment.

name: Fleet Admiral Morrow
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: High-ranking admiral who succeeded Admiral Nogura. He commissioned the failed transwarp drive project and tried to decommission the Starship Enterprise.

name: Igrilan Kor
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: Reprentative of Andorian admirals in the 2280s. Friend of Ambassador Shras. Part of the inquiry group looking into the fallout from Project Genesis.

name: Lt. Slater
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Night shift communications officer aboard Starship Excelsior. Expert in ordnance disposal. Likes archery, vampire stories, and orange sherbet. A true romantic.

name: Pavel Chekov
lore: After a long career, Ensign Chekov was a guest at the U.S.S. Enterprise-B launch. Commander who assisted as a nurse due to a lack of medical staff.

name: Peter Preston
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Diligent cadet. Nephew of Mr. Scott. Called a tiger by Admiral Kirk. Stayed at his post during the attack by the U.S.S. Reliant, when most other trainees ran.

name: President Ra-ghoratreii
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Efrosian who succeeded Hiram Roth. Redefined relations with the Klingons and the Cardassians during his time in office. Not above the law.

name: Saavik
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Vulcan science officer aboard U.S.S. Grissom. Friend to David Marcus. She studied the rapid development of both Genesis and a similarly aging Captain Spock.

name: Brask
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Typical reserve gunner serving in the Klingon Defense Force. Expert marksman. Understood Kruge's order to only target the engines of the Starship Enterprise.

name: Frexor
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: One of many Klingon technicians serving in the Klingon Defense Force. Beamed down to Genesis with Kruge and Regnor to investigate the planet.

name: Garvock
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Typical Klingon soldier aboard the I.K.S. Chontay. He escorted Captain Kirk to the bridge after beaming up from Sha Ka Ree. Collects antique d'k tahgs.

name: General Grokh
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Intelligence officer recently promoted to serve on the High Council. Assisted General Chang with developing the I.K.S. Kla'Diyus. Opposed to the peace initiative.

name: General K'Ron
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Characteristic of High Council logistics experts. Encouraged Azetbur to attack the Federation now, rather than becomes slaves under their rule.

name: General Lompoc
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Representative of Klingon scientific advisors to the High Council. Enjoyed the gagh served aboard the U.S.S. Enterprise-A. Not fond of Shakespeare.

name: K'mbol
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Typical military surgeon. Expert in Klingon anatomy. Assigned by the High Council to single-handedly oversee the medical needs to Chancellor Gorkon.

name: Magistrate K'Rea
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Senior judge for the High Council. Gave Captain Kirk and Dr. McCoy a lenient sentence in the interest of fostering amity for the forthcoming peace talks.

name: Prisoner Martia
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Female Chameloid and shape-shifter who posed as a male to access the mines on Rura Penthe. Martia conspired with Koth to stage an execution.

name: Prisoner McCoy
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: The human Dr. McCoy was sentenced to mining duties on Rura Penthe for the remainder of his life. He unsuccessfully tried to save Chancellor Gorkon.

name: Spock Son of Sarek
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Half brother to Sybok. Under orders from General Korrd, Klaa allowed the 1/2 Vulcan, 1/2 human Mr. Spock to act as gunner for the I.K.S. Chontay.

name: Starship Saratoga
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: NCC-1887. Commanded by Captain Alexander. Patrolled the Neutral Zone in 2286. Unsuccessfully attempted to communicate with the whale probe.

name: The Genesis Device
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Torpedo created by Project Genesis. Reorganizes matter at the subatomic level to achieve rapid terraforming on a planetary scale. Its matrix utilizes dangerously unstable protomatter.
game_text: Use as Equipment (until placed). On your turn, if not playing Federation, may place on Planet mission here. If unsolved at start of your next turn, choose: worth double points OR zero points. (Unique.)

name: Engine Imbalance
lore: An improperly balanced warp drive system poses a serious hazard. Even a minor misalignment can propel a ship into an artificial wormhole.
game_text: Place on ship. It may not fly by a location without stopping, and its RANGE is exhausted each time it moves. Cure with 2 ENGINEER, Computer Skill, and Physics.

name: "God"
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: "This starship. Could it carry my wisdom beyond the Barrier? ...Then I shall make use of this starship... bring it closer, so that I might... join with it.
game_text: Unless two Away Team members each have INTEGRITY>7, place on mission; destroys one ship here (opponent's choice). You must have a ship here to attempt mission.

name: Hero Worship
lore: "Doctor Cochrane, I know this sounds silly, but can I shake your hand?"
game_text: Stops non-Borg crew or Away Team members with the most and fewest Skill Dot icons. (In case of ties, stops all tied personnel.)

name: I Hate You
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: "The sins of all our fathers, is being dumped on us – The sons. The only choice we're given is HOW MANY MEGATONS? And I eschew you! And I say SCREW YOU! And I hope you're blue too."
game_text: To get past requires Anthropology, Youth, and no Music present. Nullified by Vulcan Nerve Pinch.

name: Linguistic Legerdemain
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Undiscovered County
lore: "We must respond personally. The universal translator would be recognized."
game_text: Unless Anthropology and Exobiology present, X=1+number of affiliation icons on this mission with no matching personnel present; place on mission; it cannot be attempted.

page_title: Now Would Be a Good Time (TMPR)
name: Now Would Be a Good Time
base_name: Now Would Be a Good Time
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: With insufficient transporter power for Scotty to beam him off the aircraft carrier Enterprise, Chekov was captured and interrogated by the U.S. Navy. Being Russian didn't help him.
game_text: Your Transporter Skill here with transporters may beam up Away Team. Otherwise, one personnel present (opponent's choice) is captured; others stopped. Discard dilemma..

name: Subspace Shock Wave
lore: Dangerous aftermath of a stellar, planetary, or lunar explosion. The shock wave created by the "incident" on Praxis was felt even beyond the boundaries of Klingon space.
game_text: Ship is damaged and two crew members are killed (random selection) unless a Navigation personnel who has CUNNING>7 present. Discard dilemma.

name: The Whale Probe
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: Alien space probe of unknown origin. Traveled to Earth to contact the extinct humpback whale. Its powerful transmission caused total power loss aboard nearby ships and starbases.
game_text: Place on mission. End of every turn, moves one location toward and off far end of spaceline. All ships, personnel, and facilities are in stasis while here. (Unique.)

name: V'Ger
lore: Massive living machine created by an unknown race around the lost NASA space probe Voyager VI. Left a trail of destruction during its return to Earth in search of its creator.
game_text: Ship is destroyed unless 2 Empathy OR Diplomacy, Anthropology, and Computer Skill present. Discard dilemma.

name: The Nexus
game_text: '''Seeds like a Space/Planet dilemma. When encountered, place on far end of spaceline. End of every turn, moves one location toward other end. (Not duplicatable.) All personnel here are placed under Nexus (in play for uniqueness only). Destroys all ships here. At end of spaceline, place on table. At any time, players may relocate their personnel here to a Planet mission or time location. (Immune to Revolving Door.)

name: Transport Inhibitor
lore: Device that emits an energy field preventing the operation of transporters within a radius of several meters. Used by the Enterprise crew in their defense against the Son'a.
game_text: If your personnel present, you may prevent any beaming to or from this equipment. Opponent may destroy equipment if their personnel are present and unopposed.

name: Transporter Drones
lore: Typical reconnaissance devices modified by the Son'a to fire isolinear tags. Transporters can lock onto a tagged object, overcoming any interference with normal targeting scanners.
game_text: Participates in battle like a personnel, using STRENGTH=8 (may not be modified) vs. adversary's CUNNING. May capture, and beam to your ship here, an adversary it stuns.

name: Duj Saq
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Klingon for "land the ship." Though K'Vort-class ships were larger and more heavily armed than the B'rel design they were based upon, only the 23rd-century original had this ability.
game_text: Plays on table. Your B'rel-class ships may report on planets that have a matching affiliation icon. Each may use 1 RANGE to land or take off once each turn. (Captain's Order.)

name: Fal-tor-pan
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Vulcan refusion of the body and katra. The ritual was performed successfully for the first time since ancient legend between Leonard H. McCoy, son of David, and Spock, son of Sarek.
game_text: Plays on table. At any time, if top card of your discard pile is a Vulcan personnel, you may place it here. Personnel here may report to the planet Vulcan as if from your hand.

page_title: I Just Love Scanning for Life-Forms (TMPR)
name: I Just Love Scanning for Life-Forms
base_name: I Just Love Scanning for Life-Forms
lore: "Life-forms... you tiny little life-forms... you precious little life-forms... where are you?"
game_text: Plays to reveal up to three cards from the top of any draw deck (six if your own). Discard all non-personnel cards; replace remaining cards in any order. Discard event.

name: Isomagnetic Disintegrator
lore: Don't give an isomagnetic disintegrator to a Klingon showing signs of jak'tahla unless you want him to use it.
game_text: Plays on table. Shuffle your hand into your discard pile, then exchange your discard pile for your draw deck. Draw four cards (may not be converted to downloads). Discard event.

page_title: To Be or Not to Be (TMPR)
name: To Be or Not to Be
base_name: To Be or Not to Be
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: taH pagh taHbe'. DaH mu'tlheghvam vlqelnlS. quv'a', yabDaq San vaQ cha, pu' je SIQDI'? pagh, Seng blQ'a'Hey SuvmeH nuHmey SuqDI', 'ej, Suvmo', rlnmoHDI'?
game_text: Plays on table. May discard event just after a battle your opponent initiated to damage all opposing ships (including cloaked ships) in that battle. (Immune to Kevin Uxbridge.)

name: Ceti Eel
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
game_text: Plays on table (once each turn, for free). On your turn, you may place on a personnel present with Khan. Personnel becomes Non-Aligned, is under your control, is attributes all –3, and is not discarded at end of turn by Revenge Is A Dish Best Served Cold. Nullified if personnel is an android or Hologram. You may not place more than two Ceti Eels on personnel during any turn (even with Mas'ud).

name: Release This Pain
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: "Share your pain with me… and gain strength from the sharing."
game_text: Plays once each turn (for free) on a personnel present with your Sybok. Personnel loses all Treachery, is under your control, gains Sha Ka Ree, and is compatible with your Sha Ka Ree cards.

page_title: I Do Not Take Orders From You! (TMPR)
name: I Do Not Take Orders From You!
base_name: I Do Not Take Orders From You!
lore: Admiral Dougherty knew the Son'a were devious and dangerous, but never imagined how far Ru'afo would go until it was too late. "The Federation will never know what happened here."
game_text: Plays at start of a personnel battle you initiated (once per battle). Each of your personnel who has Treachery x2 may kill an opposing personnel who has lower CUNNING.

name: Lure of the Nexus
lore: Though exiting the nexus is as simple as wishing it so, its temptations are so great that few desire to leave. Those pulled away against their will are forever changed by their experience.
game_text: Prevent a personnel from leaving The Nexus. OR Relocate all personnel under The Nexus aboard a ship about to be destroyed by it; relocate ship to adjacent location. Discard interrupt.

page_title: No, Kirk... The Game's Not Over (TMPR)
name: No, Kirk... The Game's Not Over
base_name: No, Kirk... The Game's Not Over
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: "From hell's heart, I stab at thee! For hate's sake... I spit my last breath at thee!"
game_text: Plays if you just changed a mission's point value using The Genesis Device. Discard all planet facilities, landed ships, and ships in orbit there, and all personnel on planet.

name: Prefix Code Transmission
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Each starship is assigned a unique security code to prevent remote access to its vital systems. With knowledge of the code, a ship can be ordered to lowers its own shields.
game_text: Plays on your ship when firing on a target that has a matching affiliation or faction icon or that your infiltrator is aboard. Opposing DEFENSE total reduced by half (round down).

name: Smooth As an Android's Bottom?
lore: Geordi once told Data that technological perfection can shave too close. That, of course, depends on the desired results.

name: The Needs of the Many...
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: "...outweigh...." "The needs of the few." "Or the one." Captain Spock made the ultimate sacrifice not because it was noble, but because it was logical.
game_text: Nullifies a dilemma or damage marker if it would destroy your ship. Discard one of that ship's crew members (opponent's choice).

page_title: What Does God Need With a Starship? (TMPR)
name: What Does God Need With a Starship?
base_name: What Does God Need With a Starship?
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: "Excuse me. I'd... just like to ask a question."
game_text: Nullifies "God." OR Plays once per game. Opponent chooses: you may download a ship to any location or you may stop or unstop (your choice) any ship in play.

name: Analyze Radiation
lore: Briar Patch Region ● Sector 441: Conduct analysis of the metaphasic particles in this nebula.
game_text: Span -2 for all Son'a ships.

name: Insurrection
lore: Briar Patch Region ● Ba'ku planet: Prevent the Son'a attempt to forcibly relocate the Ba'ku race.
game_text: Ba'ku may report on planet (for free).

name: Observe Ritual
lore: Vulcan: Transport crew member to Vulcan homeworld to participate in a cultural ceremony.
game_text: Vulcans and Amanda Grayson may report on planet.

page_title: The Discovery of Sha Ka Ree (TMPR)
name: The Discovery of Sha Ka Ree
base_name: The Discovery of Sha Ka Ree
lore: Great Barrier Region • Sha Ka Ree: "...to undertake the greatest adventure of all time..."

name: Collect Metaphasic Particles
game_text: Seeds or plays on Ba'ku Planet. Your personnel may attempt it using these requirements:Any Son'a personnel + Injector Assembly One in orbit + Treachery x2 + no opposing ships or personnel hereWhen you solve, you may skip opponent's next turn and, for rest of game, all your personnel are STRENGTH +2, add Youth, and you may unstop them each once each turn.

page_title: Revenge Is a Dish Best Served Cold (TMPR)
name: Revenge Is a Dish Best Served Cold
base_name: Revenge Is a Dish Best Served Cold
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
game_text: Seeds on table during facility phase; you may download U.S.S. Reliant. Once each turn, your Khan (or personnel with "Khan" in lore) may report for free aboard U.S.S. Reliant; at end of every turn, you must discard all other personnel you have in play. At start of each of your turns, if your Khan and The Genesis Device are aboard your U.S.S. Reliant, score 30 points (only 15 if opponent has any Kirk in play).

name: Admiral Cartwright
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Militant admiral opposed to Chancellor Gorkon's peace initiative. Used his covert contacts in mounting a conspiracy to assassinate the Klingon leader.

name: Admiral Kirk
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: While Captain Kirk regretted accepting promotion, he commanded the Starship Enterprise in later crises. Time away from the center seat did not diminish his ingenuity.

name: Amanda Grayson
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: Human wife of Ambassador Sarek. Admires the Vulcan way, but taught her son Captain Spock that the capacity of human emotion is just as great.

name: Ambassador Sarek
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Vulcan ambassador. Sent Admiral Kirk to recover the body of his son Captain Spock. Reciprocated Kirk's effort by defending him to the Federation Council.

name: Captain Spock
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: ½ Vulcan, ½ human. Mr. Spock was restored from death by the Genesis wave – and his friends' resolve.

name: Captain Styles
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Overconfident captain of the Starship Excelsior for a failed transwarp test. Planned to break old Starship Enterprise speed records. Was really in for a shock.

name: Captain Sulu
lore: After moving through the ranks aboard the Starship Enterprise, Lt. Sulu earned a captaincy in 2290. Holds loyalty in high regard, his crew as dear as family.

name: Carol Marcus
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Molecular biologist. Head of Project Genesis. Once romantically involved with Admiral Kirk. Asked that he leave her to raise David Marcus in her world, not his.

name: Clark Terrell
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Captain of U.S.S. Reliant. Has a strong sense of duty. Has never met Admiral Kirk, but knows something of him from a few stories told by Commander Chekov.

name: Commander Chekov
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Over the years, Ensign Chekov's distinguished career would include many promotions, and positions as acting science officer, security chief, navigator, and first officer.

name: Commander Rand
lore: After serving on the Starship Enterprise, Yeoman Rand desired greater duties. She rose to transporter chief and Starship Excelsior's communications officer.

name: Commander Uhura
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: While Lt. Uhura had promotions and transfers, she seized each chance to return to Starship Enterprise. Got to play for a captive audience on Nimbus III.

name: David Marcus
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Gifted scientist. Like his father, often bends the rules. His impatience was Project Genesis' breakthrough and downfall. Proud - very proud - to be Admiral Kirk's son.

name: Demora Sulu
lore: Daughter of Captain Sulu. Helmsman of the U.S.S. Enterprise-B. James T. Kirk declared: "It wouldn't be the Enterprise without a Sulu at the helm."

name: Dmitri Valtane
lore: Starship Excelsior science officer. Monitored the 2293 disaster on the Klingon moon Praxis. Host of a parasitic memory virus. Thinks Vulcans need to relax.

name: Dr. Chapel
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: After her first tour aboard the Starship Enterprise, Nurse Chapel earned a medical doctorate. She later accepted a post at Starfleet Command.

name: Dr. McCoy
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Leonard H. "Bones" McCoy. Retired from Starfleet in 2270, but returned a year later on Admiral Kirk's request. Retired again in 2293. Would again return.

name: Ensign Tuvok
lore: 29-year-old Vulcan on first deep space assignment aboard Captain Sulu's Starship Excelsior in 2293. Joined Starfleet under pressure from his parents.

name: Henreid
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Typical first officer. Assigned to Starship Excelsior in 2285. Stood in for the helmsman, who was on leave when Admiral Kirk stole the Starship Enterprise.

name: Ilia
lore: Deltan navigator assigned to the Starship Enterprise. Her Oath of Celibacy is on record. Was romantically involved with Willard Decker while posted to Delta IV.

name: J.T. Esteban
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Captain of the U.S.S. Grissom. Has served as such for over four years without serious incident, due largely to his cautious, "by the book" command style.

name: Jacobson
lore: Typical member of the medical staff aboard the Starship Enterprise, serving under Dr. McCoy and Dr. Chapel. Specialist in microcellular biology.

name: James T. Kirk
lore: Famous captain thought lost in 2293. Returned from the Nexus 78 years later to make a difference once more.

name: John Harriman
lore: Son of a respected Federation official. Captain of U.S.S. Enterprise-B. Usually confident in dealing with reporters, but on the ship's maiden voyage was having an off day.

name: Lojur
lore: Conservative helmsman of the Starship Excelsior. Serves adequately in the position, but is less knowledgeable about the ship and its limitations than Captain Sulu.

name: Mark Tobiaston
lore: Communications officer, fully rated on Excelsior-class ships. Linguistics expert who has authored an analysis on similarities of the Vulcan and Romulan languages.

name: Matthew Dougherty
lore: Conflicted admiral under orders from the Federation Council to oversee the Ba'ku relocation. Dislikes working with Ru'afo, but will do it for the Federation.

name: Mr. Scott
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Scotty knows his ship like the back of his hand. With his help, a chimpanzee and two trainees could run her.

name: Saavik
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Vulcan cadet mentored by Captain Spock. She prefers to do things "by the book." Was determined to learn how Admiral Kirk beat the Kobayashi Maru.

name: St. John Talbot
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Ambassador to the worthless lump of rock known as Nimbus III. Released the pain of his cynicism when Sybok enlisted his help in the search for Eden.

name: T'Lar
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Revered elder. High priestess of the ancient temple at Mount Seleya. The only Vulcan known to have actually performed a successful fal-tor-pan ceremony.

name: Tahglio
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Typical guard for Federation Security. Given a low-priority post on Earth after a poor performance review at his last assignment. His next review showed no improvement.

name: Valeris
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Vulcan protégé of Captain Spock whom he intended as his replacement. She made a choice to sabotage negotiations with the untrustworthy Klingon Empire.

name: Voight
lore: Science officer aboard U.S.S. Enterprise-B. Joined Starfleet to pursue her interest in alien environments. Has Irish lineage dating back nearly four centuries.

name: Willard Decker
lore: Son of Commodore Decker. Succeeded Admiral Kirk as captain of the Starship Enterprise, at Kirk's recommendation. Personally oversaw its refit.

name: Azetbur
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Daughter of Chancellor Gorkon; became chancellor herself in 2293. Pursued his dream of peace with the Federation, signing the historic Khitomer Accords.

name: Brigadier Kerla
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Military advisor to the High Council leader. Loyally served both Chancellor Gorkon and Azetbur, though bitterly opposed to peace with the Federation.

name: Captain Kang
lore: Respected warrior. Named his firstborn son in honor of Curzon Dax. Watched the careers of the Starship Enterprise crew since encountering them in 2268.

name: Ch'dak
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Characteristic member of the I.K.S. Kla'Diyus crew. A pilot rated on many designs, he enjoyed the new tactics enabled by the ability to attack while cloaked.

name: Chancellor Gorkon
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Klingon leader who first embraced the notion of peace with the Federation. His vision mapped the way to the undiscovered country – the future.

name: Colonel Worf
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Warrior and father of Mogh. He represented Captain Kirk and Dr. McCoy at their trial. His low political standing improved once they were proved innocent.

name: General Chang
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Chief of staff of the High Council leader. Conspired to assassinate Chancellor Gorkon and ensure no peace. Likes Shakespeare, especially in the original Klingon.

name: General Korrd
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Once-renowned military strategist exiled to Nimbus III by the High Council. Released the pain of his dishonor when Sybok enlisted his help in the search for Qui'tu.

name: Kamarag
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: Ambassador to the Federation. Believed Admiral Kirk wanted Project Genesis as a weapon against Qo'noS. Predicted there would be no peace while Kirk lived.

name: Karnog
lore: Science officer aboard the I.K.S. Amar. Tried to analyze the sensor data from the intruder V'Ger. Unfortunately, his expertise was in the planetary sciences.

name: Klaa
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Aggressive captain. He hunted the U.S.S. Enterprise-A without authorization in 2287. Later demoted and assigned menial translation duties on Qo'noS.

name: Komal
lore: Typical chief surgeon of a K't'inga-class ship. Friend of Krase. Strongly opinionated, he often provides his captain with advice, whether asked to or not.

name: Kor'choth
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Typical bodyguard of the High Council leader. Lost an arm defending Chancellor Gorkon. Refused prosthetic replacement. Gave evidence at the subsequent trial.

name: Koth
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Warden of the penal asteroid Rura Penthe. His greatest pleasures are watching fights among his inmates and delivering his welcoming speech to new prisoners.

name: Krase
lore: Captain of the I.K.S. Amar. His tendency to rash behavior has earned him a ruthless reputation – even by Klingon standards.

name: Kruge
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Klingon commander with a festering hatred of the Federation. Attempted to seize the secret of the Genesis weapon – the secret of ultimate power.

name: Maltz
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Klingon serving under Kruge. Prefers the night shift. Captured when his ship was commandeered. Willing to die for this dishonor. Admiral Kirk saw otherwise.

name: Regnor
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Trained medic serving under Kruge. Like most serving aboard smaller Klingon vessels, is more often called upon as a soldier.

name: Torg
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Kruge's first officer. Led the boarding party sent to secure the Starship Enterprise. His promotions came slowly. Doesn't know when he's being spoken to.

name: Valkris
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Klingon operative romantically involved with Kruge. Obtained top secret documents on Project Genesis. It was the pinnacle of her career in espionage.

name: Vixis
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Klaa's first officer. Tracked the U.S.S. Enterprise-A by intercepting their distress signal and impersonating Starfleet Command. She has wonderful muscles.

name: Woteln
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Technican at the Morska listening post. Representative of those performing less glorious duties in service of the Klingon Empire. "Dujvetlh'e' nuq? ...rIn."

name: George and Gracie
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: Two humpback whales, male and female, raised in captivity on 20th-century Earth. Gracie is pregnant.

name: Dr. Gillian Taylor
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: 20th-century marine biologist. Helped Admiral Kirk safely bring George and Gracie to the 23rd-century, where she then signed on aboard a Starfleet vessel.

name: Dr. Gillian Taylor
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: 20th-century marine biologist. Helped Admiral Kirk safely bring George and Gracie to the 23rd-century, where she then signed on aboard a Starfleet vessel.

name: Dr. Tolian Soran
lore: El-Aurian refugee "rescued" from the Nexus in 2293 by the U.S.S. Enterprise-B. Spent the next 78 years obsessed with returning there, no matter the cost.

name: Gallatin
lore: Ru'afo's first officer. Once the most vengeance-minded of the Son'a, recent time with the Ba'ku – and a persuasive Federation captain – has softened his hatred.

name: J'Onn
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Humanoid settler of Nimbus III. Release the pain of his impoverishment when Sybok enlisted his help in the search for the knowledge sought by all since time began.

name: Joachim
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Khan's lieutenant and most trusted friend. Augment who acted as first officer on the U.S.S. Reliant when, after nearly two decades, they escaped Ceti Alpha V.

name: Khan
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Genetically engineered augment exiled to Ceti Alpha V by Admiral Kirk. Seeks to avenge his wife's death.

name: Martia
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Chameloid prisoner on Rura Penthe. She helped set up Captain Kirk and Dr. McCoy to get a full pardon. Great shape-shifter, though it takes "a lot of effort."

name: Mas'ud
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Specimen of late 20th-century genetic engineering. Augment who swore loyalty to Khan. Studied the effects of the Ceti eel while trapped on Ceti Alpha V.

name: Pa'rena
lore: Son'a female. Chief science officer of the Li'seria. Part of the team that perfected mass production of ketracel-white for trade with the Dominion.

name: Rae'alin
lore: One of the Son'a assigned to the Ba'ku duck blind operation. Has been secretly looking for opportunities to steal technology from the Federation installation.

name: Ru'afo
lore: Leader of the Son'a, a people banished from their home planet by the Ba'ku. Will let nothing stand in the way of his revenge upon them, least of all his Federation allies.

name: Sam'po
lore: Tactical officer aboard the Li'seria. Among the most far gone of the Son'a – will likely die within a few months unless he receives metaphasic treatment.

name: Sarod
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Loyal augment follower of Khan. He served as the group's physician. With healthy "supermen" rarely taxing him, he knew of nothing to save Lt. McGivers.

name: Sharic
lore: Typical Tarlac, born into indentured servitude of the Son'a. Ru'afo's personal body sculpture attendant. Very good at what she does.

name: Sybok
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Vulcan son of Ambassador Sarek and half-brother to Captain Spock. Banished for his belief in Sha Ka Ree.

name: Wajahut
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Eugenics Wars augment. Escaped on the Botany Bay with Khan. With superior intellect and knowledge of that ship, she quickly adapted to the U.S.S. Reliant.

name: Caithlin Dar
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Ambassador to Nimbus III. Hides disdain for the position with overeagerness. Released the pain of her deception when Sybok enlisted her help in the search for Vorta Vor.

name: Nanclus
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Romulan Ambassador to the Federation in 2293. Conspired with Admiral Cartwright and General Chang in the assassination of Chancellor Gorkon.

name: H.M.S. Bounty
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: Bird-of-prey captained by Kruge on a covert mission to the Genesis Planet. Stolen and commanded by Admiral Kirk; re-christened with historical irony by Dr. McCoy.

name: H.M.S. Bounty
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: Bird-of-prey captained by Kruge on a covert mission to the Genesis Planet. Stolen and commanded by Admiral Kirk; re-christened with historical irony by Dr. McCoy.

name: Starship Constitution
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: With new modifications, ships of this class were built long after the original's launch. Starfleet continued this practice of refitting older designs into the 24th century.
game_text: Download Any Universal Federation Classic Films personnel

name: Starship Enterprise
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Venerable Starfleet ship refit in 2270. Completed many successful missions before being transferred to Captain Spock's command and retired for use as a training vessel.

name: Starship Excelsior
lore: Unsuccessful transwarp test ship later refitted as the prototype for one of Starfleet's most durable and ubiquitous classes of ship. Commanded by Captain Sulu.

name: U.S.S. Enterprise-A
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: Specially commissioned in 2286 to replace the famous ship lost one year earlier. Proudly continued the mission of its predecessor under the command of James T. Kirk.
game_text: Any Federation Classic Films personnel OR James T. Kirk

name: U.S.S. Enterprise-B
lore: Third Federation ship so christened, launched on stardate 9715. Became fully operational the following Tuesday.
game_text: El-Aurians may report aboard.

name: I.K.S. Amar
lore: One of the first K't'inga-class ships. Leader of the battle group dispatched to escort an unidentified intruder out of Klingon space in 2271.

name: I.K.S. Chontay
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Bird-of-prey captained by Klaa. The highlight of its mission was shooting space garbage until its pursuit of the U.S.S. Enterprise-A through the Great Barrier.

name: I.K.S. K'elric
lore: One of three ships that ended The Albino's raids on Klingon colonies. Intercepted the Starship Excelsior in the Azure Nebula. Commanded by Captain Kang.

name: I.K.S. K't'inga
lore: Though the basic form of the Klingon cruiser had been the same since the 22nd century, this design introduced in the 2270s boasted upgrades to all major systems.
game_text: Any Universal Klingon Classic Films personnel

name: I.K.S. Kla'Diyus
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Unique vessel able to fire while cloaked. Commissioned and commanded by General Chang, who ordered the designers killed to preserve the secret of its existence.

name: Kronos One
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Battle cruiser of the Klingon Chancellor in the late 23rd century. Under command of Chancellor Gorkon, had a fateful rendezvous with the U.S.S. Enterprise-A.

name: Injector Assembly One
lore: Specialized ship designed to collect metaphasic radiation particles from the ring system of the Ba'ku planet – a procedure tested extensively by Ru'afo in simulations.
game_text: May report to location of your Son'a ship . Download Collect Metaphasic Particles

name: Li'seria
lore: Flagship of the small Son'a fleet and base of operations for their entire race. Commanded by Ru'afo.
game_text: Son'a shuttlecraft may report, be carried, and launch aboard.

name: Son'a Battleship
lore: Fast and deadly, the largest of Son'a ships carry isolytic subspace weapons banned by the Khitomer Accord.
game_text: Son'a shuttlecraft may report, be carried, and launch aboard.

name: Son'a Shuttle
lore: Small craft capable of atmospheric flight. Used to strafe the Ba'ku village and launch Son'a transporter drones.
game_text: Transporter Drones may report aboard (for free, once each turn).

name: U.S.S. Reliant
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: NCC-1864. Placed at the disposal of Project Genesis to locate a suitable Stage Three testing site. Captured at Ceti Alpha V and subsequently commanded by Khan.

name: U.S.S. Reliant
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: NCC-1864. Placed at the disposal of Project Genesis to locate a suitable Stage Three testing site. Captured at Ceti Alpha V and subsequently commanded by Khan.

property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan

name: Camp Khitomer
lore: 2293 Khitomer: Site of the ground-breaking peace talks between the Federation and the Klingon Empire.
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Native to this timeline: all cards with both Classic Films and Alternate icon. Once per turn, one such card reporting at this location may report for free.

name: Cetacean Institute
lore: 1986 Earth: Marine biology research laboratory and public aquarium located in Sausolito, California.
game_text: Seeds or plays on table; download George and Gracie here. Native to this timeline: Dr. Gillian Taylor and George and Gracie.

name: Kirk's Reading Glasses
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Eighteenth century spectacles. A birthday present from Dr. McCoy in 2285. Admiral Kirk sold them for 100 dollars in 1986. Would have been worth more if the lenses were intact.
game_text: Immediately plays on table. Once each turn, you may exchange a card in hand for a card in your discard pile.

name: Row, Row, Row Your Boat
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Even amongst old friends, conflicts can arise. Captain Spock initially struggled to comprehend the meaning behind the lyrics of his compatriots' chosen campfire song.
game_text: To get past requires 2 Music OR total attributes > 63 from up to 3 personnel.

name: This is Ceti Alpha Five!
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Commander Chekov was wrong about one potential test site for Project Genesis being lifeless. "Botany Bay?! ...Oh no!"
game_text: If Away Team unopposed, opponent may relocate up to three augments here. Your Transporter Skill here with transporters may beam up one personnel. Place on mission; no downloading personnel here.

name: Charter a Space Flight
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Visiting a bar in 2285, Dr. McCoy attempted to find a pilot offering passage to the forbidden Genesis planet. He was hoping for no questions asked and no Starfleet entanglements.
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. At end of each turn, you may discard a Non-Aligned ship from hand to relocate your Away Team to a planet within the printed RANGE of that ship.

name: Operation Retrieve
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: On the assumption that diplomacy would fail, Colonel West drafted a daring rescue plan to return the captured Starfleet officers being held on Rura Penthe.
game_text: Plays on a personnel you own who is a captive OR under opponent's control. Personnel returns to hand. If they are , you may immediately play them (for free). Discard event.

name: Paradise City
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Capital of the so-called "Planet of Galactic Peace." The dregs of the galaxy were conned into settling on this worthless lump of rock. Many hide their pain.
game_text: Seeds at Nimbus III. J'Onn may seed here. In place of your normal card play, you may download Sybok here.

name: Space Lab Regula 1
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Advanced research biolab. Home to stage one testing of Project Genesis. Commanded by Carol Marcus.
game_text: Seeds at Regula I. Dilemmas that require SCIENCE to overcome, cure, or nullify, when revealed, stop a personnel (random selection). Download Science Kit

name: He Took Away my Pain!
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Dr. McCoy carried the guilt of allowing his father to die shortly before a cure was found. Sybok helped McCoy let go of this burden.

name: To Rule in Hell
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
game_text: Seeds on Ceti Alpha V. Your Khan may seed here and your Non-ALigned cards may report here. You may discard two cards from hand to relocate your Khan (and any personnel you control present with your Khan) to here. When your opponent encounters Augment Aggression, you may forfeit its download and relocate up to three of your augments to that location instead.

name: Double Dumbass on You!
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: Navigating an unfamiliar culture, with its unique idioms and colorful metaphors, can be quite a challenge.

lore: Mutara Region • Regula I: Assess long-term stability of artificially created habitable areas.

name: Bones
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: The katra of Mr. Spock inhabited the body of his human friend Dr. McCoy. Has all their marbles. Needed to go and climb the steps of Mount Seleya.

name: Colonel West
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Assassin, master of disguise, and provocateur. He conspired with Admiral Cartwright to incite a war between the Klingon Empire and the Federation.

name: Commander Kyle
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Lt. Kyle earned a promotion while serving aboard U.S.S. Reliant. Marooned on Ceti Alpha V by Khan.

name: Commander Sulu
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Father of Demora Sulu. Lt. Sulu spent years serving under Admiral Kirk. Fell under Sybok's influence.

name: Commander Uhura
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Lt. Uhura served aboard the Starship Enterprise for many years. Sybok helped put her in touch with feelings she'd always been afraid to express.

name: L'Kel
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Typical crewman working under Kruge. Assigned to join Torg's boarding party. Eager to bring glory to his house by capturing the infamous Starship Enterprise.

name: Aranty
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Large humanoid prisoner serving his sentence on Rura Penthe. Friends with Martia. Wanted Captain Kirk's obedience to the Brotherhood of Aliens. And his coat.

name: Clark Terrell
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Captain of the U.S.S. Reliant. Surrendered his ship while controlled via Ceti eel. Provided Khan with the coordinates to beam up the Genesis Device.

name: Commander Chekov
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: First officer of the U.S.S. Reliant who misidentified Ceti Alpha VI. Khan remembered Ensign Chekov from the Starship Enterprise. Controlled via Ceti eel.

name: Kjott
property_logo: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
lore: Humanoid prisoner on Rura Penthe. Overconfident bully. Proudly displays his genitals, in keeping with his cultural norms. Few know they aren't just knees.

name: Miss Kendra
property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Typical human waitress working in San Francisco in 2285. Old acquaintance of Dr. McCoy. She was surprised when he didn't order his usual poison.

name: Pennett
property_logo: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
lore: Genetically enhanced augment, typical of Khan's followers. Grateful to leave Ceti Alpha V behind. She quickly adapted to 23rd century technology.

name: Professor Scott
property_logo: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
lore: Mr. Scott visited Plexicorp in 1986, posing as a scholar from Edinburgh. Called "the miracle worker" by his friends. Scotty is an old Aberdeen pub crawler.

name: Refugee Guinan
lore: El-Aurian who fled from the assimilation of her homeworld. Hates the Borg. Was ripped from the Nexus in 2293. Left an echo of herself behind.

name: Sfreett
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Feline humanoid dancer. She was working on Nimbus III when Sybok took charge of Paradise City. Likes the arid atmosphere of the desolate world.

name: Shuttle Galileo
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: Large Federation shuttlecraft assigned to the U.S.S. Enterprise-A. Transported Sybok's Army of Light off Nimbus III to begin their quest for Sha Ka Ree.
game_text: May take off or land once each turn.

lore: Large Federation shuttlecraft assigned to the U.S.S. Enterprise-A. Transported Sybok's Army of Light off Nimbus III to begin their quest for Sha Ka Ree.
game_text: May take off or land once each turn.

name: Chariot of "God"
property_logo: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
lore: In 2287, the Galactic Army of Light commandeered the Federation starship U.S.S. Enterprise-A to traverse the Great Barrier and travel to Sha Ka Ree.

property_logo: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
lore: Common class of reconfigurable cargo vessel. Sometimes used as a passenger or courier transport.

name: A Little Fun Every Day
lore: While Anij taught Jean-Luc Picard to appreciate the beauty of a single moment, Artim taught Data to enjoy the value of play and to explore with childlike wonder.

name: High Ground
lore: Against direct orders, Jean-Luc Picard led the Ba'ku to climb nearer to kelbonite deposits in the mountains to evade intensive scans by the Son'a and avoid planetary evacuation.
game_text: To get past requires STRENGTH>40 if mission shows less than 30 points, STRENGTH>50 if it shows 30 points, or STRENGTH>60 if it shows more than 30 points.

name: Reman Dagger
lore: Traditional blade weapon developed on Remus. Shinzon used such a weapon to provide a blood sample for Beverly Crusher to examine and authenticate his story.
game_text: Each of your personnel present is STRENGTH +1. (Cumulative.) You may mortally wound your Reman present in personnel battle to mortally wound their adversary.

name: Reman Disruptor Rifle
lore: Energy rifle used by Reman assault teams. Has added blades for short range combat and a reduced anti-proton signature compared with standard Romulan disruptor rifles.
game_text: Reman use only. Each of your personnel present is STRENGTH +3. (Cumulative.) Your Remans present who have SECURITY or Leadership all add OFFICER.

name: Reman Scepter
lore: Traditional metal mace used by the Remans as a symbol of power and authority. The Viceroy carried such a staff during Shinzon's reign. Can also be used as a hand weapon.
game_text: Once every turn, if present with your Reman leader, you may draw a card when you play a Reman or an Equipment with "Reman" in title. (Unique.)

name: Oppression of the Remans
lore: The Reman miners worked together, doing whatever was required to survive the cruelty of the Romulan guards.

name: Personal Demons
lore: Shinzon felt his existence meaningless while Jean-Luc Picard was still alive. To make his mark, he vowed neither the Romulans nor the Federation would stop his Reman uprising.
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. While Shinzon is aboard the Scimitar, when a Federation or ROmulan non-Reman personnel is killed, score one point for each.

name: Versatile Vessel: Crew Transport
lore: A backbone of Starfleet during the 2360s and the 2370s, Nebula-class ships performed scientific research, deep space exploration, border patrol, and transportation duties.
game_text: Plays on your Nebula- or Military Freighter- class ship; download Rescue Personnel to this ship; it may target an Away Team in same quadrant at a different location.

name: Senate Chamber
lore: Guile and cunning are needed to survive in the legislative body of the Romulan Star Empire
game_text: Seeds or plays on Romulus. Once each turn, one Romulan V.I.P. OR one Romulan OFFICER with a Star Trek: Nemesis property logo OR one HQ card may play for free here. (Not duplicatable.)

name: Battle Stations: All Hands
lore: During crisis situations, the whole crew needs to pull together, from the captain to the lowest ranked crewman.
game_text: Seeds on table. Once each turn, if you have Battle Stations: Sovereign Class in play, you may play up to one unique, one Enigma, and one Universal personnel for free. You may not otherwise play personnel "for free.".

name: Battle Stations: Core Protection
lore: During alert situations, warp core integrity can be enhanced with forcefields to help ensure continuous flow of power.
game_text: Seeds on table. While you have Battle Stations: Sovereign Class in play, you may draw three cards in place of your normal card draw. During your turn, ignore effects from your other cards that allow or require you to draw cards.

name: Deliberately Discarded
lore: The Remans strategically left B-4's body parts to be found.

name: Engage the Borg
lore: Admiral Hayes mobilized the fleet in 2373, summoning all ships to defend Sector 001 against a Borg incursion.
game_text: Seeds on table. Your non-Alternate Universe Federation personnel with a Star Trek Generations, Star Trek Insurrection, or Star Trek Nemesis property logo gain First Contact. Score 5 points each time you destroy Borg Ship dilemma or a Borg ship in battle.

name: Formidable Warriors
lore: Reman troops were used as front line soldiers during the Dominion War, proving their mettle in the fiercest encounters

name: In Darkness there is Strength
lore: One side of Remus always faces its sun. Due to the temperature extremes, the Remans live on the dark side of their planet.
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. The first time you play a Reman from hand each turn, if played to Remus or your Romulan outpost, you may play a Universal Reman there for free.

name: The New Reman Flagship
game_text: Seeds on table. Your Remans, Scimitar, any Shinzon, and Equipmwnt may play to Remus. Once each turn, if you do not have a headquarters or time location in play, one such personnel may do so for free. Once each turn, you may kill your Reman to download an Equipmwnt with "Reman" in title OR kill two of your Remans to download Scimitar. Discard if you play a personnel that is not Romulan or Non-Aligned.

name: The Reman Mines
lore: Remus, the third planet of the Romulus system, is rich in dilithium and a base for Romulan heavy weapons production.
game_text: Seeds or plays on Remus. For each of your Romulan ships placed in your point area by Process Ore: Mining here, your ships are WEAPONS +1 (limit +3). Once solved, your Romulan ships are RANGE +2.

name: A Few Loose Ends
lore: Matthew Dougherty wanted to keep his plans with the Son'a to relocate the Ba'ku a secret. "You've done a terrific job. Now pack your bags and get the hell out of here."
game_text: Plays just after opponent solves (or completes a Borg Only objective targeting) a mission. If their score is higher than yours, all their personnel are stopped. OR Nullifies No Loose Ends.

name: Change of Heart
lore: Donatra appealed to Suran for support when she realized that Shinzon's goals did not match theirs, and that his sins would mark them for generations to come.
game_text: Plays on your unstopped personnel with Honor and OFFICER to cause a random selection present to be cancelled and re-selected. OR Nullifies Rules of Obedience.

name: Escape
lore: Pursued by the natives of Kolarus III, Jean-Luc Picard decided that the best course of action was to drive straight off a cliff, into the safety of an awaiting shuttlecraft.

name: Confront Duplicate
lore: Bassen Rift: Challenge adversary in nebula that disrupts long-range communications.
game_text: None

name: Activate Thalaron Weapon
game_text: Plays on a homeworld. Target your Scimitar in Romulus System Region. If your staffed Scimitar is here, you may probe:Romulan: Emitters extended. Ignore Romulan when probing.Command: If emitters extended, generator primed.Interrupt: If generator primed, weapon deployed: All personnel at this mission (or at all missions in this region) not aboard Scimitar are killed. Discard objective.

name: Investigate Warp Signature
game_text: Seeds on Earth; you must download Launch the Phoenix. Your personnel may attempt Earth using these requirements:Astrophysics + Anthropology + (Vulcan Lander OR CUNNING>30)When solved, mission worth 30 points (instead of printed value) or 40 points if Phoenix in orbit at this mission or Montana Missile Complex.

name: Recover Stolen Material
game_text: Seeds at the same mission as Space Lab Regula I, Armagosa Observatory, or a Science Lab. You may immediately seed an Artifact here. Your non-Federation crew or Away Team may attempt with these requirements:SECURITY x3 + STRENGTH > point value of missionWhen solved, if you did not earn an Artifact here, you may download up to three Equipment here. (Unique.)

name: Seventeen of Seventeen
lore: Identification: PURSUIT DRONETask: Intercept former shipmates of Hawk.Biological distinctiveness: Human.

name: Beverly Crusher
lore: Chief Medical Officer of the U.S.S. Enterprise-E. She helped activate B-4. Confirmed Shinzon was a clone, and that he was dying. Mother of Wesley Crusher.

name: Data
lore: Soong-type android and brother of B-4. He sang at the wedding of William T. Riker and Deanna Troi. Would willingly lay down his life for his shipmates.

name: Jean-Luc Picard
lore: Argo pilot itching to try some unsafe velocities. Human captain of the U.S.S Enterprise-E. Later discovered he had been cloned by the Romulans.

name: Martin Madden
lore: Human commander who took over as first officer of the U.S.S. Enterprise-E. He followed some bad advice from William T. Riker. Descendant of Jeremiah Hayes.

name: Wesley Crusher
lore: Son of Beverly Crusher. Returned to Starfleet briefly while not exploring with The Traveler. Recently assigned to U.S.S. Titan as assistant chief engineer.

name: Geordi La Forge
lore: Human engineer. His VISOR made him an unwitting pawn for the Sisters of Duras. Was frustratingly slow to observe his ship's shield frequencies.

name: B-4
lore: Prototype Soong-type android. Elder brother to Data and Lore, with a less sophisticated positronic brain.

name: B-4 (AI)
lore: Prototype Soong-type android. Elder brother to Data and Lore, with a less sophisticated positronic brain.

name: Guinan
lore: Former U.S.S Enterprise El-Aurian bartender. She's been married twenty-three times. Plans to re-open her bar at 10 Forward Avenue in Los Angeles.

name: Donatra
lore: Honorable commander and military advisor. Patriot who enlisted as a trooper. Opposed Shinzon when she saw his genocidal plans. Commands the Valdore.

name: Hiren
lore: Former Romulan admiral who replaced Neral as praetor. Rejected Shinzon's proposed alliance as he has no love for his Reman neighbors.

name: Mullen
lore: Romulan tactical officer and aide to Donatra. Served aboard the Valdore during the Battle of Bassen Rift in 2379. He is well-versed in Romulan military history.

name: Noram
lore: One of many commanders who supports greater integration of Reman troops in the Romulan military. Dissident who conspired with Talvin and Tal'Aura.

name: Suran
lore: Ambitious commander of the Soterus. Dissident who opposed Hiren's government. He conspired with Shinzon, seeking to strengthen the Romulan military.

name: Talvin
lore: Typical commander. He conspired with Tal'Aura and Noram to wipe out senate opposition to Shinzon. Dissident who sympathises with the Reman cause.

name: Thalpet
lore: Senior Reman scientist who worked on miniaturizing the thalaron radiation generator used by Tal'Aura. Served aboard the Scimitar. Elder brother of Chagrith.

name: Upexi
lore: Skilled Reman marksman who led many successful campaigns as a trooper. Though proven adept, he has yet to accept a command of his own.

name: Vkruk
lore: Reman mentor to Young Shinzon in the hellish mines, eventually becoming his viceroy. Looked up to by his fellow Remans, but lacks their beastliness.

name: Young Shinzon
lore: Human clone of Jean-Luc Picard. While still a minor, the original infiltration plan for him was abandoned. He was instead sent to work as a miner on Remus.

name: Sevek
lore: Vulcan expert in planetary development. He served with Solkar in 2063 and was one of the first Vulcans to openly visit Earth. Does not enjoy human music.

name: Solkar
lore: Vulcan explorer who made first contact with humans in 2063. Commands a Vulcan Lander. He found Zefram Cochrane's musical tastes to be fascinating.

name: T'Shonra
lore: Vulcan sensor specialist who visited Earth in 2063. She politely declined Zefram Cochrane's offer of an alcoholic beverage, even if it was "the good stuff."

name: U.S.S. Farragut
lore: NCC-60597. Sent to salvage the U.S.S. Enterprise saucer section on Veridian III. Aided the colonists on Ajilon Prime after a Klingon attack in 2373.

name: Norexan
lore: Prototype warbird designed to supersede the aging D'deridex-class and replace the extensive losses the Romulan fleet suffered during the Dominion War.

name: Scorpion One
lore: Reman shuttlecraft and attack flier often deployed during the Dominion War. Stolen by Jean-Luc Picard and Data to escape captivity aboard the Scimitar.
game_text: May report to Remus or aboard your Scimitar. Engage Shuttle Operations

name: Valdore
lore: Romulan warbird which turned against the Scimitar and aligned with the U.S.S. Enterprise-E at the Battle of Bassen Rift. Named after a 22nd-century admiral.
game_text: May initiate battle against Romulan.

name: Vulcan Lander
lore: Vulcan vessel in use during the 21st century. Solkar commanded during first contact with Earth.
game_text: May take off or land (uses 1 RANGE).Anthropology

name: Distracting Technology
lore: The Xyrillian holodeck was centuries ahead of most Alpha Quadrant races' recreational facilities. "If we had one of these on Enterprise, I'd never ask for shore leave."
game_text: Place on ship. If ship is 22nd Century or Original Series , all crew with that icon are stopped this turn. Any player voluntarily moving or attacking with this ship must first discard 2 cards from hand.

name: Promethean Quartz
lore: A mysterious crystal found in the Gamma Quadrant by Vash was later revealed to be an egg of a spaceborne life-form.
game_text: Opponent may download and seed a Selfless dilemma here. Unless Exobiology, SCIENCE and CUNNING>40 OR Archaeology, ENGINEER and STRENGTH>40, crew or Away Team stopped. Discard dilemma.

name: The Arsenal: Weapons Demonstration
lore: The automated weapons system on Minos also attacked orbiting starships. "The 607 does it all... neutralize ground personnel, even destroy enemy space vessels."
game_text: To get past, choose your ship here (even a cloaked or landed ship): opponent may Tactic Draw . You may lose 10 points to prevent one Tactic Draw , or 20 points to prevent both.

name: 48th Rule of Acquisition
lore: "The bigger the smile, the sharper the knife."
game_text: Plays on your Ferengi ship. While Gold-Pressed Latinum aboard, ship is WEAPONS +1 for each Diplomacy aboard (limit +3).

name: Astrometrics Lab
lore: Seven of Nine and Harry Kim combined astrometric technology from Starfleet and the Borg. Their enhanced sensors helped them plot a more efficient route home.
game_text: Plays on your ship. Once each turn, if Stellar Cartography aboard, you may discard the top card of your draw deck to make this ship RANGE +3 until end of turn.

name: Border Checkpoint
lore: In order for the U.S.S. Defiant to enter Cardassian territory in 2371, Benjamin Sisko used a holofilter to appear as a Kobheerian and allow the ship to pass the Cardassian patrols.
game_text: Plays on a mission with "array" or "listening post" in lore. Once each turn, when you play a non-Federation ship here, you may draw a card..

name: Versatile Vessel: Applied Science
lore: The Romulan scientists aboard the Apnex strategically used an undetected muon feedback wave to destabilize the U.S.S. Enterprise's dilithium chamber.
game_text: Plays on your Nebula- or Science- class ship or scout ship. Once each turn, you may select SCIENCE OR Geology OR Stellar Cartography OR Astrophysics. Until re-selected, adds that skill.

name: Vulcan Observation
lore: After taking their initial steps into deep space, Jonathan Archer and his crew felt the gaze of their pointy-eared neighbors looking over their shoulder a little too often.
game_text: Plays on an opponent's Planet mission. Add the skills of each Vulcan ship here to this mission's requirements (add double those skills instead if this mission is Federation or Starfleet).

name: Cytherian Lure
lore: Great Barrier Region • Cytheria: Exchange knowledge with advanced race.
game_text: Cytherians in this quadrant instead force travel here.

name: Monitor Traffic
lore: Morska Listening Post: Identify ships crossing busy border.
game_text: Border Checkpoint may seed here.

name: Assembly Transport
lore: Bajoran transport used by various dignitaries and members of the Vedek Assembly. This class of transport is named after a forested area on Bajor.
game_text: RANGE and SHIELDS +1 for each vedek aboard (limit 4).

name: Type-2 Galor
lore: Vessel used by the Cardassian Union from the outbreak of hostilities with the Federation until the 2360s when it was replaced by the Type-3 Galor.
game_text: WEAPONS +3 while you have a captive.

name: U.S.S. Defiant
lore: Federation starship commandeered and commanded by Kudak'Etan. Encountered a little problem.
game_text: Attributes all -3 unless Ketracel White in crew.

name: U.S.S. Ambassador
lore: Mainstay Federation vessel of the mid-24th century. NCC-10521. The design had more maneuverability than many of its counterparts of that era.

name: U.S.S. Sovereign
lore: Prototype advanced cruiser developed in the early 2370s. First ship of its class. NCC-73811. Part of a special Federation task force in 2384.
game_text: Attributes all +1 if Enterprise-E aboard.

name: Pequod
lore: Cruiser commanded by Takirac. The first to install holographic projectors. Renamed after a ship from Takirac's favorite hunting simulation, Moby Dick.
game_text: WEAPONS and SHIELDS +4 vs. Selfless .

name: Klingon Transport
lore: Shuttlecraft of Klingon design. Koral commanded one in 2370. Was intercepted before his rendezvous.
game_text: May report with 2 personnel (one must have Smuggling) to any Non-Aligned mission.

name: Soterus
lore: Warbird commanded by Suran during the Battle of Bassen Rift. Survived the conflict but sustained significant damage. Sister ship to the Valdore.
game_text: While in battle, may draw an extra Tactic.

name: Close That Door!
lore: A delicate stellar cartography experiment was ruined by Jean-Luc Picard when he opened a door at three o'clock in the morning to find out why he couldn't get his Earl Grey.
game_text: To get past requires SCIENCE and Stellar Cartography. Nullify by discarding a doorway from hand.

name: Dark Matter Pockets
lore: The Mar Oscura Nebula has an unusually high concentration of dark matter. Intersecting such pockets can temporarily phase bulkheads or entire planets out of existence.
game_text: Opponent may download Gaps in Normal Space adjacent to here. To get past requires 2 SCIENCE (at planet ) OR Navigation and Stellar Cartography (at Space ).

name: Stratagem
lore: To find the Xindi weapon, Jonathan Archer's crew constructed an elaborate simulation in which he and Degra had escaped together from a Xindi-Insectoid prison and stolen a shuttle.
game_text: Unless crew or Away Team has all printed skills on an opponent's captive (opponent's choice; nullified if none), opponent may peek at any one card. Discard dilemma.

name: Taspar Egg
lore: Boiled taspar egg is a Cardassian delicacy. Raw taspar egg can serve as nourishment during especially desperate times, or be used to debase a prisoner during torture.
game_text: While you have a captive, your Cardassian personnel present are either INTEGRITY +2 or INTEGRITY -2. You may change this at any time, even when facing a dilemma. (Unique.).

name: Extracted Confessions
lore: Skilled interrogators always get the information they seek. "...current assignment?" "Special operations on Celtris III."
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Each time you score points from Interrogation, score 1 additional point. (Cumulative.) Your TNG guls gain each different regular skill on your captives affected by your copies of Torture (at their highest levels).

name: Secret Prison
lore: Gul Madred commanded this hidden interrogation facility where Jean-Luc Picard was questioned in 2369.
game_text: Seeds or plays at Celtris III. Has a Brig.

name: Know Your Enemy
lore: Experienced officers can anticipate their opponents' moves.
game_text: Seeds on table if your missions are all different and show less than 35 points. End of each turn, if all of your missions share an affiliation icon and you are neither playing that affiliation nor Borg, draw a card.

name: Latest Provocation
lore: A failed covert operation by the Federation allowed the Cardassian Union to gain an advantage in its negotiations.
game_text: Seeds on table. At the end of each of your turns, if you are playing only Cardassian, you may draw one additional card. Discard if you voluntarily initiate battle, attempt a mission, or play a Punishment card.

name: Covert Incursion
lore: McAllister Region • C-5 Nebula: Hide invasion force amid intense particle flux.

name: Mine Enemy Fleet
lore: McAllister Region • Nebula near Minos: Position explosives near hidden ships.
game_text: When solved, may damage opponent's ships in region.

name: Repair Sabotage
lore: Nebula near Cardassian Outpost 47: Evade detection while fixing damaged systems.

name: Secure Covert Transportation
lore: Torman V: Arrange passage into neighboring territory without detection.
game_text: *+5 if Smuggling in Away Team.

name: Dispatch Metagenic Experts
game_text: Seeds or plays on table. Target an Alpha Quadrant Cardassian mission Planet mission (opponent's if possible). If your non-Cardassian Away Team there has Biology, Physics, and 2 SECURITY at end of turn, objective complete: opponent chooses one of those personnel to be captured and relocated to their facility, crew, or Away Team, you may download Get Him Cleaned Up, then discard objective (score points).

name: Get Him Cleaned Up
game_text: Plays on table if your Dispatch Metagenic Experts is complete. When your crew completes a Cardassian mission nebula mission, objective complete: you may return one personnel you own who is a captive (your choice) to your facility, draw up to 3 cards, and your Cardassian mission missions showing 30 points or less solved this game (even those already solved) are worth +5 points if solved by your crew or Away Team.

name: Admiral Kennelly
lore: Human who conspired with the Cardassians. He sent Ro Laren to make a secret offer to Orta, but secretly planned to betray and eliminate the terrorist cell.

name: Admiral Kennelly (AI)
lore: Human who conspired with the Cardassians. He sent Ro Laren to make a secret offer to Orta, but secretly planned to betray and eliminate the terrorist cell.

name: Andro
lore: Cardassian pilot serving in Starfleet in a different quantum reality. Worf encountered him aboard an alternate U.S.S. Enterprise in 2370.

name: Andro (AI)
lore: Cardassian pilot serving in Starfleet in a different quantum reality. Worf encountered him aboard an alternate U.S.S. Enterprise in 2370.

name: Ansomah
lore: One of many Cardassian scientists serving aboard the Bralek. He accompanied Ocett to Vilmor II when the secret of the DNA program was revealed.

name: Belcalis
lore: Typical Cardassian intelligence asset. His undercover team, dressed as monks, attacked a Maquis cell at the Juhraya colony. Later promoted to legate.

name: Glinn Telak
lore: Communications officer aboard the Vetar. He liaised with Gul Evek about a hostage situation on Dorvan V. Injured during a Maquis attack in 2370.

name: Gul Evek
lore: Cardassian who commands the Vetar. Evek lost two of his three sons in a war with the Federation. He doesn't want to lose the last son the same way.

name: Human
lore: Human interrogated by Gul Madred. Chose to remain imprisoned to protect Beverly Crusher. Near the end, Jean-Luc Picard believed he could see five lights.

name: Jil Orra
lore: One of many Cardassian children who admire their parents' military service. Daughter of Gul Madred. Cares for her pet wompat. Curious about humans.

name: Lepel
lore: Representative of Cardassian prison guards serving on Celtris III. Inspired by Gul Madred, he desires to learn about other species and their weaknesses.

name: Mekar
lore: Typical Cardassian working for Gul Madred. Cook and field medic. He provides taspar eggs for nutrition: boiled for the officers, live for the prisoners.

name: Vengar
lore: Cardassian crewman on the Vetar. He was briefly taken hostage while assessing buildings and equipment expected to be left behind on Dorvan V.

name: Beverly Crusher
lore: Doctor and metagenics expert serving on the U.S.S. Enterprise. She covertly went to Celtris III with Worf and Jean-Luc Picard. Very, very grateful to Solok.

name: Data
lore: Soong-type android appointed as executive officer by Edward Jellico. He viewed Jellico's changes and targets as attainable goals.

name: Deanna Troi
lore: ½ Betazoid, ½ Human counselor aboard the U.S.S. Enterprise. She started wearing more formal bridge attire at the direction of Edward Jellico.

name: Edward Jellico
lore: Efficient human captain of the U.S.S. Enterprise who abrasively reorganized shipboard operations. He is an expert on Cardassian behaviour. Born on Mars.

name: Gates
lore: One of many human conn officers aboard the U.S.S. Enterprise. Amazing pilot. She was a race-winning athlete during her academy days.

name: William T. Riker
lore: Skilled human pilot. U.S.S. Enterprise first officer, until Edward Jellico relieved him of that role after they clashed over Jean-Luc Picard's capture.

name: Worf
lore: Klingon chief of security aboard the U.S.S. Enterprise. In 2369, he was assigned to infiltrate Celtris III. Expert in Mok'bara. Father of Alexander Rozhenko.

name: Vetar
lore: Cardassian warship commanded by Gul Evek. Often patrols the Demilitarized Zone. Attacked by the Maquis in 2370 until the U.S.S. Enterprise arrived.
game_text: WEAPONS and SHIELDS +2 while you have a captive.

name: U.S.S. Cairo
lore: Commanded by Edward Jellico prior to and following his temporary assignment to the U.S.S. Enterprise. Assigned to help defend Minos Korva in 2369.
